12c2481d04b4.title: AI on the Lot 2026_LTX-2.3_IC LoRA (Union Control)
12c2481d04b4.description: The second bonus workflow for AI on the Lot 2026, made available for ComfyUI 101 workshop attendees to open and follow along if time allows. A video editing workflow using LTX 2.3 with the Union Control IC LoRA and canny control. Provide a modified frame from your video and the workflow propagates that change across the clip. For example, take a frame from a video of a shirtless boxer, edit a red shirt onto him, and the output video will show him wearing the red shirt throughout.
12c2481d04b4.metaDescription: Propagate a single-frame edit across an entire clip using LTX 2.3, Union Control IC LoRA, and canny guidance in ComfyUI for consistent, structure-preserving video edits.
12c2481d04b4.extendedDescription:
This workflow performs reference-based video-to-video editing with LTX 2.3, steered by the Union Control IC LoRA and canny edge guidance. You supply a single edited frame from your clip (for example, painting a red shirt onto a boxer), and the pipeline propagates that visual change to every frame in the video while preserving motion and structure. The core processing happens in the custom processing block (UUID: 9278a6c3-b46a-4e21-8d09-5103f85ffec6), which runs LTX 2.3 inference with the Union Control IC LoRA and integrates canny control to keep edges and silhouettes consistent across time.

Technically, LoadVideo ingests your source clip and feeds frames into the inference block, where canny edge maps are used as a structural prior so the subject’s pose and scene layout remain stable. LoadImage brings in your manually edited reference frame, which the IC LoRA uses as an appearance guide to replicate the change throughout the sequence. After processing, VHS_VideoCombine assembles the generated frames back into a video, and SaveVideo writes the final output to disk. This approach is ideal when you want targeted, consistent replacements—like color swaps, wardrobe fixes, or logo/graphic updates—without re-shoots or heavy roto work.
howToUse: Open the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. Confirm the nodes are present: LoadVideo, LoadImage, the main processing block (UUID: 9278a6c3-b46a-4e21-8d09-5103f85ffec6), VHS_VideoCombine, and SaveVideo.

In LoadVideo, select your source clip. For best results, use a stable shot with clear subject framing. Keep resolution and duration reasonable for your GPU; shorter clips and moderate resolutions render faster.

Export a representative frame from the same clip (e.g., via your video player), make your visual change in an external editor (paint a new shirt color, add a logo, etc.), then load that edited image into the LoadImage node. Use a frame where the target area is clearly visible.

Open the main processing block (UUID: 9278a6c3-...). Adjust key settings if exposed: control strength (how strongly the edit propagates), canny thresholds (edge sensitivity), guidance/CFG scale, steps, and seed. Higher control strength and lower canny thresholds push stronger edits; higher thresholds preserve more of the original structure.

Queue the workflow. Preview a few frames to check consistency and the extent of the edit. If the change is too strong or too subtle, tweak control strength, canny thresholds, or choose a clearer reference frame, then re-run.
When satisfied, let the run complete. VHS_VideoCombine assembles frames into a video, and SaveVideo writes the final file to disk. Review the output and iterate as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Wardrobe and color continuity fixes across b‑roll or interview clips (e.g., recolor a shirt or jacket).
Brand compliance updates, like swapping product colors or adding a logo consistently across a sequence.
Quick look-dev for costume/prop variations without re-shooting.
Replacing or harmonizing graphic elements on moving subjects (badges, patches, simple decals).
Previsualization when testing alternate art directions on existing footage.

faqItems.question: Do I need to train anything for my specific video?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow uses LTX 2.3 plus the Union Control IC LoRA as a general-purpose conditioning method. You provide one edited frame as a reference, and the model propagates that change across the clip.

faqItems.question: How should I choose the reference frame?
faqItems.answer: Pick a clear frame where the target area is fully visible and not heavily motion‑blurred or occluded. The more unambiguous your edit, the easier it is for the model to generalize it across the sequence.

faqItems.question: What do the canny settings influence?
faqItems.answer: Canny thresholds control edge sensitivity. Lower thresholds capture more fine detail (pushing stronger edits but risking overreach), while higher thresholds preserve broader structure (maintaining pose and layout but reducing how much the edit can reshape details). Adjust alongside control strength to balance fidelity and change.

faqItems.question: How long of a clip can I process?
faqItems.answer: That depends on your GPU memory and patience. Start with short segments at moderate resolution. If needed, split long videos into sections, process each, and reassemble downstream in your editor.

13ba3af78782.title: LTX-2.5: Text to Video
13ba3af78782.description: Generate cinematic video from a text prompt using LTX-2.5, a production-ready diffusion model that outputs a single video file with optional spatial upscaling for enhanced resolution. Ideal for film previsualization, commercial storyboards, and high-volume content creation pipelines.
13ba3af78782.metaDescription: Generate cinematic text-to-video with LTX-2.5 in ComfyUI. Select resolution, refine settings, optionally upscale, and export a single video file.
13ba3af78782.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a plain text prompt into a cinematic video using Lightricks' LTX-2.5, a production-ready diffusion model. The core of the graph is the LTX-2.5 text-to-video node (UUID: 8b4f085c-1bb3-4ecd-aeed-603a8d6d3970), which consumes your prompt, resolution, and generation settings to synthesize a coherent clip. A ResolutionSelector node feeds width and height values that are aligned to the model’s preferred multiples-of-32, and a SaveVideo node encodes the result as a single video file. A MarkdownNote is included in the graph to surface quick tips and resolution guidance right inside ComfyUI.

Under the hood, LTX-2.5 uses a Pixel Diffusion, keyframes-first approach: it establishes strong visual anchors and then diffuses motion between them, helping maintain temporal consistency and cinematic pacing. You can steer fidelity and GPU memory use by pairing the ResolutionSelector with the model’s parameters. For example, 0.5 megapixels at 16:9 maps to 960x544, while 0.3 MP maps to 736x416; both are safe starting points on modest GPUs. When you need extra detail, enable the node’s optional spatial upscaling to boost resolution without re-generating motion from scratch, then finalize with SaveVideo at your target FPS and file path.
howToUse: Load the LTX-2.5: Text to Video workflow JSON in ComfyUI and confirm the LTX-2.5 node (UUID: 8b4f085c-1bb3-4ecd-aeed-603a8d6d3970) is present without missing-model warnings.
In ResolutionSelector, choose your aspect ratio and target megapixels to auto-fill width and height (multiples of 32). Start around 0.4–0.6 MP for quicker previews.
Open the LTX-2.5 node and enter your text prompt. Set generation options such as seed (for reproducibility), the number of frames or duration, and FPS to control clip length and motion cadence.
Optionally enable spatial upscaling in the LTX-2.5 node to enhance detail. Adjust upscale factor or target size if available, keeping an eye on VRAM usage.
Configure SaveVideo with the desired FPS and output path, then Queue Prompt. Review the saved clip, iterate on prompt or resolution, and re-run until you’re satisfied.
suggestedUseCases: Film previsualization and animatics for planning shots and camera moves.
Commercial storyboards and product hero shots to convey motion intent to clients.
Social media motion concepts and loops to validate ideas quickly.
Concept art with motion to communicate mood, lighting, and pacing.
Rapid content generation for high-volume pipelines needing consistent, local runs.

faqItems.question: Why does the workflow use a ResolutionSelector instead of typing width and height manually?
faqItems.answer: LTX-2.5 performs best with dimensions that are multiples of 32. ResolutionSelector maps practical megapixel targets to valid sizes (for example, 0.5 MP at 16:9 → 960x544), helping you balance detail, speed, and VRAM without guesswork.

faqItems.question: How does LTX-2.5 keep motion consistent across frames?
faqItems.answer: The model uses a Pixel Diffusion, keyframes-first strategy to establish strong visual anchors and then diffuse motion between them. This reduces temporal drift and improves coherence in complex scenes.

faqItems.question: What controls affect performance and memory use the most?
faqItems.answer: Resolution and frame count are the biggest factors. Start with lower megapixels (0.3–0.6 MP) and shorter clips to iterate, then scale up. Enabling spatial upscaling increases memory use; raise it only after you are happy with motion and composition.

faqItems.question: What does SaveVideo output, and can I change FPS?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo writes a single video file to disk from the generated clip. You can set FPS in the node to match your target pacing and ensure the saved file aligns with your project’s delivery specs.

148dc613d99c.extendedDescription:
This workflow teaches you how to steer Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash to generate a video that features specific people, products, or objects without ever cutting to the original photos. It does this by binding each loaded reference image to a role tag (for example, <IMAGE_REF_0>, <IMAGE_REF_1>) and then using those tags inside your scene description so the model knows which visual subject to synthesize into the shot. The core is the GeminiVideoOmniV2 node running in reference mode, fed by one or more LoadImage nodes for character and style/product references, and finalized by a SaveVideo node to write the result to disk. A MarkdownNote in the graph documents the prompt pattern and tag usage.

Technically, each reference image is converted into a visual embedding that conditions Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash during generation. When you reference the bound tags in your prompt (for example, "Use <IMAGE_REF_0> as the model; use <IMAGE_REF_1> as the makeup palette product"), the model synthesizes frames that include those subjects while never showing the source images as frames. You can combine character references with a separate style or product board, direct the scene in plain language (actions, camera moves, lighting, location), and, when enabled in the node, generate native audio. This makes it ideal for brand-consistent shorts, character-driven storytelling, and product placement where control over who/what appears on screen matters.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm your Gemini API setup for the GeminiVideoOmniV2 node (set your Google AI Studio API key in the node or as an environment variable as required).

Import your reference images with LoadImage nodes. For the example, place input/terracotta_eyeshadow_palette.png (required) and your model photo (e.g., input/asian_female_model_beige_suit.png) into the input folder and connect each LoadImage output to the GeminiVideoOmniV2 image reference inputs.

Open GeminiVideoOmniV2. In its prompt/instruction field, assign roles using tags that match your connections, then direct the scene. Example: "Use <IMAGE_REF_0> as the hero makeup palette product. Use <IMAGE_REF_1> as the on-camera model. Warm studio lighting, slow push-in, the model opens the palette and applies the terracotta shade; include soft ambient music. Do not display the raw reference photos."

Optionally add a style board as another LoadImage and bind it to a tag (e.g., <IMAGE_REF_2> as style reference). Keep the prompt clear: location, action beats, camera movement, mood, and any brand tones. If the node exposes duration, resolution, or audio toggles, set them here.
Run the graph. The GeminiVideoOmniV2 node will generate the video conditioned on your references and pass it to SaveVideo. When complete, open the saved file from your ComfyUI output directory.

Iterate: if identity or product fidelity is weak, tighten the role lines (repeat the tag once in the opening sentence, name the role explicitly), simplify conflicting style requests, and ensure your reference images are clear, well-lit, and show the subject prominently.
suggestedUseCases: Product showcases where a specific item (palette, shoe, gadget) must appear on screen without cutting to the original product photo.
Character-led social shorts that keep the same person across multiple scenes or episodes for consistency.
Brand-consistent explainer clips using a style board plus a presenter portrait as separate references.
In-situ product placement within lifestyle shots (e.g., a model interacts with a referenced item in a café or studio).
Pitch animatics or mood tests combining a character reference with a visual style sheet.

faqItems.question: How do I correctly bind images to roles?
faqItems.answer: Load each image with a LoadImage node and connect it to the GeminiVideoOmniV2 image reference inputs. In your prompt, refer to them with the exact tags used by the node (e.g., <IMAGE_REF_0>, <IMAGE_REF_1>). Immediately assign a role: "Use <IMAGE_REF_0> as the product" or "Use <IMAGE_REF_1> as the presenter." Keep those tags near the start of the prompt so the model prioritizes them.

faqItems.question: Will the reference photos ever appear directly in the video?
faqItems.answer: No. In this workflow the images are used as visual references only. Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash conditions on their content to synthesize new frames; it does not insert the source photos as frames.

faqItems.question: Can I mix character and style references in one generation?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Provide separate LoadImage nodes for character/product and style boards, bind each to its own tag, and clarify their roles in the prompt (e.g., "<IMAGE_REF_0> character, <IMAGE_REF_1> product, <IMAGE_REF_2> style reference"). Avoid conflicting instructions (e.g., opposing lighting or wardrobe notes) to maintain fidelity.

faqItems.question: Why doesn’t the person or product look consistent with my reference?
faqItems.answer: Common causes are unclear role assignment, low-quality references, or conflicting prompt details. Put the tags at the start, describe each role plainly, use high-resolution, well-lit references where the subject is large in frame, and reduce competing style constraints. If needed, shorten the scene description and focus on essentials (location, key action, lighting).

171dea657096.title: Utility Video Upscale
171dea657096.description: Upscale videos to sharper, higher-resolution outputs with Wan2.2, with precise control over detail, denoise strength, and sizing parameters in Utility Video Upscale.
171dea657096.metaDescription: Upscale videos to HD/4K with Wan2.2 in ComfyUI. Control denoise/detail, choose valid resolutions, preview before/after, and rebuild at source FPS.
171dea657096.extendedDescription:
Utility Video Upscale is a compact ComfyUI pipeline for turning soft, low-res clips into sharper, higher-resolution videos using a Wan2.2 upscaler node (custom node ID 8c62a455-6744-43c8-9352-543905ed4db7). The flow is straightforward: LoadVideo ingests your source, GetVideoComponents extracts metadata such as FPS and frame count, and ResolutionSelector lets you pick a valid target size (width and height divisible by 64) with presets for common formats like Full HD (~2.1 MP) and 4K (~8.3 MP). The Wan2.2 node handles the heavy lifting, exposing practical controls for denoise strength and detail so you can balance clean-up versus texture preservation.

For clarity and iteration, the workflow includes a Before vs After Comparison group that uses ImageFromBatch to select a frame and ImageStitch to create a side-by-side composite, helping you dial in settings before a full run. Once satisfied, CreateVideo rebuilds the clip at the chosen resolution (typically using the source FPS passed from GetVideoComponents), and SaveVideo writes the result. Because Wan2.2 processes a limited number of frames per run (up to about 121 frames) and is VRAM-bound, the workflow is designed to be predictable and memory-conscious while giving you precise control over upscale size and perceived sharpness.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the Load Video group. Use the LoadVideo node to select your source clip. GetVideoComponents will automatically read metadata like FPS and frame count.
Open the Target Resolution group. In ResolutionSelector, choose a preset (e.g., 1920x1088 for FHD or 3840x2176 for 4K) or set custom dimensions. Ensure both width and height are divisible by 64.

In the Utility Video Upscale group, tune the Wan2.2 upscaler (node ID 8c62a455-6744-43c8-9352-543905ed4db7). Start with moderate denoise (around mid-range) and a conservative detail setting; raise detail only as needed for more texture.

Use the Before vs After Comparison group to preview results. Pick a representative frame with ImageFromBatch and view the side-by-side composite from ImageStitch. Adjust denoise/detail or resolution until the preview looks right.
When satisfied, confirm CreateVideo is using the FPS from GetVideoComponents so playback speed matches the source. Check CreateVideo/SaveVideo settings for your preferred container/quality.
Execute the graph. If your clip exceeds the practical limit for Wan2.2 (about 121 frames) or VRAM, process in segments and concatenate the parts afterward.
suggestedUseCases: Upscaling archival or smartphone footage to clean Full HD or 4K for social posts and client deliverables.
Prepping sharper plates for VFX or editorial while preserving motion consistency across frames.
Enhancing gameplay captures or screen recordings for higher-quality uploads without re-recording.
Creating before/after comparisons for QA or client reviews using the side-by-side frame preview.

faqItems.question: Why must the width and height be divisible by 64?
faqItems.answer: Upscale models like Wan2.2 operate on feature grids that expect image dimensions aligned to 64-pixel blocks. Use sizes like 1920x1088 (not 1920x1080) or 3840x2176 to avoid padding and artifacts.

faqItems.question: How many frames can I process at once with Wan2.2?
faqItems.answer: Wan2.2 is practical up to about 121 frames per run, and the exact limit depends on available VRAM. For longer clips, split the video into segments and process each segment separately.

faqItems.question: How should I set denoise strength and detail?
faqItems.answer: Start with moderate denoise to clean compression noise without erasing real texture, and keep detail conservative to avoid oversharpening. Increase detail gradually if the result still looks soft; lower it (and denoise) if edges look harsh or halos appear.

faqItems.question: Does the workflow keep the original audio?
faqItems.answer: This pipeline focuses on frames. If your CreateVideo/SaveVideo nodes don’t mux audio, export the upscaled video and merge the original audio in a video editor or FFmpeg. If your CreateVideo supports audio inputs, connect them from GetVideoComponents.

181a9571c9a0.extendedDescription:
Graphic Color Remixer is a compact ComfyUI workflow that takes a single input graphic and produces 4, 9, or 16 colorway variations based on your chosen vibe and palette. It’s designed for fast exploration of themes without changing the original layout—perfect for logos, icons, posters, packaging, or UI mockups where geometry must remain intact.

Technically, the pipeline is minimal and efficient: LoadImage imports your source graphic, which is passed into a custom node that handles the remixing. howToUse: Open ComfyUI and load the 'Graphic Color Remixer' workflow. Confirm the custom remixer node (5772692b-9d2a-4a1f-b676-71b8fd315078) is present. If it’s missing, install the extension that provides this node and restart ComfyUI.
In the LoadImage node, select your source graphic (PNG/JPG). Flat graphics with clear shapes (logos, icons, posters, UI elements) produce the most consistent recolors.

Select the remixer node (5772692b-9d2a-4a1f-b676-71b8fd315078) and set: a) Vibe or style intent (e.g., 'retro neon', 'earthy minimal'), b) Desired color palette (palette name or hex values, depending on the node UI), and c) Variation count: 4, 9, or 16.

If the node requires Nano Banana API access, supply or verify your API key/credentials in the node’s settings or your ComfyUI environment. A single API generation will be used to produce all requested variations.
In SaveImage, set your file naming prefix and output directory. This helps batch the results clearly (for example, 'remix_neon_').
Queue the workflow and run it. Review the saved outputs, then iterate—adjust vibe, tweak palette values, or switch the variation count (2x2, 3x3, 4x4) to compare options quickly.
suggestedUseCases: Brand palette testing: Re-skin logos or icons across multiple brand color directions in one pass.
UI theme exploration: Generate quick light/dark or seasonal theme colorways for the same layout.
Packaging and poster colorways: Preview multiple color directions without redrawing or re-laying out assets.
Social and campaign variants: Produce consistent on-brand color sets for graphics across platforms.
Icon set re-skins: Create multiple, cohesive color treatments for icon libraries while preserving shapes.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow change the layout or just the colors?
faqItems.answer: It focuses on color remapping. Shapes, composition, and text placement are preserved; only the palette and overall vibe shift. Use clean, well-contrasted source graphics for best results.

faqItems.question: Why can I only choose 4, 9, or 16 variations?
faqItems.answer: The remixer node is optimized for square sets (2x2, 3x3, 4x4). This yields balanced comparisons and efficient batching from a single Nano Banana generation.

faqItems.question: Do I need a local model checkpoint?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow doesn’t include a LoadCheckpoint node. The custom remixer node offloads the generative step to the Nano Banana API and then expands that single response into multiple color variants.

faqItems.question: How do I provide a color palette or vibe?
faqItems.answer: Open the remixer node (5772692b-9d2a-4a1f-b676-71b8fd315078) and enter your vibe text (e.g., 'warm vintage') and palette details (palette name or hex codes, depending on the node’s UI). If the node supports presets, you can select them directly.

By default, the template is set up to render at 720p and 24 fps, but you can change width/height and fps to match vertical (9:16), square (1:1), or cinematic (21:9) formats. The workflow can run prompt-only for pure text-to-video, or optionally take in a starting frame through LoadImage to guide composition, subject placement, or style from the first frame.

Technically, Flux3ImageToVideoNode expands your prompt into a sequence of frames with temporally consistent motion. Core controls you’ll use include the prompt text, seed (for repeatability), width/height (aspect and resolution), number of frames (duration), and fps. If you provide a reference image via LoadImage, the node can use it as an initialization frame to better lock framing and identity; the influence of this can be tuned inside the Flux3ImageToVideoNode. Once the frames are generated, SaveVideo assembles them into a single clip. Note that this workflow outputs silent video; if you need audio, add it later in a video editor.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure Flux3ImageToVideoNode is available. If it uses an API backend, enter your API key in the node’s settings as required.
Open Flux3ImageToVideoNode and write a clear prompt describing subject, action, setting, and style (e.g., "A golden retriever splashing through shallow waves at sunset, handheld, cinematic").
Optional: Use LoadImage to import a reference frame and connect it to the init/conditioning input on Flux3ImageToVideoNode to guide framing or style.

Set output parameters: width/height for your target aspect ratio, fps, and the number of frames to reach your desired length (e.g., 240 frames at 24 fps ≈ 10 seconds). Choose a seed to lock in results or randomize for more variety.
Adjust guidance/creativity controls in Flux3ImageToVideoNode (e.g., CFG/guidance scale or image influence if present) to balance prompt adherence vs. creative variation.
Queue the workflow. When generation finishes, SaveVideo will write the clip to disk. Preview the result and iterate on the prompt, duration, or settings as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Social media teasers in vertical or square formats without needing filmed footage.
Ad mockups and concept tests to visualize motion and scene pacing quickly.
Cinematic establishing shots or mood clips for previsualization and pitch decks.
Animated story beats from a single still reference to maintain framing and identity.
Style exploration passes (e.g., handheld vs. tripod, dusk vs. daylight) using prompt-only variations.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow generate audio?
faqItems.answer: No. With SaveVideo, the workflow exports a silent video. Add music, dialogue, or sound design later in a video editor or a separate audio pipeline.

faqItems.question: Can I guide the video with a still image?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Load a reference image with LoadImage and connect it to Flux3ImageToVideoNode. Then adjust the node’s image influence/strength (if available) so the model follows your frame without overconstraining motion.

faqItems.question: How do I change duration and frame rate?
faqItems.answer: Set fps and the number of frames. Duration ≈ frames ÷ fps (e.g., 240 frames at 24 fps ≈ 10 s). SaveVideo will encode at the fps you specify.

faqItems.question: What aspect ratios are supported and how do I avoid VRAM errors?
faqItems.answer: Any aspect ratio is supported by setting width/height. Taller or wider frames and higher resolutions use more memory; start at 720p, keep batch size to 1, and increase resolution gradually.

1880d7035ea2.title: Any Image → Any Aspect Ratio
1880d7035ea2.description: Upload any image and input your desired aspect ratio. Generate an outpainted version of your image to perfectly fit the new dimensions.
1880d7035ea2.metaDescription: Transform any image to fit any aspect ratio using outpainting with Nano Banana 2 in ComfyUI. Perfect for content creators and designers.
1880d7035ea2.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow is designed to transform any image into a new aspect ratio by utilizing advanced outpainting techniques. At its core, the workflow leverages the Nano Banana 2 model, known for its robust image completion capabilities. The process begins by uploading an image and specifying the desired aspect ratio, such as 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, or 4:5. The workflow then adapts the original image to fit the new dimensions, filling in the additional space with content that seamlessly extends the image's natural environment. This is achieved through a series of nodes, including LoadImage for importing the image, ImageCompositeMasked for handling the outpainting, and PreviewImage for visualizing the results.

What makes this workflow particularly useful is its ability to maintain the visual integrity of the original image while expanding its dimensions. This is ideal for content creators who need to adapt images for various platforms with different aspect ratio requirements. The integration of custom nodes like comfyui_essentials, controlaltai-nodes, and masquerade-nodes-comfyui further enhances the workflow's flexibility and precision, ensuring high-quality outputs that are both aesthetically pleasing and contextually relevant.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the interface.
Upload your desired image using the LoadImage node.
Select your target aspect ratio from the available options.
The workflow will process the image, adapting it to the new aspect ratio using the Nano Banana 2 model.
Preview the outpainted image using the PreviewImage node to ensure it meets your expectations.
Export the final image or animated GIF/WebM as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Adapting images for social media platforms with specific aspect ratio requirements.
Creating promotional materials that require consistent visual dimensions.
Enhancing landscape or architectural photography by expanding the scene.
Generating content for digital displays or presentations with varied aspect ratios.
Producing animated GIFs or WebM files from single images for dynamic content.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow with any image format?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow supports most common image formats, including JPEG, PNG, and BMP.

faqItems.question: What if the outpainted areas don't match the original image's style?
faqItems.answer: The Nano Banana 2 model is designed to blend seamlessly, but you can adjust parameters or manually refine the output if needed.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to revert to the original image after processing?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can always reload the original image and start the process again if you're not satisfied with the results.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow handle extreme aspect ratios?
faqItems.answer: While the workflow can manage a wide range of aspect ratios, extremely disproportionate dimensions may require additional manual adjustments for optimal results.

18da3456241d.title: Wan 2.1 Image to Video
18da3456241d.description: Generate videos from images using Wan 2.1.
18da3456241d.metaDescription: Animate a single image into a short video with Wan 2.1 in ComfyUI using WanImageToVideo, CLIP/T5 encoders, and KSampler. Clear steps, tips, and FAQs.
18da3456241d.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single image into a short video using Wan 2.1’s image-to-video pipeline. The core is the WanImageToVideo node, which prepares temporal conditioning (frame count, fps, and motion cues) and routes it into diffusion. Text guidance is encoded through CLIPTextEncode (backed by CLIPLoader loading the UMT5 XXL text encoder), while the starting image is embedded with CLIPVisionEncode using weights from CLIPVisionLoader. The model backbone is loaded via UNETLoader (Wan2.1) and VAELoader (Wan VAE). ModelSamplingSD3 sets the correct sampling profile, and KSampler performs denoising across the sequence of latent frames. Finally, VAEDecode converts latents to RGB frames, CreateVideo assembles them at your chosen fps/size, and SaveVideo writes the result to disk.

The workflow is organized for clarity: Step1 - Load models, Step2 - Upload start_image, Step3 - Video size, Step4 - Prompt. You’ll set width/height and frame rate in the Video size group, provide a clean source image via LoadImage, and craft a text prompt (plus optional negative prompt) to steer style and content. This makes it ideal for animating character turnarounds, subtle portrait motions, or product hero shots—all from a single still—while keeping results predictable through the start image and reproducible via seed and KSampler settings.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and load models (Step1 - Load models): use UNETLoader to select the Wan 2.1 UNet, VAELoader for the Wan VAE, CLIPLoader for the UMT5 XXL text encoder (e.g., umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors), and CLIPVisionLoader for the vision backbone.
Upload your starting image (Step2 - Upload start_image) with LoadImage. For best results, crop the image so its aspect ratio matches the target video size.
Set video parameters (Step3 - Video size): choose width, height, frame count, and fps. Keep the resolution modest at first if GPU memory is limited, then scale up.

Write your prompt (Step4 - Prompt) in CLIPTextEncode. Add a negative prompt to filter unwanted traits (e.g., "jpeg artifacts, low quality"). Use clear action words to encourage motion (e.g., turning, waving, rotating).

Verify sampling and diffusion: ensure ModelSamplingSD3 is connected and KSampler has reasonable steps, guidance (CFG), and a fixed seed for reproducibility. Leave the sampler profile as provided for Wan 2.1.
Queue and run. Inspect the preview frames decoded by VAEDecode; adjust prompt, size, steps, or frames as needed. When satisfied, CreateVideo assembles the frames and SaveVideo outputs the final file.
suggestedUseCases: Character turnarounds or subtle pose changes for concept art and VTuber assets.
Product hero animations from catalog photos (e.g., slow rotate, glinting highlights).
Portrait micro-animations (breathing, hair sway, gentle head turn).
Stylized mood shots for storyboards or animatics from a single panel.
Social clips that animate static artwork without a full 3D pipeline.

faqItems.question: Which models do I need and where do they go?
faqItems.answer: Load Wan 2.1’s UNet via UNETLoader, the matching VAE via VAELoader, the UMT5 XXL text encoder via CLIPLoader (e.g., umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors), and a CLIP vision backbone via CLIPVisionLoader. Place the files in your ComfyUI models folders (e.g., models/unet, models/vae, models/text_encoders or models/clip, models/clip_vision) or point the loader nodes directly to their locations.

faqItems.question: My video looks warped or cropped. How do I fix aspect issues?
faqItems.answer: Match the start image’s aspect ratio to your target width/height in the Video size group. Crop the source image accordingly before loading. Keeping the subject centered and well-lit also helps the model maintain structure during motion.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce VRAM usage or speed up generation?
faqItems.answer: Lower the resolution (width/height), reduce the number of frames, and try fewer diffusion steps in KSampler. Start small (fewer frames, lower size), confirm the look, then scale up gradually.

faqItems.question: Does it support non-English prompts and negative prompts?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The workflow encodes text with the UMT5 XXL text encoder, which works well with English and other languages (e.g., Chinese). You can also supply a negative prompt via CLIPTextEncode to suppress unwanted artifacts or styles.

faqItems.question: Why are results too static or too jittery?
faqItems.answer: For more motion, add clear action verbs and reduce overly strict descriptors that lock the pose. For smoother outputs, balance frame count and fps, keep resolution reasonable, and refine the negative prompt to remove busy backgrounds or unwanted detail that can flicker.

18f288d70060.title: HY 3D: Smart Topology
18f288d70060.description: Upload a high-poly 3D model file. Generate a lower-polygon, topologically optimized 3D model with a specified reduction level.
18f288d70060.metaDescription: Optimize high-poly 3D models with HY 3D: Smart Topology for efficient rendering and storage.
18f288d70060.extendedDescription: The HY 3D: Smart Topology workflow is designed to streamline the process of optimizing 3D models by reducing their polygon count while maintaining essential details. This workflow is particularly useful for those working with high-poly models that need to be simplified for applications such as real-time rendering or efficient storage. It utilizes the Hunyuan3D model to intelligently reduce the complexity of a 3D model without compromising on quality. The process begins with the Load3D node, which allows users to upload their high-poly models in formats such as .glb or .obj. The core of the workflow is the TencentSmartTopologyNode, which applies advanced algorithms to achieve the desired level of topology optimization. Finally, the SaveGLB node outputs the optimized model in a format ready for further use or distribution.
howToUse: Start by loading your high-poly 3D model using the Load3D node. Ensure your file is in .glb or .obj format and under 200MB.
Configure the TencentSmartTopologyNode to specify the desired level of polygon reduction for your model.
Run the workflow to process the model through the topology optimization algorithm.
Once processing is complete, use the SaveGLB node to export the optimized 3D model.
Review the output model to ensure it meets your quality and performance requirements.
suggestedUseCases: Preparing 3D models for real-time rendering in video games.
Reducing file size for efficient storage and distribution of 3D assets.
Optimizing models for use in augmented reality applications.
Streamlining 3D printing workflows by simplifying complex models.

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for input?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports .glb and .obj file formats for input models.

faqItems.question: What is the maximum file size for input models?
faqItems.answer: Input models should not exceed 200MB in size.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow handle topologized models?
faqItems.answer: No, it is recommended to use non-topologized high-poly models for optimal results.

faqItems.question: What types of models are best suited for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is highly applicable to hard surface models and those generated by Hunyuan3D.

1a126268f912.title: Moonvalley: Pose Control
1a126268f912.description: Apply human pose and movement from one video to another.
1a126268f912.metaDescription: Transfer human poses from one video to another using the Moonvalley model in ComfyUI for seamless video-to-video transformation.
1a126268f912.extendedDescription:
The 'Moonvalley: Pose Control' workflow is designed to transfer human poses and movements from one video to another, utilizing the advanced capabilities of the Moonvalley model. This workflow is particularly useful for video creators and animators who want to replicate specific movements or choreography across different characters or settings. The core of the workflow involves several key nodes, including LoadVideo for importing the source video, MoonvalleyVideo2VideoNode for processing and applying the pose data, and SaveVideo for exporting the final video. By leveraging these nodes, users can achieve highly accurate and realistic pose transfer, making it an invaluable tool for creative video production.

Technically, the workflow operates by first loading a reference video that contains the desired movements. The MoonvalleyVideo2VideoNode then analyzes this input to extract pose data, which is subsequently applied to a target video. This process is facilitated by the Moonvalley model, known for its robust video-to-video transformation capabilities. The workflow ensures that the transferred poses are seamlessly integrated into the new video, maintaining natural movement flow and synchronization. This makes it particularly useful for projects requiring precise motion replication, such as dance videos, sports analysis, or cinematic effects.
howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI and ensure you have the Moonvalley model installed.
Use the LoadVideo node to import your reference video, ensuring it is at least 5 seconds long.
Configure the MoonvalleyVideo2VideoNode by selecting the desired output parameters and linking it to the LoadVideo node.
Run the workflow to process the pose data and apply it to your target video.
Use the SaveVideo node to export the final video with the transferred poses.
Review the output video to ensure the pose transfer meets your expectations and make adjustments if necessary.
suggestedUseCases: Animating characters in a new setting by transferring dance moves from a reference video.
Creating sports training videos by applying professional athlete movements to amateur footage.
Enhancing cinematic scenes by replicating choreographed actions across different characters.
Developing educational content by demonstrating complex movements in various contexts.
Producing creative video content for social media by mixing and matching poses from different sources.

faqItems.question: What type of videos work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Videos that clearly capture human movement, such as dance or sports footage, work best as reference videos for accurate pose transfer.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for videos shorter than 5 seconds?
faqItems.answer: No, the reference video must be at least 5 seconds long to ensure sufficient pose data is captured for effective transfer.

faqItems.question: Do I need any special hardware to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: While no specific hardware is required, a powerful GPU will significantly speed up the processing time and improve performance.

faqItems.question: How do I troubleshoot login issues with the API?
faqItems.answer: Ensure you are using a secure network and have the correct API credentials. Refer to the API Node documentation for detailed troubleshooting steps.

1af3df552a07.title: Qwen-Image Union Control
1af3df552a07.description: Generate images with precise structural control using Qwen-Image's unified ControlNet LoRA. Supports multiple control types including canny, depth, lineart, softedge, normal, and openpose for diverse creative applications.
1af3df552a07.metaDescription: Generate images with precise control using Qwen-Image's ControlNet LoRA, supporting canny, depth, lineart, and more for diverse creative outputs.
1af3df552a07.extendedDescription:
The Qwen-Image Union Control workflow is designed to provide users with precise structural control over image generation using the Qwen-Image model's unified ControlNet LoRA. This workflow integrates multiple control types, such as canny, depth, lineart, softedge, normal, and openpose, allowing for a wide range of creative applications. By leveraging these controls, users can guide the image generation process to produce results that closely match their artistic vision or project requirements. 

Technically, this workflow utilizes a series of nodes to process and refine images. The 'LoadImage' node initializes the process by importing the reference image. The 'Canny' node is employed to detect edges, providing a structural outline that guides the image generation. The 'ImageScaleToTotalPixels' node ensures that the input image is resized appropriately to avoid poor output results. The 'PreviewImage' node allows users to visualize the intermediate results, while the 'SaveImage' node finalizes the process by saving the generated image. This workflow is particularly useful for artists and designers who require a high degree of control over the structural aspects of their images.
howToUse: Load the Qwen-Image Union Control workflow in ComfyUI.
Import your reference image using the 'LoadImage' node.
Select the desired control type (e.g., canny, depth) in the workflow settings.
Adjust the image size using 'ImageScaleToTotalPixels' if necessary.
Preview the generated image using the 'PreviewImage' node.
Save the final image with the 'SaveImage' node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating concept art with precise structural elements.
Enhancing architectural visualizations with detailed lineart.
Generating character designs with controlled poses using openpose.
Producing illustrations with specific depth and perspective.
Developing soft-edged graphics for marketing materials.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of the 'Canny' node in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The 'Canny' node is used to detect edges in the reference image, providing a structural outline that guides the image generation process.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for generating images from scratch?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is designed to work with reference images, providing structural control. For generating images from scratch, consider using a different workflow that does not rely on reference images.

faqItems.question: How do I choose the right control type for my project?
faqItems.answer: The choice of control type depends on the desired outcome. For example, use 'canny' for edge detection, 'depth' for 3D effects, and 'openpose' for pose control.

faqItems.question: What should I do if the output image quality is poor?
faqItems.answer: Ensure that the input image is appropriately sized using the 'ImageScaleToTotalPixels' node to prevent quality issues. You can also adjust control settings to refine the output.

1c0a3a9faad3.title: Topaz: Image Enhance Bloom 2
1c0a3a9faad3.description: Enhance AI-generated images with Bloom 2, a creative upscaling model that adds new detail, texture, and visual elements while offering a Creativity control from 1–9 for subtle refinement or bold reinterpretation. It accepts 1 input image and produces 1 enhanced output, with optional Face Recovery, Color Preservation, and grain settings for fine-tuned results. Ideal for improving AI artwork and illustrations, adding realism to CG renders, and refining facial detail in generated portraits.
1c0a3a9faad3.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow to enhance and creatively upscale images with Topaz Bloom 2, featuring creativity control, face recovery, color preservation, and grain.
1c0a3a9faad3.extendedDescription:
This workflow enhances a single input image using the TopazImageEnhanceV2 node configured with the Bloom 2 model. Bloom 2 is a creative enhancement and upscaling model that can add plausible detail, texture, and visual elements to AI art, illustrations, portraits, and CG renders. The key control is the Creativity setting (1–9), which lets you choose between subtle refinement and bold reinterpretation. Optional toggles for Face Recovery and Color Preservation help maintain natural facial features and original color palettes, while a Grain control can add film-like texture to reduce a too-clean, synthetic look.

Technically, the pipeline is straightforward: LoadImage brings your source into the graph, TopazImageEnhanceV2 (set to Bloom 2) performs the enhancement, ImageCompare previews the before/after for quick A/B evaluation, and SaveImageAdvanced writes the result with custom naming and format options. A MarkdownNote in the workflow provides quick tips, including the note that if the prompt field is left empty, the model will auto-generate guidance. This makes the workflow fast to adopt while still offering fine-grained control when you need it.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then open it to view the nodes: LoadImage → TopazImageEnhanceV2 (Bloom 2) → ImageCompare → SaveImageAdvanced.
In LoadImage, select your source image (PNG/JPG). This becomes the input for Bloom 2.

Open TopazImageEnhanceV2 and set Model to Bloom 2. Adjust Creativity (1–9): 1–3 for subtle cleanup, 4–6 for balanced enhancement, 7–9 for bold reinterpretation. Optionally enable Face Recovery and Preserve Color, and set Grain if you want film-like texture. Leave the prompt empty to auto-generate, or provide a short descriptive prompt to steer detail and style.

Run the graph. Use the ImageCompare node’s output to A/B check the original vs. enhanced result. If colors shift too much, turn on Preserve Color; if faces look over-processed, enable Face Recovery and reduce Creativity slightly.

Iterate settings as needed and re-run. When satisfied, open SaveImageAdvanced to set output folder, filename pattern, and format (PNG for lossless, JPG for smaller files), then run to export the final image.
suggestedUseCases: Refining AI-generated illustrations by adding crisp edges, richer textures, and cohesive fine detail.
Enhancing CG renders to add plausible micro-detail and surface texture for more realism.
Improving facial detail and skin texture in AI portraits with Face Recovery and low-to-mid Creativity.
Upscaling concept art or mood boards for print-ready presentation without manual repainting.
Polishing game asset textures or matte paintings, with Preserve Color to maintain palette fidelity.

faqItems.question: What does the Creativity setting do, and how should I choose a value?
faqItems.answer: Creativity (1–9) controls how much new detail and reinterpretation Bloom 2 adds. Use 1–3 for gentle cleanup, 4–6 for balanced, and 7–9 for stronger stylistic changes. Start low and increase gradually while checking ImageCompare to avoid over-processing.

faqItems.question: How do I prevent unwanted color shifts?
faqItems.answer: Enable Preserve Color in the TopazImageEnhanceV2 node. This keeps hue and overall palette closer to your input. If the image still looks off, try lowering Creativity and disabling Grain, then reintroduce them incrementally.

faqItems.question: How can I keep faces looking natural?
faqItems.answer: Turn on Face Recovery and use a lower Creativity (around 2–4) for portraits. This combination restores facial structure while avoiding excessive hallucinated detail. Use ImageCompare to ensure expressions and identity remain consistent.

faqItems.question: Do I need to write a prompt?
faqItems.answer: No. If you leave the prompt field empty, the model will auto-create guidance. If you want to steer the result, add a concise prompt (e.g., “clean linework, fine fabric texture, realistic skin pores”) to nudge the enhancement toward your target style.

1c77e82713b7.title: Video Upscale: Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5
1c77e82713b7.description: Upload a video to enhance its resolution using the Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 model. This workflow produces sharper 4K output with reduced artifacts compared to previous versions.
1c77e82713b7.metaDescription: Compare video upscaling with Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 for sharper 4K output and reduced artifacts. Discover the best approach for video enhancement.
1c77e82713b7.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow compares video upscaling techniques using the Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 model against its predecessors. The primary focus is on enhancing video resolution to 4K while minimizing artifacts and preserving sharpness. The Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 model is designed to produce clearer and more detailed output, making it a preferred choice for high-quality video enhancement. By utilizing nodes such as LoadVideo, SaveVideo, and TopazVideoEnhance, this workflow provides a streamlined process for users to upscale their videos efficiently.

Key differences between the Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 model and earlier versions include improved artifact reduction and sharper image quality. The workflow leverages advancements in AI-driven video processing, offering a significant upgrade in terms of visual fidelity. Users can expect a noticeable improvement in video clarity and detail, making this workflow ideal for professionals seeking high-resolution outputs for various applications.
howToUse: Upload your video file using the LoadVideo node in ComfyUI.
Select the TopazVideoEnhance node and configure it to use the Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 model.
Adjust the settings to upscale the video resolution to 4K.
Run the workflow to process the video and enhance its quality.
Use the SaveVideo node to save the enhanced video to your desired location.
Compare the output with previous versions to evaluate improvements in sharpness and artifact reduction.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing video quality for professional film production.
Improving the resolution of archival footage for historical documentaries.
Upscaling home videos for better viewing on 4K displays.
Optimizing video content for streaming platforms that require high resolution.
Creating high-quality video presentations for corporate or educational purposes.

faqItems.question: What improvements does the Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 model offer over previous versions?
faqItems.answer: The Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 model offers enhanced artifact reduction and sharper image quality, resulting in clearer and more detailed 4K video output.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow handle video artifacts?
faqItems.answer: The workflow uses advanced AI algorithms within the Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 model to minimize artifacts, ensuring a cleaner and more visually appealing video.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for batch processing multiple videos?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can configure the workflow to process multiple videos by queuing them in the LoadVideo node, allowing for efficient batch processing.

faqItems.question: Is there a significant difference in processing time between this model and previous versions?
faqItems.answer: While the Topaz Starlight Precise 2.5 model may require slightly more processing time due to its advanced capabilities, the quality improvements typically justify the additional time investment.

1c8383fd62e5.title: FLUX Virtual Try-On
1c8383fd62e5.description: Upload a person photo and a garment image. Generate a virtual try-on result with the garment applied to the person while preserving face and pose.
1c8383fd62e5.metaDescription: ComfyUI FLUX Virtual Try-On: apply a garment image to a person photo while preserving face and pose, with before/after compare and easy saving.
1c8383fd62e5.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow performs virtual try-on by taking two inputs—a person photo and a garment image—and compositing them into a realistic outfit preview while preserving the subject’s face and pose. The core is the FluxVTONode (FLUX Virtual Try-On model), which receives the Person (LoadImage) and Garment (LoadImage) inputs, then outputs a single try-on result that keeps identity features from the person image and transfers the garment’s texture and shape.

Around the model node, utility nodes make the process practical and reviewable. ImageCompare lets you place the original person image alongside the try-on result for instant before/after inspection, and ImageStitch can assemble a simple contact sheet (e.g., garment, person, and result in one panel). Finally, SaveImage writes the synthesized try-on to disk. The included MarkdownNote summarizes quick-start guidance so you can load images, run the queue, and iterate quickly with minimal configuration.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. Identify the two LoadImage nodes: the top one is Person, the bottom one is Garment (see the MarkdownNote for quick-start hints).
Choose a clear, front-facing person photo with the upper body visible and minimal occlusions. For the garment, use a well-lit, front-facing product image on a simple background (no model).
Drop the images into their respective LoadImage nodes. Confirm both are connected into FluxVTONode and that the FluxVTONode output routes to SaveImage, ImageCompare, and (optionally) ImageStitch.
Click Queue Prompt/Execute. The FluxVTONode will align and transfer the garment onto the person while preserving the face and pose.

Review outputs: use ImageCompare for a quick before/after view, and ImageStitch if the workflow provides a 3-up panel (garment, original person, result). If alignment looks off, try a person photo with a straighter pose or a garment image with a clearer frontal view, then run again.
When satisfied, configure the SaveImage output path/filename if needed and re-run (or right-click the saved preview) to export the final try-on image.
suggestedUseCases: E-commerce mockups: preview how a product might look on a model without a physical photoshoot.
Wardrobe planning: visualize outfit ideas on a photo of yourself for styling decisions.
Content creation: generate consistent outfit visuals for social posts or mood boards.
Fashion iteration: quickly test prints or textures on a base silhouette before sampling.
Client approvals: share realistic try-on previews to align on look-and-feel early.

faqItems.question: What images work best for the Person and Garment?
faqItems.answer: For the person: a front-facing photo with the torso clearly visible, good lighting, and minimal occlusions (crossed arms, bags, or hair covering the neckline). For the garment: a front-facing product image on a simple background with the item fully visible. Clean, well-framed inputs help the FluxVTONode align and transfer details more accurately.

faqItems.question: Will the model change the face or pose?
faqItems.answer: No. The FluxVTONode is designed to preserve the subject’s face and overall pose from the person image. If you notice artifacts near the neckline or face, try a person photo with fewer obstructions and a garment image that clearly shows the collar/shoulder area.

faqItems.question: Which clothing types are supported?
faqItems.answer: The workflow works best with tops, tees, shirts, jackets, dresses, and similar front-view garments. Highly complex items (e.g., scarves, very loose sleeves, layers) or extreme poses can be challenging and may produce distortions. Clear, frontal views improve results.

faqItems.question: How do I compare and export results?
faqItems.answer: Use ImageCompare to view the original person image next to the try-on output for quick checks. ImageStitch can create a single panel with garment, person, and result for sharing. Adjust the SaveImage node’s directory/name to export the final image.

SaveVideo then writes the result to disk as a standard video file, preserving the embedded audio when present.

Technically, the workflow is minimal and direct: LoadImage (optional) feeds an initial frame into GrokVideoNode, which synthesizes the motion and soundtrack from your prompt and/or reference image, and SaveVideo commits the output to a file. Keeping duration capped at 15 seconds ensures responsive generation and stays within the model’s capabilities. The result is a practical pipeline for rapid concepting, animating stills, or creating short social-ready clips without leaving ComfyUI.
howToUse: Load the Grok: Video generation workflow in ComfyUI and verify the three nodes are present: LoadImage (optional), GrokVideoNode, and SaveVideo.

Choose a generation mode: leave LoadImage unused for text-to-video, or load a still frame in LoadImage to drive image-to-video. Ensure the LoadImage output is connected to the GrokVideoNode if you want image conditioning.

Open GrokVideoNode and enter a clear prompt describing subject, motion, and scene. If the node exposes controls (e.g., duration up to 15 seconds, resolution, or randomness/seed), set them to match your goal. Keep the duration at or under 15 seconds.
Configure SaveVideo with your desired output directory and filename pattern. Confirm its input is connected to the GrokVideoNode's video output.
Queue and run the workflow. When complete, locate the saved file from SaveVideo and preview it—audio should be synchronized with the generated visuals.
Iterate: refine your prompt, swap or adjust the starting image, and re-run. For consistent results across runs, reuse the same seed if that control is available in GrokVideoNode.

faqItems.question: What is the maximum duration I can generate?

1fb07c3b4b99.title: LTX 2.3 - EditAnything - Video Editing via Prompt
1fb07c3b4b99.description: This experimental workflow uses an IC LoRA to attempt to Add, Remove, Change, or Convert elements of a video. For example, you can add a dog to a scene, or change the art style.
1fb07c3b4b99.metaDescription: Edit video content with text prompts in ComfyUI. Add, remove, or restyle objects using an experimental IC LoRA with VHS_LoadVideo and VHS_VideoCombine.
1fb07c3b4b99.extendedDescription:
LTX 2.3 - EditAnything is an experimental ComfyUI workflow that performs text-driven edits on existing video clips. Using an in‑context (IC) LoRA, it attempts to add, remove, replace, or restyle objects directly inside each frame without manual masking. The pipeline is simple: VHS_LoadVideo decodes your source clip into frames, a custom IC‑LoRA edit node (UUID 2e37ecc9-770a-4ac2-972c-e953901f49d3) applies the text instruction to those frames, and VHS_VideoCombine stitches the edited frames back into a video. A MarkdownNote node in the canvas provides author guidance and caveats.

Technically, the IC LoRA conditions the diffusion/edit process with your prompt so the model can infer where and how to apply changes across frames. Because the edit is prompt-only and experimental, temporal consistency will vary; shorter clips, clearer prompts, and conservative edit strength typically preserve motion and identity better. VHS_LoadVideo and VHS_VideoCombine (from VideoHelperSuite) handle robust frame I/O and encoding, so you can iterate quickly by tweaking the edit node’s prompt and strength, then re-queuing to compare results side by side.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. Ensure the VideoHelperSuite extension is installed so VHS_LoadVideo and VHS_VideoCombine are available.
Open VHS_LoadVideo and select your input video. Optionally set trim range, resize to your target resolution, and normalize the frame rate if needed.

Locate the IC‑LoRA edit node (UUID 2e37ecc9-770a-4ac2-972c-e953901f49d3). Enter a clear edit prompt (e.g., “add a small brown dog on the left sidewalk” or “convert to watercolor style”). If available, adjust negative prompt to protect elements you want unchanged (e.g., “preserve background, avoid extra people”).

Tune the edit intensity and consistency controls in the edit node (e.g., strength/denoise and guidance). Use lower strength for subtle restyles; increase strength for adding or removing objects. Keep seeds fixed when comparing variations.
In VHS_VideoCombine, set the output FPS, format/codec (e.g., MP4/H.264), quality, and output path. Lower FPS or resolution if you need faster previews.
Click Queue Prompt. Review the output video and iterate: refine the prompt, adjust strength/guidance, or shorten the clip to improve temporal stability.
suggestedUseCases: Add or remove small props/animals in casual clips for social content without hand-drawn masks.
Quick product swaps in B‑roll (e.g., replace a bottle or logo) for rough concept previews.
Art‑style conversion of travel or vlog footage (e.g., watercolor, anime, pencil sketch).
Background cleanup by discouraging clutter (e.g., remove stray objects) via negative prompting.
Concept testing for creative direction before committing to manual VFX or rotoscoping.

faqItems.question: What does the IC LoRA do in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The in‑context LoRA conditions the edit model with your text instruction so it can infer where and how to apply changes across frames. It’s mask‑free and prompt‑driven, so clarity in your prompt and conservative strength help maintain temporal consistency.

faqItems.question: How can I improve temporal consistency and reduce flicker?
faqItems.answer: Keep clips short (2–5 seconds), avoid hard cuts, use stable camera shots, write precise prompts, lower the edit strength for subtle changes, and keep the seed fixed while you iterate. If the background shifts, add negative prompts like “preserve background, avoid extra objects.”

faqItems.question: Does this preserve audio?
faqItems.answer: No. VHS_VideoCombine outputs a silent video. If you need audio, re‑mux the original track with the edited video using a video editor or ffmpeg.

faqItems.question: What video formats are supported?
faqItems.answer: VHS_LoadVideo works with common formats (e.g., MP4, MOV, WEBM). If a file fails to load or decode reliably, transcode it to MP4 (H.264) before importing.

231992fee1a6.title: AI on the Lot 2026 - QwenVL - i2t
231992fee1a6.description: The third workflow released for AI on the Lot 2026, made available for ComfyUI 101 workshop attendees to open and follow along if they choose. A simple image-to-text prompt creator using Qwen VL, useful for generating prompts from reference images.
231992fee1a6.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Convert images to high-quality captions or answers using Qwen-VL with AILab_QwenVL, LoadImage, and PreviewAny for fast image-to-text.
231992fee1a6.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns any image into descriptive, instruction-following text using Qwen-VL inside ComfyUI. It’s a simple, reliable chain: LoadImage brings your source frame or photo into the graph, AILab_QwenVL runs the Qwen-VL vision-language model to generate captions or answers based on your instruction, and PreviewAny displays the resulting text directly in the UI. Because AILab_QwenVL accepts both an image and a prompt, you can steer the output toward concise alt text, detailed scene breakdowns, tags, or even OCR-style transcriptions.

Technically, AILab_QwenVL encodes the visual content and decodes text conditioned on your instruction (e.g., "Describe this scene in one sentence" or "List objects with counts"). You can typically adjust generation behavior (such as temperature or maximum output length, if exposed by your node build) to balance creativity vs. precision. The minimal node graph keeps it fast and teachable—ideal for creating consistent captions, production notes, or metadata without extra post-processing nodes. PreviewAny then renders the string output so you can copy it straight from ComfyUI.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the three-node chain: LoadImage → AILab_QwenVL → PreviewAny.
In LoadImage, select or drag-and-drop the image you want to describe (frame, product shot, storyboard panel, etc.).
Open AILab_QwenVL and choose your installed Qwen-VL model variant if selectable. Enter a clear instruction, e.g., "Provide a concise caption highlighting setting, main subjects, and actions."
Optionally fine-tune generation settings (e.g., temperature for determinism, maximum tokens for length) if those controls are available in your AILab_QwenVL node.
Queue/Run the workflow. When it finishes, read the generated text in PreviewAny and copy it for your use.
Iterate: refine the instruction (e.g., ask for bullet points, tags, or verbatim transcription), swap the image in LoadImage, and re-run until you get the desired output.
suggestedUseCases: Automatic alt text and SEO-friendly image captions for websites and CMSs.
Shot descriptions and continuity notes for film/TV production stills or on-set frames.
E-commerce product summaries and tag extraction from catalog photos.
Social media caption starters tailored to mood, setting, or call to action.
Quick OCR-style transcription from signs, menus, and posters in images.

faqItems.question: What exactly does AILab_QwenVL do in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: AILab_QwenVL runs a Qwen-VL vision-language model on the input from LoadImage. It takes your instruction (prompt) plus the image, then generates text—such as a caption, list of objects, or an answer to a question about the image—which PreviewAny displays.

faqItems.question: Do I need an internet connection or API key to run this?
faqItems.answer: It depends on how AILab_QwenVL is configured in your environment. Many setups load local model weights and run fully offline. If your node is configured to call a remote backend, you may need network access or credentials. Check your node’s model selection and documentation.

faqItems.question: How can I control the style and length of the output?
faqItems.answer: Guide the model with explicit instructions (e.g., "One-sentence caption," "Return keywords separated by commas," or "Output JSON with fields: setting, subjects, actions"). If your node exposes settings like maximum tokens or temperature, use them to limit length and make results more deterministic.

faqItems.question: How do I get more accurate results (especially for text in images)?
faqItems.answer: Use clear, specific prompts (e.g., "Transcribe all legible text exactly, line by line"), provide sufficiently large, sharp images, and reduce temperature for factual tasks. If the scene is busy, crop to the relevant area before running LoadImage so the model focuses on what matters.

23226868cf80.title: Grok Imagine Image 2.0: Image Edit
23226868cf80.description: Grok Imagine Image 2.0 performs precise image editing and text rendering using xAI's Aurora engine, letting you modify specific elements, swap backgrounds, or restyle scenes through natural language with crisp short-text output. It takes up to 3 reference images and generates at 1K or 2K resolution across 14 aspect ratios, with strong character consistency across scenes. Ideal for poster and cover design, product and brand visuals, or multi-scene character workflows.
23226868cf80.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: precise image edits and short-text rendering with Grok Imagine 2.0 (Aurora). Use up to 3 references, 1K/2K output, and 14 aspect ratios.
23226868cf80.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial walks you through Grok Imagine Image 2.0: Image Edit, a prompt-based image editing workflow powered by xAI’s Aurora engine. The workflow is intentionally simple: LoadImage brings in your source and up to three optional reference images, GrokImageEditNodeV2 interprets your natural-language instructions to apply precise edits (like background swaps, restyling, or adding short text), and SaveImage writes the final render to disk. You can target 1K or 2K output and pick from 14 aspect ratios, making it easy to generate poster-ready or platform-specific visuals.

Under the hood, GrokImageEditNodeV2 conditions the edit on the provided base image plus any reference images to maintain visual identity and style. This enables strong character consistency across scenes, reliable product look alignment, and crisp short-text rendering for cover titles or label callouts—without manual masking. Because the node centralizes key settings (prompt, aspect ratio, and resolution), you can iterate quickly: refine the prompt, swap a reference, and re-render until the composition and typography meet your needs.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then add your base image with a LoadImage node. Optionally add up to three more LoadImage nodes for reference images (e.g., character, product, or style).

Connect the base image (and any reference images) to GrokImageEditNodeV2. In the node, write a clear prompt describing the desired changes (e.g., “Swap to a sunset beach background, cinematic lighting, preserve subject identity”).

Set output parameters in GrokImageEditNodeV2: choose 1K or 2K resolution and select an aspect ratio from the 14 available options that matches your target use (poster, cover, widescreen, square, etc.).

For text rendering, include exact wording in your prompt and be specific about placement and styling (e.g., “Add title ‘DAWN RISING’ in bold uppercase, centered at top, high contrast”). Keep text short for best legibility.
Execute the graph. Review the preview output and adjust the prompt or references to refine composition, identity, style, or text clarity.
When satisfied, connect the GrokImageEditNodeV2 output to SaveImage and run to export the final image to your output directory.
suggestedUseCases: Poster and cover design with crisp, short titles and strong subject presence
Product photography updates (background swaps, lighting/style harmonization) for e-commerce
Brand and campaign visuals that maintain consistent color, style, and iconography
Multi-scene character workflows where identity must remain consistent across settings
Social media and ad creatives that need fast aspect-ratio variants at 1K or 2K quality

faqItems.question: How many reference images can I use, and what are they for?
faqItems.answer: You can connect up to three reference images to GrokImageEditNodeV2. Use them to preserve subject identity, transfer style, or anchor product/brand details so the edit remains consistent across scenes.

faqItems.question: Do I need a mask to swap backgrounds or restyle part of the image?
faqItems.answer: No mask is required. GrokImageEditNodeV2 applies edits from natural-language instructions. For tighter control, use precise prompts (e.g., describe the subject and the background separately) and start from a well-framed base image.

faqItems.question: What resolutions and aspect ratios are supported?
faqItems.answer: The node renders at 1K or 2K resolution and offers 14 aspect ratios. Choose the aspect ratio that matches your output target (e.g., poster, square, vertical) to avoid unwanted cropping later.

faqItems.question: How do I get the best text rendering quality?
faqItems.answer: Keep text short (titles, labels, or brief slogans), specify the exact string, case, and placement in the prompt, and request high contrast against the background. If needed, generate a clean background or reserved space first, then iterate on type styling.

2620e5135442.title: Gemini Omni Flash: Video Edit
2620e5135442.description: Edit videos with natural language using Gemini Omni Flash, transforming a single input video into one edited output based on your descriptive instructions. Specify the duration and aspect ratio in your prompt, and leverage Omni's world knowledge for intuitive edits like changing backgrounds or adding atmosphere. Ideal for quick social media remixes, cinematic scene adjustments, and iterative video refinements without technical prompts.
2620e5135442.metaDescription: Edit videos with natural language in ComfyUI using Gemini Omni Flash. Load a clip, set duration/aspect ratio, preview, and export an AI-edited video.
2620e5135442.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow lets you edit a single input video using natural language instructions powered by the GeminiVideoOmni node. The graph is straightforward: LoadVideo ingests your source clip, the Prompt Constructor subgraph (node id 331103d2-d660-4a88-abf0-1117dc46b2df) builds a well-formed prompt with the required duration and aspect ratio, GeminiVideoOmni sends the video plus prompt to the Gemini Omni Flash API, and the results are displayed with PreviewAny and saved with SaveVideo. A MarkdownNote in the canvas provides quick tips and reminders.

Technically, LoadVideo decodes frames and metadata, then the Prompt Constructor concatenates your natural language edit with explicit settings like "duration: 5s" and "aspect ratio: 9:16". GeminiVideoOmni uses these to guide the model: the aspect ratio determines the output canvas, and the duration constrains the target clip length. The model returns an edited clip that adheres to your instructions (e.g., background changes, mood/atmosphere adjustments, reframing), which you can quickly review in PreviewAny and export via SaveVideo. For best results, keep prompts concrete, always include duration and aspect ratio, and iterate in short passes.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. You should see LoadVideo, the Prompt Constructor subgraph (331103d2-d660-4a88-abf0-1117dc46b2df), GeminiVideoOmni, PreviewAny, SaveVideo, and a MarkdownNote.

Configure GeminiVideoOmni: add your Gemini API key (in the node or via the node’s documented environment setting) and pick the intended model variant if exposed. Ensure you have internet access and valid API quota.
Open LoadVideo and select your source clip. Short clips (e.g., a few seconds) and moderate resolutions tend to return faster, more consistent edits.

Open the Prompt Constructor subgraph. Set duration (e.g., 5s) and aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9, 1:1, or 9:16). In the instruction field, describe the edit clearly, for example: "Make it dusk with light fog, keep the subject sharp, add a soft cinematic grade, crop to 9:16." The subgraph outputs a complete prompt string.

Run the graph. Use PreviewAny to review the generated clip. If framing or length isn’t as expected, refine the aspect ratio and duration in the Prompt Constructor and be explicit in your wording (e.g., "keep original motion," "center the subject," "trim to first 5 seconds").
When satisfied, set filename/codec options in SaveVideo and execute to export. Iterate by adjusting your prompt or the Prompt Constructor inputs to produce improved or alternate edits.
suggestedUseCases: Social media remixes: reframe to 9:16, shorten to 5–8 seconds, and add a quick mood/grade for Shorts/Reels/TikTok.
Cinematic adjustments: change time of day, add atmosphere (fog, haze), and apply a consistent color tone for scene polish.
Background tweaks: request subtle background replacements or cleanups for B‑roll and product shots.
Reframing and focus: center the subject, apply gentle crop/zoom, and maintain composition across a short highlight clip.
Promo snippets: trim a longer clip into concise, platform-ready teasers with clear aspect ratio and duration.

faqItems.question: Do I have to specify duration and aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The GeminiVideoOmni node expects both in the prompt so the model knows the output canvas and time budget. Use clear formats like "duration: 5s" and "aspect ratio: 9:16" in the Prompt Constructor.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow keep audio?
faqItems.answer: No. This setup focuses on visual edits, and the output from SaveVideo is typically silent. If you need audio, re-sync your original track or music in a video editor after export.

faqItems.question: Does my video stay on my machine?
faqItems.answer: GeminiVideoOmni calls the Gemini API, so your media and instructions are sent to the service provider. Avoid sensitive content and be mindful of your API’s usage, privacy, and content policies.

faqItems.question: How can I get more reliable results?
faqItems.answer: Keep clips short (a few seconds), be explicit and constrained in your instructions, always include duration and aspect ratio, and iterate. Use concrete guidance like "keep the subject centered," "subtle fog only," or "retain original motion" to reduce ambiguity.

2652985596d8.title: Wan2.1 VACE Control Video
