787cfd599758.title: MiniMax: Text to Video
787cfd599758.description: Generate high-quality videos directly from text prompts. Explore MiniMax's advanced AI capabilities to create diverse visual narratives with professional CGI effects and stylistic elements to bring your descriptions to life.
787cfd599758.metaDescription: ComfyUI MiniMax text-to-video tutorial: set up the API node, craft prompts, and save high-quality clips with SaveVideo in a secure environment.
787cfd599758.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial walks you through a minimal, reliable text-to-video pipeline powered by the MiniMax API. The core of the workflow is the MinimaxTextToVideoNode, which sends your text prompt to MiniMax’s text-to-video service and returns a generated video clip. A MarkdownNote node is included in the graph to remind you of the provider’s secure network requirements (localhost access, HTTPS usage, and ensuring you can reach the API). Finally, a SaveVideo node writes the returned clip to disk so you can review and reuse it in your projects.

Technically, the MinimaxTextToVideoNode handles the API call and response lifecycle inside ComfyUI. You supply the prompt (and any parameters the node exposes, such as clip length or resolution if available), the node waits for the remote job to complete, and then forwards the resulting video to SaveVideo. SaveVideo stores the clip in your ComfyUI output directory using the file name settings you configure. Because inference happens on the MiniMax service, local GPU requirements are minimal—the main considerations are correct API credentials/configuration and meeting the secure networking rules noted in the MarkdownNote.
howToUse: Load the MiniMax: Text to Video workflow JSON into ComfyUI and confirm the MinimaxTextToVideoNode, SaveVideo, and MarkdownNote nodes appear.
Open the MarkdownNote and review the secure environment requirements: run from localhost (127.0.0.1), use HTTPS for web services, and ensure you can reach the MiniMax API.
Select the MinimaxTextToVideoNode and enter your text prompt. If the node exposes fields like duration or resolution, set them as needed. Add your API credentials/endpoint if required.
Configure the SaveVideo node: choose a clear filename prefix and (if available) format settings so your clip is written to the desired output folder.
Click Queue Prompt (or Run) in ComfyUI. Wait for the node to complete the API job and for SaveVideo to write the resulting video.
Open the saved file from the ComfyUI output directory to review. Iterate on your prompt and node parameters to refine motion, style, and composition.
suggestedUseCases: Creating quick concept animations for storyboards or previsualization.
Generating short social media clips with distinct stylistic directions (e.g., cinematic, CGI-inspired).
Producing motion references for VFX and motion design teams during early ideation.
Exploring narrative variations rapidly by iterating on text prompts.
Building a prompt library for consistent brand or artistic looks across multiple clips.

faqItems.question: Do I need a powerful GPU to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No. The MinimaxTextToVideoNode calls the MiniMax API for generation, so heavy compute happens remotely. Your local machine only needs to run ComfyUI and maintain a network connection.

faqItems.question: Why does the node fail or time out?
faqItems.answer: Common causes are networking or credential issues. Confirm you meet the secure environment requirements (localhost access or HTTPS for web services), your API key/endpoint are correct, and your firewall allows outbound requests to the MiniMax API.

faqItems.question: How can I control duration, resolution, or aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: Use any parameters the MinimaxTextToVideoNode exposes in your workflow. If a setting isn’t available in the node UI, consult the MiniMax provider docs for supported options. Some services may also respect prompt cues (e.g., 9:16) but this is not guaranteed.

faqItems.question: How do I get cleaner, more on-style results?
faqItems.answer: Write specific prompts that include subject, action, environment, and style cues (e.g., cinematic lighting, stylized CGI). Keep motions simple for short clips, avoid overly rapid scene changes, and iterate in small steps. If the node supports it, adjust duration and other parameters conservatively.

7a6ab8b6e694.title: VFX - Bullet Time Effect
7a6ab8b6e694.description: Upload an image or describe a scene, then get **one optimized prompt** built to reproduce the bullet time effect: **frozen action, slow-motion energy, and a cinematic camera orbit around the subject**.
7a6ab8b6e694.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate a Seedance 2.0 bullet time video from an image or text using Gemini for prompt crafting and ByteDance reference video generation.
7a6ab8b6e694.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds a convincing bullet time sequence from either a reference image or a plain-text scene description. It does this in two stages. First, the Generate Bullet Time Seedance 2.0 Prompt group uses a GeminiNode to synthesize a single, highly focused prompt that emphasizes frozen action, slow‑motion energy, and a cinematic orbit around your subject. If you load a still via LoadImage, that visual context informs the prompt; otherwise, the node relies purely on your text description. A MarkdownNote in the graph explains what the node expects and how to phrase your ideas.

Next, the Generate Video group feeds the optimized prompt (and, when provided, your reference image) into the ByteDance2ReferenceNode, which drives Seedance 2.0 to render the shot. The node is the core video generator: it accepts the guidance prompt and optional reference to anchor subject identity and pose while simulating an orbiting camera and time‑frozen moment. PreviewAny lets you check the output right away, and SaveVideo writes the final clip to disk. The result is a short, loop‑ready bullet time pass you can iterate on quickly by adjusting the prompt, seed, or reference strength.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON titled "VFX - Bullet Time Effect" in ComfyUI. Locate the three groups: Load Images, Generate Bullet Time Seedance 2.0 Prompt, and Generate Video.

Provide your input: either drop a still into the LoadImage node (clear subject, some background margin) or type a concise scene description into the GeminiNode prompt field. Keep it focused on one subject and action to freeze.

Queue the Generate Bullet Time Seedance 2.0 Prompt group. The GeminiNode returns one optimized prompt tuned for the bullet time look (frozen action, slow‑motion energy, orbiting camera). Inspect the generated text if PreviewAny is connected to its output.

Open the ByteDance2ReferenceNode in the Generate Video group. Confirm the optimized prompt is connected and, if you provided an image, that the reference input is wired from LoadImage. Optionally adjust available settings such as duration, resolution, guidance/reference strength, or seed.
Queue the Generate Video group. Watch the clip in PreviewAny; if satisfied, use SaveVideo to export the result to your chosen folder and filename.

Iterate for refinement: tweak the description you give to Gemini (e.g., orbit direction, focal length, debris or confetti suspended), change the seed for variants, or swap the reference image to lock identity and pose more tightly.
suggestedUseCases: Stylized product hero spins where the object appears suspended mid‑air while the camera orbits.
Fashion or portrait bullet time beats for reels or intros that emphasize pose and fabric motion.
Sports action freezes (kick, dunk, serve) that hold the peak moment while circling the athlete.
Fight choreography highlights where the camera wraps around a mid‑strike pose.
Cinematic reveals of gadgets or props with floating particles to sell the time‑stop effect.

faqItems.question: Do I need a reference image, or can it work from text only?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports both. For consistent identity and pose, load a reference image via LoadImage. If you prefer pure text, provide a clear description to the GeminiNode; the optimized prompt will drive Seedance 2.0 without a reference, though subject fidelity may vary.

faqItems.question: How do I get a cleaner orbit and fewer artifacts around the subject?
faqItems.answer: Use a high‑resolution image with the subject centered, good contrast, and some background margin. Avoid heavy motion blur and occlusions. In ByteDance2ReferenceNode, increase reference guidance/strength if available to better anchor identity, and try a different seed for stability. Prompts that explicitly mention orbit direction, focal length (e.g., wide or telephoto), and suspended particles can improve coherence.

faqItems.question: Why doesn’t it do a full 360° around my subject?
faqItems.answer: From a single image, the model infers unseen views; it can simulate an orbit but cannot reveal fully occluded sides reliably. You can suggest a partial arc in the prompt (e.g., “quarter‑orbit left to right”) and keep backgrounds simple to reduce hallucinations.

faqItems.question: Do I need API keys or special hardware?
faqItems.answer: GeminiNode and ByteDance2ReferenceNode typically call external services and require valid API keys or configuration in their node settings. Check each node’s docs or your ComfyUI custom node configuration. Because the heavy lifting may be remote, local hardware demands are modest; generation time depends on the service and settings.

7b973ace62af.title: Gemini Omni Flash: Image to Video
7b973ace62af.description: Generate a video from two images using Gemini Omni Flash, which interprets natural language prompts to control duration and aspect ratio. The workflow accepts 2 input images and produces 1 video output. Ideal for creating short brand clips, dynamic social media content, and iterative video edits through conversational prompting.
7b973ace62af.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate a short video from two images with Gemini Omni Flash. Control duration and aspect ratio via prompt. Preview and save the final clip.
7b973ace62af.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns two still images into a short video using Google’s Gemini Omni Flash via the GeminiVideoOmni node. You provide a start image and an end image (two LoadImage nodes), then guide the motion, duration, and framing with a natural-language prompt. A built-in Prompt Constructor subgraph (custom node: b83478ba-1f3e-4e62-9869-c8a0c8e9a5f5) helps you explicitly include the required duration and aspect ratio in the final prompt string—both are mandatory for Gemini Omni Video. The GeminiVideoOmni node then generates a single video clip that you can preview with PreviewAny and export with SaveVideo.

Technically, the workflow wires your two image tensors and the constructed text prompt into GeminiVideoOmni, which requests a video from the Gemini Omni Flash model. Duration and aspect ratio are parsed from the prompt (for example: "duration: 4s, aspect_ratio: 16:9"), while the rest of your text describes the motion (e.g., zooms, pans, morphs, reveals). The MarkdownNote nodes embedded in the graph provide quick reminders and tips as you work. The result is a fast, conversational way to iterate on short brand clips, vertical social posts, and before/after reveals—without manual keyframing.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote tips to understand required inputs and prompt format.
Load your two images: connect the first LoadImage node to your starting frame and the second LoadImage node to your ending frame (recommended: similar framing and resolution).

Open the Prompt Constructor subgraph (custom node b83478ba-1f3e-4e62-9869-c8a0c8e9a5f5). Set duration (e.g., 3s, 5s) and aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9, 9:16), then write a clear motion description. Example: "duration: 4s, aspect_ratio: 9:16. Smooth vertical reveal transitioning from the first image to the second with a gentle camera push-in."

Confirm the Prompt Constructor output feeds into GeminiVideoOmni along with both image inputs. If required by your setup, ensure Gemini API credentials are configured for the GeminiVideoOmni node/extension.
Queue the workflow. Watch the output in PreviewAny once the generation completes. If the motion or framing isn’t right, adjust the prompt (especially duration/aspect_ratio) and re-run.
When satisfied, set the file path/options in SaveVideo and run again to export the final clip.
suggestedUseCases: Brand logo stingers that transition from a product shot to a branded end card.
Before-and-after reveals for marketing, beauty, home improvement, or restoration.
Social media shorts in 9:16 that morph between two campaign visuals.
Title/opening transitions for YouTube or reels using two style frames.
Quick A/B variations of a motion concept by iterating with conversational prompts.

faqItems.question: How do I control video duration and aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: Gemini Omni Video requires both to be specified in the prompt. Use the Prompt Constructor subgraph to inject them, e.g., "duration: 4s, aspect_ratio: 16:9" followed by your motion description.

faqItems.question: Do I need two images, and in what order?
faqItems.answer: Yes—this workflow is designed for two inputs: the first LoadImage is the start frame and the second is the end frame. For subtle motion from a single still, you can reuse the same image in both inputs.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key or special setup?
faqItems.answer: If your GeminiVideoOmni node/extension requires credentials, configure a valid Google Gemini API key in the node settings or environment as documented by the ComfyUI extension you installed.

faqItems.question: Why is there no audio in the output?
faqItems.answer: Gemini’s video generation returns a silent clip. Use a video editor to add music or sound effects after exporting from SaveVideo.

howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and ensure the GeminiVideoOmniV2 and SaveVideo nodes are present.

faqItems.question: How do I provide my Gemini API key?

faqItems.question: Can I start from an image and animate it?

faqItems.question: How do I control video size and shape?

faqItems.question: Why does motion look choppy or unstable?
faqItems.answer: Increase keyframe interpolation in GeminiVideoOmniV2 to smooth transitions and stabilize subjects. Also keep prompts precise and avoid large prompt changes between iterations. Lowering resolution can reduce artifacts on slower hardware or networks.

7cecbe192fc2.title: Googly Eyes
7cecbe192fc2.description: LTX 2.3 LoRA that makes anyone in the input video have Googly Eyes. This workflow utilizes the Googlyeyes LTX 2.3 LoRA by TheBurgstall
7cecbe192fc2.metaDescription: Add googly eyes to any video in ComfyUI using an LTX‑Video 2.3 LoRA. Load, trim, process, and export with VHS nodes for fast, consistent edits.
7cecbe192fc2.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow applies TheBurgstall’s Googlyeyes LoRA for LTX-Video 2.3 to any input clip, turning ordinary footage into a playful googly‑eyes edit. It ingests your video with VHS_LoadVideo, trims the timeline using skip_first_frames and frame_count, and then routes the frames through the LTX 2.3 inference group (node id: 2e37ecc9-770a-4ac2-972c-e953901f49d3), where the Googlyeyes LoRA is loaded over the LTX‑Video 2.3 base model. Finally, VHS_VideoCombine reassembles the processed frames back into a video at the original frame rate.

Technically, the pipeline is video‑to‑video: frames decoded by VHS_LoadVideo are processed in sequence by the LTX 2.3 node that applies the LoRA to emphasize and transform eye regions while preserving overall scene structure. Because it runs through a video‑aware model pipeline, the effect tends to remain consistent across adjacent frames. The simple set of controls—especially skip_first_frames and frame_count—makes it practical to target only the part of the timeline you want, saving VRAM and time on longer clips.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure required components are available: Video Helper Suite (VHS_LoadVideo and VHS_VideoCombine) and an LTX‑Video 2.3 pipeline node. Confirm the LTX‑Video 2.3 base model and TheBurgstall “Googlyeyes” LoRA are installed and selectable in the LTX node/group (id: 2e37ecc9-770a-4ac2-972c-e953901f49d3).

Open the VHS_LoadVideo node and choose your source clip. Set skip_first_frames to trim the start of the clip, and set frame_count to the number of frames you want processed (for example, skip_first_frames: 60 and frame_count: 480 to process frames 60–540 of a 600‑frame clip).

In the LTX 2.3 node/group, select the LTX‑Video 2.3 base model and the Googlyeyes LoRA by TheBurgstall. If a LoRA weight/strength control is available, start at 1.0; reduce it for a subtler effect or increase slightly if the eyes aren’t pronounced enough.
Leave other LTX settings at their defaults for a first pass. For longer or high‑resolution videos, consider testing a short segment first by lowering frame_count to verify quality and VRAM usage.
Verify that the output of the LTX node routes into VHS_VideoCombine. Confirm the frame rate is coming from VHS_LoadVideo and set an output filename/preset if exposed by your VHS_VideoCombine version.
Click Queue Prompt to render. When complete, find the resulting video in your ComfyUI output directory. Review and, if needed, adjust LoRA strength or trim controls and re‑queue.
suggestedUseCases: Quick comedic edits for social media or reaction videos where exaggerated googly eyes boost humor.
Lightweight creative masking over faces for internal demos or drafts (not a privacy or de‑identification solution).
Kids’ content and classroom projects that benefit from playful visual effects without complex editing.
Rapid prototyping to learn LTX‑Video 2.3 video‑to‑video workflows and LoRA application in ComfyUI.

faqItems.question: Which models do I need for this to work?
faqItems.answer: You need the LTX‑Video 2.3 base model and TheBurgstall’s Googlyeyes LoRA. Make sure both are installed and selectable in the LTX 2.3 node/group (id: 2e37ecc9-770a-4ac2-972c-e953901f49d3).

faqItems.question: Does this work on both live‑action and anime?
faqItems.answer: Yes. It can work on both. Best results come from clips with clear, front‑facing eyes and minimal motion blur. Very dark, low‑contrast, or profile shots may reduce the effect’s consistency.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce VRAM usage or speed up processing?
faqItems.answer: Process shorter segments first by lowering frame_count, trim with skip_first_frames, and keep your input resolution modest. Scale up or extend the timeline only after confirming quality and performance.

faqItems.question: Can I keep my original audio?
faqItems.answer: This workflow focuses on visual processing. If your VHS_VideoCombine version doesn’t mux audio, export audio from your editor and remux it with the processed video in a video editor or command‑line tool.

7dca0438edf4.title: Adjustment Frame Workflow
7dca0438edf4.description: A Director-style AI workflow that generates a shot, refines camera angle, and produces multiple video takes across top models so you can quickly choose the best result.
7dca0438edf4.metaDescription: Director-style ComfyUI workflow to block a shot, refine camera angle, and generate multiple video takes via Grok, Kling, and Gemini—then pick the best.
7dca0438edf4.extendedDescription:
The Adjustment Frame Workflow is a director-style pipeline for turning a written shot idea into multiple polished video takes you can compare side-by-side. It stages your work like a real set: first you block the shot as a still, then you refine the camera, and finally you roll multiple takes across different model backends. A Text Multiline node captures your prompt (what the image is and the action you want), and the 1A) GENERATE SHOT STILL group produces a reference frame you can review with PreviewImage/PreviewAny before spending any credits.

Next, the 1B) CONTROL CAMERA ANGLE group routes your shot through QwenMultiangleCameraNode to generate camera-aware variations (e.g., wide vs. close-up, low vs. high angle, focal length cues). Utility nodes like RegexExtract and ComfyMathExpression help parse camera directions from your text and normalize values like duration, fps, or resolution. In 2) GENERATE VIDEO(S), you can send the approved composition to one or more API partners—GrokVideoNode, KlingVideoNode, and GeminiNode—optionally anchoring identity or style via ByteDance2ReferenceNode. Image Resize ensures each model receives a compatible resolution, PreviewAny lets you compare takes interactively, and SaveVideo writes out the best result. SetNode/GetNode pass key parameters between groups so your shot intent, camera notes, and timing remain consistent. This workflow is especially useful because you only “roll” once you like the frame and angle—preventing credit waste while getting clear, comparable outputs from top models.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the DIRECTOR'S CHAIR notes to skim the instructions. In the Text Multiline node, describe the subject and the action you want to see.
Run only the 1A) GENERATE SHOT STILL group to create a reference frame. Use PreviewImage/PreviewAny to check composition, subject, and style. Do not press Play on the whole graph yet.

Adjust camera intent in 1B) CONTROL CAMERA ANGLE. In QwenMultiangleCameraNode, add cues like shot size (wide/medium/close-up), angle (low/high/eye-level), and lens hints (24mm/50mm). Re-run 1A/1B until the still and angle look right.

Set technical parameters: use PrimitiveInt and ComfyMathExpression nodes to define clip length/fps or number of takes; match each model’s preferred resolution with Image Resize. If you need character or style consistency, connect a reference image to ByteDance2ReferenceNode.
Enable one video backend at a time in 2) GENERATE VIDEO(S) (e.g., GrokVideoNode, KlingVideoNode, or GeminiNode). These API partner nodes consume credits—verify you have credits before running.
Press Play to generate your first take. Compare outputs in PreviewAny, switch or tweak nodes as needed, and repeat per model. When satisfied, send the chosen take to SaveVideo to export.
suggestedUseCases: Previsualization for directors: quickly test camera angles and motion before a live shoot.
Storyboarding: turn a written beat into multiple angle options to align a team.
Product and explainer clips: lock composition with a still, then iterate motion across models.
Social media content: A/B test tone, pacing, and framing for Reels/TikTok/Shorts.
Character consistency tests: use ByteDance2ReferenceNode to keep a subject’s look stable across takes.

faqItems.question: Which nodes require credits, and how do I avoid wasting them?
faqItems.answer: The API partner nodes—GrokVideoNode, KlingVideoNode, and GeminiNode—consume credits. ByteDance2ReferenceNode typically pairs with an external generation call as well. Work only inside 1A/1B first (local and free nodes like PreviewImage, PreviewAny, Image Resize, ComfyMathExpression, SetNode/GetNode) until your still frame and camera angle are locked. Then enable a single video node and render.

faqItems.question: How do I control the camera angle and framing?
faqItems.answer: Use QwenMultiangleCameraNode in 1B) CONTROL CAMERA ANGLE. Add clear cues such as shot size (e.g., "medium shot"), angle ("low angle"), lens ("35mm"), and motion intent ("slow dolly-in"). RegexExtract helps parse these from your text, and the node produces consistent camera-aware variations you can preview before video generation.

faqItems.question: Can I change video length and resolution?
faqItems.answer: Yes. PrimitiveInt and ComfyMathExpression nodes set timing values like duration/fps. Use Image Resize to match model-specific resolution requirements. Note that supported lengths vary by model—some allow longer clips than others—so check each node’s limits and adjust accordingly.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the subject’s look consistent across takes?
faqItems.answer: Provide a clean, well-lit still as a reference and route it through ByteDance2ReferenceNode before your chosen video backend. Keep the composition similar to your approved still, and avoid large mid-scene camera changes. Small prompt changes can shift identity—lock your description once the still is approved.

7e47ce4777e7.title: Tripo3.0: Image to Model
7e47ce4777e7.description: Transform images or sketches into 3D models with Tripo 3.0's sharp geometry and production-ready PBR textures.

The process begins with the 'LoadImage' node, which imports your 2D image or sketch into the workflow. The 'TripoImageToModelNode' then takes center stage, converting the flat image into a 3D model with remarkable precision.

Once the initial model is created, the workflow employs a series of specialized nodes to refine and enhance the model. The 'TripoRefineNode' ensures that the geometry is sharp and accurate, while the 'TripoTextureNode' applies high-quality textures that are ready for production use. For those looking to animate their models, the 'TripoRigNode' and 'TripoRetargetNode' provide robust rigging and retargeting capabilities. Finally, the 'SaveGLB' node allows users to export their models in the GLB format, suitable for a wide range of applications. This comprehensive workflow not only simplifies the process of creating 3D models from 2D images but also ensures that the output is of high quality and ready for immediate use in various digital environments.
howToUse: Load your 2D image or sketch using the 'LoadImage' node.
Connect the image to the 'TripoImageToModelNode' to generate a 3D model.
Use the 'TripoRefineNode' to enhance the model's geometry.
Apply textures with the 'TripoTextureNode' for a polished finish.
Rig and retarget animations using 'TripoRigNode' and 'TripoRetargetNode'.
Export the final model with the 'SaveGLB' node for use in various applications.
suggestedUseCases: Create detailed 3D models for video game assets from concept art.
Transform architectural sketches into 3D visualizations for presentations.
Generate production-ready models for use in virtual reality environments.
Design custom 3D printed objects from hand-drawn sketches.
Develop animated characters for film and television using rigging and retargeting features.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for creating animated models?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow includes 'TripoRigNode' and 'TripoRetargetNode' for rigging and retargeting, making it suitable for animation projects.

faqItems.question: What file format does the workflow export?
faqItems.answer: The workflow exports models in the GLB format, which is widely used for 3D applications and supports PBR textures.

faqItems.question: Is prior 3D modeling experience required to use this workflow?

81ba03930d2b.title: Utility Merge Video
81ba03930d2b.description: Concatenate 2 videos with the Utility Merge Videos (Subgraph).
81ba03930d2b.metaDescription: Concatenate 2 or 4 videos in ComfyUI with a simple subgraph. Load, merge, and save clips end-to-end. Requires matching resolution.
81ba03930d2b.extendedDescription:
Utility Merge Video is a simple, reliable ComfyUI workflow for stitching clips end-to-end. It uses two or four LoadVideo nodes to decode your source files into frame batches, passes them into the Utility Merge Videos (Subgraph) node (ID: fbb76376-8768-4ece-9b41-a646f5e46ac3), and concatenates those frame sequences in order. The merged frames are then written to disk with SaveVideo.

Technically, the subgraph concatenates batches rather than compositing them, so the result plays one clip after another. A switch inside the Utility Merge Videos subgraph lets you choose between 2-input and 4-input modes. All inputs must share the same resolution; otherwise, the graph will error at merge time. The SaveVideo node controls the output file path, format (via extension), and playback FPS; the final FPS you set there determines how the concatenated frames will play back. A MarkdownNote node in the graph provides quick reminders right where you work.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the Utility Merge Videos (Subgraph), LoadVideo nodes, and the SaveVideo node.
In each LoadVideo node, select your source files for Clip A and Clip B (and C, D if needed). Ensure all videos share the same resolution.
Open the Utility Merge Videos (Subgraph) and set its switch to 2-input or 4-input mode. Verify that the inputs (A, B, C, D) are connected in the order you want them to appear.
Open SaveVideo and set the output path and file extension (e.g., .mp4). Choose the target FPS and any quality parameters available in your SaveVideo node.
Queue and run the workflow. ComfyUI will read each source, concatenate the frame batches, and write the merged video to the path you set.
If you encounter a resolution mismatch error, resize your clips beforehand or insert a resize node on each input stream before the subgraph, then re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Join an intro bumper, main segment, and outro into a single deliverable.
Merge AI-generated scene clips from separate runs into one continuous video.
Combine camera takes that were split across multiple files into a single timeline.
Assemble short social posts or stories recorded in parts into one upload-ready clip.
Create a simple before-then-after sequence without using a full video editor.

faqItems.question: Do the input videos need the same resolution and FPS?
faqItems.answer: Resolution must match for all inputs. The final playback FPS comes from the SaveVideo node. If source FPS differs, frames are still concatenated, but the output plays at the SaveVideo FPS you choose.

faqItems.question: How do I change the order of the clips?
faqItems.answer: Connect the LoadVideo outputs to the Utility Merge Videos inputs (A, B, C, D) in the order you want. The subgraph concatenates in that input order.

faqItems.question: Can I keep or merge audio tracks?
faqItems.answer: This workflow focuses on visual frames. Many SaveVideo configurations do not mux audio. If you need audio, remux it in an external tool after export or extend the graph with audio-capable nodes if available in your setup.

faqItems.question: Can I merge more than four videos?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Chain merges by running the workflow multiple times (e.g., merge four clips, then merge the result with more clips) or duplicate the subgraph and build a longer chain.

825e6fb23c2c.title: Krea 2 Moodboards
825e6fb23c2c.description: A simple Krea 2 workflow for testing and comparing different Krea moodboard styles. Each section uses a separate prompt, moodboard ID, and save node, making it easy to try multiple visual directions from one workflow. Users can bypass inactive sections, swap in their own Krea moodboard ID, adjust moodboard strength, and generate clean test outputs.
825e6fb23c2c.metaDescription: Test and compare Krea 2 moodboard styles in ComfyUI. Six parallel branches with per‑section prompts, moodboard IDs, and clean SaveImage outputs.
825e6fb23c2c.extendedDescription:
Krea 2 Moodboards is a compact ComfyUI workflow designed to A/B test style directions using Krea's moodboard–conditioned text-to-image generation. Each of the six labeled sections (Ethereal Romanticism, Digitally Broken Realism, Neon Dreams, Technicolor Madhouse, Country Club Surrealism, Liminal Nightmare) runs the same pipeline: PrimitiveNode inputs feed a Krea2ImageNode, and results are written by a dedicated SaveImage node. MarkdownNote nodes annotate each group so you can navigate quickly. Because each section has its own prompt, moodboard_id, moodboard_strength, and save target, you can compare multiple visual directions from one run without cross‑contamination.

Technically, the PrimitiveNode instances hold strings and numbers (prompt text, moodboard ID UUIDs, strength values, optional seed/size if exposed). Those values flow into Krea2ImageNode, which sends a generation request to the Krea 2 image API conditioned by the provided moodboard_id. The SaveImage at the end of each branch writes clean, labeled outputs using per‑section filename prefixes. ComfyUI’s bypass toggle lets you disable inactive sections for faster iteration. The workflow ships with example prompts and moodboard IDs in the Author Notes (e.g., 7947e7b8-750e-4dbd-877a-d554d86f85d1, 176345d7-b1e0-4b44-bf06-ce4d7b8b8062, aa2178a3-36f1-47f6-8d2a-c3578d5329af), making it easy to drop in a style and start testing immediately.
howToUse: Load the Krea 2 Moodboards workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the Krea2ImageNode custom node is installed. Add your Krea API key in the node’s settings or your environment per the node’s documentation.
Decide which sections you want to test first and bypass the others. Use the MarkdownNote labels to find each group (01–06).

For each active group, set the PrimitiveNode values: paste a moodboard_id (you can use the example UUIDs from the Author Notes or your own), write a prompt, and choose a moodboard_strength. Optionally set a seed and size if those inputs are exposed in your Krea2ImageNode version.
Open the SaveImage node in each active group and set a clear filename_prefix (e.g., mb01_ethereal_) so outputs from different styles don’t overwrite each other.
Click Queue Prompt to generate. The Krea2ImageNode will call the Krea 2 API for each active branch, and SaveImage will write results to your output folder.
Iterate: adjust moodboard_strength to balance style vs prompt, refine prompts, swap moodboard IDs, or duplicate a group to add more style variants.
suggestedUseCases: Style A/B testing for art direction and look‑development before committing to a concept
Client reviews: produce side‑by‑side variations aligned to different moodboards
Prompt engineering under controlled style conditions to learn how wording changes outcomes
Building a style library by batch‑generating references per moodboard
Previsualization for campaigns where consistent mood and color language are critical

faqItems.question: What is a moodboard_id and where do I get it?
faqItems.answer: It’s the UUID that identifies a Krea moodboard. Copy it from your Krea account or moodboard page and paste it into the PrimitiveNode feeding the Krea2ImageNode. The workflow includes example IDs in Author Notes you can test with.

faqItems.question: How do I balance the moodboard’s style with my prompt?
faqItems.answer: Use the moodboard_strength input. Lower values give your prompt more control; higher values enforce the moodboard’s look more strongly. Start mid‑range, then nudge up or down based on how much of the board’s palette, composition, and texture you want to see.

faqItems.question: Why are some branches not generating images?
faqItems.answer: Make sure the branch isn’t bypassed, the Krea API key is configured for Krea2ImageNode, and the moodboard_id is valid. Also confirm SaveImage has a writable output path and unique filename_prefix to avoid collisions.

faqItems.question: Can I add more than six moodboards?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Duplicate any Moodboard group (PrimitiveNodes → Krea2ImageNode → SaveImage), update the MarkdownNote label, and point the new PrimitiveNodes to your new moodboard_id and prompt.

834ab8919949.title: Seedance2.5 1080P: Image to Video
834ab8919949.description: Generate cinematic 1080P video clips from a single image using Seedance 2.5, animating the still into a moving scene with synchronized sound, music, and dialogue for clips up to 30 seconds across any aspect ratio. Ideal for breathing life into product shots, extending concept art into motion, and creating engaging social media content from photographs.
834ab8919949.metaDescription: Animate a single image into 1080p video in ComfyUI with Seedance 2.5. Configure motion, duration, and aspect ratio, then export clips up to 30 seconds.
834ab8919949.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single still image into a polished 1080p video clip using Seedance 2.5 via the ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2. The graph is intentionally simple and reliable: LoadImage brings your source frame into the pipeline, ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 synthesizes motion-conditioned frames from that reference, and SaveVideo encodes the output sequence to a playable MP4 at your chosen frame rate and aspect ratio. You control duration (up to ~30 seconds), FPS, motion strength, and seeding for reproducible results.

Technically, the ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 uses the input image as a visual prior, generating a temporally coherent frame sequence that preserves identity and structure while introducing camera-like moves (e.g., gentle pans, zooms, and parallax) and scene dynamics. Because resolution and aspect ratio are configurable, you can produce 1920x1080 landscape, 1080x1920 vertical, or square clips while maintaining 1080 on the long edge. SaveVideo then assembles frames at the specified FPS. Note: this minimal graph outputs video only; to add music, dialogue, or foley, mux audio afterward or extend the workflow with audio nodes/external tools.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and verify required nodes are available: LoadImage, ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 (Seedance 2.5), and SaveVideo.
Load your source still via LoadImage. For best results, pre-crop it to your target aspect ratio (e.g., 16:9, 9:16, or 1:1) to avoid unintended cropping or stretching.

In ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2, set key parameters: duration (seconds, up to ~30), FPS (e.g., 16–24 for efficiency, 30 for smoother motion), motion strength (lower = subtle parallax, higher = bolder movement), and a fixed seed for reproducibility.

Choose your 1080p target size. For landscape, use 1920x1080; for vertical, 1080x1920; for square, 1080x1080. Ensure these dimensions are reflected both in the generation node (if width/height are exposed) and in SaveVideo.
Execute the graph. Inspect the preview frames for artifacts or identity drift; if needed, reduce motion strength or the clip length and re-run with the same seed.
Export with SaveVideo at your chosen FPS. If you need audio (music, VO, or dialogue), add it in a video editor or extend the workflow to mux an external audio track.
suggestedUseCases: Breathing life into product shots with subtle camera moves and parallax for ecommerce or ads.
Extending concept art or keyframes into motion to pitch scenes or mood pieces.
Turning portraits or lifestyle photos into eye-catching vertical clips for social media.
Animating architectural renders to demonstrate space and depth with gentle camera motion.
Creating loopable background visuals from static graphics for events or stream overlays.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow generate audio (music or dialogue) along with the video?
faqItems.answer: No. This graph outputs video only via SaveVideo. To add music, VO, or dialogue, mux an audio file afterward in your editor or extend the workflow with audio/muxing nodes.

faqItems.question: What resolution and aspect ratios are supported?
faqItems.answer: Any common aspect ratio works. For 1080p deliverables, use 1920x1080 (landscape), 1080x1920 (vertical), or 1080x1080 (square). Keep the long edge at 1080 and match your source image’s aspect ratio to minimize cropping.

faqItems.question: How long can the clip be, and what are performance considerations?
faqItems.answer: Up to ~30 seconds is practical. Longer clips and higher FPS increase VRAM and render time. For mid-range GPUs, start with 16–24 FPS and moderate motion strength; if VRAM is limited, consider shorter durations or 720p tests first.

faqItems.question: Can I automate this via the ComfyUI API?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Serialize the workflow JSON and POST it to ComfyUI’s /prompt endpoint. Provide your image as a file path (server-side) or base64. Set duration, FPS, resolution, and seed in the ByteDance2ReferenceNodeV2 before triggering the run.

83ff3768d42b.title: Wan2.1 VACE Reference to Video
83ff3768d42b.description: Create videos that match the style and content of a reference image. Perfect for style-consistent video generation.
83ff3768d42b.metaDescription: Generate style-consistent videos from a single image using Wan2.1 VACE in ComfyUI. Guide motion with prompts and export MP4 or animated WebP.
83ff3768d42b.extendedDescription:
Wan2.1 VACE Reference to Video turns a single image into a short video that preserves your reference’s style and subject while introducing motion guided by text prompts. The core of the workflow is the WanVaceToVideo node, which fuses a loaded reference image (LoadImage) with prompt text encoded by CLIPTextEncode. The diffusion backbone is provided by the Wan 2.1 VACE models—use UNETLoader and VAELoader in the “Load models here” group to select either Wan2.1-VACE-1.3B or Wan2.1-VACE-14B. A ModelSamplingSD3 node configures the sampler, and KSampler handles denoising with your chosen steps and cfg scale. If you need stylistic adapters, LoraLoader lets you apply a matching LoRA to the same diffusion model family.

After sampling, VAEDecode reconstructs frames from latents. TrimVideoLatent helps you set exact duration, and the “First Frame control” group (ImageToMask, SolidMask, MaskToImage, RepeatImageBatch) can lock or protect parts of the initial frame for stronger identity or composition retention. PreviewImage nodes allow quick QC during iteration. Finally, CreateVideo aggregates frames and you can export via SaveVideo (MP4) or SaveAnimatedWEBP for lightweight previews. Author guidance: default steps=20 and cfg=6.0 work well; with CausVid LoRA use fewer steps (2–4) and a low cfg (~1.0). For resolution, VACE-1.3B is suited to 480p, while VACE-14B delivers higher quality and supports 480p and 720p at the cost of longer render time.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then open the “Load models here” group. Point UNETLoader and VAELoader to your chosen Wan2.1 VACE checkpoint (1.3B for faster 480p drafts, 14B for higher quality and 720p). Ensure CLIPLoader matches the model family. Optionally add a LoRA in LoraLoader that matches the same base model.
In “Load reference image,” use LoadImage to bring in your source image. Set the target resolution in the “Video Size” group to match your image’s aspect ratio to avoid warping.

Enter your positive and negative prompts in the “Prompt” group via CLIPTextEncode. Keep descriptions specific (subject, motion, camera) and use negatives to filter artifacts. If using a CausVid LoRA, lower steps to 2–4 and cfg to ~1.0 per the notes.
Configure generation in “Sampling & Decoding”: set steps and cfg in KSampler (default 20/6.0). ModelSamplingSD3 should be connected to KSampler as provided. Choose or fix a seed for reproducibility.

Set length and control: in WanVaceToVideo choose the number of frames. The helper in “Value = Length(WanVaceToVideo) - 1” keeps CreateVideo in sync. Use “First Frame control” (ImageToMask/SolidMask/MaskToImage) if you need to preserve identity or parts of the first frame; TrimVideoLatent if you need to shorten the sequence.
Queue the workflow. Inspect PreviewImage outputs to validate frames. When satisfied, export with SaveVideo (MP4) in the “Save Video (Mp4)” group, or use SaveAnimatedWEBP for quick web previews.
suggestedUseCases: Brand or character style continuity: turn a single key image into on-brand motion snippets for social posts.
Product hero spins and parallax moves derived from a catalog photo while preserving materials and design cues.
Concept art turnarounds: bring a static character or creature sheet to life with subtle, guided camera motion.
Animated portraits and intros where identity and art style must remain consistent across frames.
Storyboard previz: rapidly prototype shot motion from a single frame before full production.

faqItems.question: Which model should I pick: VACE-1.3B or VACE-14B?
faqItems.answer: Use 1.3B for faster drafts at 480p and lower VRAM. Choose 14B for better detail, stronger temporal coherence, and 720p support, noting longer render times and higher memory use.

faqItems.question: How do I control video length and frame rate?
faqItems.answer: Set the frame count in WanVaceToVideo. The helper node “Value = Length(WanVaceToVideo) - 1” keeps CreateVideo aligned. Set FPS and output settings in CreateVideo/SaveVideo. Use TrimVideoLatent to shorten or fine-tune duration without re-running the full pipeline.

faqItems.question: How can I keep the subject consistent across frames?
faqItems.answer: Enable the “First Frame control” group. Use SolidMask or ImageToMask to define protected areas, then MaskToImage to apply them. Combine with a moderate cfg (around 6) and a fixed seed in KSampler to improve identity and layout stability.

faqItems.question: Can I use LoRAs with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Load a LoRA via LoraLoader that matches the exact Wan diffusion model family you’re using. Follow the author’s guidance for CausVid LoRA (steps 2–4, cfg ≈1.0). Mismatched LoRAs can degrade quality or fail to load.

840b6e4c3983.title: Wan Animate 2.2 Character Replacement Workflow
840b6e4c3983.description: Wan Animate 2.2 — Character & Scene Replacement - Uses Nano Banana 2 to generate a reference image from the first frame, then swaps the full scene. Optimized for human subjects.
840b6e4c3983.metaDescription: Replace characters in videos with Wan Animate 2.2 for realistic human animations. Optimized for human subjects using advanced AI models.
840b6e4c3983.extendedDescription:
The Wan Animate 2.2 Character Replacement Workflow is designed to replace characters and scenes in video content using advanced AI models. This workflow leverages the power of the Wan 2.2 Animate model, which is specifically optimized for human subjects, ensuring that the character replacement is both stable and convincing. The process begins by utilizing the Nano Banana 2 model to generate a reference image from the first frame of the video. This image serves as the basis for replacing the character throughout the entire video sequence. The workflow employs several custom nodes, including ComfyUI-WanAnimatePreprocess and ComfyUI-segment-anything-2, to segment and process the video frames effectively.

Technically, the workflow uses a combination of nodes such as VHS_LoadVideo to load the video, and GeminiNanoBanana2 to apply the character replacement based on the reference image. The SaveVideo node is then used to output the final animated video. This workflow is particularly useful for creators looking to produce high-quality character animations in video content, offering a seamless integration of AI-driven techniques to enhance video production capabilities. By focusing on human subjects, it ensures that the facial and body features are rendered with high fidelity, making it ideal for projects that require realistic character animations.
howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI and ensure all necessary models and custom nodes are installed.
Import your video file using the VHS_LoadVideo node to start the process.
Select a reference image from the first frame using the GeminiNanoBanana2 node for character replacement.
Run the workflow to process the video frames and apply the character replacement.
Use the SaveVideo node to export the final animated video with the replaced character.
Review the output to ensure the character replacement meets your expectations.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional videos with customized characters.
Producing educational content with animated human figures.
Developing short films or animations with unique character designs.
Enhancing social media content with engaging character animations.
Generating marketing materials with personalized video characters.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow be used with non-human subjects?
faqItems.answer: While the workflow is optimized for human subjects, it can technically be used with non-human subjects, but the results may not be as stable or convincing.

faqItems.question: What is the best resolution for input videos?
faqItems.answer: The workflow includes a Target Resolution group to help optimize video resolution. However, starting with a high-resolution video is recommended for the best results.

faqItems.question: How long does it take to process a video?
faqItems.answer: Processing time can vary based on video length and system performance, but typically, it may take several minutes to an hour for a standard-length video.

faqItems.question: Do I need a powerful GPU to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: A powerful GPU is recommended to efficiently run the workflow, especially for high-resolution videos or longer sequences.

847f17f3f95c.title: Qwen Image Edit for Illustration v 1.0
847f17f3f95c.description: This workflow leverages Qwen Edit with a finetuned illustration LoRA for better illustrated content editing.
847f17f3f95c.metaDescription: Turn photos into clean illustrations with Qwen Image Edit + an illustration LoRA. Text-guide your edits and save stylized results directly in ComfyUI.
847f17f3f95c.extendedDescription:
Qwen Image Edit for Illustration v1.0 is a text-guided image editing workflow that turns your existing images into clean, stylized illustrations while preserving structure. It combines the Qwen Image Edit model with an illustration-focused LoRA so you can apply style changes (e.g., "convert this product photo into a flat vector illustration") without redrawing from scratch. The core path is simple: LoadImage brings in your source, PrimitiveStringMultiline captures your edit instruction, the model loader node (c7f5c302-e46e-4a0f-91bd-0aec474e7659) loads the Qwen Image/Qwen Image Edit weights, LoraLoaderModelOnly merges the illustration LoRA into the base model, the edit node (eba40a3a-f6c5-48ac-b58e-55525d06b373) runs inference, and SaveImage writes the result.

Technically, the LoRA is injected on-the-fly by LoraLoaderModelOnly, biasing the Qwen Edit model toward illustrated outputs while keeping the underlying content aligned with your source image. The edit node consumes the input image plus your instruction and uses the merged model to generate a new frame that follows your prompt. The included MarkdownNote provides in-graph tips, and all required model files are available from the Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI and Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-Edit_ComfyUI Hugging Face repos linked in the author notes.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. Ensure you have the Qwen Image/Qwen Image Edit models and the illustration LoRA downloaded from the linked Hugging Face repos.
Open the model loader node (c7f5c302-e46e-4a0f-91bd-0aec474e7659) and point it to your Qwen Image/Qwen Image Edit weights as described in the repository readme.
In LoraLoaderModelOnly, select the illustration LoRA file and set its strength. Start with a moderate value; you can increase it if the style isn’t strong enough.
Use LoadImage to bring in your source image. Keep the resolution moderate for faster iterations, then upscale later if needed.
Enter a clear, single-purpose edit instruction in PrimitiveStringMultiline (e.g., "convert to flat 2D illustration, pastel palette, minimal shading, keep layout and proportions").

Run the workflow. The edit node (eba40a3a-f6c5-48ac-b58e-55525d06b373) will apply the instruction using the LoRA-merged model, and SaveImage will write the result to your ComfyUI output folder. If needed, iterate by adjusting LoRA strength and the edit parameters on the Qwen Edit node.
suggestedUseCases: Turn product photos into flat, on-brand illustrations for catalogs, pitch decks, and e-commerce thumbnails.
Convert character or portrait photos into clean manga/comic styles while preserving facial identity and pose.
Create consistent illustrated variants of UI assets or icons from mixed-source references.
Stylize slide imagery or infographics into cohesive, minimal illustrations for presentations.
Simplify busy backgrounds and unify color palettes to match brand style guides.

faqItems.question: Which models do I need and where do I get them?
faqItems.answer: Download the Qwen Image/Qwen Image Edit weights and the illustration LoRA from the Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI and Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-Edit_ComfyUI Hugging Face repos (see links in the workflow notes). Point the model loader node to the base weights and LoraLoaderModelOnly to the LoRA file.

faqItems.question: How do I control how strong the illustration style looks?
faqItems.answer: Use the LoRA strength in LoraLoaderModelOnly as your primary control. If the node exposes guidance or edit-strength parameters on the Qwen Edit node (eba40a3a-…), adjust those as secondary controls. Increase LoRA strength for bolder style; reduce it to keep more photographic detail.

faqItems.question: Can I make only stylistic changes and keep content intact?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Write instructions that focus on style, color, and rendering (e.g., “flat shading, soft pastel palette”) and avoid adding or removing objects. This nudges the model to preserve composition and subject while changing the look.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow support region-specific edits or masking?
faqItems.answer: This graph is designed for global, instruction-based edits. For targeted regions, use a masking-enabled variant of the Qwen Edit workflow or add a mask path and a compatible edit node that accepts masks.

857e50707831.title: SeedVR2: Image Upscale
857e50707831.description: Upload an image to upscale it with SeedVR2 and generate a high-definition output.
857e50707831.metaDescription: Upscale images with SeedVR2 for high-definition results using ComfyUI. Enhance clarity and detail with this efficient workflow.
857e50707831.extendedDescription:
The SeedVR2: Image Upscale workflow is designed to enhance the resolution of images using the SeedVR2 model, which is renowned for its ability to upscale visuals while maintaining high-definition quality. This workflow leverages several key nodes, including LoadImage, SaveImage, and ImageCompare, alongside the custom node seedvr2_videoupscaler from the comfyui_essentials package. These nodes work in concert to load an image, apply the upscale process, and save the enhanced output, ensuring a seamless transition from input to output. The ImageCompare node is particularly useful for evaluating the quality of the upscaled image against the original, providing a visual confirmation of the improvements made.

Technically, the workflow operates by first loading the input image using the LoadImage node. The image is then processed through the seedvr2_videoupscaler node, which applies advanced algorithms to increase the image resolution. After processing, the SaveImage node stores the high-definition output, while the ImageCompare node allows users to visually assess the differences between the original and upscaled images. This workflow is particularly useful for applications where image clarity and detail are paramount, such as in digital art, photography, and video production.
howToUse: Load the SeedVR2: Image Upscale workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadImage node to upload the image you wish to upscale.
Ensure the seedvr2_videoupscaler node is correctly configured to process your image.
Run the workflow to apply the upscale process.
Use the ImageCompare node to compare the original and upscaled images.
Save the enhanced image using the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing digital artwork for print or display.
Improving the quality of low-resolution photographs.
Upscaling video frames for higher resolution playback.
Refining textures in game development for better visual fidelity.
Preparing images for high-definition presentations or marketing materials.

faqItems.question: What is the maximum resolution I can achieve with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The maximum resolution depends on the capabilities of the SeedVR2 model and your system's processing power. Typically, it can upscale images to several times their original size while maintaining quality.

faqItems.question: Do I need any special hardware to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: While no special hardware is required, a powerful GPU will significantly speed up the processing time and handle larger images more efficiently.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for batch processing multiple images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can adapt the workflow to process multiple images by iterating over a set of images with the LoadImage node and saving each output individually.

faqItems.question: How does the ImageCompare node help in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The ImageCompare node allows you to visually assess the quality improvements by comparing the original and upscaled images side by side, ensuring the upscale meets your expectations.

Upload a pose reference video to be used for pose estimation.

Utilize the Wan Animate model to create a new video that follows the poses from the control video.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of the DWPose Estimator in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The DWPose Estimator extracts pose information from an input video, creating a control video that guides the animation process in generating new content.

faqItems.question: Can I use any video as a pose reference?

faqItems.question: What is the role of Wan Animate in this workflow?

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the output video matches my expectations?

88c94d64ca5d.title: Comfy for Advertising - Storyboard Creation
88c94d64ca5d.metaDescription: Create 6-panel ad storyboards from a shot list, then elevate them to styleframes using OpenAI or Gemini image nodes in ComfyUI.
88c94d64ca5d.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow builds advertising storyboards fast by turning a plain 6‑panel grid and a shot list into clean black‑and‑white sketch frames, then optionally upgrades those sketches into production‑quality styleframes. The STORYBOARD GENERATOR group takes your shot descriptions from INPUT SHOT LIST, merges them with consistent style instructions via StringConcatenate, and feeds them to either OpenAIGPTImage1 (OpenAI’s gpt‑image‑1) or GeminiImage2Node for image generation. The first image you load is used as the panel grid reference, guiding the model to sketch simple line drawings inside each box and place the shot description as a caption beneath each frame. BatchImagesNode handles all six shots in one go, and SaveImage writes the finished storyboard to disk. MarkdownNote nodes in the graph provide in‑canvas guidance, while PrimitiveNode values set defaults like monochrome line style and panel count.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm your API credentials for OpenAIGPTImage1 and/or GeminiImage2Node are configured in their node settings.
In INPUT SHOT LIST, paste up to six clear shot descriptions (one per panel). Keep them concise and visual; leave a shot blank if you want that panel empty.
In INPUT SKETCH + MOODBOARD, LoadImage the storyboard grid as the first image (high-contrast boxes work best). Optionally add moodboard references to steer style later.
Choose your generator: enable either OpenAIGPTImage1 or GeminiImage2Node (bypass the one you’re not using). The StringConcatenate node already packages style guidance and each shot’s text.

Run the STORYBOARD GENERATOR group. BatchImagesNode will process all panels, producing a single 6-panel black-and-white sketch board with simple lines and per-frame captions. Inspect outputs from SaveImage.
Optional: For higher-fidelity visuals, pass the sketch and moodboard images into the STYLEFRAME GENERATOR group to produce production-quality stills, then SaveImage the results.
suggestedUseCases: Pitch decks and client reviews: fast, consistent 6-panel storyboards for TVC or social spots.
Internal previsualization: iterate on framing and product beats before committing to shoots.
Style exploration: convert a rough sketch board plus moodboard into polished keyframes.
E-commerce and product launches: storyboard hero shots and transitions for short ads.
Social cutdowns: quickly adapt a master shot list into multiple 6-panel narratives.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow keep a consistent black‑and‑white sketch style?
faqItems.answer: The StringConcatenate node injects shared style instructions (simple line art, monochrome, no intricate detail) into every panel prompt. Using one generator (OpenAIGPTImage1 or GeminiImage2Node) across the batch further stabilizes style.

faqItems.question: How do I switch between OpenAI and Gemini for generation?
faqItems.answer: Use the provided generator nodes and bypass the one you aren’t using. Both accept the same prompt and reference inputs prepared upstream, so you can A/B compare results without changing your shot list.

faqItems.question: Will it actually draw inside my grid and put Helvetica captions under each frame?
faqItems.answer: The first loaded image is used as the grid reference, and the prompt instructs the model to draw within boxes and place captions below in Helvetica. Generative models approximate typography; if you need exact fonts, add a text overlay/compositing step after generation.

faqItems.question: Can I change the number of panels or leave some blank?
faqItems.answer: This template targets a 6-panel board. You can leave a panel blank by providing no text for that shot. To change panel count, duplicate/adjust the BatchImagesNode path and update prompt text/layout guidance to match a new grid.

The Grok model's advanced capabilities allow for nuanced interpretation of the input images, making this workflow a powerful tool for creators looking to convert static art into engaging video content.
howToUse: Load the 'Grok: Reference to Video' workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the 'LoadImage' node to upload your reference images (up to 6).
Connect the images to the 'GrokVideoReferenceNode' to process them.
Configure the Grok model settings as needed for your project.

suggestedUseCases: Creating animated videos from character reference images for storytelling.

Animating concept art for visual presentations.
Producing educational videos with consistent character visuals.

faqItems.question: How many reference images can I use in this workflow?

faqItems.question: What is the role of the Grok model in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The Grok model interprets and transforms static reference images into a coherent video sequence, maintaining visual consistency.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the video output settings?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can configure the Grok model settings within the workflow to tailor the video output to your needs.

faqItems.question: What formats are supported for exporting the video?

894c44a995a2.title: Wan2.7: Video Edit
894c44a995a2.description: Upload a video and corresponding images to edit and replace characters or scenes using the Wan2.7 model.
894c44a995a2.metaDescription: Edit videos by swapping characters or scenes using reference images with Wan2.7 in ComfyUI. Load video/images, configure Wan2VideoEditApi, and export.
894c44a995a2.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates reference-guided video editing with Wan2.7. You load a source clip with LoadVideo, provide one or more reference images with LoadImage, and let the Wan2VideoEditApi node apply character or scene replacements consistently across frames. The node calls the Wan2.7 model to infer identity, attire, and style cues from your references, then synthesizes edited frames that preserve the original camera motion and timing. Finally, SaveVideo assembles the frames into a finished MP4/WEBM with your chosen frame rate and quality.

Technically, the Wan2VideoEditApi node takes three essential inputs: the decoded video frames, the reference image tensor(s), and your textual directions (prompt and optional constraints). It uses the Wan2.7 backbone to align reference identity/style with the target footage while maintaining temporal coherence, so edits remain stable over time rather than flickering frame to frame. This makes the workflow especially useful for swapping a character across an entire shot or re-dressing a scene without rotoscoping. The minimalist node set—LoadVideo → LoadImage → Wan2VideoEditApi → SaveVideo—keeps the pipeline simple while still offering strong control through prompts, reference choice, and edit strength settings exposed by the API node.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and verify the four core nodes are present: LoadVideo, LoadImage, Wan2VideoEditApi, and SaveVideo. Ensure Wan2.7 is selected in the API node if a model selector is available.
In LoadVideo, choose your source clip. Short clips (5–10 seconds) are ideal for first runs. If the node exposes trim or frame range, set it to test a small segment before processing the full video.

Add one or more LoadImage nodes and pick high-quality reference images for the character or scene you want to introduce. Prefer images that match the target clip’s angle, lighting, and pose. Connect the LoadImage outputs to the reference inputs on Wan2VideoEditApi.

Open Wan2VideoEditApi and enter a clear prompt describing the desired replacement (e.g., the character’s outfit, identity, or scene style). If available, adjust controls like negative text, edit strength/blend, guidance, and seed to balance fidelity to the original video versus the reference.
Connect the edited video output from Wan2VideoEditApi to SaveVideo. In SaveVideo, choose your output format and frame rate—matching the source fps often yields the most natural motion.

Click Queue Prompt to run. Review the result; if identity or style wavers, improve reference images (closer angle/lighting), refine your prompt, or reduce edit strength. Re-run on the full clip once you’re satisfied.
suggestedUseCases: Character replacement for social content or short films without manual rotoscoping.
Wardrobe or style swaps (e.g., turning a casual outfit into a uniform) while preserving original performance.
Background or scene re-dressing to match a storyboard, season, or theme.
Brand or product visualization by placing a consistent style/look across a sequence.
Continuity fixes when reshoots aren’t possible, e.g., adjusting props or attire across takes.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key or internet connection for Wan2VideoEditApi?
faqItems.answer: The Wan2VideoEditApi node typically calls a remote Wan2.7 service, which may require credentials and an active internet connection. Check the node’s settings or your ComfyUI extension docs to configure any required keys.

faqItems.question: How can I get stable identity and fewer artifacts?
faqItems.answer: Use high-resolution reference images that match the video’s angle and lighting, keep prompts specific (describe attire, colors, and style), and tune the edit strength to avoid overdriving the look. If your node exposes a seed, lock it for reproducibility.

faqItems.question: Can I edit only part of a video?
faqItems.answer: Yes. If LoadVideo or the API node exposes a frame range, use it to test or limit the edit. Otherwise, trim the source clip externally before loading it, then process just that segment in ComfyUI.

faqItems.question: Does the exported video include audio?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo in ComfyUI generally exports silent video. To keep audio, export the edited clip and then remux the original audio track using a video editor or a tool like FFmpeg.

895960b69952.title: Kling O1: Video Edit
895960b69952.description: Edit videos with natural language commands, featuring video reference mode for quick generation of high-quality style transfers, element additions, and background modifications.
895960b69952.metaDescription: Edit videos using natural language commands for style transfers, element additions, and background modifications with Kling O1: Video Edit workflow.
895960b69952.extendedDescription:
The Kling O1: Video Edit workflow is designed to transform video editing by leveraging natural language commands. This workflow utilizes the Kling model, allowing users to perform high-quality style transfers, add elements, and modify backgrounds in videos with ease. At the core of this workflow are nodes like LoadImage, SaveVideo, and KlingOmniProEditVideoNode, which facilitate the seamless integration of reference images and videos. The workflow is particularly effective in scenarios where quick and precise video edits are required, making it a valuable tool for both amateur and professional video editors.

Technically, the workflow begins by loading video components using the LoadVideo and GetVideoComponents nodes. Common steps inside this kind of node include detecting clothing regions, pose-aware alignment/warping, and clean blending to avoid artifacts around edges. Because everything runs inside ComfyUI, you can iterate quickly by swapping inputs, adjusting the node’s settings (if exposed in your build), and re-queuing to refine fit, coverage, and output size.

Run the graph: queue/execute the workflow. The Clothes Changer node will align the outfit to the character’s pose and composite the clothing onto the person, then pass the result to SaveImage.

You describe the change in plain language—such as “replace the background with a minimalist white studio” or “remove the product label and keep everything else the same”—and the model returns a single, temporally consistent edited clip.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce flicker or inconsistencies across frames?

faqItems.question: Does the workflow preserve audio?

faqItems.question: Any tips on performance and limits?

8e090ccf5a29.title: AI on the Lot 2026 - Z-Image Turbo - t2i

8e090ccf5a29.metaDescription: ComfyUI Z-Image Turbo text-to-image workflow using Qwen 3 4B text encoder; simple T2I with SaveImage output and reproducible seeds.
8e090ccf5a29.extendedDescription:
This template is a compact, text-to-image workflow built around the Z-Image Turbo generator, designed to get from prompt to output with minimal setup. At its core is a single custom Z-Image Turbo T2I node (node id f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1) that encapsulates text encoding and image generation, paired with a SaveImage node to write results to disk and a MarkdownNote for in-graph guidance. The template is configured to use the Qwen 3 4B text encoder weights (qwen_3_4b.safetensors) for prompt conditioning.

Technically, the Z-Image Turbo node handles the end-to-end generation: it ingests your prompt (and optional negative prompt), encodes it with the specified text encoder, and runs the model’s internal sampler to produce an image tensor. That tensor is passed directly to SaveImage, which exports PNGs to your ComfyUI output folder using the configured filename prefix. Because the heavy lifting is wrapped in a single node, you get a clean, reliable T2I pipeline that’s easy to iterate: tweak prompts, resolution, seed, and sampling controls in one place, then save consistent, reproducible outputs.
howToUse: Load the "AI on the Lot 2026 - Z-Image Turbo - t2i" template in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote for any in-graph instructions or links.
Download qwen_3_4b.safetensors from the provided model link and place it in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders (create the folder if needed). Restart ComfyUI so the node can find it.

Open the Z-Image Turbo T2I node (id f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1) and fill in your Prompt (and optional Negative Prompt). Set resolution, seed (or -1 for random), and other exposed sampling controls as desired.

Start with moderate settings for speed and quality balance (e.g., a mid-size resolution and default sampling values). Increase steps or adjust guidance/CFG only as needed to refine detail or adherence to the prompt.
Run the queue. The node will generate images and pass them to SaveImage, which writes PNGs to your ComfyUI output directory. Adjust the SaveImage filename prefix if you want clearer organization.
Iterate: refine your prompt phrasing, lock the seed for consistent variations, and use a negative prompt to suppress unwanted elements. Re-run until you reach the look you want.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept art and style studies from short text prompts
Product or packaging mockups to explore form, color, and materials
Storyboard frames and previsualization for film or animation
Mood boards and look development for branding or UI themes
Illustrations for articles, blogs, and creative writing prompts

faqItems.question: How do I get repeatable results for the same prompt?
faqItems.answer: Set a fixed seed value in the Z-Image Turbo node instead of using random (-1). Keep resolution and sampling controls the same; then re-run to reproduce the same image or make controlled variations by changing only one parameter at a time.

faqItems.question: I’m running out of VRAM or generation is slow. What should I change?

faqItems.question: My images aren’t saving. How do I fix SaveImage issues?

8f2cf0df5da6.title: LTX Cleanplate for VFX
8f2cf0df5da6.description: Prompt an object, and SAM3 + LTX 2.3 mask-conditioned inpainting remove it and rebuild the clean background plate."
8f2cf0df5da6.metaDescription: Create clean plates for VFX: SAM3 masks + LTX 2.3 mask-conditioned inpainting remove objects and rebuild background in ComfyUI.
8f2cf0df5da6.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds a clean background plate by removing an object from video using SAM3-driven masks and a mask-conditioned LTX-2.3 In‑Outpainting IC‑LoRA. The pipeline loads your clip with VHS_LoadVideo/VHS_VideoInfo, extracts frames via GetVideoComponents, and uses LoadSAM3Model → SAM3VideoSegmentation to seed a mask for the object you want to remove. SAM3Propagate tracks that mask across the shot, and SAM3VideoOutput provides a per‑frame OBJECT_MASK. To ensure seamless fills, LTXVDilateVideoMask expands the mask (e.g., s10/t1) and GrowMaskWithBlur feathers the edges.

The masked region is then green‑filled by LTXVInpaintPreprocess, and CreateVideo re‑encodes those preprocessed frames. That green plate, together with the OBJECT_MASK and your minimal background‑only prompt, feeds the LTX 2.3 In‑Outpainting IC‑LoRA (packaged here as a subgraph node), which is explicitly mask‑conditioned to generate only inside the masked area. Utility nodes like VHS_GetImageCount, ComfyMathExpression, and GetImageRangeFromBatch let you preview limited frame ranges before a full run. Finally, SaveVideo writes the cleanplate result for downstream compositing.
howToUse: Load the workflow, then import your source clip with VHS_LoadVideo. Confirm resolution and FPS with VHS_VideoInfo/GetVideoComponents.

In the SAM3 MASK group: load your SAM3 weights with LoadSAM3Model. Use SAM3VideoSegmentation to mark the object on a clear reference frame (positive/negative points or a box, as supported), then run SAM3Propagate to track the mask. Preview masks with SAM3VideoOutput/MaskToImage.
Refine the mask edges: increase LTXVDilateVideoMask size (start around 10) to cover motion blur/parallax and add feathering with GrowMaskWithBlur (e.g., 12–16 px) to avoid hard seams.

In LOAD FOOTAGE / SET PROMPT TO REMOVE: keep the text prompt empty or describe only the background inside the hole (never the entire scene). Example: “brick wall and window frame, soft shadows, no person.”

Run GENERATE. LTXVInpaintPreprocess will green‑fill the masked area; CreateVideo re‑encodes this guide plate; the LTX 2.3 In‑Outpainting IC‑LoRA subgraph uses the plate and OBJECT_MASK to synthesize new content only inside the hole.

Review the output and save with SaveVideo. If artifacts persist, increase dilation or feather, adjust the prompt to focus on background cues, or test a shorter range using VHS_GetImageCount + GetImageRangeFromBatch before re‑running the full clip.
suggestedUseCases: Building a clean background plate for compositing after removing talent, crew, or boom reflections.
Location cleanup: erase signage, rigs, cables, or production gear from tracking shots.
Product/video retouching: remove labels or stickers while restoring underlying surfaces.
Crowd/object removal in establishing shots where a consistent background can be reconstructed.
Prep plates for 2D/3D inserts by clearing foreground obstructions.

faqItems.question: How should I write the prompt for best results?
faqItems.answer: Keep it empty or describe only the background inside the masked area (e.g., “asphalt road with painted lines, soft shadow”). Avoid mentioning the removed object or unrelated foreground items—this can cause duplication or hallucinations.

faqItems.question: My edges flicker or show seams. What should I tweak?
faqItems.answer: Increase LTXVDilateVideoMask size to cover motion blur and expand beyond the object, then raise GrowMaskWithBlur feather radius to soften transitions. Also re‑seed SAM3 on a clearer frame and re‑propagate if the tracked mask drifts.

faqItems.question: Can I test a short section before processing the full video?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use VHS_GetImageCount to see the total frames and GetImageRangeFromBatch (optionally with ComfyMathExpression) to select a small frame window for quick iterations, then switch back to the full range once satisfied.

faqItems.question: Does the saved video include audio?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo typically outputs a silent file. If you need audio, re‑mux the original track in your NLE or a tool like ffmpeg. If your setup routes audio via GetVideoComponents, you can also handle pass‑through externally after render.

8f82ff60ae5e.title: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash: Video Edit
8f82ff60ae5e.description: Edit videos through natural language conversation with Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash. Upload a clip (10 seconds or less) and describe the change: swap backgrounds, restyle scenes, add or remove elements, and the model applies the edit while preserving everything you did not mention. Add \"Keep everything else the same\" for maximum consistency; simple prompts work best. Outputs video with native audio at 16:9 or 9:16, with 1080p/4K output available.
