8f82ff60ae5e.metaDescription: Edit 10s videos by prompt with Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash in ComfyUI. Swap backgrounds, restyle, and export 16:9 or 9:16 with audio at 1080p/4K.
8f82ff60ae5e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow lets you edit a short video by simply describing the change you want. LoadVideo ingests your clip (the template includes input/hooded_wanderer_planet_bridge.mp4 as a ready-to-run test), and GeminiVideoOmniV2 sends both the video and your plain‑language instruction to Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash. The model applies targeted edits—like swapping backgrounds, restyling a scene, or adding/removing elements—while leaving everything else untouched. For maximum fidelity, include a line such as “Keep everything else the same.” Simple, direct prompts tend to produce the most consistent results.

On output, SaveVideo writes the edited clip to disk with the native audio preserved. You can choose 16:9 or 9:16 and render at 1080p or 4K, making it suitable for landscape or vertical content. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides quick tips. The recommended input duration is 10 seconds or less to ensure responsive processing and stable edits. This setup is ideal for rapid remixes and iterative refinement without regenerating entire scenes from scratch.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure you’re on the latest version. Configure your Gemini API key in the ComfyUI settings or directly in the GeminiVideoOmniV2 node (as required by your setup).
In LoadVideo, set the input to input/hooded_wanderer_planet_bridge.mp4 (included) or drag in your own clip (10 seconds or less). Confirm the clip plays correctly in the node’s preview if available.

Select the GeminiVideoOmniV2 node and write a concise instruction describing just the change you want (e.g., “Replace the background with a neon city at night. Keep everything else the same.”). Choose the desired aspect ratio (16:9 or 9:16) and resolution (1080p or 4K) in the node’s settings.
Optionally add brief refinement details (color palette, time of day, or specific objects to add/remove), but avoid overloading the prompt. Keep the instruction simple and unambiguous.
Queue and run the workflow. The model processes the video and returns an edited clip; SaveVideo writes the result to your output directory, preserving the original audio track.
Review the output and iterate. If something drifted, make the prompt more explicit (e.g., “Do not change the subject’s clothing. Keep the camera motion identical.”) and re-run to refine.
suggestedUseCases: Background replacement for B‑roll or social clips without re-shooting (e.g., turn a bridge scene into a futuristic city).
Style restyling and color grading matches (film look, seasonal changes, day-to-night) while preserving composition.
Object cleanup: remove a distracting sign, add a subtle prop, or hide a logo.

faqItems.question: What clip length works best?

faqItems.question: Will the original audio be preserved?

faqItems.question: How do I maximize consistency across frames?

8fe7ed30c4ec.title: VFX Passes to Video
8fe7ed30c4ec.description: Turn one reference image into a blendable VFX keyframe with chromatic aberration, glow, lens flare, film finish, and generate a Seedance 2.0 cinematic video.
8fe7ed30c4ec.metaDescription: Create layered VFX passes on a still image and generate a Seedance 2.0 cinematic video with chromatic aberration, glow, lens flare, and film finish.
8fe7ed30c4ec.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single reference image into a layered VFX keyframe and then uses that keyframe to drive a Seedance 2.0 cinematic video. In the Generated VFX Passes group, effect layers are built as separate passes—chromatic aberration, glow/bloom, lens flare, and a film finish—then composited with ImageBlend nodes. Glow is created with ImageBlur and blended with Screen; lens flare is a black-background overlay blended with Screen; chromatic aberration is applied as a full-frame pass blended with Normal. Blend strengths are exposed via PrimitiveFloat nodes, and you can preview any stage with PreviewAny or save stills with SaveImage.

Once the composited keyframe looks right, it’s routed into ByteDance2ReferenceNode in the Seedance 2.0 Output group to generate a motion clip that inherits the look of your keyframe. GeminiImage2Node and GeminiNode are used in the graph to construct and refine the image-based passes, while ImageBlend controls how each pass stacks. Finally, SaveVideo writes the Seedance 2.0 output to disk. This setup is useful because you can dial in a cinematic look non-destructively on a still, audition each pass in isolation, and then get a consistent, blendable look carried through to video—all from one reference frame.
howToUse: Load the workflow and drop your reference image into the Input group’s LoadImage node. Use PreviewAny to confirm resolution and framing.
In Generated VFX Passes, adjust PrimitiveFloat sliders that feed each pass (chromatic aberration amount, glow intensity, lens-flare opacity, film finish strength). Preview each pass with PreviewAny.

Verify blend modes in the ImageBlend nodes: use Normal for the chromatic aberration pass, Screen for the glow/bloom pass, and Screen for the black-background lens-flare overlay. Tweak blend strengths until the composite looks balanced.
Optionally SaveImage at key points to compare different looks or archive a final VFX keyframe. Use PreviewAny on the final composite to check edges, highlights, and grain.
Send the final composite output to the Seedance 2.0 Output group’s ByteDance2ReferenceNode. Set the node’s basic generation parameters as needed (e.g., seed or duration if exposed by the node).
Run the Seedance 2.0 section and write the result with SaveVideo. Review the clip; if needed, return to the Blend Controls and PrimitiveFloat values to refine the look and regenerate.
suggestedUseCases: Turn a polished hero still into a short cinematic motion clip with consistent VFX for trailers or social teasers.
Add filmic glow, subtle chromatic aberration, and lens flare to a product shot, then animate it for ad bumpers.
Create a stylized, blendable keyframe for music videos and motion graphics, ensuring the look holds together in motion.
VFX look development: quickly test glow/halation and flare treatments on stills before committing to a longer render.
Thumbnail-to-video workflows where a designed cover image becomes a short, on-brand motion snippet.

faqItems.question: How do I disable a specific pass (e.g., lens flare) without breaking the graph?
faqItems.answer: Set that pass’s PrimitiveFloat strength to 0 or switch its ImageBlend alpha to 0. You can also temporarily bypass it by disconnecting the pass input to the corresponding ImageBlend node.

faqItems.question: Why does the glow look too strong or wash out highlights?
faqItems.answer: Screen blends can quickly blow out bright regions. Lower the glow PrimitiveFloat value feeding the ImageBlend, reduce ImageBlur radius for a tighter bloom, and preview at 100% to judge highlight roll-off.

faqItems.question: How can I reduce visible color fringing from chromatic aberration?
faqItems.answer: Dial back the chromatic aberration pass’s strength (PrimitiveFloat) and keep its ImageBlend mode on Normal. Small values usually sell the effect without distracting edges.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the video matches my keyframe look?
faqItems.answer: Finalize the composite keyframe first (use SaveImage and PreviewAny), then feed that exact output into ByteDance2ReferenceNode. Keep effect strengths moderate and consistent; re-run SaveVideo if you adjust blends.

90d086fef9e3.title: Tattoo Generator
90d086fef9e3.description: Turn your tattoo design ideas into reality with this AI tattoo generator app. Explore unique tattoo styles, get instant design inspiration, and create custom tattoo concepts in seconds — perfect for planning your next piece.
90d086fef9e3.metaDescription: ComfyUI Tattoo Generator: build tattoo prompts, switch styles, set resolution, preview, and save clean concept images for client-ready inspiration.
90d086fef9e3.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI Tattoo Generator turns written ideas into clean tattoo concept images using a streamlined, prompt-first pipeline. You type your idea in a PrimitiveStringMultiline node, optionally provide a small JSON snippet, choose a style with a ComfySwitchNode, and the workflow assembles a polished prompt with StringConcatenate. A ResolutionSelector lets you pick a canvas size that suits patch-style, sleeve elements, or flash-sheet compositions. The core image is produced by the generation node identified as e46f5b18-9edb-4755-bec5-b38521684b4c, wrapped by a CustomCombo that encapsulates the underlying text-to-image model and default inference settings. You can preview instantly with PreviewAny and export final images via SaveImage.

Technically, the prompt flow is handled by string utilities and simple logic: JsonExtractString can pull a field (for example, a preferred style) from a JSON string if you supply one; ComfySwitchNode toggles between built-in tattoo aesthetics (e.g., blackwork, fine-line, geometric) and feeds that choice into StringConcatenate to form the final prompt. ResolutionSelector passes width/height to the generator, ensuring the model inside the CustomCombo receives consistent parameters. The result is a focused, tattoo-oriented text-to-image workflow that encourages clear subject descriptions and style discipline, ideal for iterating fast on client briefs or exploring variations before committing to a stencil.
howToUse: Load the Tattoo Generator workflow in ComfyUI and locate the key I/O nodes: PrimitiveStringMultiline (idea input), ComfySwitchNode (style), ResolutionSelector (size), PreviewAny, and SaveImage.

Enter your idea in PrimitiveStringMultiline. You can write plain text (e.g., "a raven with geometric accents") or a JSON string with fields (e.g., {"idea":"raven with geometric accents","style":"blackwork"}).
If you didn’t provide a style in JSON, choose one with ComfySwitchNode. The selected style is merged into the final prompt with StringConcatenate.
Pick an output size in ResolutionSelector. Use square for flash-style tiles, portrait for forearm/calf concepts, or landscape for bands and panels.
Queue/Run the workflow. The CustomCombo routes your prompt and resolution into the generator node (e46f5b18-9edb-4755-bec5-b38521684b4c), and PreviewAny shows the result as soon as it’s ready.
If you’re happy with the design, trigger SaveImage to export. Iterate by adjusting the idea text, switching styles, or trying alternate resolutions.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid style exploration: generate the same subject across blackwork, fine-line, geometric, or watercolor-inspired looks to compare directions.
Client pre-visualization: turn a short brief into several clean concept options during consultations.
Flash sheet development: batch-create cohesive tiles by fixing a style and resolution while varying the subject prompt.
Motif refinement: iterate on line density and detail by adjusting descriptive terms (e.g., "minimal linework, high contrast" vs. "ornamental, dotwork shading").

faqItems.question: Do I have to use JSON, or can I just type plain text?
faqItems.answer: Plain text works fine. If you do provide a JSON string, the JsonExtractString node can pull a specific field (e.g., "style") to help auto-assemble the prompt. Otherwise, set the style with the ComfySwitchNode.

faqItems.question: Which model does this workflow use, and can I change it?
faqItems.answer: The generation happens inside the CustomCombo and the generator node (ID e46f5b18-9edb-4755-bec5-b38521684b4c). If your setup exposes a model selector in that combo, you can swap it. Otherwise, replace the combo/generator with your preferred text-to-image node configured for tattoo-friendly outputs.

9394f9968da3.title: Wan Animate 2: Motion Transfer
9394f9968da3.description: Animate a still character using a driving video with Wan Animate 2, transferring motion directly from video frames without any pose extraction or skeleton preprocessing. The output preserves the reference character's identity while generating a fresh background and camera movement from your text prompt. Ideal for motion transfer, action mimicry, and character animation replacement projects.
9394f9968da3.metaDescription: Animate a still character with Wan Animate 2 by transferring motion from a driving video. Prompt controls background and camera. No pose extraction needed.
9394f9968da3.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates end-to-end motion transfer using Wan-Animate-2 (by Wan-Video/Alibaba): a single reference image (your character) is animated to follow the motion in a driving video, without any pose keypoint or skeleton extraction. The core of the graph is the "Motion Transfer (Wan Animate 2)" subgraph powered by custom Wan-Animate-2 nodes (UUIDs: 11706f8a-428d-4ef9-b24f-863f651c1b0b, 79280513-53b2-4417-93f8-f3e116bb6736, b798a87e-23ec-483d-ab9b-6af5b298d0ad). These nodes accept your reference image, the per-frame motion signal from the driving video, and a text prompt that guides background look and camera feel. Because motion is learned directly from frames, setup is fast and robust—no OpenPose or preprocessing passes.

LoadImage provides the character identity, while LoadVideo and GetVideoComponents extract the driving frames and fps. BatchImagesNode replicates the reference image so each video frame gets its own paired identity input. GetImageSize and ComfyMathExpression are used to keep resolution and aspect ratio consistent between inputs and outputs. PreviewAny lets you inspect intermediate frames, and CreateVideo + SaveVideo assemble the generated frames back into a video using the original fps. For longer clips, you manually duplicate the Motion Transfer subgraph (native looping support is pending upstream) and connect it in sequence so the pipeline can process the entire driving video.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then set your inputs: use LoadImage for the reference character and LoadVideo for the driving video. GetVideoComponents will extract frames and fps automatically.
Confirm output size and aspect. Use GetImageSize on the reference (or driver), then use ComfyMathExpression to set/scale width and height so the model and CreateVideo stay consistent.
Open the Motion Transfer (Wan Animate 2) subgraph and set your text prompt to describe background and camera mood. Keep prompts identity-safe (avoid describing a different character).
Run the first Motion Transfer subgraph. BatchImagesNode will duplicate the reference image to match the number of driving frames, and PreviewAny can be used to spot-check results.

If your driving video is longer than one pass supports: select the bypassed Motion Transfer subgraph above, press Ctrl+B to enable, update it so prompt/size match the first one, and link its image output to BatchImagesNode. Duplicate the subgraph with Ctrl+C then Ctrl+Shift+V as many times as needed to cover the full video.
Finally, feed the generated frames to CreateVideo, set fps from GetVideoComponents, and SaveVideo to write the final animation to disk.
suggestedUseCases: Character replacement: make a mascot or stylized avatar perform motions from a live-action reference.
Action mimicry: transfer dance, sports, or gesture performances onto your character for social clips.
Previsualization: quickly block animation for ads, cinematics, or mockups without rigging.
Educational content: demonstrate motion studies by applying the same movement to multiple characters.
Game/VTuber prototyping: iterate on character motion ideas directly from found footage.

faqItems.question: Do I need OpenPose or a skeleton extraction step?
faqItems.answer: No. Wan-Animate-2 performs direct motion transfer from the driving video frames. The workflow does not require keypoints or pose preprocessing.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the character identity consistent?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, well-lit reference image with minimal occlusion and a simple background. Keep the aspect ratio consistent, and avoid prompts that describe a different character or facial features that conflict with your reference.

faqItems.question: How do I match the timing and duration of the driving video?
faqItems.answer: GetVideoComponents provides fps for the driving clip—pass that to CreateVideo so playback matches the source timing. To retime, adjust the fps in CreateVideo (higher fps = faster playback, lower fps = slower).

faqItems.question: My clip is long. How do I process the whole video?
faqItems.answer: Native loop support is still under review. For now, duplicate the "Motion Transfer (Wan Animate 2)" subgraph: enable the bypassed copy (Ctrl+B), ensure its prompt and size match the first, connect its image output to BatchImagesNode, then copy-paste (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Shift+V) enough segments to cover the full driving video.

93c182d3aefb.title: LTX-2.5 (Pro): Text to Video

93c182d3aefb.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate cinematic text-to-video clips with LTX 2.5 using LtxApi25TextToVideo and SaveVideo, including native multi-shot scene support.
93c182d3aefb.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a text prompt into a finished video clip using the LTX 2.5 model via the LtxApi25TextToVideo node. Your prompt (and optional multi-shot structure) is sent to the LTX 2.5 API, which returns generated video content with sharp detail and coherent motion. The downstream SaveVideo node then writes the result to your ComfyUI output folder as a ready-to-share file.

Technically, the LtxApi25TextToVideo node is the core generator: it packages your prompt and settings, submits them to the remote LTX 2.5 service, and provides the resulting clip to the graph. LTX 2.5 supports native multi-shot scenes, making it possible to maintain character and style across cuts when you structure your prompt appropriately. The SaveVideo node handles final assembly and export, letting you choose a filename and frame rate while keeping the workflow simple and fast.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. Confirm you can see the LtxApi25TextToVideo node feeding into the SaveVideo node.

Open LtxApi25TextToVideo. Enter your text prompt. If your node version supports it, add multi-shot structure (e.g., separate shots in your prompt) to keep characters and style consistent across cuts. Add your API credentials or endpoint if required.

Optionally adjust any available generation settings in LtxApi25TextToVideo (for example, duration, aspect ratio, or randomness/seed if exposed). Use concise, visual language and consistent character descriptors for best results.
Open SaveVideo and set a clear filename or prefix and your desired FPS. Confirm the output directory is correct.
Queue the workflow and run it. The LtxApi25TextToVideo node will contact the LTX 2.5 service, generate the video, and pass it to SaveVideo for export.
Review the output video. Iterate by refining your prompt or node settings, then re-run. For multi-shot scenes, keep shot descriptions tight and reuse character and style cues to maintain continuity.
suggestedUseCases: Storyboards and animatics with multi-shot continuity for pre-production planning.
Product b-roll and short promotional clips with clear camera and motion cues.
Character-driven scenes that maintain look and style across quick cuts.
Social media teasers and mood pieces requiring fast turnaround.

faqItems.question: How do I create multi-shot scenes that keep characters consistent?
faqItems.answer: Structure your prompt as multiple shots with clear, consistent descriptors for characters, wardrobe, lighting, and style. If your node version exposes a multi-shot field or shot list, use it; otherwise, separate shots within the prompt text. Reuse the same character and style cues across shots.

faqItems.question: Can I control duration, resolution, or randomness?
faqItems.answer: Adjust whatever controls your LtxApi25TextToVideo node exposes. Some versions include parameters like duration, aspect ratio/resolution hints, and a seed or randomness setting. If a control is not visible, it may not be supported by your build or API plan.

faqItems.question: Where is the video saved and what format is it?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo writes the rendered clip to your ComfyUI output folder using the filename or prefix you set, at the FPS you choose. The exact container/codec depends on your SaveVideo configuration.

94ed41b87579.title: AI on the Lot 2026 - Z-Image Turbo - t2i + Upscale
94ed41b87579.description: The second workflow released for AI on the Lot 2026, made available for ComfyUI 101 workshop attendees to open and follow along if they choose. Same text-to-image setup using Z-Image Turbo, now with an upscale step added for higher resolution output.
94ed41b87579.metaDescription: Prompt to polished: text-to-image with built-in upscaling and side-by-side compare in ComfyUI. Generate, compare, and save high-quality results fast.
94ed41b87579.extendedDescription:
AI on the Lot 2026 - Z-Image Turbo - t2i + Upscale is a streamlined ComfyUI workflow that takes you from a text prompt to a polished, high-resolution image in one pass. It centers on a custom text-to-image node (Z-Image Turbo; UUID f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1) to generate the initial image and then routes the output through an integrated upscale stage for added detail and clarity. The SaveImage node captures your outputs to disk, while the ImageCompare node produces a side-by-side composite so you can visually judge how much quality the upscale added—and whether any artifacts were introduced.

Technically, the workflow chains a T2I generation step into an upscaling step, minimizing manual wiring and keeping your iteration loop tight. You enter your prompt (and optional negative prompt) in the Z-Image Turbo node, adjust core generation controls like seed, steps, and guidance (as exposed by the node), and set your target resolution or scale factor for the upscale stage. The ImageCompare node receives both the base and upscaled images to output a comparison image, and SaveImage records each stage with consistent filenames for easy A/B review. Because the T2I node accepts whichever checkpoint you load in your ComfyUI environment, you can pair this workflow with your preferred model without changing the graph.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON into ComfyUI (Drag-and-drop the file onto the canvas or use the ComfyUI Manager to import).

Open the Z-Image Turbo node (UUID f2fdebf6-dfaf-43b6-9eb2-7f70613cfdc1) and enter your prompt and, if available, a negative prompt. Set seed, steps, and guidance to taste. If the node exposes model/vae inputs, point them to your preferred checkpoint.
Set your output size or upscale factor within the same node (or its connected upscale controls). Start with a modest scale (e.g., 2x) for clean detail without oversharpening.
Click Queue Prompt (or run) to execute the T2I stage followed by the upscale stage. The ImageCompare node will generate a side-by-side composite of the base vs. upscaled result.
Review the comparison image to check detail retention and artifacts. Tweak prompts, seed, steps, guidance, or upscale factor as needed and re-run.
When satisfied, let the SaveImage node write both the base and upscaled outputs to disk. Optionally edit the filename prefix in SaveImage to keep your versions organized.
suggestedUseCases: Upscaling concept art or mood boards from quick prompts to presentation-ready images.
Creating higher-resolution product mockups or pack shots directly from text prompts.
Generating social media graphics that need crisp edges and readable text after upscaling.
Storyboards and previsualization where you iterate fast at low res, then upscale the best frames.
Thumbnail and banner creation with built-in A/B comparison to ensure clarity at target sizes.

faqItems.question: Which models does this workflow use for text-to-image?
faqItems.answer: The workflow does not bundle a specific model. The Z-Image Turbo node uses whichever checkpoint you load in your ComfyUI environment (as exposed by that node). Point it to your preferred base model and VAE, and the rest of the graph will work unchanged.

faqItems.question: How do I control the upscale amount and avoid over-sharpening?
faqItems.answer: Use the upscale factor or strength controls attached to the Z-Image Turbo/upscale stage. Start at 2x and increase only if needed. If edges look crunchy, reduce the upscale factor, lower the sharpening/strength (if available), or slightly increase generation steps for a cleaner base before upscaling.

faqItems.question: What is ImageCompare showing me?
faqItems.answer: ImageCompare creates a side-by-side composite of the base (pre-upscale) image and the upscaled image. Use it to check detail gains and spot artifacts. If you don’t see the comparison, confirm both image outputs are connected to ImageCompare’s inputs before running.

faqItems.question: How can I reproduce a result later?
faqItems.answer: Set and record a fixed seed in the Z-Image Turbo node and keep your prompt, steps, guidance, and upscale settings unchanged. SaveImage will write files with consistent naming; keeping the same seed and parameters will yield repeatable outputs with the same model and node settings.

9654558acd06.title: Kling O1: Text to Video

This ComfyUI workflow turns plain-language prompts into short videos using the Kling O1 model. At its core is the KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode, which sends your prompt to the Kling service and receives a generated clip. The SaveVideo node consumes that output and saves it to a file, where you can control basics like output path and frame rate. For best results, write prompts that clearly define the subject, action, setting, and camera behavior (for example: "wide shot, slow dolly-in, golden-hour lighting"). Keep durations and resolutions within the node’s supported ranges to reduce errors and queue times. If the node exposes a seed, fix it to make variations more reproducible.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON into ComfyUI. Install the Kling node package if prompted, then open the KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode and configure its API credentials (e.g., API key/endpoint) as required by the node.

Queue and run the workflow. The Kling node will submit the request to the service and return the generated clip when ready. Monitor ComfyUI’s console/log for progress or errors.
Review the saved video, then iterate: keep the seed fixed for controlled changes, tweak the prompt and timing, and adjust size/fps to balance fidelity, motion smoothness, and generation time.

Previsualization for motion, lighting, or composition before full production.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use this workflow?

faqItems.question: What resolutions and durations are supported?
faqItems.answer: Limits depend on the Kling O1 service and the node’s implementation. Use the options exposed by KlingOmniProTextToVideoNode and stay within the recommended ranges shown in the node’s UI or documentation to avoid errors or long queue times.

faqItems.question: How can I get smoother motion and fewer artifacts?

977fefa2b934.title: Image → Song → Audio-Reactive Video
977fefa2b934.description: Create songs with ACE Step 1.5 XL and audio-reactive videos with LTX 2.3 and the Audio-Reactive LoRA.
977fefa2b934.metaDescription: Create a song with ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo and turn one image into an audio‑reactive video using LTX 2.3 + Audio‑Reactive LoRA in ComfyUI.
977fefa2b934.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a single image into a music-backed, audio‑reactive video by combining text-to-music generation (ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo) with image-to-video animation (LTX 2.3) enhanced by an Audio‑Reactive LoRA. You provide one image and a short creative brief; the workflow uses a GeminiNode to draft both "style tags" for the visuals and "lyrics" for the song in one pass. A RegexExtract node then splits that text at '---': everything before becomes visual style tags for LTX 2.3, and everything after becomes lyrics fed to ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo. The generated song is saved via SaveAudioMP3 and then drives the reactivity of the video, which is saved with SaveVideo.

Technically, the pipeline is organized into groups: Load Image, Create ACE Step 1.5 Prompts, Create Audio‑Reactive LoRA Prompt, Regex Extract, ACE Step 1.5 XL, and LTX 2.3 with Audio‑Reactive LoRA. The Audio‑Reactive LoRA (see the linked model card) adds motion effects that follow the music; adjust its strength between 1.0 and 2.0 (1.4+ for stronger effects) for best results. PreviewAny helps you check intermediate outputs (prompts, audio, and frames) before final render, while MarkdownNote contains quick tips inside the graph. The result is a streamlined image → song → audio‑reactive video pipeline that’s easy to iterate: tweak style tags and lyrics, re‑generate the track, and re‑render the video until it matches your creative intent.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote group for quick pointers.
Add your source image to the LoadImage node (single image works best).
In the GeminiNode, enter a brief describing visual style and lyrics. Ensure the output is split by '---' with style tags before and lyrics after (you can also paste your own text in that format).
Run the prompt nodes. The RegexExtract group will route everything before '---' to the LTX 2.3 style prompt and everything after '---' to ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo as lyrics.
Generate the song with the ACE Step 1.5 XL group and confirm SaveAudioMP3 is writing the file where you expect. PreviewAny can help you check the audio and prompts.
Set the Audio‑Reactive LoRA strength (1.0–2.0; try 1.4+ for stronger motion), then run the LTX 2.3 group to animate your image. Finally, render with SaveVideo and review the result in PreviewAny.
suggestedUseCases: Turn fan art or album art into a lyric video with motion synced to a freshly generated song.
Create short, reactive social media loops from a product or poster image paired with a custom jingle.
Make podcast or stream intro videos from a cover image with audio‑driven motion.
Generate mood pieces: ambient track + subtle, style‑driven camera movement from a single still.
Rapid concept reels: iterate lyrics and style tags to explore look-and-sound directions quickly.

faqItems.question: How does the '---' split work and why is it needed?
faqItems.answer: The RegexExtract node captures everything before '---' as style tags for LTX 2.3 and everything after as lyrics for ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo. This guarantees each model receives a purpose‑built prompt from a single GeminiNode output.

faqItems.question: How do I control how reactive the motion is?
faqItems.answer: Use the Audio‑Reactive LoRA strength in the LTX 2.3 group. A range of 1.0–2.0 is recommended; try ~1.4 or higher for stronger effects. More dynamic audio (clear percussion, drops, and swells) will also produce more noticeable motion.

faqItems.question: Can I use my own audio instead of generating with ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Replace or bypass the ACE branch and feed your audio into the LTX 2.3 + Audio‑Reactive LoRA input path (use a compatible audio loader node in ComfyUI). Ensure the video duration matches your track length.

faqItems.question: Any tips for better visual results?
faqItems.answer: Start with a clean, high‑quality image; keep style tags concise and specific; use reasonable resolutions your GPU can handle; and iterate: adjust style tags, LoRA strength, and re‑render. PreviewAny helps validate prompts and frames before the final save.

9851c174a194.title: ACE-Step 1.5XL Turbo: Text to Music
9851c174a194.description: Generate high-quality music from text prompts using the distilled 4B ACE-Step model. Produces commercial-ready audio in just 8 inference steps without CFG.
9851c174a194.metaDescription: Text-to-music in ComfyUI with ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo: encode prompts, sample in 8 steps without CFG, decode to audio, and export MP3 fast.
9851c174a194.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a plain-language text prompt into finished music using the ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo model. Your prompt is encoded by TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 (backed by DualCLIPLoader) into audio-aware conditioning. EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio creates a blank latent audio canvas at your chosen length, and UNETLoader loads the distilled 4B ACE-Step checkpoint (acestep_v1.5_xl_turbo_bf16.safetensors). ModelSamplingAuraFlow configures the sampler schedule tuned for ACE-Step, and KSampler performs just 8 diffusion steps to synthesize the latent audio. The audio is then reconstructed with VAELoader + VAEDecodeAudio and saved via SaveAudioMP3.

What makes this workflow practical is its “turbo” configuration: no classifier-free guidance (CFG) is used, enabled by ConditioningZeroOut feeding an intentionally empty negative conditioning. This keeps prompts straightforward (focus only on what you want), while ModelSamplingAuraFlow and KSampler deliver fast, stable results. The graph is organized into Model and Prompt groups for clarity, and uses PrimitiveInt/PrimitiveNode for quick edits to seed, steps, and duration. The result is a tight, teachable text-to-music pipeline you can run repeatedly for variations or integrate as a reusable subgraph.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and install any missing custom nodes required by the listed node types. Keep the Model and Prompt groups expanded for clarity.

Download acestep_v1.5_xl_turbo_bf16.safetensors and place it in ComfyUI/models/diffusion (or your configured diffusion_models folder). In the Model group, confirm UNETLoader points to this file. Ensure VAELoader and DualCLIPLoader are connected.

In the Prompt group, enter your music description in TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 (e.g., "warm lo‑fi hip‑hop beat, mellow Rhodes, 85 BPM, vinyl crackle, relaxed mood"). Leave negative prompt handling as-is—ConditioningZeroOut disables CFG on purpose.

Set duration in EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio (choose the seconds/samples field provided by the node). Use PrimitiveInt/PrimitiveNode to set seed and confirm KSampler steps are 8. ModelSamplingAuraFlow should be connected to KSampler.
Click Queue/Execute. KSampler will generate the audio latents in ~8 steps, VAEDecodeAudio will reconstruct the waveform, and SaveAudioMP3 will write the result to disk.

Review the output. For new variations, change the seed; for stronger adherence, refine the prompt with genre, instruments, tempo, and production terms. If needed, slightly adjust steps (e.g., 8–12) while keeping CFG disabled.
suggestedUseCases: Quickly producing background beds for social videos, reels, and shorts from concise prompts.
Drafting podcast intros/outros or stingers with consistent style and length.
Creating prototype game loops and ambient soundscapes during early design phases.
Generating ad/jingle ideas for client pitches where fast iteration matters.
Stock music variations for content libraries with prompt-based tagging.

faqItems.question: Why is CFG disabled, and can I use negative prompts?
faqItems.answer: This workflow intentionally disables classifier-free guidance using ConditioningZeroOut for fast, stable sampling. Negative prompts are ignored in this setup. If you need negatives, replace ConditioningZeroOut with an explicit negative encoder path and enable CFG in KSampler—but that changes the workflow’s behavior.

faqItems.question: How do I control duration and structure (e.g., 10–30 seconds)?
faqItems.answer: Set the length in EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio (seconds or samples, depending on the node’s fields). The model interprets structure via text (e.g., “16‑bar trap loop,” “slow build and soft drop”). For longer pieces, generate multiple segments and arrange them in a DAW.

faqItems.question: What sampler settings should I use for best results?
faqItems.answer: Keep KSampler at 8 steps with ModelSamplingAuraFlow connected—this is tuned for ACE-Step 1.5 XL Turbo. If you hear artifacts, try modest increases (e.g., 10–12 steps). Maintain CFG disabled to match the workflow’s design.

faqItems.question: What format does it export, and can I change it?

99aec65eea89.title: MelBandRoFormer Audio Separation
99aec65eea89.description: Load an audio file and separate it into vocal and instrumental stems using the MelBandRoFormer model. Outputs two MP3 files for isolated vocals and background music.
99aec65eea89.metaDescription: Isolate vocals and instrumentals from any track in ComfyUI using MelBandRoFormer. Load audio, separate stems, and export two MP3 files fast and clean.
99aec65eea89.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow performs high-quality voice isolation using the MelBandRoFormer model. It takes a single mixed audio track and separates it into two stems: isolated vocals and instrumental accompaniment. The pipeline starts with LoadAudio to ingest your source file, then MelBandRoFormerModelLoader loads the pretrained weights (MelBandRoformer_fp16.safetensors) from models/diffusion_models. The core separation happens in MelBandRoFormerSampler, which runs inference and outputs two audio tensors—one for vocals and one for background music—ready for export via paired SaveAudioMP3 nodes.

Technically, MelBandRoFormer applies a transformer-based architecture that operates in band-split, time–frequency space to estimate source components. In practice, that means it learns masks that suppress accompaniment when extracting vocals and vice versa, yielding cleaner stems with fewer musical artifacts. The included MarkdownNote provides inline guidance inside the canvas. Because the workflow is node-driven, you can easily swap SaveAudioMP3 for a WAV saver, change output filenames, or tweak Sampler options like chunking/overlap (if exposed by your node version) to balance speed, memory use, and separation quality.
howToUse: Install the custom node: Add ComfyUI-MelBandRoFormer to ComfyUI/custom_nodes and restart ComfyUI.
Place the model file: Copy MelBandRoformer_fp16.safetensors into ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/.
Load the workflow: Open the MelBandRoFormer Audio Separation workflow JSON in ComfyUI.
Select your input: In the LoadAudio node, browse to your song, podcast, or clip.
Load the model: In MelBandRoFormerModelLoader, confirm the path to MelBandRoformer_fp16.safetensors.
Run separation: Execute the graph. The MelBandRoFormerSampler outputs vocals and instrumental to two SaveAudioMP3 nodes, which write the respective MP3 files to your output folder.
suggestedUseCases: Create karaoke or backing tracks by removing vocals from songs.
Extract clean acapellas for remixes, mashups, or sampling.
Podcast post-production: separate speech from background music for independent leveling and noise control.

faqItems.question: What audio formats can I load and save?

faqItems.question: The stems have some bleed or artifacts. How can I improve quality?
faqItems.answer: Try increasing overlap or adjusting chunk size in MelBandRoFormerSampler if those controls are exposed by your node version. Also ensure the input isn’t clipped and avoid overly compressed masters when possible. For final polish, apply light noise gating or spectral denoising to the vocal stem.

faqItems.question: Can this separate more than two stems (e.g., drums, bass, other)?

9bd4bdaa49c0.title: Qwen3.0: Text Generation

9bd4bdaa49c0.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow for Qwen3-4B-Thinking text generation. Load the model, set decoding params, and generate detailed, reasoned responses in PreviewAny.
9bd4bdaa49c0.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns Qwen 3.0 (4B, Thinking variant) into a drop-in text generator you can run inside a node graph. It loads the Qwen3-4B-Thinking weights with CLIPLoader, feeds your prompt and decoding settings to TextGenerate, and displays the final text in PreviewAny for quick copy-out. A MarkdownNote node is included in the graph with usage tips so you can remember the key parameters at a glance.

Under the hood, TextGenerate performs standard autoregressive decoding with adjustable parameters like temperature, top_p, and max new tokens. CLIPLoader is used here to point ComfyUI at the Qwen 3.0 text encoder weights (qwen_3_4b.safetensors) stored in models/text_encoders. The result is a compact, reproducible setup for generating detailed, reasoned responses, ideal for drafting explanations, outlining ideas, and iterating on prompt engineering directly in ComfyUI. As of 2026/03, ComfyUI supports the 4B Qwen 3.0 model for this workflow.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then locate the MarkdownNote for a quick parameter overview.
Download qwen_3_4b.safetensors and place it in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders. In the CLIPLoader node, select this file so the model loads without errors.
Open the TextGenerate node and enter your prompt. Optionally add a system or style instruction at the top of the prompt to steer tone and structure.
Set decoding parameters: start with temperature 0.2–0.7, top_p around 0.9, and choose a max new tokens value large enough for your expected answer length.
Click Queue/Execute. When generation completes, the output text will appear in the PreviewAny node. Copy the result from the preview panel.
Iterate for quality: lower temperature for precision, raise it for creativity; increase max new tokens for longer answers; add explicit formatting instructions (e.g., bullets) to improve structure.

faqItems.question: How do I control response style, length, and creativity?

faqItems.question: The output stops mid-sentence. What should I change?

9be3d7110c75.title: SAM3 - Remove Background via Prompt
9be3d7110c75.description: Isolate any subject from an image using a text prompt — just type what you want to keep (e.g. `character`, `dog`, `car`) and the workflow cuts it out and saves it as a PNG with a transparent background.
9be3d7110c75.metaDescription: Cut out subjects from images via text prompt in ComfyUI. Use SAM3Segment to create clean PNGs with transparent backgrounds—fast, simple, and precise.
9be3d7110c75.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow isolates a subject from any image using a simple text prompt and exports a PNG with a transparent background. It links a LoadImage node to a SAM3Segment node, then into SaveImage. You type what you want to keep (for example, "character", "dog", or "red car"), and the SAM3Segment node generates a precise foreground mask and applies it as an alpha channel so everything else becomes transparent.

Technically, SAM3Segment performs prompt-aware segmentation over the input image, producing a binary mask for regions that best match the prompt. That mask is composited with the original RGB to produce an RGBA cutout. Because the node is designed to work well out of the box, most settings can remain at their defaults. The included MarkdownNote provides a quick reminder of the two essentials: connect an image and provide a clear prompt. SaveImage then writes the final cutout as a PNG, preserving transparency for downstream compositing in design, video, or web workflows.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the nodes: LoadImage → SAM3Segment → SaveImage (plus a MarkdownNote with tips).
In LoadImage, pick your source image. Use the highest-resolution version you have for cleaner edges.
Select the SAM3Segment node and enter a concise prompt describing the subject you want to keep (e.g., "dog", "blue sneaker", "sports car").
Leave other SAM3Segment settings at defaults unless you have a specific reason to change them; the node is tuned for general use.
Run the workflow. Inspect the viewer (if connected) or proceed directly to the SaveImage output to confirm the cutout.
In SaveImage, set an output folder and run. The result is a PNG with transparency where non-matching regions have been removed.

Character isolation for thumbnails and social banners without manual masking.
Quick compositing in design tools by exporting ready-to-place transparent PNGs.
Prepping assets for video overlays or motion graphics where alpha channels are required.

faqItems.question: How do I improve edge quality or fine details like hair or fur?

faqItems.question: Can it isolate multiple instances of the same object?
faqItems.answer: It may select multiple instances if they all match the prompt, but results depend on the image. If you only want one instance, refine the prompt with distinguishing attributes (e.g., "front red car" vs. "cars") or run on a cropped version containing just the target subject.

faqItems.question: What format is the output and does it include transparency?
faqItems.answer: The SaveImage node writes a PNG with an alpha channel. The background becomes transparent wherever the prompt-based mask excludes the image.
