a262dd6de9ce.title: Seedream 5.0 Pro: Text to Image
a262dd6de9ce.description: Generate images from text prompts using Seedream 5.0 Pro, producing one high-quality output. Ideal for creative concept art, marketing visual mockups, and rapid ideation for design projects.
a262dd6de9ce.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate a single high-quality image from text with ByteDance Seedream 5.0 Pro using ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 and SaveImageAdvanced.
a262dd6de9ce.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns your text prompt into a single, high-quality image using ByteDance’s Seedream 5.0 Pro model, wrapped by the ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2. You type your prompt, optionally set a seed and resolution, and the node makes an API call to Seedream 5.0 Pro to generate one image. The result is then passed to SaveImageAdvanced, which writes the output to disk with your chosen filename pattern and folder.

Technically, ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 handles prompt text and common generation controls such as seed (for reproducibility) and image size (width/height supported by the API). Many versions of this node also expose guidance (CFG) and steps; if available in your build, you can fine-tune detail and prompt adherence. The node returns the generated image tensor, which SaveImageAdvanced persists according to your output directory and naming settings. This design keeps the graph minimal and focused: one model call for a clean, single-image result, ideal for fast iteration on concept art, mockups, and design ideation.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and ensure the ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 custom node is installed. If not, install it (e.g., via ComfyUI Manager) and restart ComfyUI.
Open ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 and add your Seedream/ByteDance API key. Use the node’s API key field or an environment/config method if your installation supports it.

Enter your text prompt. Optionally set a negative prompt (if exposed in your node version), choose a fixed seed for reproducible results, and select a supported width/height. If the node exposes guidance (CFG) or steps, start with moderate values and adjust as needed.
Configure SaveImageAdvanced: set the output directory and a filename prefix (for example, include the project name or seed).
Click Queue/Run. Preview the generated image in ComfyUI and find the saved file in your configured output folder.
Iterate: refine the prompt, tweak seed and resolution, and re-run. For variations, change the seed; to keep a look, reuse the same seed and adjust wording subtly.
suggestedUseCases: Creative concept art and moodboards for films, games, and branding
Marketing visual mockups and campaign ideation
Rapid product ideation and hero image drafts
Social media visuals that need quick, on-brief imagery

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Enter your ByteDance/Seedream API key in the node’s API key field or configure it via environment variables if your installation supports that. Without a valid key, the node cannot call the Seedream 5.0 Pro API.

faqItems.question: How do I get consistent, repeatable results?
faqItems.answer: Set a fixed seed in ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2. Using the same prompt, resolution, and parameters with the same seed will produce consistent results, subject to any upstream API changes.

faqItems.question: What image sizes are supported?
faqItems.answer: Use width/height values supported by the Seedream 5.0 Pro API (often specific multiples). If a size isn’t accepted, try common square values like 1024×1024 or consult the node/API documentation for allowed dimensions.

faqItems.question: Can I generate multiple images at once?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is set up for a single high-quality output. If your ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 build supports a batch or count parameter, you can increase it. Otherwise, duplicate the node or re-run with different seeds for variations.

a335e0968d76.title: Music Generator
a335e0968d76.description: This app uses Stable Audio 3 to generate full music tracks, instruments, SFX or one shots.
a335e0968d76.metaDescription: Generate stereo music, instruments, SFX, and one-shots from text using a Stable Audio 3 ComfyUI workflow with duration control and advanced saving.
a335e0968d76.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns short text ideas into stereo audio using Stable Audio 3. At its core is a Stable Audio 3 generator node (UUID: 8b66c757-fe2f-4184-91f3-479a19deb565) that accepts a prompt and timing controls to synthesize full tracks, instrument phrases, sound effects, or one‑shot samples. A PrimitiveFloat node provides precise numeric control (for example, duration in seconds), and SaveAudioAdvanced writes the resulting waveform to disk with your chosen name and location. A MarkdownNote in the graph offers quick, in‑workflow tips.

Technically, your prompt and numeric parameters flow into the Stable Audio 3 node, which renders a stereo waveform guided by style, instrumentation, mood, and length cues in your text. The output plugs directly into SaveAudioAdvanced so you can batch or iteratively export results. This setup is useful for fast ideation and production: short durations (e.g., 0.5–2 s) are great for one‑shots, a few seconds for SFX, and longer spans for music beds—all without leaving ComfyUI.
howToUse: Load the Music Generator workflow JSON in ComfyUI and confirm all nodes are green (loaded).
Open the MarkdownNote in the graph for a quick overview and any author tips.

In the Stable Audio 3 node (UUID: 8b66c757-fe2f-4184-91f3-479a19deb565), enter a concise text prompt that names genre, instruments, mood/energy, and any key descriptors (e.g., "uplifting synthwave, analog bass, punchy drums, 100 BPM feel").

Set the desired duration using the connected PrimitiveFloat node (for example, 0.8 for a one‑shot, 3–5 for SFX, 15–60 for music beds). Adjust any additional controls exposed by the Stable Audio 3 node as needed.
Configure SaveAudioAdvanced to choose the output folder and filename pattern. Enable auto‑save if you want files written without manual intervention.
Click Queue Prompt. When the run completes, listen to the saved file. Iterate by refining the prompt or duration to hone style, tightness, or impact.
suggestedUseCases: Quick background music beds for videos or streams from a plain‑language prompt.
Game and film SFX prototyping (impacts, whooshes, ambience) generated on demand.
Instrument riffs, motifs, and loops for songwriting or beatmaking inspiration.
One‑shot samples (kicks, snares, hits, stingers) to load into a sampler or DAW.
Podcast and content branding (intros, outros, transitions) tailored by mood.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key or special model files?
faqItems.answer: That depends on your Stable Audio 3 node setup. Some installs call a cloud API (you’ll need to add an API key in the node or environment), while others may use a locally available model or backend. Check the node’s settings and your ComfyUI console for credential or model path prompts.

faqItems.question: How long can the audio be?
faqItems.answer: Use the PrimitiveFloat to set duration. Practical maximums depend on the Stable Audio 3 backend and your hardware or API limits. Longer durations take more time and resources; start short (e.g., 5–15 s) and increase as needed.

faqItems.question: What format and quality does it save?
faqItems.answer: The workflow produces stereo audio from Stable Audio 3 and passes it to SaveAudioAdvanced, which writes the file to disk. Check the SaveAudioAdvanced node’s options and the saved file’s metadata in your OS or DAW to confirm format and quality settings available in your setup.

faqItems.question: How do I get more consistent results or controlled variations?
faqItems.answer: Keep prompts consistent in style, instrumentation, and mood terms. If the Stable Audio 3 node exposes a seed or variation parameter, fix the seed for repeatability or change it to explore variations. Small, targeted prompt edits (e.g., "add muted guitar" or "lower reverb") help guide iterative refinement.

a39b591d8c3b.title: Qwen Image Layer Decomp for Illustration v1
a39b591d8c3b.description: Workflow example for using Qwen Image layer decomposition tools to help separate layers in a scene.
a39b591d8c3b.metaDescription: Tutorial workflow for Qwen-based image layer decomposition in ComfyUI. Separate an illustration into clean layers and masks for compositing or editing.
a39b591d8c3b.extendedDescription:
Qwen Image Layer Decomp for Illustration v1 is a guided layer-separation workflow for turning a flat illustration into editable layers and masks. It routes a loaded image through ImageScaleToMaxDimension to a recommended working size (640 px for speed, 1024 px for detail), then drives a custom Qwen-based decomposition stage that predicts per-element mattes you can save as PNGs. A PrimitiveStringMultiline node provides an optional, high-level text prompt so you can nudge the model toward the objects you want isolated (for example: "character, foreground props, midground buildings, sky").

Technically, the core is implemented with two custom nodes (f754a936-daaf-4b6e-9658-41fdc54d301d and 1ea4fa01-a81b-4420-a03c-f60019e69a92). The first performs the Qwen image layer decomposition using diffusion-style sampling controls (the author’s baseline is 50 steps, CFG 4.0), trading runtime for mask quality. The second is used for selection/refinement of the predicted layers (cleaning edges or exporting specific passes). LoadImage and SaveImage handle I/O, while MarkdownNote contains on-canvas guidance and links. The result is a practical, prompt-guided layer extraction pipeline that’s ideal for compositing, recoloring, and 2.5D motion work.
howToUse: Update ComfyUI to the latest version and ensure the required Qwen decomposition custom nodes and model files are installed (follow the node’s README). Open the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote for any prerequisites.
Load your source artwork with LoadImage. Set ImageScaleToMaxDimension to 640 for faster iteration or 1024 for higher-fidelity edges while keeping aspect ratio intact.

In PrimitiveStringMultiline, enter an optional prompt describing the scene and desired layers (e.g., "main character, sword, foreground flowers, background sky"). You can leave it empty to run with the node’s defaults.

Open the custom decomposition node (ID: f754a936-daaf-4b6e-9658-41fdc54d301d) and start with the provided sampler settings: Steps = 50, CFG = 4.0. Increase steps for cleaner mattes; decrease for speed. Then run the graph.

Inspect the outputs. If edges look soft or bleed into neighbors, try a higher input size (1024) or a few more steps. If halos appear, slightly lower CFG. Use the refinement/selection node (ID: 1ea4fa01-a81b-4420-a03c-f60019e69a92) to pick specific layers or clean transitions.
Save per-layer images or masks via the connected SaveImage nodes. For compositing, prefer PNG with alpha. Iterate on the prompt (naming the elements you care about) to improve the separation.
suggestedUseCases: Isolating characters and props from illustrated scenes for recoloring, relighting, or texture edits.
Preparing clean foreground/midground/background passes for parallax and 2.5D motion graphics.
Separating UI/mockup elements from flat renders to quickly iterate on layout and styling.
Extracting objects from concept art to build reusable asset libraries for game or film previz.
Creating precise masks for targeted inpainting or localized image-to-image edits.

faqItems.question: What models or files do I need, and where do they go?
faqItems.answer: This workflow relies on custom Qwen image layer decomposition nodes. Install the node repo as instructed by its README and place the required model weights in the paths it specifies (typically under ComfyUI/models or a subfolder the node creates). Then restart ComfyUI so the nodes detect the weights.

faqItems.question: It feels slow—how can I speed it up?
faqItems.answer: Reduce Steps (e.g., from 50 to 30–40), lower the working size to 640 px in ImageScaleToMaxDimension, and keep CFG around 3.5–4.0. These changes noticeably cut runtime with modest quality tradeoffs. For the final pass, switch back to 1024 px and a few more steps.

faqItems.question: Do I have to write a prompt?
faqItems.answer: No—the PrimitiveStringMultiline prompt is optional. However, short, concrete descriptions of the elements you want (e.g., "character, cape, sword, sky") often produce more accurate and neatly separated layers than running with defaults.

faqItems.question: How do I get crisper edges and fewer halos?
faqItems.answer: Use a larger input (1024 px), increase Steps slightly (e.g., +10), and avoid very high CFG values. After decomposition, use the refinement/selection node to clean transitions. If needed, lightly feather or contract the mask in your compositor for final polish.

a3e50e79cb89.title: Hunyuan Video 1.5 Text to Video
a3e50e79cb89.description: Generate high-quality 720p videos from text prompts with cinematic camera control, emotional expressions, and physics simulation. Supports multiple styles including realistic, anime, and 3D with text rendering.
a3e50e79cb89.metaDescription: Text-to-video with Hunyuan Video 1.5 in ComfyUI. Generate 720p clips from prompts, with optional 1080p upscaling, camera control, and super-resolution.
a3e50e79cb89.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns text prompts into coherent 720p videos using the Hunyuan Video 1.5 model, with optional 1080p upscaling and super-resolution. It’s organized into clear groups: Step 1 - Load models, Step 3 - Prompt, Step 4 - Video Size, Custom Sampler, and an optional Video Upscale 1080P (Ctrl-B to enable). The pipeline loads Hunyuan’s text encoders with DualCLIPLoader and encodes your prompt via CLIPTextEncode. EmptyHunyuanVideo15Latent defines the temporal canvas (resolution, frame count, FPS), while RandomNoise sets the seed. UNETLoader brings in the Hunyuan Video 1.5 UNet, and SamplerCustomAdvanced (driven by KSamplerSelect, BasicScheduler, and CFGGuider) performs diffusion steps to synthesize video latents at 720p. VAELoader plus VAEDecode (or VAEDecodeTiled for memory efficiency) converts latents to frames, which CreateVideo stitches into a final clip, saved with SaveVideo.

For higher fidelity, the workflow includes a latent-space upscaling path. LatentUpscaleModelLoader and HunyuanVideo15LatentUpscaleWithModel can boost resolution before decoding, and HunyuanVideo15SuperResolution refines details after generation. EasyCache is available to accelerate repeated runs by caching encodings, at the cost of some visual quality. The default step count is set to 20 for reasonable render times; increasing steps (e.g., toward the Hunyuan team’s original settings) improves detail but extends inference time. If you encounter VRAM limits, set weight_dtype to fp8_e4n3fn and switch to VAEDecodeTiled.
howToUse: Load the template in ComfyUI and ensure the required Hunyuan Video 1.5 weights and text encoders are downloaded. In Step 1 - Load models, point VAELoader, DualCLIPLoader, and UNETLoader to the correct files. If VRAM is low, set weight_dtype to fp8_e4n3fn.

Open Step 3 - Prompt and enter a detailed prompt describing subject, style, and camera moves (e.g., “low-angle dolly shot, shallow depth of field, cinematic lighting”). If a negative prompt path exists in your template, fill it to suppress unwanted artifacts.
Go to Step 4 - Video Size. Set width/height for 720p (e.g., 1280x720), choose frames and FPS (e.g., 48–96 frames at 16–24 fps for 2–6s clips). Set a seed in RandomNoise for reproducibility.

In Custom Sampler, keep 20 steps for faster drafts or raise to 30–50 for higher quality. Adjust CFGGuider (e.g., 3–7) to balance prompt adherence vs. naturalness. Leave KSamplerSelect and BasicScheduler at their defaults unless you’re experimenting.

Run the base path to produce a 720p video. The UNet sampling will output latents, VAEDecode (or VAEDecodeTiled) will convert to frames, CreateVideo will assemble them, and SaveVideo will write the file.

Optional: Enable Video Upscale 1080P (Ctrl-B). Load a latent upscaler in LatentUpscaleModelLoader, run HunyuanVideo15LatentUpscaleWithModel, then HunyuanVideo15SuperResolution for extra sharpness. Use VAEDecodeTiled if decoding becomes slow or memory-heavy.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic concept previews for film or advertising with controllable camera motions.
Stylized shorts (realistic, anime, or 3D look) for social media or motion moodboards.
Product hero shots and explainer clips with guided camera paths and text rendering.
Educational micro-simulations and physics-inspired sequences (e.g., falling, gliding, collisions).
Animatics and previsualization where timing, framing, and movement need quick iteration.

faqItems.question: How can I improve quality without huge render times?
faqItems.answer: Start at 20 steps for drafts. For finals, raise to 30–40 steps, keep 720p base resolution, and enable HunyuanVideo15SuperResolution. If you need 1080p, use the latent upscaler path but expect longer runtimes.

faqItems.question: I get OOM errors or black frames. What should I change?
faqItems.answer: Lower width/height and/or frame count, set weight_dtype to fp8_e4n3fn, switch to VAEDecodeTiled, and disable the 1080p upscaler group. Close other GPU apps and reduce CFG or steps if needed.

faqItems.question: How do I control camera movements and emotion in the video?
faqItems.answer: Describe shots explicitly in the prompt (e.g., “handheld close-up, slow push-in, rack focus, emotional smile”). Mention lens and lighting cues (“35mm, golden hour, volumetric light”). Keep sentences concise and avoid conflicting directives.

faqItems.question: What does EasyCache do, and when should I use it?
faqItems.answer: EasyCache stores intermediate encodings to speed up iterations (useful when only small prompt tweaks change). It trades some visual fidelity for speed; use it for look development, then disable for final renders.

faqItems.question: What is multi-reference consistency?

faqItems.question: Why use quantized weights in this workflow?

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the best results from this workflow?

a4e8aec9d618.title: Wan2.7: Image to Video
a4e8aec9d618.description: Upload an image and audio file to generate a video with synchronized sound, using the first and last frames for control.
a4e8aec9d618.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Convert image(s) and audio into a synchronized video using Wan2.7 with first/last frame control for guided motion.
a4e8aec9d618.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow shows you how to turn a still image (or a pair of start/end images) and an audio track into a coherent video with sound using Wan2.7. The core is the Wan2ImageToVideoApi node, which takes your reference image(s) and audio, then synthesizes the in-between frames so the video begins on your first frame, transitions naturally, and lands on your last frame. LoadImage nodes feed the first and last control frames, while SaveVideo writes the final output to disk.

Technically, the first and last frames act as strong compositional anchors: Wan2.7 preserves the subject and layout at those endpoints and generates motion between them. The audio you provide is used to align timing and pacing so the video duration matches the track and motion evolves in sync. Keep your start and end images aligned in aspect ratio and subject framing for cleaner transitions. The SaveVideo node then packages the generated frames (and the synchronized audio from the API) into a playable video file.
howToUse: Open ComfyUI and load the "Wan2.7: Image to Video" workflow.
On the first LoadImage node, choose your starting reference image (this will be the first frame).
Optionally set a second LoadImage node as the ending control frame. If you skip this, the first image will guide both start and end.
Open the Wan2ImageToVideoApi node and select your audio file. Review any available settings (e.g., resolution/aspect ratio or duration if exposed) to match your image and desired runtime.
Queue and run the workflow. The Wan2.7 model will generate in-between frames guided by your first/last images and the audio timing.
When the run completes, the SaveVideo node will write the final video. Open the saved file to review motion and audio sync.
suggestedUseCases: Social posts that animate a still brand image to music for short promos.
Before-and-after reveals where the first and last frames bookend a smooth motion transition.
Cinemagraph-style loops that start and end on nearly identical frames for seamless playback.
Portrait or product hero shots that gain subtle camera motion synced to a soundtrack.
Title cards or splash screens that animate in and settle on a final design.

faqItems.question: Do I need two images, or can I use just one?
faqItems.answer: You can use one or two. One image will guide both the start and end, creating motion that returns to the original framing. Adding a second image as the last frame lets Wan2.7 transition toward a different final composition.

faqItems.question: How does the audio affect the output?
faqItems.answer: The audio defines the video’s duration and helps align motion pacing. Choose a track with the length you want. If the node exposes timing controls, keep them consistent with the audio to avoid truncation or extra silence.

faqItems.question: What resolution and aspect ratio should I use?
faqItems.answer: Match the aspect ratio between your first and last frames, and keep a reasonable resolution your hardware or API quota can handle. Higher resolutions need more compute and time—start smaller to validate motion, then scale up.

faqItems.question: How can I get cleaner, more stable motion?
faqItems.answer: Use sharp, well-lit images with consistent subject size and framing across the first and last frames. Avoid drastic changes in viewpoint or lighting between endpoints. If available, reduce motion intensity settings for subtler moves.

a50ab9e1df59.title: Noise Injected VideoGen
a50ab9e1df59.description: Upload a starting image and a mask video to define the injection area. Generate a dynamic video by injecting noise patterns from a dedicated noise video, with AI auto-generated prompts.
a50ab9e1df59.metaDescription: Transform static images into dynamic videos with noise injection and AI prompts using the Noise Injected VideoGen workflow in ComfyUI.
a50ab9e1df59.extendedDescription: The Noise Injected VideoGen workflow is designed to transform static images into dynamic videos by leveraging noise patterns and AI-generated prompts. This workflow begins with a static image and a mask video that defines the area of noise injection. The process utilizes the 'VHS_LoadVideo' node to load a noise video, which is then combined with the static image using 'VHS_VideoCombine'. The 'AILab_QwenVL' node plays a crucial role in generating AI-driven prompts that guide the transformation process, ensuring that the resulting video is both coherent and visually engaging. The workflow employs 'comfyui-animatediff-evolved' and 'comfyui-frame-interpolation' nodes to enhance the fluidity and realism of the video transitions, making it an excellent tool for creating professional-grade video content from simple images.
howToUse: Load your starting image using the 'LoadImage' node in ComfyUI.
Upload your mask video to define the noise injection area using the 'VHS_LoadVideo' node.
Load a noise video pattern with the 'VHS_LoadVideo' node to be injected into the image.
Use the 'AILab_QwenVL' node to generate AI prompts that will guide the video transformation.
Combine the image and noise video with 'VHS_VideoCombine' and process it through 'comfyui-animatediff-evolved' for dynamic video generation.
Preview the result using 'PreviewAny' and save the final video with 'SaveVideo'.
suggestedUseCases: Creating dynamic video advertisements from static product images.
Enhancing social media content with engaging video effects.
Developing unique video art installations from photographs.
Producing educational content with animated visuals from diagrams.

faqItems.question: What type of images work best with this workflow?

faqItems.question: How do AI-generated prompts affect the video?
faqItems.answer: AI-generated prompts guide the transformation process, ensuring that the video remains coherent and visually appealing.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to adjust the intensity of the noise injection?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can adjust the intensity by modifying the parameters in the 'VHS_VideoCombine' node and related settings.

a58c512532df.title: Swap Product in Character’s Hand, UGC Style
a58c512532df.description: Upload a photo of a character holding a product and your brands product. Generate an image with the products swapped.

This ComfyUI workflow is designed to seamlessly swap a product in a character's hand with another product, particularly useful for user-generated content (UGC) in marketing. By leveraging advanced AI models such as Gemini3 Pro Image Preview and Nano Banana Pro, this workflow ensures high-quality image manipulation that maintains the natural look and feel of the original photo. The process begins with the 'LoadImage' node, where users upload an image of a character holding a product. The 'GeminiImage2Node' processes the image, identifying and isolating the product for replacement. The custom node 'e20a7fb5-3d72-41c9-a78c-fdf287ec46ec' then integrates the new product image provided by the user, ensuring it fits seamlessly into the original context. Finally, the 'SaveImage' node outputs the modified image, ready for use in marketing materials or social media campaigns.

Technically, this workflow utilizes the power of AI to detect and replace objects within images, a task that traditionally requires manual editing skills. By automating this process, the workflow not only saves time but also ensures consistency and quality across multiple images. The integration of models like Google and Nano Banana Pro enhances the accuracy of object detection and replacement, making this workflow particularly useful for brands looking to quickly adapt their marketing visuals to different products or campaigns.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure all necessary models are installed.
Use the 'LoadImage' node to upload a photo of a character holding a product.
Upload your brand's product image using the designated input node.
The 'GeminiImage2Node' will process the image, isolating the product for replacement.
Review the output image in the 'SaveImage' node to ensure the product swap is seamless.
Save the final image for use in your marketing materials or social media.
suggestedUseCases: Creating personalized marketing visuals for different product lines.
Generating user-generated content with swapped products for social media campaigns.
Testing how different products look in lifestyle images for e-commerce sites.
Quickly adapting advertising materials for seasonal or promotional products.

faqItems.question: What kind of images work best with this workflow?

faqItems.question: Can this workflow handle complex backgrounds?

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for input and output?

a6b2c3fe248c.title: AI on the Lot 2026_Qwen-Image-Edit-2511
a6b2c3fe248c.description: A bonus workflow for AI on the Lot 2026, made available for ComfyUI 101 workshop attendees to open and follow along if time allows. An image editing workflow powered by Qwen-Image-Edit-2511.
a6b2c3fe248c.metaDescription: Instruction-based image and video frame editing in ComfyUI using Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 and Qwen2.5-VL encoder, optimized for fast 4-step Lightning inference.
a6b2c3fe248c.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow shows how to perform fast, instruction-based image edits using Qwen-Image-Edit-2511. It wires a simple I/O path—LoadImage (or VHS_LoadVideo for frames) into a compact Subgraph node (ID cdb2cf24-c432-439b-b5c8-5f69838580c9)—and ends with SaveImage. Inside the subgraph, the edit is driven by the Qwen 2.5 VL text encoder (qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors) and a lightweight LoRA tuned for speed (Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning-4steps-V1.0-bf16.safetensors). The subgraph encapsulates the model plumbing so you can focus on a plain-language instruction like “make the sky overcast” or “remove the background,” then preview results quickly.

Technically, the workflow routes your source image (or video frames) into the subgraph, where the Qwen 2.5 VL encoder interprets your instruction text and conditions the edit. The Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 Lightning LoRA applies the learned edit behavior while keeping inference fast with very few sampling steps. Because this is packaged as a Subgraph, you get a clean graph and consistent defaults—you can double-click or open the subgraph to inspect or tweak internals as needed. SaveImage captures each result frame to disk; when fed by VHS_LoadVideo, you’ll get a numbered image sequence you can reassemble externally if you want a final video.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then read the MarkdownNote for a quick overview.

Download the models from the Author Notes: place qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors in models/text_encoders and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning-4steps-V1.0-bf16.safetensors in models/loras. Restart ComfyUI if needed so they appear in dropdowns.

Choose your input: use LoadImage for a single image, or VHS_LoadVideo to bring in a clip (the node outputs frames). Make sure the chosen input is connected to the Subgraph node (ID cdb2cf24-c432-439b-b5c8-5f69838580c9).

Open the Subgraph node and enter a clear instruction for the edit (e.g., “remove the background to white,” “replace the sky with sunset clouds,” or “turn the car red”). Keep defaults for the Lightning 4-step flow unless you specifically need stronger/weaker edits.
Click Queue Prompt to run. Watch the preview; iterate on your instruction wording if needed for precision (e.g., specify colors, materials, or style adjectives).
Find your results in the SaveImage output folder. If you edited a video, you’ll get an image sequence (one file per processed frame) you can reassemble into a video using your preferred tool.
suggestedUseCases: Product photo cleanup: remove backgrounds, unify lighting, or standardize surface colors for catalogs.
Quick look development: swap skies, adjust time of day, or add simple scene elements for previsualization.
Brand consistency passes: nudge color tones and accessories across multiple shots to match a style guide.
Social content polish: refine thumbnails and hero images with small, targeted edits in seconds.
Frame-by-frame video touch-ups: apply the same light edit across a short clip and export as an image sequence.

faqItems.question: Do I need any extra extensions or custom nodes?
faqItems.answer: Core nodes (LoadImage, SaveImage, MarkdownNote) are built-in. The workflow uses a Subgraph node (ID cdb2cf24-…) and optionally VHS_LoadVideo for video frames. If you don’t see VHS_LoadVideo, install the VideoHelperSuite (VHS) extension. Then place the provided model files in models/text_encoders and models/loras as noted.

faqItems.question: Where do I put the model files?
faqItems.answer: Place qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511-Lightning-4steps-V1.0-bf16.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/loras. Restart ComfyUI so they appear in any model/LoRA selectors inside the subgraph.

faqItems.question: How can I get cleaner or more accurate edits?
faqItems.answer: Use high-quality input images, write precise instructions (mention target objects, colors, and context), and keep the edit scope focused. If results are too strong or weak, adjust the subgraph’s exposed edit controls (e.g., strength/intensity if available) or try slightly different phrasings. Running at moderate resolutions also helps stability.

faqItems.question: Can this do masked or region-specific edits?
faqItems.answer: This template focuses on instruction-based global edits and does not include masking nodes. You can often localize changes by writing specific instructions (e.g., “only change the jacket color to navy”), or you can extend the workflow by adding a masking path if you need precise region control.

faqItems.question: How do I turn edited frames back into a video?
faqItems.answer: This workflow saves frames via SaveImage. After processing, import the numbered image sequence into a video editor or use a command-line tool (e.g., ffmpeg) to encode a video. If you prefer an in-graph export, add a video writer node and connect it after the edit stage.

a781503cf508.title: MiniMax H3: Image to Video
a781503cf508.description: Turn a starting image into a short, high-quality video clip with MiniMax H3, a unified multimodal model that generates visuals and synchronized audio in a single pass. The workflow takes 1 input image and produces 1 video output, with optional text or reference media to steer motion, style, or sound. Ideal for rapid concept visualization, character-driven animation tests, and creating shareable social media clips with built-in sound design.
a781503cf508.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: convert one image into a short video with synchronized audio using MiniMax H3, auto-scaled resolution, and one-click MP4 export.
a781503cf508.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a single still image into a short, coherent video clip with synchronized stereo audio using MiniMax H3. At its core is the MiniMax H3 generation node (id: 4c314f31-ecda-4b08-ae98-faaba1bf613f), which performs a single forward pass to synthesize both video frames and audio that match the scene. The image you provide through LoadImage sets the subject and overall style; you can optionally add short text guidance inside the MiniMax H3 node to suggest motion, pacing, or mood.

To help the model run efficiently and preserve composition, the workflow routes the input through GetImageSize and a Use Image Size group that keeps aspect ratio intact. ResolutionSelector and ImageScaleToTotalPixels work together to pick a target size that fits MiniMax H3’s recommended megapixel budgets and the multiple-of-32 constraint required by the model. The generated clip is then written out by SaveVideo as a single MP4 containing the video stream (and the model’s generated audio, if enabled), ready for quick review or sharing. Model assets used by the generator include the video VAE (minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors) and the audio VAE (minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors).
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote inside the graph for any inline tips.

Install the MiniMax H3 assets: download minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors and minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors from the provided links, then point the MiniMax H3 node (id: 4c314f31-ecda-4b08-ae98-faaba1bf613f) to these files if paths are required.
Add your starting image via the LoadImage node. The GetImageSize node and Use Image Size group will propagate its aspect ratio to downstream resolution nodes.

Choose a target size: use ResolutionSelector to pick a megapixel budget appropriate for your GPU (for example, 0.4–0.8 MP for mid-tier cards). ImageScaleToTotalPixels will compute width/height in multiples of 32 while keeping your image’s aspect.

Open the MiniMax H3 node and (optionally) enter brief text guidance for motion or mood, set duration and fps, and pick a seed. Keep prompts concise and descriptive (e.g., "slow push-in, gentle breeze, soft ambient music").

Run the graph. Review the MP4 saved by SaveVideo. If you see artifacts or drift, try a lower resolution, a shorter duration, or a new seed; if the motion feels too subtle or too strong, adjust the guidance inside the MiniMax H3 node and rerun.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept visualization for scenes, environments, or product shots with ambient sound.
Character animation tests to explore personality and motion beats from a single pose.
Social media teasers or loops that need built-in sound design without a separate audio pass.
Mood boards and previsualization clips for pitches or storyboards.
Stylized kinetic stills for marketing thumbnails, banners, or hero images made dynamic.

faqItems.question: Which files do I need to download for MiniMax H3 to generate video and audio?
faqItems.answer: Download the MiniMax video VAE (minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors) and audio VAE (minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors) from the links in the workflow notes. In the MiniMax H3 node (id: 4c314f31-ecda-4b08-ae98-faaba1bf613f), set the paths if the node exposes them, then reload models if required.

faqItems.question: How do I pick the right resolution?
faqItems.answer: Use ResolutionSelector with a megapixel budget that matches your GPU VRAM. The ImageScaleToTotalPixels node will output dimensions that are multiples of 32 and preserve your input image’s aspect via GetImageSize. If you encounter OOM errors, lower the MP target or shorten the duration.

faqItems.question: Can I get silent video only?
faqItems.answer: Yes. In the MiniMax H3 node, disable audio generation (if exposed) or ignore the audio output when wiring to SaveVideo. The SaveVideo node will still write the video stream as MP4.

faqItems.question: How do I control motion and style?
faqItems.answer: Your input image anchors style and identity. For motion, add concise guidance in the MiniMax H3 node (e.g., camera moves, tempo, ambience). Keep prompts short and concrete. For stronger effects, try a higher duration or different seed; for more subtle motion, reduce duration or simplify the guidance.

a84541c0018a.title: Image Stitch  2x2 Grid
a84541c0018a.description: Combine four input images into a 2x2 grid. Automatically resizes mismatched images and outputs a single 2048x2048 image.
a84541c0018a.metaDescription: Create a 2x2 image grid from four images, resized and combined into a 2048x2048 output using ComfyUI's Image Stitch workflow.
a84541c0018a.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow is designed to seamlessly combine four separate images into a cohesive 2x2 grid, outputting a single image with a resolution of 2048x2048 pixels. The workflow employs several key nodes to ensure each image fits perfectly within the grid, even if the input images vary in size. The `LoadImage` nodes are used to bring in the individual images, which are then processed through the `ResizeImageMaskNode` to standardize their dimensions. This resizing step is crucial for maintaining the grid's uniformity and ensuring each image aligns correctly. The `ImageStitch` nodes are the core of this workflow, first joining the top-left and top-right images into a single row, and then the bottom-left and bottom-right images into another row. Finally, a third `ImageStitch` node stacks these two rows vertically to complete the grid. The resulting image is saved using the `SaveImage` node. This workflow is particularly useful for creating composite images for presentations, social media posts, or any application where a unified image layout is desired.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and prepare your four images.
Use the `LoadImage` nodes to import each of the four images into the workflow.
The `ResizeImageMaskNode` will automatically adjust any mismatched image sizes to ensure uniformity.
The `ImageStitch` nodes will combine the images into a 2x2 grid, first horizontally, then vertically.
Finally, the `SaveImage` node will output the completed 2048x2048 image grid to your desired location.
suggestedUseCases: Creating Instagram posts with a cohesive visual layout.
Designing mood boards or inspiration grids for creative projects.
Compiling product images into a single promotional image.
Generating comparison grids for side-by-side image analysis.
Crafting digital photo albums or collages.

faqItems.question: What happens if my images are different sizes?
faqItems.answer: The `ResizeImageMaskNode` will automatically resize all images to ensure they fit perfectly within the grid.

faqItems.question: Can I use more than four images?
faqItems.answer: This specific workflow is designed for four images. For more images, you would need to modify the workflow to accommodate additional images and grid configurations.

faqItems.question: What format should my images be in?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports common image formats such as JPEG and PNG. Ensure your images are in a compatible format before loading them.

faqItems.question: Is there a limit to the image resolution I can use?
faqItems.answer: While there is no strict limit, using very high-resolution images may increase processing time. The final output will always be 2048x2048 pixels.

a8d874e28508.title: Flux.2 Klein 9B: Image Extend
a8d874e28508.description: Use the FLUX.2 Klein 9B model to intelligently extend and expand image content. Input an image to generate seamless outpainting and extended compositions.
a8d874e28508.metaDescription: Extend images seamlessly with the Flux.2 Klein 9B model using ComfyUI's outpainting workflow. Perfect for artists and designers.
a8d874e28508.extendedDescription:
The 'Flux.2 Klein 9B: Image Extend' workflow is designed to expand and enhance images using the FLUX.2 Klein 9B model. This workflow excels at outpainting, a technique that extends the boundaries of an image while maintaining its original style and content. It leverages a combination of advanced nodes such as SamplerCustomAdvanced, CLIPLoader, and RandomNoise to generate seamless extensions of the input image. By using the ComfyUI-Color-Matcher and comfyui-kjnodes, the workflow ensures color consistency and style coherence, making it particularly useful for artists and designers looking to create expansive compositions from limited source material.

Technically, the workflow begins by loading an image and encoding it into a latent space using the VAEEncode node. The Flux2Scheduler and UNETLoader nodes work together to generate new image data that blends naturally with the existing content. The process is guided by the CFGGuider and KSamplerSelect nodes, which help refine the image generation based on the input prompts and conditions. Once the outpainting is complete, the VAEDecode node converts the latent representation back into a visible image format, ready for saving or further editing.
howToUse: Load the 'Flux.2 Klein 9B: Image Extend' workflow in ComfyUI.

Adjust the ImagePadForOutpaint settings to define the outpainting area.

a9241caf70ac.title: Character Portrait Relighting
a9241caf70ac.description: Upload a portrait of your character and create multiple cinematic lighting conditions while maintaining character consistency.
a9241caf70ac.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Relight a character portrait into cinematic variants using GeminiImage2Node with the Nano Banana Pro model—fast, consistent identity.
a9241caf70ac.extendedDescription:
Character Portrait Relighting is a compact ComfyUI workflow that takes a single portrait and renders it under different, cinematic lighting conditions while keeping the character’s identity consistent. It uses three nodes end-to-end: LoadImage to ingest your source portrait, GeminiImage2Node to perform image-to-image relighting through an external API, and SaveImage to write the results. The workflow is configured to run the Nano Banana Pro model inside GeminiImage2Node, which is well-suited for photoreal portrait work.

Technically, the relighting happens by conditioning the generation on your uploaded image plus a text prompt that describes the lighting setup you want (for example: "soft key light from camera-left, warm rim light, low-fill, filmic contrast"). GeminiImage2Node sends the image and prompt to the API, returning a relit image that preserves pose and facial structure based on the input. You can keep identity tight by favoring higher image-to-image preservation (often exposed as a strength or guidance setting). To produce multiple looks from the same portrait, duplicate GeminiImage2Node (each with a different lighting prompt) and route them all from the same LoadImage, then save each result with its own label via SaveImage.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure GeminiImage2Node is installed and authorized (set your API key per the node’s instructions). In GeminiImage2Node, select the Nano Banana Pro model.
Load your source portrait with the LoadImage node. Use a clean, front-facing or 3/4 view image with good detail; higher resolution inputs generally yield better results.

Open GeminiImage2Node and enter a precise lighting prompt (e.g., "Rembrandt lighting, warm key from left, cool rim from right, soft fill, cinematic contrast"). Set the image preservation/strength so features stay consistent; set a seed if you want repeatable outputs.

To generate multiple lighting looks in one run, duplicate GeminiImage2Node (and a corresponding SaveImage) for each lighting prompt. Connect each GeminiImage2Node’s image input to the same LoadImage output.
For each SaveImage node, set a clear filename prefix (e.g., relight_rembrandt, relight_rimlight) and choose your output directory. Connect each GeminiImage2Node output to its SaveImage.
Queue the workflow. Review results, then adjust prompts or the preservation/strength setting to tighten identity or add drama (harder shadows, stronger rim) and re-queue as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Previsualizing portrait lighting setups for photo or film shoots (key/fill/rim variations) without reshooting.
Creating consistent character sheets for games/animation with multiple moods from the same face.
Marketing and social assets: fast A/B testing of headshot lighting for different platforms or campaigns.
Concept art lighting studies (no re-sculpting or repainting required) while preserving core likeness.
Storyboards and pitch decks needing fast, cinematic portrait variants from a fixed character.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow keep the character’s identity consistent?
faqItems.answer: GeminiImage2Node performs image-to-image generation conditioned on your uploaded portrait. Keep a higher image-preservation/strength setting, avoid prompts that describe changes to facial features or makeup, and start from a clean, well-lit input. Using a fixed seed also helps repeatability.

faqItems.question: What resolution do I get back?
faqItems.answer: By default, the output matches the resolution returned by the API for the selected model (often similar to the input). SaveImage writes exactly the resolution produced by GeminiImage2Node. If the node exposes size controls, set them there before running.

faqItems.question: Do I need a powerful GPU to run this?
faqItems.answer: No. GeminiImage2Node calls an external API, so heavy compute runs remotely. ComfyUI orchestrates the request and saves the results. A local GPU is not required for this workflow.

faqItems.question: Can I relight only parts of the image (e.g., keep background unchanged)?
faqItems.answer: This minimal workflow doesn’t include masking. You can often constrain changes with careful prompting, but for precise control consider extending the graph with masking/inpainting steps or pre-masking your input before LoadImage.

a9294d9380a6.title: Image Upscale: Traditional Interpolation

a9294d9380a6.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow focuses on upscaling images using traditional interpolation methods, providing a balance between speed and quality. The workflow employs a series of nodes, starting with 'LoadImage' to import the original image. The 'ImageScaleBy' node is then used to upscale the image by a specified factor, utilizing traditional interpolation algorithms such as bilinear or bicubic. These methods are known for their efficiency and ability to preserve the overall look of the image without introducing significant artifacts. Finally, the 'SaveImage' node allows you to export the upscaled image, while the 'ImageCompare' node can be used to evaluate the differences between the original and upscaled images. This workflow is particularly useful for users who need quick image enlargement without the computational overhead of AI-based methods.
howToUse: Load your image into the workflow using the 'LoadImage' node.
Select the 'ImageScaleBy' node and choose your preferred interpolation method (e.g., bilinear, bicubic).
Specify the scale factor to determine how much larger the image should be.
Use the 'SaveImage' node to export the upscaled image to your desired location.
Optionally, utilize the 'ImageCompare' node to visually compare the original and upscaled images.
Review the results and adjust the scale factor or interpolation method if necessary for optimal quality.
suggestedUseCases: Quickly enlarging images for presentations or reports where processing time is critical.
Upscaling images for web use where minimal detail change is acceptable.
Preparing images for print with traditional methods to maintain a natural look.
Creating larger versions of digital artwork for display without AI-induced artifacts.

faqItems.question: What interpolation methods are available in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports traditional interpolation methods such as bilinear and bicubic, which are efficient and maintain the image's natural appearance.

faqItems.question: How does this workflow differ from AI-based upscaling?
faqItems.answer: This workflow uses traditional algorithms, which are faster and require less computational power, whereas AI-based methods often provide more detail but at a higher processing cost.

faqItems.question: Can I compare the original and upscaled images?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can use the 'ImageCompare' node to visually assess the differences between the original and the upscaled images.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for all types of images?
faqItems.answer: While it works well for most images, the results may vary depending on the image's original quality and the selected interpolation method.

aac8b0d80e73.title: SeedVR2: Video Upscaling

By using this workflow, users can transform standard-definition videos into high-definition content, suitable for modern viewing platforms.

Use the GetVideoComponents node to extract frames from the video.
Apply the SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler node to upscale each frame to the desired resolution.

Save the final high-definition video using the SaveVideo node.

Concept-to-motion tests for pitching ideas to clients or teammates.

faqItems.question: Do I need two different images, or can I use just one?

faqItems.question: How long can the generated video be?

By utilizing advanced AI models like Nano Banana, Google Gemini, and Wan2.2, this workflow seamlessly transitions from the first frame of an image to the last, creating a continuous loop. The process begins with loading an initial image and its corresponding prompt, which guides the transformation process. The workflow employs nodes such as LoadImage to import the starting image, and SaveVideo to compile the frames into a video format. The node identified by 3313ce14-acfd-4a9c-9f0c-a1b01147e934 plays a crucial role in generating intermediate frames that ensure a smooth transition between the start and end of the sequence. PreviewImage is used to monitor the progress and make necessary adjustments before finalizing the output.
howToUse: Load the 'Looped Restyler' workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadImage node to upload your starting image and input its prompt.
Configure the node 3313ce14-acfd-4a9c-9f0c-a1b01147e934 to generate intermediate frames for smooth transitions.
Monitor the progress using the PreviewImage node to ensure the loop is seamless.
Once satisfied, use the SaveVideo node to compile and save your looping video.
Review the final output to ensure it meets your expectations.
suggestedUseCases: Creating animated loops for digital art projects.
Generating engaging social media content from static images.
Producing dynamic video backgrounds for websites or presentations.
Developing creative visual effects for film and multimedia projects.
Enhancing storytelling in visual narratives with seamless loops.

faqItems.question: What type of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: High-resolution images with clear focal points tend to produce the best results, as they provide more detail for the AI to work with.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the speed of the looping video?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can adjust the frame rate in the SaveVideo node to control the speed of the loop.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to add audio to the looping video?
faqItems.answer: This workflow focuses on visual output. However, you can add audio using video editing software after exporting the video.

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the loop is seamless?
faqItems.answer: Use the PreviewImage node to check transitions between frames and adjust parameters in the 3313ce14-acfd-4a9c-9f0c-a1b01147e934 node for smoother results.

adca306765ce.title: LTX-2.3: Image Audio to Video
adca306765ce.description: Upload an image and an audio file to generate a high-quality video with synchronized lip movements using LTX-2.3.
adca306765ce.metaDescription: Create a lip-synced talking video from a single image and audio using LTX-2.3 in ComfyUI. Load image/audio, generate frames, and export an MP4.
adca306765ce.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single image and a voice recording into a lip-synced talking video using the LTX-2.3 model. You load a portrait with LoadImage and provide speech via LoadAudio or capture it live with RecordAudio. Both streams feed the LTX-2.3 generator node (98ee9e5b-467b-40aa-a534-36033f27d0b4), which synthesizes a sequence of frames where the subject speaks in time with the audio. The resulting frames are encoded to an MP4 using SaveVideo.

Under the hood, LTX-2.3 conditions on the visual identity from your reference image and the temporal features of the provided audio to drive mouth shapes and subtle facial motions over time. The node typically exposes settings like output resolution and FPS, and many builds also include a seed for reproducibility and an optional text prompt to guide motion or style. The MarkdownNote in the graph documents quick tips and links to the official Lightricks model repositories so you can download the required weights.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the LTX-2.3 weights are installed per the Lightricks repo/Hugging Face instructions. Restart ComfyUI so the LTX-2.3 node is available.
Open LoadImage and choose a clear, front-facing portrait where the mouth is fully visible. Square or centered crops generally produce the most stable results.
Provide audio: either drop in a file with LoadAudio (clean, speech-focused audio preferred) or record directly with RecordAudio. Keep background noise minimal.

Configure the LTX-2.3 generator node (98ee9e5b-467b-40aa-a534-36033f27d0b4): set FPS (e.g., 24 or 25), output resolution (match your image or a square size), and choose a seed if you want repeatable output. If a prompt field is available, describe desired motion (e.g., slight head turns, natural blinks).

Connect the node outputs as shown in the workflow so the generated frames feed into SaveVideo. If your SaveVideo build supports audio muxing, connect the same audio there; otherwise, you’ll add audio in post.

Click Queue Prompt to run. When complete, SaveVideo will write an MP4 of the synthesized talking head. Review lip sync and motion; adjust FPS, resolution, prompt, or image crop for refinements and re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Voiceover announcements where a brand mascot or presenter speaks a short script from a single still image.
Educational explainers with a talking avatar created from a photo of a host or character.
News-style shorts or social clips generated quickly from a portrait and a recorded message.
Localization or drafts of dubbed content where you need a fast lip-synced visual for review.
Animated profile intros or podcast promos using a host’s image and teaser audio.

faqItems.question: Do I need a specific image type for best results?
faqItems.answer: Use a front-facing portrait with good lighting and the mouth unobstructed (no hands, mics, or heavy objects covering lips). Center the face and use a reasonable resolution (e.g., 512–1024 px on the short side). Avoid extreme angles and busy backgrounds.

faqItems.question: What audio format works best?
faqItems.answer: Clean, speech-focused audio produces the most accurate mouth movements. WAV or high-bitrate MP3 typically work; mono voice tracks are preferred. Minimize reverb and background noise to improve alignment and realism.

faqItems.question: Will the exported video include the audio track?
faqItems.answer: That depends on your SaveVideo node build. Some variants can mux audio; others export a silent MP4. If yours is silent, combine the output video with the same audio in an editor or a separate muxing step.

faqItems.question: How can I improve lip sync and overall quality?
faqItems.answer: Start with a clear, centered portrait and clean audio. Match FPS to your target platform (e.g., 24–30). If a prompt field is available, describe subtle motions (blinks, small head turns) to avoid a static look. Try different seeds for variety, and consider cropping the face tighter if the mouth region appears too small.

ae12a241076c.title: Relight Composited Product
ae12a241076c.description: Upload a composited image of your product, draw a mask in the mask editor and relight your product into the scene.
ae12a241076c.metaDescription: Relight your composited product images seamlessly with this ComfyUI workflow. Perfect for enhancing product photos with realistic lighting.
ae12a241076c.extendedDescription: The 'Relight Composited Product' workflow in ComfyUI is designed to enhance product images by allowing users to adjust the lighting of a specific area within a composited image. This is particularly useful for product photographers and e-commerce businesses looking to create visually appealing images that stand out. The workflow leverages the Qwen-Image-Edit model, known for its advanced image editing capabilities, to achieve realistic lighting adjustments. By using the 'comfyui-inpaint-cropandstitch' custom node, users can precisely target areas of the image to relight, ensuring seamless integration with the existing scene. This workflow is beneficial for improving the visual aesthetics of product images without the need for complex photo editing software.
howToUse: Load your composited product image into the ComfyUI interface using the LoadImage node.
Use the mask editor to draw a mask over the area of the product you wish to relight.
Apply the Qwen-Image-Edit model to adjust the lighting within the masked area.
Utilize the comfyui-inpaint-cropandstitch node to ensure the relighted area blends seamlessly with the rest of the image.
Save the edited image using the SaveImage node to complete the process.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing product images for e-commerce websites to attract more customers.
Adjusting lighting in product photos for marketing materials.
Creating consistent lighting across a series of product images for a catalog.
Improving the visual appeal of product images for social media promotions.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for non-product images?
faqItems.answer: While designed for product images, this workflow can be adapted for any composited image where specific relighting is needed.

faqItems.question: What if the relighted area doesn't blend well with the image?
faqItems.answer: Ensure that the mask is accurately drawn and make use of the comfyui-inpaint-cropandstitch node to achieve a seamless blend.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for beginners?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow is user-friendly and does not require advanced photo editing skills, making it accessible for beginners.

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported for the input image?
faqItems.answer: The LoadImage node supports common formats like JPEG and PNG, ensuring compatibility with most image files.

aeb71e383642.title: Qwen3.5: Text Generation
aeb71e383642.description: Use the Qwen3.5 model to analyze an input image and generate descriptive text prompts. This workflow performs image captioning and reverse prompt engineering.
aeb71e383642.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Use Qwen3.5 to caption images and auto-generate reverse-engineered prompts with TextGenerate, from model setup to exporting results.
aeb71e383642.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates how to use Qwen3.5 inside ComfyUI to analyze an image and generate descriptive text that doubles as ready-to-use prompts. It performs both image captioning and reverse prompt engineering: you provide an image via LoadImage, and the TextGenerate node, powered by Qwen3.5, returns structured descriptions or prompt candidates you can paste into your image-generation pipelines.

Technically, the CLIPLoader node is pointed at the Qwen3.5 weights (qwen3.5_4b_bf16.safetensors) stored under models/text_encoders/. That model handle feeds into the TextGenerate node, which accepts the loaded image and an instruction prompt (for example, "Produce 3 concise, diffusion-ready prompts"). The node then runs inference and returns text, which you can view with PreviewAny. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides inline guidance and prompt tips, making it easy to iterate on instruction wording, temperature, and token length to dial in results.
howToUse: Download qwen3.5_4b_bf16.safetensors and place it in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/. Restart ComfyUI so the model is indexed.
Load the provided workflow. Verify the CLIPLoader node points to the Qwen3.5 model and shows as loaded (node turns ready).
Open LoadImage and select the image you want to analyze. Use a clear, well-lit source for the best descriptions.

Open TextGenerate and confirm it is connected to the Qwen3.5 model (from CLIPLoader). Edit the instruction/system prompt (e.g., request 2–4 diffusion-ready prompts including subject, medium, camera/lens, lighting, style, and optional negatives). Adjust generation parameters like temperature and max tokens if exposed.
Queue the workflow. When it finishes, read and copy the generated text from PreviewAny. If needed, tweak the instruction or parameters and re-run for refinement.
Optionally, use MarkdownNote in the workflow as a place to store your favorite instruction templates and examples for consistent outputs across images.
suggestedUseCases: Reverse prompt engineering: derive SD/SDXL/FLUX-friendly prompts from reference images.
Alt-text and SEO descriptions for product images or blog visuals.
Dataset bootstrapping: quick, consistent captions to seed annotation workflows.
Creative briefs and shot lists based on visual references.
Asset tagging and library organization with detailed, style-aware descriptors.

faqItems.question: How is this different from basic image captioning?
faqItems.answer: Beyond plain descriptions, the workflow can generate structured, diffusion-ready prompts (subject, medium, lens, lighting, style, and optional negatives) when you specify that format in the TextGenerate instruction.

faqItems.question: Do I need an internet connection to run this?
faqItems.answer: No. Once you download qwen3.5_4b_bf16.safetensors into ComfyUI/models/text_encoders/, the workflow runs locally in ComfyUI.

faqItems.question: How can I improve the quality or usefulness of the generated prompts?
faqItems.answer: Use clear, high-quality images; provide a precise instruction template (e.g., ask for 3 concise prompts with subject, medium, lens, lighting, style, and negatives); and tune generation parameters like temperature (for more or less creativity) and max tokens (for longer outputs).

faqItems.question: Can I swap in a different Qwen3.5 variant?
faqItems.answer: Yes, as long as it’s packaged for use with the TextGenerate node and placed where CLIPLoader can load it (models/text_encoders/). Update the CLIPLoader selection to the desired variant and keep the instruction format consistent.

aeb81743ddf7.title: Step 3: Contact Sheet Workflow
aeb81743ddf7.description: Upload 8 images (in order) to be used as keyframes for 7 Kling 3.0 FFLF videos.
aeb81743ddf7.metaDescription: Create a 1080p contact sheet and 7 FFLF clips from 8 keyframes using ComfyUI with Kling 3.0. Batch images, verify order, and generate smooth, controlled transitions.
aeb81743ddf7.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial walks you through a contact sheet workflow that turns 8 ordered images into a structured storyboard and 7 adjacent keyframe pairs for Kling 3.0 FFLF video generation. The pipeline starts with LoadImage and BatchImagesNode to ingest your files in a strict left-to-right timeline. A set of utility/custom nodes (IDs: f7abaa3a-5e87-4354-bab6-f43320cd490f, 02da9128-7c15-4c46-96bc-1dd68e5bc490, 3426003b-7b3a-4d37-8a2f-e0f8adb05712, c61d617f-c72d-4f4c-8659-bd6f884d1a1e, 4b301c11-bc16-4096-9441-e0648a04aa4d, 2ab1ef49-3518-4f71-b703-f8ef12f32214, b3fe4254-e196-429e-9f45-96c92113e406) handle layout, pairwise splitting (1-2, 2-3, …, 7-8), and packaging to downstream video nodes. PrimitiveNode exposes the core knobs—1080p resolution, frame rate, per-shot duration, and optional padding—while Reroute keeps the graph readable. SaveVideo exports a 1080p preview so you can quickly verify sequencing and framing before running the heavier generations.

For FFLF (first/last-frame–guided) generation, each adjacent image pair is passed to the Kling 3.0 node to synthesize motion constrained by your start and end frames—ideal for consistent, controllable transitions across a 7-shot sequence. If enabled, a Gemini-3.1-flsih-lite helper node can auto-summarize shot intents between each pair to keep prompts consistent (optional metadata only; it’s not required for rendering). The result is a fast, reliable way to validate continuity, then batch-generate seven cohesive clips at a clean 1920×1080 output.
howToUse: Load the “Step 3: Contact Sheet Workflow” JSON in ComfyUI and confirm all nodes are green (LoadImage, BatchImagesNode, PrimitiveNode, SaveVideo, Kling 3.0, and helper nodes).

Import 8 images in the exact storytelling order. Use BatchImagesNode for a single multi-file load (ensure filenames sort correctly) or update individual LoadImage nodes. Keep all images at or near 16:9 to avoid cropping at 1080p.
Open PrimitiveNode parameters and set 1920×1080 resolution (author note: 1080p), FPS, and per-shot duration. These control both the preview pacing and the Kling 3.0 request timing.
Optionally enable the Gemini-3.1-flsih-lite node if you want brief auto-generated descriptors between keyframe pairs. These notes can be passed as lightweight guidance to the Kling 3.0 prompts.
Queue the graph to generate a 1080p contact sheet preview with SaveVideo. Review the output to confirm frame order, aspect ratio, and pacing before running the FFLF jobs.
Run the Kling 3.0 FFLF nodes to create 7 videos (pairs 1–2, 2–3, …, 7–8). Check the output/video directory for saved clips. If anything looks off, adjust order/duration in PrimitiveNode and re-queue.
suggestedUseCases: Storyboard-to-motion: Validate a visual narrative, then convert each transition into a guided clip.
Product feature reveals: Morph between feature shots for smooth, controlled transitions.
Character turnarounds: Interpolate between posed keyframes for stylized motion studies.
Before/after sequences: Create clear, steady transitions between states or designs.
Location shifts: Guide scene changes while preserving composition across cuts.

faqItems.question: Why does the workflow require exactly 8 images?
faqItems.answer: It’s designed to create 7 FFLF videos from adjacent pairs. With 8 ordered keyframes, the pairs are 1–2, 2–3, …, 7–8. If you need more or fewer shots, duplicate/remove the pair-splitting path accordingly.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the frames are in the correct order?
faqItems.answer: Use BatchImagesNode with naturally sorting filenames (e.g., 01, 02, …, 08). If loading individually, double-check each LoadImage path. The contact sheet preview from SaveVideo is the quickest way to verify.

faqItems.question: My images don’t match 16:9—will they be cropped or stretched?
faqItems.answer: Set the PrimitiveNode output to 1920×1080 and choose consistent image sizes. If your sources vary, add a resize/crop step before batching to avoid unwanted letterboxing or distortion in the preview and Kling outputs.

faqItems.question: Kling 3.0 calls are failing or timing out—what should I check?
faqItems.answer: Confirm your Kling node/API configuration, rate limits, and per-shot duration. Try lowering resolution or length, queueing fewer segments at a time, and ensuring stable network connectivity before re-running.

aeda3ae212cd.title: 3x3 Brand Icon Assets Grid

By uploading a reference image of an icon and entering specific brand information, this workflow generates nine unique icons that maintain consistency with your brand's style. howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure all required models and nodes are installed.
Upload your reference icon image using the LoadImage node.
Enter your brand information and stylistic preferences in the input fields provided by PrimitiveStringMultiline nodes.
Adjust any additional parameters using the PrimitiveInt nodes to refine icon characteristics.
Run the workflow to generate a 3x3 grid of unique, brand-aligned icons.

suggestedUseCases: Creating a cohesive set of icons for a new product line.

Designing promotional materials with consistent branding.

faqItems.question: Can I use any image as a reference for the icons?

faqItems.question: What if the generated icons don't match my brand's colors?

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the icons are unique yet consistent?
