afa2656c1d4e.title: Seedance2.5 1080P: Text to Video
afa2656c1d4e.description: Generate cinematic 1080P video clips from text descriptions using Seedance 2.5, supporting clips up to 30 seconds with synchronized sound, music, and dialogue across any aspect ratio. Ideal for short comedy scenes, product showcases, and creative storytelling.
afa2656c1d4e.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate 1080p text-to-video with audio using Seedance 2.5 via ByteDance2TextToVideoNode and SaveVideo. Up to 30s, any aspect ratio.
afa2656c1d4e.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns plain text descriptions into cinematic 1080p video clips with optional synchronized sound using Seedance 2.5. At its core is the ByteDance2TextToVideoNode, which sends your prompt and generation settings (duration, resolution, aspect ratio, FPS, seed) to the Seedance 2.5 backend and returns a finished video stream that can include music, ambience, and simple dialogue aligned to the scene. The SaveVideo node then writes the result to disk as an MP4, preserving the audio track when present.

Technically, you control the visual output by setting width/height (1920x1080 by default) or any custom aspect ratio the model supports, plus a duration cap of up to 30 seconds. The node also exposes a seed so you can iterate with reproducible variations. Because generation is API-based, you get consistent performance without local GPU setup. The simple two-node graph keeps things lean: ByteDance2TextToVideoNode handles synthesis; SaveVideo handles encoding and file naming—ideal for quick iterations, social-ready formats (landscape, square, vertical), and prompt-driven story beats.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then open the ByteDance2TextToVideoNode and SaveVideo nodes.
Add your API credentials to ByteDance2TextToVideoNode (if required by your setup) so it can reach the Seedance 2.5 service.

Write a clear prompt that includes visual direction and optional audio cues (e.g., tone of music, ambience, or simple dialogue). Set Duration (≤ 30s), Resolution (e.g., 1920x1080), Aspect Ratio (if not 16:9), FPS, and Seed.
If you want sound, ensure audio generation is enabled in ByteDance2TextToVideoNode and keep audio cues concise (e.g., “soft piano music,” “crowd chatter,” “character says: ‘Let’s go!’”).
In SaveVideo, set your filename and confirm the output directory. Queue the graph and wait for the ByteDance2TextToVideoNode to finish; SaveVideo will write the MP4.
Review the result, then iterate: tweak the prompt wording, adjust duration/FPS/aspect ratio, or change the seed for variations.
suggestedUseCases: Short comedy skits with simple dialogue and matching background music
Product teasers highlighting features with on-brand soundtrack
Storyboarding and previsualization for film or animation
Social media shorts in vertical or square formats
Scene mood tests (lighting, motion, soundtrack) for creative direction

faqItems.question: How do I get synchronized audio (music or dialogue) in the video?
faqItems.answer: Include audio cues directly in your prompt (e.g., “uplifting synth music,” “footsteps echo,” or “character whispers: ‘Hello’”) and ensure audio is enabled in ByteDance2TextToVideoNode. Keep cues short and specific so Seedance 2.5 can align them plausibly to the scene.

faqItems.question: What are the limits for clip length and resolution?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is designed for clips up to 30 seconds. 1080p (1920x1080) is the default, but you can set other aspect ratios by adjusting width/height (e.g., 1080x1920 for vertical or 1080x1080 for square). Higher resolutions or longer durations may increase generation time and are not guaranteed beyond the stated limits.

faqItems.question: Can I reproduce a result exactly using the same seed?
faqItems.answer: Using the same prompt, settings, and seed often yields similar results, but exact reproducibility is not guaranteed across API versions or model updates. For stable iterations, keep all parameters identical and only change one variable at a time.

faqItems.question: Where is the video saved and what format is used?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo writes an MP4 file to your configured output directory (commonly ComfyUI/output). If the ByteDance2TextToVideoNode returns an audio track, it is preserved in the saved MP4.

afd30ccf8238.title: ACE-Step 1.5 Music Generation AIO
afd30ccf8238.description: Input style tags and lyrics to generate a full song. The workflow uses the ACE-Step 1.5 model to produce commercial-grade music in under 10 seconds on consumer hardware.
afd30ccf8238.metaDescription: Generate songs from style tags and lyrics using ACE‑Step 1.5 in ComfyUI. Set duration, prompt, and export MP3 fast with a clean, reproducible workflow.
afd30ccf8238.extendedDescription:
ACE-Step 1.5 Music Generation AIO is a text-to-audio ComfyUI workflow that turns style tags and lyrics into a complete song. You provide short descriptors like "modern pop, female vocal, lush synths" plus your lyrics, and the graph handles the rest—sampling, decoding, and exporting MP3—so you can audition ideas in seconds on consumer hardware. It’s organized into clear groups—Step 1: Load Model, Step 2: Duration, Step 3: Prompt—so you always know where to set the checkpoint, how long the track should be, and what the model should sing or sound like.

Under the hood, CheckpointLoaderSimple loads the ACE-Step 1.5 checkpoint (ace_step_1.5_turbo_aio.safetensors). TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5 converts your style tags and lyrics into ACE-specific conditioning vectors. ConditioningZeroOut is used to cleanly disable unused conditioning channels (for example, when you’re not providing a secondary or negative prompt), preventing unintended bias. EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio creates an empty latent audio canvas for the exact duration you request. ModelSamplingAuraFlow configures the correct sampler/scheduler combination for ACE-Step 1.5, and KSampler iteratively refines the latent into a coherent track based on your prompt. VAEDecodeAudio turns the final latent into waveform audio, and SaveAudioMP3 writes the result to your ComfyUI output folder. PrimitiveNode widgets expose practical knobs like steps, CFG, seed, and seconds so you can tweak speed, quality, and reproducibility.

This setup is useful for fast songwriting demos, genre exploration, and content beds. You get precise control over duration and a repeatable workflow via the seed. The graph ships with sensible defaults so you can generate a short track quickly, then dial in higher quality by raising steps or refining style tags and lyric phrasing.
howToUse: Place the ACE-Step checkpoint in ComfyUI/models/checkpoints (e.g., ace_step_1.5_turbo_aio.safetensors), then load the provided workflow JSON in ComfyUI.
Step 1 – Load Model: Open the CheckpointLoaderSimple node and select the ACE-Step 1.5 checkpoint. This provides the model weights to the rest of the graph.
Step 2 – Duration: In EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio (via its connected PrimitiveNode controls), set the target length in seconds. This defines how long the generated audio will be.
Step 3 – Prompt: In TextEncodeAceStepAudio1.5, enter concise style tags (genre, mood, instrumentation, vocal type) and paste your lyrics. Keep tags focused and lyrics clear for best intelligibility.

Quality and speed: Adjust KSampler parameters exposed via PrimitiveNode—steps (more steps = higher quality but slower), CFG (start moderate), and seed (fixed for reproducibility or -1/random for variety). ModelSamplingAuraFlow is preconfigured; leave it as-is for correct ACE-Step sampling.

Run the workflow. When it completes, VAEDecodeAudio will output audio that SaveAudioMP3 writes to your ComfyUI output directory. Preview the result and iterate by refining style tags, lyrics, or sampler settings.
suggestedUseCases: Songwriting drafts: Turn lyric snippets and style directions into quick melody-and-arrangement ideas.
Genre exploration: Test how the same lyrics sound across pop, hip-hop, EDM, rock, or cinematic tags.
Ad/jingle prototypes: Rapidly generate short, on-brief music cues for pitches and client approvals.
Social/video beds: Produce background tracks tailored to mood and pacing from a simple prompt.
Education: Demonstrate text-to-music conditioning and sampling concepts in a classroom or workshop.

faqItems.question: Where do I put the model and how do I load it?
faqItems.answer: Place ace_step_1.5_turbo_aio.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/checkpoints. In the workflow’s Step 1 – Load Model group, open CheckpointLoaderSimple and select the file.

faqItems.question: How do I control the length and structure of the song?
faqItems.answer: Set the duration in EmptyAceStep1.5LatentAudio (via its PrimitiveNode control). This sets the exact seconds of audio. You can hint at structure with your lyrics and style tags, but explicit verse/chorus segmentation is not guaranteed.

faqItems.question: My output is noisy or unclear. What should I adjust first?
faqItems.answer: Try increasing KSampler steps moderately, lower CFG if artifacts appear, and refine style tags to be specific (e.g., "warm pop ballad, intimate female vocal, soft piano"). Ensure unused conditioning is disabled via ConditioningZeroOut and keep lyrics concise and well-punctuated.

faqItems.question: Can I reproduce a result exactly?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Set a fixed seed in the PrimitiveNode feeding KSampler. Using the same model, prompts, duration, steps, and CFG will produce highly consistent results.

b1ab45b906ca.title: Ideogram P-Image: Text to Image
b1ab45b906ca.description: Generate images from text descriptions using Ideogram's fast P-Image model, which delivers quality comparable to leading image models at significantly lower cost and latency. One text prompt is accepted and one image is output, with controls for quality level and resolution. Ideal for rapid iteration in design workflows, high-volume content production, and cost-sensitive A/B testing of visual concepts.
b1ab45b906ca.metaDescription: ComfyUI text-to-image with Ideogram P-Image. Control quality and resolution, preview results, and save outputs for fast, cost-effective visual iteration.
b1ab45b906ca.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a single text prompt into a finished image by calling Ideogram’s P-Image model through ComfyUI. It assembles your request with BuildJsonPromptIdeogram, sends it to the IdeogramPImage node (the API caller for the P-Image model), and returns the generated image for immediate viewing and export. You get simple controls for quality level and resolution so you can balance fidelity, speed, and cost per render.

PreviewAny provides live feedback at two key points: you can inspect the structured JSON payload before it’s sent, and you can review the returned image. CreateBoundingBoxes adds optional composition guides in the preview to help you plan framing or safe areas—useful when iterating on layouts—without constraining the actual generation. When you’re happy with the output, SaveImageAdvanced writes images to disk with flexible file naming, making it easy to archive versions and run batch iterations for design reviews or A/B testing.
howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI and open the graph. Locate the key nodes: BuildJsonPromptIdeogram, IdeogramPImage, PreviewAny, CreateBoundingBoxes, and SaveImageAdvanced.
Open IdeogramPImage and enter your Ideogram API credentials as required by the node. Select the P-Image model (if selectable), then choose your desired quality preset and resolution.
In BuildJsonPromptIdeogram, write a clear prompt describing the subject, style, and any key attributes. Ensure its quality and resolution fields match your targets (if exposed).
Optional: Use CreateBoundingBoxes to define composition guides (e.g., rule-of-thirds or text-safe regions). These boxes display in PreviewAny for planning but do not constrain the model’s output.

Queue the prompt. Watch PreviewAny: first confirm the JSON payload looks correct, then review the generated image once IdeogramPImage returns it. Adjust prompt, quality, or resolution and re-run to iterate.
When satisfied, configure SaveImageAdvanced (output folder, filename pattern, format) and run. The node will save your final images for sharing or further processing.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid design ideation for branding, thumbnails, and mood boards where fast iterations matter.
High-volume content generation for social posts or blog hero images with consistent settings.
Cost-sensitive A/B testing of ad visuals by varying prompt phrasing, quality, and resolution.
Early-stage product mockups or concept art to explore materials, lighting, and composition.
Internal creative reviews where previews, bounding-box guides, and named exports streamline feedback.

b34841f6789c.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Generate 5–15s text-to-video with MiniMax H3 (Hailuo-03), including native stereo audio, and save the clip with SaveVideo—no GPU required.
b34841f6789c.extendedDescription:

The MinimaxHailuo03TextToVideoNode sends your prompt to the MiniMax API, which renders a 5–15 second clip with native stereo audio. Because computation happens in the MiniMax cloud, you don’t need a local GPU to create results.

Technically, you control the generation by setting the text prompt (and optional negative prompt), duration, aspect ratio or resolution, and seed for reproducibility. Short, directive prompts with clear subjects, actions, and camera cues tend to perform best (for example: “A futuristic drone flies over neon city streets at night, smooth tracking shot, cinematic lighting”). The SaveVideo node finalizes the output path and filename, preserving the audio track produced by MiniMax H3, so you get an immediately shareable MP4 without extra post-processing.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm both nodes are present: MinimaxHailuo03TextToVideoNode and SaveVideo.
Open MinimaxHailuo03TextToVideoNode and enter your API credentials (as required by your setup), then write a concise prompt. Optionally add a negative prompt to avoid unwanted elements.
Set generation parameters: choose duration (5–15s), aspect ratio or resolution (e.g., 16:9, 9:16, or 1:1), and an optional seed if you want reproducible results.
Configure SaveVideo with your desired output path and filename (e.g., outputs/minimax_h3_clip.mp4).
Click Queue/Execute. The node will call the MiniMax API, generate the clip with stereo audio, and SaveVideo will write the returned video to disk.
Preview the result. If needed, iterate: refine the prompt (clear subject, action, style, and camera motion), adjust duration or aspect ratio, and re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept visualization for pitches, moodboards, and look development.
Short-form social media clips (vertical 9:16) with native audio for immediate posting.
Advertising and film pre-visualization: quick animatics to explore camera moves and blocking.
Product teasers and motion studies for marketing or e-commerce.

faqItems.question: Do I need a GPU to run this workflow?

faqItems.question: What video length can I generate?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is designed for short clips. Set the duration within the 5–15 second range supported by the MiniMax H3 model to ensure reliable results.

faqItems.question: Does the output include audio?
faqItems.answer: Yes. MiniMax H3 produces a video with native stereo audio. SaveVideo writes the clip to disk with the audio track included—no separate mixing is required.

faqItems.question: How can I improve prompt results?
faqItems.answer: Be specific and directive: include subject, action, setting, style, and camera motion (e.g., “slow dolly,” “aerial tracking”). Use a negative prompt to remove unwanted artifacts, and set a seed for consistent iterations.

b35c9fa7658c.title: Grok Imagine Image Quality: Edit
b35c9fa7658c.description: Enhance image quality with advanced text rendering and creative control using Grok Imagine Image Quality. Input images or prompts for improved detail and fidelity.

This ComfyUI workflow streamlines high-quality image editing with the Grok Imagine Image Quality service. It connects three nodes in a simple path: LoadImage brings in your source, GrokImageEditNode sends your instructions (prompt) and the image to Grok’s API for enhancement and text cleanup, and SaveImage writes the improved result to disk. Technically, GrokImageEditNode acts as the bridge to the Grok Imagine Image Quality endpoint, applying server-side upscaling, denoising, and advanced text rendering to improve clarity and readability while respecting your guidance. Your text prompt steers the edit (e.g., “sharpen details, clean signage text, preserve colors”), and any available controls in the node (such as strength, guidance, or resolution—depending on the node version) modulate how strongly the API alters the input. SaveImage then captures the returned image frames to your chosen output folder with your preferred filename prefix.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. Confirm the nodes are connected: LoadImage → GrokImageEditNode → SaveImage.

Provide input: either select a source image in LoadImage for image-to-image enhancement, or (if supported by your GrokImageEditNode version) run prompt-only without a source image to generate a new one.

Open GrokImageEditNode and enter a clear instruction prompt (e.g., “enhance detail, sharpen edges, fix garbled text, preserve layout”). If your node exposes options like strength, guidance, or output size, adjust them to control how aggressive the edit should be.
In SaveImage, set a descriptive filename prefix and verify the output directory. This helps you track iterations as you refine prompts.
Queue and run the workflow. Watch the GrokImageEditNode status; when complete, check the output folder for the enhanced image.
Iterate: refine your prompt for text-heavy scenes (keep wording concise, specify exact phrases, and ask for high contrast) and rerun to converge on the cleanest result.
suggestedUseCases: Cleaning up UI screenshots and slide graphics so small fonts and icons look crisp.
Polishing product photos by improving label legibility and fine surface details.
Restoring scanned posters or flyers with better text clarity and reduced noise.
Creating social media visuals with readable overlaid text from a concise prompt.
Upscaling and refining AI-generated images where text came out distorted.

faqItems.question: Do I need an API key to use GrokImageEditNode?

faqItems.question: Can I generate an image from text only, without an input image?

faqItems.question: How do I preserve composition while improving text and details?
faqItems.answer: Use restrained prompts that describe enhancement, not new content (e.g., “improve clarity, fix text, preserve layout”). If the node exposes a strength or guidance slider, lower values tend to keep the original composition more faithfully.

faqItems.question: What file formats are supported?
faqItems.answer: LoadImage typically supports common formats like PNG and JPG. SaveImage saves PNG by default in standard ComfyUI setups; adjust the node settings if your installation offers alternate formats.

b37902cee452.title: LTX-2.5: Image to Video
b37902cee452.description: Generate video from a single image using LTX-2.5, producing a high-fidelity clip with industry-leading pixel quality and native multishot capability that holds character, environment, and lighting across connected scenes. Ideal for cinematic production, VFX shot creation, and content pipelines requiring fast, locally deployable video generation.
b37902cee452.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: convert a single image into a high-quality video with LTX-2.5. Load, set resolution, render frames, and save to MP4—fully local.
b37902cee452.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a single still image into a smooth, high-fidelity video using LTX-2.5, Lightricks’ open video generation model. The pipeline is intentionally simple and production-minded: LoadImage ingests your source frame, ResolutionSelector locks in a model-friendly size (multiples of 32) and aspect ratio, the LTX-2.5 generator node (UUID: 6e397a2b-68f7-48f6-8930-f3a5491a163c) synthesizes a coherent motion sequence, and SaveVideo encodes the frames to a ready-to-use MP4. A MarkdownNote in the graph provides in-UI guidance and links.

Under the hood, LTX-2.5 uses a keyframes-first "Pixel Diffusion" approach to propagate detail and structure consistently across time. This helps preserve subject identity, lighting, and scene composition from your source image while introducing controllable motion. ResolutionSelector ensures your chosen 16:9 dimensions conform to model stride (multiples of 32), which is critical for stability and VRAM efficiency. Because it runs locally, you can iterate quickly, tune duration (frames/fps), and adjust motion strength to meet the needs of previz, VFX look development, and content pipelines.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then read the MarkdownNote for an overview and tips.
Open the LoadImage node and select your source image (e.g., input/neon_cyborg_portrait.png) or browse to your own asset.
Set output size in ResolutionSelector. Choose a 16:9 preset that matches your VRAM (e.g., 0.6 MP -> 1056x608). Keeping dimensions as multiples of 32 is required.

On the LTX-2.5 node (UUID 6e397a2b-68f7-48f6-8930-f3a5491a163c), set clip length and tempo by adjusting frame count and FPS. Optionally tune seed and motion intensity for more or less camera/subject movement.
Confirm SaveVideo settings (output path and FPS should match the generator). Queue the workflow and run.
When the job completes, retrieve the MP4 from the SaveVideo output folder and review. Iterate on resolution, frames/FPS, or motion settings as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic previz: generate quick moving plates from style frames to evaluate mood, lighting, and camera feel.
VFX look development: create motion studies from key concept art to test continuity of materials and lighting.
Product hero shots: turn a single packshot into a subtle orbit or parallax clip for promos and landing pages.
Social shorts and loops: produce eye-catching micro-animations from stills for reels, stories, and ads.
Animatic building blocks: rapidly assemble moving beats from boards before committing to full production.

faqItems.question: Why does the workflow use ResolutionSelector and multiples of 32?
faqItems.answer: LTX-2.5 (like many diffusion models) operates on stride-aligned dimensions. Using multiples of 32 prevents internal padding/resize artifacts, improves stability, and is more VRAM-efficient. The ResolutionSelector node helps you pick valid 16:9 sizes (e.g., 1056x608 for ~0.6 MP).

faqItems.question: How long can my clip be, and what affects render time?
faqItems.answer: Clip duration is frames ÷ FPS (e.g., 96 frames at 24 FPS ≈ 4 seconds). Render time and memory scale with resolution, frame count, and motion complexity. Start with modest settings (e.g., 0.6–0.8 MP, 64–96 frames, 16–24 FPS) and increase as your VRAM and iteration time allow.

faqItems.question: How do I keep the subject stable and avoid jitter?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, high-resolution source image with a clear subject and lighting. Keep output resolution stride-aligned, reduce motion intensity for more conservative movement, and consider raising FPS while keeping motion moderate. Re-seed if you see unwanted artifacts; stability often improves after a few trials.

faqItems.question: Does this support multishot timelines?
faqItems.answer: This template focuses on a single image-to-video clip. LTX-2.5 is designed to maintain coherent style and identity across shots, but to build a multishot timeline in ComfyUI, duplicate this block with Subgraph, render each shot, and stitch the resulting clips in your editor (or a separate combine step).

b58cf4e5cec5.title: Seedance 2.0: Text to Video
b58cf4e5cec5.description: Generate cinematic videos from text prompts with synchronized audio, controlled camera motion, and stable visuals. Input text descriptions to output high-quality video sequences.
b58cf4e5cec5.metaDescription: Create cinematic text-to-video clips in ComfyUI with Seedance 2.0. Control duration, fps, and resolution using ByteDance2TextToVideoNode, then export with SaveVideo.
b58cf4e5cec5.extendedDescription:
Seedance 2.0: Text to Video turns plain-language prompts into cinematic video clips inside ComfyUI. The workflow is built around ByteDance2TextToVideoNode running the Seedance 2.0 model to synthesize a coherent sequence of frames directly from text. You control duration (frame count), playback speed (fps), resolution, and seed, which together determine the look, timing, and repeatability of the output. SaveVideo then encodes the generated frames into a single video file (e.g., MP4/WebM) at your chosen frame rate.

Technically, ByteDance2TextToVideoNode conditions a video diffusion process on your prompt and iteratively produces a temporally consistent stack of images. Fixing the seed and keeping motion cues clear in the prompt helps maintain stable visuals across frames. Describing camera-like behavior in the text (e.g., “slow dolly in,” “static tripod,” “handheld”) guides motion without extra nodes. SaveVideo collects the node’s frame output and writes it to disk; if you need music or sound effects, export your video and sync audio later in a video editor.
howToUse: Load the Seedance 2.0: Text to Video workflow in ComfyUI and confirm ByteDance2TextToVideoNode is connected to SaveVideo.
Open ByteDance2TextToVideoNode and select the Seedance 2.0 model (or ensure it’s already loaded). Set resolution, frame count (duration), and fps.
Write a concise prompt describing subject, setting, mood, and motion (e.g., lens or camera feel). Optionally set a seed for repeatable results.
Run a short preview first (lower resolution and fewer frames) to check composition, motion, and style.
Refine the prompt and settings for stability (e.g., keep motion cues simple), then increase frames/resolution for a final render.
In SaveVideo, match the fps to the generation node, choose the container/codec and output path, then run to encode and save your video.
suggestedUseCases: Concept teasers and storyboards that visualize scripts or scene ideas quickly.
Social media intros and loops with controlled pacing and mood.
Product and feature previews where stable framing and motion are important.
Mood films for music tracks by timing clip duration to an external soundtrack.
Educational or explainer cutaways that illustrate abstract ideas visually.

faqItems.question: How do I keep visuals stable across frames?
faqItems.answer: Use a fixed seed, keep the subject and setting clearly defined in the prompt, and avoid conflicting motion cues. Start with a shorter duration to validate stability before rendering longer clips.

faqItems.question: How can I control camera motion?
faqItems.answer: Describe the motion in the prompt (e.g., “static shot,” “slow dolly-in,” “smooth pan left”). Clear, simple motion language tends to produce more predictable results than mixing multiple complex moves.

faqItems.question: What resolution and fps should I start with?
faqItems.answer: Begin at a modest resolution (e.g., 512–720p range) and 12–24 fps to iterate quickly. Once satisfied, scale up resolution or fps. Higher settings increase VRAM usage and render time.

faqItems.question: Does the workflow generate or embed audio?
faqItems.answer: No. This setup uses ByteDance2TextToVideoNode for visuals and SaveVideo for encoding. Export the video and add music or sound effects in your video editor for precise sync.

b594a01df1d6.title: Seedream 5.0 Pro: Image Edit
b594a01df1d6.description: Edit images with precision using Seedream 5.0 Pro, targeting specific regions while preserving lighting, depth, and texture. Ideal for product photography edits, portrait consistency adjustments, and creating structured layouts with multilingual text.
b594a01df1d6.metaDescription: Targeted, prompt-driven image edits with Seedream 5.0 Pro in ComfyUI. Mask regions, preserve lighting and depth, and export two comparison-ready outputs.
b594a01df1d6.extendedDescription:
Seedream 5.0 Pro: Image Edit is a precision image-to-image and inpainting workflow that lets you change exactly what you want while keeping the original lighting, depth, and texture intact. It starts with LoadImage to bring in your source photo, then optionally uses Painter to create a clean mask for targeted edits. The core transformation happens in ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2, which conditions on your input image (and mask if provided) to apply prompt-driven changes without destroying structure. Finally, SaveImageAdvanced writes out clean results with controllable filenames and folders.

Technically, the mask from Painter constrains edits to specific regions, while the input image conditioning helps Seedream preserve scene geometry and materials. You’ll get two outputs: a main edited image from ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 and a second preview that reflects the Painter-guided variant—useful for quick QA and before/after comparisons. Tuning typical parameters like prompt/negative prompt, denoise strength (how much to change vs. preserve), steps, guidance (CFG), and seed lets you dial in subtle retouches for product shots, keep consistent faces across a series, or lay out multilingual text in a structured composition.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and confirm the nodes: LoadImage → (optional) Painter → ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 → SaveImageAdvanced.
Open LoadImage and select your source photo (PNG/JPG). Keep the native resolution when possible for best structure retention.
Optional: Double-click Painter to brush a mask over areas you want changed. Paint white where edits should apply and leave black where the image must be preserved.

Configure ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2: set your prompt and negative prompt, choose a modest denoise strength for subtle edits (e.g., 0.2–0.45), adjust steps and guidance/CFG, and fix a seed for repeatable results.
Run the graph. The model will condition on your input (and mask if used) to produce two outputs: the main edited image and a Painter-informed preview for quick review.
In SaveImageAdvanced, set the output folder and filename pattern. Inspect both results, compare changes, and iterate by tweaking prompts, denoise strength, or the mask as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Product photography cleanup: remove dust, add subtle highlights, or swap labels while preserving material and lighting.
Portrait consistency: nudge hairstyle, makeup, or attire details across a series with a fixed seed and controlled denoise.
Structured layouts with multilingual text: place or refine text in specific areas using a mask for clean alignment.
Object replacement in scenes: change a prop or logo in a bounded region without disturbing background depth cues.

faqItems.question: What does ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 do in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: It’s the core image-to-image/inpainting model node. It conditions on your input image (and optional mask) plus your prompt to apply localized, structure-preserving edits.

faqItems.question: How do I limit changes to only part of the image?
faqItems.answer: Use the Painter node to create a mask: paint white where edits should occur and black where they should not. Feed this mask into ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2 so only the painted region is modified.

faqItems.question: How can I keep results consistent across multiple images?
faqItems.answer: Use the same prompt, negative prompt, seed, steps, guidance/CFG, and keep denoise strength low to moderate. Consistent framing and lighting in your source images also help Seedream preserve structure.

faqItems.question: Why do I get two outputs, and which one should I use?
faqItems.answer: The first is the main edited result from ByteDanceSeedreamNodeV2. The second is a Painter-guided preview that mirrors the masked edit for quick comparison. Use the main edited image for final delivery, and the preview for QA.

b6e55869de51.title: HiDream I1 Full
b6e55869de51.description: Generate images with HiDream I1 Full - Complete version with 50 inference steps for highest quality output.
b6e55869de51.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial for HiDream I1 Full: SD3-style text-to-image with 50 steps, UniPC sampler, and shift=3.0 for high-quality, prompt-accurate results.
b6e55869de51.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow generates high-quality images with the HiDream I1 Full model using a clean, SD3-style pipeline. It loads the HiDream UNet via UNETLoader, the matching text encoders with QuadrupleCLIPLoader, and prepares the canvas with EmptySD3LatentImage. Prompts are processed by CLIPTextEncode (positive and negative), sampling is configured through ModelSamplingSD3 (including the model-specific shift parameter), and KSampler performs 50 inference steps with the UniPC sampler and Simple scheduler for stable, detailed outputs. Finally, VAEDecode converts latents back to RGB and SaveImage writes the results to disk.

The included settings mirror HiDream’s official recommendations: steps=50, sampler=uni_pc, scheduler=simple, cfg=5.0, and shift=3.0. This combination is optimized for fidelity and prompt adherence, making it a strong starting point for cinematic, moody, or stylized scenes. Because the workflow uses EmptySD3LatentImage and QuadrupleCLIPLoader, it stays compatible with SD3-style prompts and latent geometry, while VAELoader ensures proper decoding for consistent color and detail.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI. In the “Step 1 - Load Models” group, point UNETLoader to your HiDream I1 Full weights (e.g., hidream_i1_full_fp16.safetensors or the fp8 variant) and set VAELoader to a HiDream-compatible VAE.
Use QuadrupleCLIPLoader to load the provided HiDream text encoders. Ensure all four encoders resolve correctly so CLIPTextEncode can process both positive and negative prompts.
In “Step 2 - Image size,” set EmptySD3LatentImage width/height, seed, and batch size. Use dimensions divisible by 8 (commonly by 64) for best stability and speed.
In “Step3 - Prompt,” enter your positive prompt in one CLIPTextEncode node and your negative prompt (e.g., "bad, ugly, jpeg artifacts") in the other. Keep prompts concise but descriptive.

Open ModelSamplingSD3 and confirm the official HiDream Full settings: shift=3.0. In KSampler, set steps=50, sampler=uni_pc, scheduler=simple, and cfg=5.0. Adjust only if you understand the trade-offs.
Run the graph. Inspect the decoded output from VAEDecode and retrieve final images from SaveImage. If needed, vary the seed or tweak width/height and prompts to iterate.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic concept art and moody environment design
Lo‑fi, grungy photography aesthetics (e.g., Polaroid-style looks)
Stylized product mockups with strong prompt control
Album covers and poster art requiring high detail and coherence
Atmospheric landscapes with dramatic lighting and color

faqItems.question: Which files do I need and where do they go?
faqItems.answer: Place the HiDream I1 Full UNet weights (e.g., hidream_i1_full_fp16.safetensors or the fp8 variant) in ComfyUI/models/unet. Load the HiDream text encoders via QuadrupleCLIPLoader (store them in your models/clip or text_encoders directory, matching your setup). Load a compatible VAE via VAELoader.

faqItems.question: What do the official sampling settings do?
faqItems.answer: They match HiDream’s recommended configuration: steps=50, sampler=uni_pc, scheduler=simple, cfg=5.0, and shift=3.0 (set in ModelSamplingSD3). This balance typically yields strong detail and prompt adherence with stable convergence.

faqItems.question: Can I change resolution, steps, or sampler?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Increase width/height (divisible by 8) for more detail at the cost of VRAM/time. Fewer steps (e.g., 30–40) are faster but may reduce fidelity. You can try other samplers/schedulers in KSampler, but UniPC + Simple is the recommended baseline for HiDream Full.

faqItems.question: How do I reduce artifacts or oversharpening?
faqItems.answer: Use a clear negative prompt (e.g., "bad, ugly, jpeg artifacts"). Keep CFG near 5.0, and avoid overly long prompts. If images look harsh, try a slightly lower CFG or reduce resolution. Ensure the correct VAE is loaded to prevent color or contrast issues.

b8c030205d86.title: Fast GAN Video Upscaler
b8c030205d86.description: Upload a video to upscale it using a fast GAN model. The output resolution is determined by your chosen model (e.g., 2x or 4x). For best results, upscale first, then resize to your target resolution.
b8c030205d86.metaDescription: Efficiently upscale videos using GAN models with ComfyUI's Fast GAN Video Upscaler workflow for high-quality video enhancement.
b8c030205d86.extendedDescription:
The Fast GAN Video Upscaler workflow is designed to efficiently upscale videos using a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) model, specifically Real-ESRGAN. This workflow is ideal for enhancing video resolution, making it suitable for applications where higher quality is desired without the need for creating new details, as diffusion models might. The workflow utilizes several key nodes, including the UpscaleModelLoader and ImageUpscaleWithModel, to apply the upscaling model to each frame of the video. It begins by loading your video with the LoadVideo node, breaking it down into frames with GetVideoComponents, and then applying the upscaling process.

Technically, the workflow leverages the Real-ESRGAN model to upscale each frame by a factor determined by the model (e.g., 2x or 4x). This is achieved through the ImageUpscaleWithModel node, which processes each frame individually before the frames are reassembled into a video using the CreateVideo node. Finally, the SaveVideo node outputs the upscaled video. This process is notably faster than diffusion-based methods, making it a practical solution for quick enhancements. For optimal results, it is recommended to first upscale the video to the highest desired resolution and then resize it to the target resolution if needed.
howToUse: Load the Fast GAN Video Upscaler workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadVideo node to upload your video file.
Select the desired upscale model (e.g., 2x or 4x) in the UpscaleModelLoader node.
Run the workflow to process the video frames with ImageUpscaleWithModel.
Reassemble the upscaled frames into a video using the CreateVideo node.
Save the final upscaled video using the SaveVideo node.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing low-resolution videos for better viewing on high-definition displays.
Preparing video content for platforms that require higher resolution uploads.
Improving the quality of archived videos for digital restoration projects.
Upscaling video game footage for content creators and streamers.
Optimizing video quality for professional presentations or marketing materials.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow add new details to my video?
faqItems.answer: No, this workflow uses GAN models to enhance existing details but cannot create new details like diffusion models.

faqItems.question: What is the best model to use for upscaling?
faqItems.answer: The choice of model depends on your needs; a 2x model doubles the resolution, while a 4x model quadruples it. Choose based on your desired output size.

faqItems.question: How fast is this upscaling process?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is designed to be faster than diffusion-based methods, making it suitable for quick video enhancements.

faqItems.question: Should I resize the video after upscaling?
faqItems.answer: For best results, it's recommended to upscale to the highest resolution first and then resize to your target resolution if necessary.

b92d5bd634b5.title: Tripo: Multiview to Model
b92d5bd634b5.description: Build 3D models from multiple angles with Tripo's advanced scanner.
b92d5bd634b5.metaDescription: Convert 2D images into detailed 3D models with Tripo's advanced multiview scanner in ComfyUI.
b92d5bd634b5.extendedDescription:
The 'Tripo: Multiview to Model' workflow is designed to transform a series of 2D images into a detailed 3D model using ComfyUI's robust node system. This workflow leverages the Tripo model, which is specifically tailored for creating 3D representations from multiple image angles. It begins with the 'LoadImage' node to import your images, followed by the 'TripoMultiviewToModelNode' that processes these images to construct a basic 3D model. The workflow then employs several specialized nodes, such as 'TripoRefineNode' and 'TripoRigNode', to enhance the model's details and prepare it for animation or further use.

The process is completed with nodes like 'TripoTextureNode' for adding realistic textures and 'SaveGLB' to export the final 3D model in a widely compatible format. This workflow is particularly useful for creators needing to generate 3D assets from limited visual data, making it ideal for applications in gaming, virtual reality, and digital art. By using multiple angles, the workflow ensures a comprehensive capture of the subject's geometry, resulting in a high-fidelity 3D model.
howToUse: Load your 2D images into the workflow using the 'LoadImage' node. Ensure you have at least two different angles.
Activate the 'TripoMultiviewToModelNode' to begin processing your images into a 3D model.
Use the 'TripoRefineNode' to enhance the model's details and improve accuracy.
Apply the 'TripoTextureNode' to add realistic textures to your model.
Preview your model using the 'Preview3D' node to check for errors or adjustments.
Export the final model using the 'SaveGLB' node for use in various applications.
suggestedUseCases: Creating 3D models for video game assets from concept art.
Developing virtual reality environments with realistic objects.
Producing digital art that requires detailed 3D representations.
Generating 3D models for educational tools and simulations.
Enhancing architectural visualizations with detailed 3D objects.

faqItems.question: What types of images are best for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: High-resolution images with clear details from multiple angles are ideal for achieving the best results.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow with only one image?
faqItems.answer: At least two images from different angles are required to create an accurate 3D model.

faqItems.question: What file format does the final model export as?
faqItems.answer: The final 3D model is exported in the GLB format, which is widely compatible with various 3D applications.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to animate the models created with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the 'TripoRigNode' prepares the model for animation by adding necessary rigging components.

b95499a55c9f.title: InfiniteTalk: Audio-Driven Full-Body Video Dubbing
b95499a55c9f.description: Upload a source Image and target audio. Generate a full-body dubbed video with synchronized motion while preserving the original identity, background, and camera movement.
b95499a55c9f.metaDescription: Create full-body dubbed videos from a single image and audio with Wan2.1 InfiniteTalk. Multi-speaker, lip-synced, camera-aware results in ComfyUI.
b95499a55c9f.extendedDescription: InfiniteTalk: Audio-Driven Full-Body Video Dubbing turns a single image and one or more audio tracks into a lip‑synced, full‑body video while preserving the original identity, background, and camera motion. The core of the pipeline is WanInfiniteTalkToVideo, which fuses features from the loaded Wan2.1 I2V model with an audio embedding to drive body and facial motion. Step1 - Load Models prepares the UNet and VAE (UNETLoader, VAELoader) for image‑to‑video synthesis, and loads text and audio backbones (CLIPLoader with CLIPTextEncode for camera/stage prompts, and AudioEncoderLoader with AudioEncoderEncode for voice features). You import the starting frame via LoadImage, then draw masks per character in the MaskEditor to localize motion to each speaker.
howToUse: Load the workflow and models. In Step1 - Load Models, point UNETLoader to Wan2_1-I2V-14B-480p_fp8 (diffusion model), load the matching VAELoader and CLIPLoader, and set AudioEncoderLoader to the provided InfiniteTalk audio encoder. Optional: apply LoraLoaderModelOnly or ModelPatchLoader if you need a style/character LoRA or an InfiniteTalk patch.

Import the start frame and create masks. Upload your image in LoadImage, then right‑click it and choose Open in MaskEditor. Brush a clean mask for Character 1 (include mouth, jaw, upper torso for natural motion). Repeat in the Step2/Step3 Character Audio and Mask groups for additional speakers, each with its own mask.

Add audio and arrange dialogue. Use LoadAudio for each speaker line. If you have multiple clips or alternating speakers, connect them with AudioConcat to build the final timeline. Keep one speaker per track when possible for cleaner lip sync.

Set prompt and conditioning. In Step3 - Prompt, describe camera behavior and scene (e.g., “The camera zooms in. Two characters are talking.”). If you want to minimize text bias and preserve the original look, use ConditioningZeroOut to dampen or remove CLIP conditioning.

Choose size and duration. In Video Size, set width/height (default 480p for the Wan2.1 I2V weights). To match longer audio, duplicate the Video Extend group: each copy adds 81 frames at 25 fps (~3.24 s). As a rule of thumb, number_of_extends = ceil(audio_length_seconds / 3.24). Select the Video Extend group box, press Ctrl‑C then Ctrl‑Shift‑V to duplicate until the total duration covers your audio.

Generate and export. Run the graph. VAEDecode, ImageBatch, and ImageFromBatch will assemble frames; CreateVideo compiles them at your chosen fps (typically 25), and SaveVideo writes the final file. Review the result; if you see drift or over‑motion, refine masks, simplify the prompt, or reduce/add LoRA influence.
suggestedUseCases: Localizing short commercial clips: keep the scene and actor identity while dubbing into a new language.
Animating character posters or key art into short talking segments with natural camera moves.
Previsualization and animatics: block dialogue timing and staging before full production.
Social content and explainers: turn a still host image into a voiced full‑body presenter.
Dialogue mock‑ups with two speakers using separate audio tracks and masks.

faqItems.question: What models and nodes are essential for this to work?
faqItems.answer: At minimum: UNETLoader with Wan2.1 I2V 14B 480p weights, VAELoader, CLIPLoader + CLIPTextEncode (for camera/scene prompts), AudioEncoderLoader + AudioEncoderEncode (for voice features), LoadImage for the start frame, WanInfiniteTalkToVideo to drive motion, VAEDecode to get frames, and CreateVideo/SaveVideo to export. LoraLoaderModelOnly and ModelPatchLoader are optional for style or InfiniteTalk patches.

faqItems.question: How do I match the video length to my audio?
faqItems.answer: Use the Video Extend group. Each copy adds 81 frames at 25 fps (~3.24 s). Compute ceil(audio_seconds / 3.24) and duplicate the group that many times (box‑select, Ctrl‑C, then Ctrl‑Shift‑V). If you have multiple audio clips, assemble them with AudioConcat first so the total duration is clear.

faqItems.question: Why does the background or identity drift?
faqItems.answer: Over‑strong text or style conditioning can push the look away from the source. Reduce CLIP influence using ConditioningZeroOut, avoid heavy style LoRAs (or lower their weight in LoraLoaderModelOnly), and keep prompts descriptive (camera, staging) rather than stylistic. Also ensure masks are tight around speaking characters so motion doesn’t bleed into the background.

faqItems.question: What audio format works best and how do I improve lip sync?
faqItems.answer: Use clean, single‑speaker audio per track where possible. Common WAV/MP3 files load via LoadAudio; if a file fails, convert to a standard WAV (e.g., 16–48 kHz, mono). Better lip sync comes from clear diction and minimal background noise. For multi‑speaker scenes, keep separate audio files and masks per character and arrange them with AudioConcat.

b993c1885a29.title: Flux.1 Dev: Text to Image
b993c1885a29.description: Generate high-quality images with Flux Dev full version. Requires larger VRAM and multiple model files, but provides the best prompt following capability and image quality.
b993c1885a29.metaDescription: Generate high-quality images from text prompts using the Flux.1 Dev workflow in ComfyUI, optimized for best prompt adherence and image quality.
b993c1885a29.extendedDescription: This ComfyUI workflow, titled 'Flux.1 Dev: Text to Image', is designed to generate high-quality images from text prompts using the Flux Dev full version. The workflow leverages multiple model files and requires substantial VRAM to operate effectively. It is particularly noted for its superior prompt-following capabilities and exceptional image quality. Key components of this workflow include the VAEDecode and SaveImage nodes, which are responsible for decoding the latent representations into images and saving the final output, respectively. The KSampler node plays a crucial role in sampling the latent space to generate diverse image outputs. The workflow also utilizes the UNETLoader and VAELoader nodes for loading the UNET and VAE models, which are essential for the diffusion process. Additionally, the CLIPTextEncodeFlux node encodes the text prompt into a format that the model can understand, ensuring that the generated images closely align with the input text.
howToUse: Load the 'Flux.1 Dev: Text to Image' workflow in ComfyUI.
Ensure you have the necessary models: flux1-dev.safetensors and the text encoders clip_l.safetensors and t5xxl_fp16.safetensors.
In Step 2, configure the desired image size according to your VRAM capacity.
In Step 3, enter your text prompt to guide the image generation process.
Run the workflow to generate the image, and use the SaveImage node to save the output to your desired location.
suggestedUseCases: Creating concept art for visual storytelling projects.
Generating high-quality images for digital marketing campaigns.
Producing unique artwork for personal or commercial use.
Developing visual content for social media posts.
Designing custom graphics for websites or applications.

faqItems.question: What are the hardware requirements for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: This workflow requires a larger VRAM due to the multiple model files and high-quality image generation process. A GPU with at least 8GB of VRAM is recommended.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow with any text prompt?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow is designed to follow prompts closely, but the quality and relevance of the generated image depend on the clarity and specificity of the prompt.

faqItems.question: How can I improve the quality of the generated images?
faqItems.answer: Ensure that you are using the correct model files and that your prompts are detailed and specific. Adjusting the image size settings to match your VRAM capacity can also help improve quality.

faqItems.question: What should I do if the generated images do not match my prompt?
faqItems.answer: Try refining your text prompt for clarity and specificity. Additionally, ensure that all model files are correctly loaded and compatible with the workflow.

ba62b8d37772.title: AnimateDiff -  IPAdapters Looping Animation
ba62b8d37772.description: Drag and drop then dream through a stack of images
ba62b8d37772.metaDescription: Create smooth looping animations between images using AnimateDiff and IPAdapters in ComfyUI. Perfect for artists and content creators.

This ComfyUI workflow, titled 'AnimateDiff - IPAdapters Looping Animation,' is designed to create seamless animated transitions between a series of images. It leverages the power of Stable Diffusion 1.5 (SD1.5) along with custom nodes such as 'comfyui-animatediff-evolved' and 'comfyui_ipadapter_plus' to achieve fluid animations. The workflow uses a combination of nodes like 'VHS_VideoCombine' and 'ImageBatchMulti' to process multiple images in sequence, creating a looping animation effect. By utilizing Weighted IPAdapters, the workflow ensures that each image transition maintains a consistent style and theme, enhancing the overall visual coherence of the animation.

Technically, the workflow begins with loading images into the 'LoadImage' node, which are then scaled appropriately using the 'ImageScaleToTotalPixels' node. The 'ImageBatchMulti' node is crucial for handling multiple images, allowing them to be processed as a batch. The 'VHS_VideoCombine' node plays a pivotal role in merging these images into a continuous video loop. This setup is particularly useful for artists and content creators looking to produce engaging visual content that smoothly transitions between different scenes or concepts. The integration of the 'comfyui-videohelpersuite' further aids in refining the video output, ensuring high-quality animations.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure all necessary custom nodes are installed.
Add your images to the 'ImageBatchMulti' node. These images will form the sequence of your animation.
Adjust the image scaling using the 'ImageScaleToTotalPixels' node to ensure uniformity across the animation.
Configure the 'Weighted IPAdapters' settings to maintain a consistent style throughout the animation.
Use the 'VHS_VideoCombine' node to merge the images into a looping video.
Preview the animation and make any necessary adjustments before exporting the final video.
suggestedUseCases: Creating animated storyboards for visual storytelling.
Developing dynamic video content for social media platforms.
Designing seamless transitions in digital art projects.
Producing looping animations for video backgrounds in presentations.
Crafting visually appealing animations for music videos.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of the 'Weighted IPAdapters' in this workflow?

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow with other versions of Stable Diffusion?

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the images transition smoothly?

faqItems.question: Is it possible to add audio to the animations created with this workflow?

baa06a413558.title: Seedance 2.0 Image to Video
baa06a413558.description: This workflow is an easy start for generating 4-15 second videos from a single image, using Seedance 2.0
baa06a413558.metaDescription: Turn a single image into a 4–15s video in ComfyUI with Seedance 2.0. LoadImage → ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode → SaveVideo. Simple setup, adjustable motion.
baa06a413558.extendedDescription:
Seedance 2.0 Image to Video turns a single still image into a short, natural-looking video. The workflow is intentionally minimal: LoadImage brings your source photo or artwork into the graph, ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode (powered by Seedance 2.0) synthesizes motion and generates a sequence of frames, and SaveVideo encodes the result as a playable clip. It’s a fast, focused way to create 4–15 second motion from a static image without extra conditioning or complex control nodes.

Technically, ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode uses Seedance 2.0 to infer a coherent motion arc anchored by consistent first and last frames, then interpolates the in-betweens to preserve subject structure and style. You control core parameters such as clip length (seconds or frames), frames-per-second, motion intensity, and (if exposed by your version) a seed for repeatability. The node outputs a frame sequence that SaveVideo compiles into a video at the chosen fps. For best results, start with a clean, well-lit image where the main subject is centered, keep motion strength moderate, and target 6–10 seconds for the most natural movement.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI and confirm the ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode (Seedance 2.0) model files are installed and detected. If the node shows missing weights, install them per the node’s repository instructions.
Open LoadImage and select your source image. Use a clean, subject-focused photo or artwork; 720–1080 px on the longer side is a good starting point for speed and quality.

Select ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode and set the clip duration (e.g., 4–15 seconds) and frames-per-second. Start with moderate motion strength; if your node version exposes a seed, set one to make results reproducible.
Queue the workflow. If you run out of VRAM or it’s slow, reduce input resolution, shorten duration, or lower fps, then re-run.
In SaveVideo, choose the output path, filename, and ensure fps matches the generation. Queue again to encode and save the video file.
Review the result and iterate: adjust motion strength, try different seeds, or fine-tune duration/fps. For smoother motion, keep durations modest and avoid extreme motion on busy backgrounds.
suggestedUseCases: Create subtle product spins or portrait cinemagraphs for social posts from a single still.
Add animated hero banners or background loops to websites using brand imagery.
Generate quick B-roll from stock photos to fill gaps in edits or mood films.
Animate concept art and storyboards to explore motion and pacing early in production.
Produce eye-catching motion thumbnails or interstitials from static key art.

faqItems.question: What image size and aspect ratio should I use?
faqItems.answer: Use clean, well-lit images around 768–1080 px on the long edge for a good quality/speed balance. Keep your desired aspect ratio; the node will resize if needed, but larger inputs require more VRAM and time.

faqItems.question: My video looks jittery or warps the subject. How can I improve it?
faqItems.answer: Lower the motion strength, shorten the duration, and increase fps if possible. Start with simpler, subject-centered images and try a different seed for stability. Reducing background clutter also helps.

faqItems.question: How do I control clip length precisely?
faqItems.answer: Set duration (in seconds or frames) in ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode and match that fps in SaveVideo. Duration = frames ÷ fps, so verify both to get the exact length you expect.

faqItems.question: Can I make a seamless loop?
faqItems.answer: Seamless loops aren’t guaranteed, but the node’s first/last frame consistency can help. Keep motion subtle and cyclical, aim for similar start/end framing, and if needed, trim or crossfade the ends in an external editor.

badeb885763a.title: HiDream I1 Fast
badeb885763a.description: Generate images quickly with HiDream I1 Fast - Lightweight version with 16 inference steps, ideal for rapid previews on lower-end hardware.
badeb885763a.metaDescription: Generate fast text-to-image previews with HiDream I1 Fast in ComfyUI. SD3-style sampling, 16 steps, and FP8 UNet for low VRAM and quick iterations.
badeb885763a.extendedDescription:
HiDream I1 Fast is a lightweight text-to-image workflow tuned for rapid previews and low-VRAM GPUs. It pairs the HiDream I1 Fast FP8 UNet (loaded with UNETLoader) with SD3-style sampling (ModelSamplingSD3) and runs just 16 inference steps in KSampler. Prompts are handled through QuadrupleCLIPLoader and CLIPTextEncode, while EmptySD3LatentImage creates the starting latent at your chosen resolution. The result is a fast, responsive pipeline that’s ideal for exploring ideas and iterating on compositions without long waits.

Technically, the workflow loads a matching VAE via VAELoader and decodes samples with VAEDecode, then writes outputs using SaveImage. ModelSamplingSD3 exposes the HiDream/SD3 “shift” parameter (commonly around 3.0 per official guidance) to balance prompt conditioning across multiple text encoders. Because the UNet is FP8 and the step count is low, VRAM use stays modest, making this a practical option for laptops or older GPUs while still producing coherent, stylized results.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI, then install/place models: put hidream_i1_fast_fp8.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models and the HiDream text encoders (e.g., clip_l_hidream) in ComfyUI/models/text_encoders. Ensure a compatible VAE is available in ComfyUI/models/vae.
Step 1 – Load Models: In UNETLoader, select hidream_i1_fast_fp8.safetensors. In QuadrupleCLIPLoader, choose the HiDream-compatible text encoders. In VAELoader, pick the VAE that matches HiDream/SD3.
Step 2 – Image size: Set your target resolution and batch size in EmptySD3LatentImage. Start with 768×768 (or 1024×576 for wides) to keep VRAM low; larger sizes cost more memory.
Step 3 – Prompt: Enter your positive and negative prompts using CLIPTextEncode. For negatives, try phrases like “bad, ugly, jpeg artifacts” to suppress common defects.

Sampling and quality: In ModelSamplingSD3, keep shift around 3.0 as a starting point (from official HiDream guidance). In KSampler, use 16 steps for speed; you can raise steps for cleaner details. Sampler/scheduler are user-selectable—uni_pc with a simple scheduler is a solid default per HiDream’s notes.

Generate: Execute the workflow. Inspect the output from VAEDecode and SaveImage. If results look soft or off-prompt, adjust shift slightly, raise steps to 20–24, refine negatives, or try a different sampler, then re-run.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept exploration for illustrations and environment studies
Style and composition iteration when art-directing a scene
Quick thumbnails and moodboards on lower-end or mobile GPUs
Batching lightweight previews before committing to high-quality renders
Fast negative-prompt testing to diagnose and reduce artifacts

faqItems.question: How do I reduce VRAM usage further?
faqItems.answer: Keep steps at 16, lower resolution in EmptySD3LatentImage, reduce batch size to 1, and ensure you’re using the FP8 model (hidream_i1_fast_fp8.safetensors). Larger images and higher steps raise memory use.

faqItems.question: What does the SD3 shift parameter do?
faqItems.answer: The ModelSamplingSD3 shift balances conditioning across the multiple text encoders used by HiDream/SD3-style models. Start near 3.0 (official guidance) and adjust slightly if prompts feel over/under-strong.

faqItems.question: Which sampler should I use?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is sampler-agnostic. Per HiDream’s notes, uni_pc with a simple scheduler is a reliable default. If you need different behavior, try Euler or DPM++ variants and compare results at the same step count.

faqItems.question: How can I improve quality if images look blurry or off-prompt?
faqItems.answer: Increase steps moderately (e.g., 20–24), refine your positive/negative prompts, tweak shift (±0.5), and consider a slightly higher resolution. Also set a fixed seed in KSampler for reproducible tuning.

bb33cc433026.title: LTX-2.3: FLF2V
bb33cc433026.description: Upload a starting image to generate a video sequence. The workflow creates a short video with consistent style and motion, beginning with your provided frame.
bb33cc433026.metaDescription: Turn a single image into a short, coherent video with LTX-2.3. Guide motion via prompts, keep style consistent, and export ready-to-share video.
bb33cc433026.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow, built around the LTX-2.3 video model, turns a single reference image into a short, coherent video clip with controllable motion and style. It uses your uploaded first frame (LoadImage in the First Frame group) as a strong visual anchor, optionally blends in an ending reference from the Last Frame group, and lets you steer the scene with natural language prompts. Text conditioning is handled by CLIPTextEncode and LTXAVTextEncoderLoader in the Conditioning group, while LTXVAddGuide fuses your reference frame(s) into the model’s conditioning stream.

Under the hood, EmptyLTXVLatentVideo creates the video latent with your chosen resolution, frame count, and FPS. RandomNoise seeds the generation, and sampling is performed with SamplerEulerAncestral guided by CFGGuider and a ManualSigmas schedule for stable, consistent motion. LTXVConcatAVLatent pairs the video latent with an audio latent (LTXVEmptyLatentAudio by default, resulting in silence) so your output is a proper A/V container. Final frames are decoded efficiently with VAEDecodeTiled and written to disk via SaveVideo. Utility nodes like GetImageSize and LTXVCropGuides help you frame the subject reliably, and LTXVPreprocess normalizes your input image to the model’s expected space. The result is a fast, practical pipeline for turning a single image into a smooth, on-style video clip.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the LTX nodes are installed. In the Model group (LTXVConditioning), set the model to LTX-2.3.
In the First Frame group, connect your starting image to LoadImage. Use LTXVCropGuides and GetImageSize to check framing, and let LTXVPreprocess normalize the image.
Optionally, add an ending reference image in the Last Frame group. Adjust LTXVAddGuide so the first/last frames guide strength matches how tightly you want to preserve look and layout.

In the Prompt group, enter your positive and negative text prompts via CLIPTextEncode. Describe motion over time (e.g., camera moves), visual specifics, and optional audio cues (these condition visuals; the default audio track is silent).

Open the Settings and Sampling groups: set frames/FPS/resolution in EmptyLTXVLatentVideo, pick a seed in RandomNoise, then tune CFGGuider (guidance scale) and SamplerEulerAncestral steps. Leave ManualSigmas at defaults unless you need a custom schedule.

Run the graph. Inspect the decoded frames from VAEDecodeTiled, then export with SaveVideo. If results drift from your subject, increase guide strength or reduce steps/CFG slightly and re-run with the same seed.
suggestedUseCases: Turning a character portrait or product shot into a simple camera move (dolly, tilt, or orbit) for social posts.
Storyboarding: create short motion beats from a single keyframe to communicate camera direction and pacing.
Style-lock reels: maintain a consistent aesthetic across multiple clips by reusing the same first frame and prompt.
Before/after transitions: guide toward a last-frame reference to visualize a transformation over a few seconds.
Silent hero loops for websites and UI backgrounds, rendered at lightweight resolutions and FPS.

faqItems.question: How do I control duration, FPS, and resolution?
faqItems.answer: Use EmptyLTXVLatentVideo in the Settings group. Set frame count for duration, FPS for playback speed, and width/height for resolution. VAEDecodeTiled helps decode higher resolutions on limited VRAM.

faqItems.question: Why does the video drift from my reference image?
faqItems.answer: Increase the guide weight in LTXVAddGuide, reduce CFG in CFGGuider, or lower sampling steps in SamplerEulerAncestral. Using a stable seed (RandomNoise) and keeping ManualSigmas at defaults often improves consistency.

faqItems.question: Can I add or generate audio?
faqItems.answer: This template wires LTXVEmptyLatentAudio, so the output is silent by default. You can keep it silent or replace that node with real audio latents. Text like “Music: …” conditions the visuals but does not synthesize audio in this setup.

faqItems.question: Do I need a last-frame image?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow works with just the first frame. Supplying a last frame and tuning LTXVAddGuide can help target a specific end look or facilitate smooth start–end transitions.

bd874c5e02d6.title: Generate UGC Video With Voice Clone
bd874c5e02d6.description: Upload an image to generate AI prompts and synthesize speech. Create a final video with accurate lip sync using Eleven Labs and LTX Video.
bd874c5e02d6.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow: auto-generate script from an image, clone voice with ElevenLabs, and create lip-synced UGC video using LTX‑2.3.
bd874c5e02d6.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow turns a single image into a short, lip‑synced UGC-style video with cloned or selected voice. It chains three stages: prompt creation from your uploaded image, speech synthesis with ElevenLabs, and video generation with LTX‑2.3. The Create Prompt group routes the image from LoadImage into GeminiNode to auto-generate two texts: a performance-ready speech script (with expression tags) and a scene description. RegexExtract parses the Gemini response to separate the “speech” and “scene” sections cleanly for downstream nodes.

For audio, you can pick a preset voice via ElevenLabsVoiceSelector or bring your own tone with ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone, then synthesize the final narration in ElevenLabsTextToSpeech and optionally save it with SaveAudioMP3. The Create Video group feeds the scene description and the audio into the LTX‑2.3 video node (UUID: 98fb87e2-23b5-4ecb-aacc-365912414a12) to produce a talking-style video with accurate lip sync, previewed by PreviewAny and written with SaveVideo. This setup is practical for rapid UGC, product explainers, testimonials, or social posts because it automates script writing from an image and guarantees voice-to-lips alignment through ElevenLabs + LTX.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the MarkdownNote for on-canvas tips. Confirm you have API keys set for Gemini (in GeminiNode) and ElevenLabs (in ElevenLabs nodes).

In Load Image, upload your reference image. Run the Create Prompt group to let GeminiNode generate both a speech script (with expression tags) and a scene description. RegexExtract will split these into separate outputs.

Choose a voice: either pick a preset in ElevenLabsVoiceSelector or clone a new one with ElevenLabsInstantVoiceClone (upload a clean 1–2 minute sample). Connect the chosen voice output to ElevenLabsTextToSpeech.
Generate narration: paste or pass the speech prompt into ElevenLabsTextToSpeech and run it. Use PreviewAny to audition the audio. Optionally, write it to disk with SaveAudioMP3.

Create the video: feed the scene description and the generated audio into the LTX‑2.3 video node (UUID: 98fb87e2-23b5-4ecb-aacc-365912414a12) inside the Create Video group. Adjust duration or other available parameters as needed.

Run the final graph. Inspect the result in PreviewAny, then export with SaveVideo. If running locally and you want sharper output, place the LTX upscaler model (ltx-2.3-spatial-upscaler-x2-1.1.safetensors) in your latent_upscale_models folder before rendering.
suggestedUseCases: UGC-style product demos: turn a product image into a short spoken walkthrough with brand-aligned voice.
Testimonials and reviews: generate a talking-head style clip from a customer photo with a friendly, cloned voice.
Social promos: quickly draft scripts from campaign visuals and render lip-synced shorts for TikTok/Reels.
Educational snippets: create narrator-led explainers from illustrative images with expressive TTS.
Creator voice packs: clone your voice once, then reuse it across multiple image-to-video posts.

faqItems.question: Do I need API keys to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Provide a valid Gemini API key in GeminiNode for prompt generation and an ElevenLabs API key in the ElevenLabs nodes for voice selection/cloning and TTS. Without Gemini, you can bypass that step by manually writing the speech and scene prompts.

faqItems.question: How does the workflow keep lips in sync with the audio?
faqItems.answer: The generated narration from ElevenLabsTextToSpeech is fed directly into the LTX‑2.3 video node, which uses the audio to align mouth movements. Keeping the final TTS file as the exact audio source ensures accurate lip sync.

faqItems.question: Can I bring my own pre-recorded narration instead of TTS?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use LoadAudio to input your narration and connect it where the TTS audio would go in the Create Video group. Skip the ElevenLabsTextToSpeech step in that case.

faqItems.question: What does RegexExtract do in this graph?
faqItems.answer: GeminiNode returns both a speech script and a scene description. RegexExtract parses that response into two clean outputs—one for ElevenLabsTextToSpeech (speech prompt) and one for the LTX‑2.3 video node (scene prompt)—to keep the pipeline reliable.

be07722555ff.title: Flux.1 Outpaint
be07722555ff.description: Extend images beyond boundaries using Flux.1 outpainting.
be07722555ff.metaDescription: Extend images beyond boundaries with Flux.1 Outpaint in ComfyUI. Perfect for creating larger scenes and enhancing image contexts.
be07722555ff.extendedDescription:

This technique is particularly useful for enhancing images by adding context or creating a larger scene from an existing image. The workflow utilizes several key nodes and models, including the Flux.1 model for outpainting, which is guided by the FluxGuidance node. The process begins with loading the necessary models and the image to be outpainted, followed by padding the image using the ImagePadForOutpaint node to prepare it for expansion. The KSampler node is then used to iteratively generate new image sections, while the VAEDecode and UNETLoader nodes work together to ensure the generated content blends seamlessly with the original image.

This workflow is particularly useful because it leverages advanced AI models to maintain the aesthetic and thematic consistency of the original image while expanding its boundaries. The use of the CLIPTextEncode node allows for the incorporation of textual prompts, guiding the outpainting process to align with specific themes or styles. This makes the workflow versatile for various applications, from artistic image creation to practical uses in design and media production.
howToUse: Load the Flux.1 Outpaint workflow in ComfyUI.
Import the image you wish to extend using the LoadImage node.
Ensure the necessary models are loaded, including Flux.1 and related text encoders.
Use the ImagePadForOutpaint node to prepare the image for outpainting.
Run the workflow to generate the extended image using KSampler and VAEDecode nodes.

suggestedUseCases: Enhancing landscape photography by extending horizons.
Creating panoramic images from standard-sized photos.
Adding contextual elements to product images for marketing.
Expanding artwork for digital displays or print media.
Generating immersive backgrounds for virtual environments.

faqItems.question: What is outpainting?
faqItems.answer: Outpainting is the process of extending an image beyond its original boundaries by generating new content that blends seamlessly with the existing image.

faqItems.question: Do I need specific hardware to run this workflow?

faqItems.question: Can I control the style of the outpainted area?

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for all types of images?
