bea767ed39db.title: Topaz: Image Enhance Wonder 3.5
bea767ed39db.description: Upscale and enhance a single image using Topaz's Wonder 3.5 generative model, which adds fine detail, reduces noise, and sharpens text and structured graphics while offering Low, Medium, and High enhancement strengths. The workflow takes 1 input image and produces 1 enhanced output alongside a side-by-side comparison view. Ideal for restoring old or compressed photos, improving product shots and marketing visuals, and preparing low-resolution images for print or large-format display.
bea767ed39db.metaDescription: Compare Topaz Wonder 3.5 Low, Medium, and High enhancement strengths side-by-side to choose the best balance of detail, noise, and text clarity.
bea767ed39db.extendedDescription:
This workflow compares an original image against a Topaz Wonder 3.5–enhanced result using a simple, controlled A/B setup. The LoadImage node provides the source, TopazImageEnhanceV2 applies Wonder 3.5 with a selectable enhancement strength (Low, Medium, or High), and ImageCompare renders a side-by-side view so you can judge fine detail, noise handling, and text/edge clarity. SaveImageAdvanced captures outputs so you can review results across runs.

Methodologically, you hold the model and input constant and vary only the enhancement strength across sequential runs. Low generally preserves natural texture and grain while reducing noise modestly; Medium aims for a balanced boost in detail and denoising; High pushes aggressive detail synthesis, stronger sharpening, and more assertive noise removal. Expect sharper text and structured graphics at higher strengths, but watch for oversharpening, altered grain, or fabricated micro-texture—especially on skin and smooth gradients. Use the A/B view to decide which trade-off best suits your subject and output requirements.
howToUse: Load your source image with the LoadImage node.
Open TopazImageEnhanceV2 and confirm the Wonder 3.5 model is selected; choose an enhancement strength (Low, Medium, or High).
Run the workflow. Use ImageCompare to review the original versus the enhanced output at 100% zoom and at the target display/print size.
Save the result with SaveImageAdvanced, adding the chosen strength to the filename or subfolder for easy tracking.
Repeat the run with a different strength using the same input. Save each version with a clear label (e.g., _low, _medium, _high).
Evaluate trade-offs: check text legibility, edge halos, skin texture, noise patterns, and any signs of fabricated detail. Select the setting that fits your use case.
suggestedUseCases: Photo restoration: find the strength that cleans compression noise while preserving film grain and natural skin texture.
E-commerce/product shots: balance crisp edges and label/text clarity without introducing sharpening halos.
Large-format print and signage: push detail and text sharpness as far as acceptable for viewing distance.
UI screenshots, documents, and technical diagrams: maximize legibility of small text and thin lines.
Upscaling social or web-compressed images: recover detail while preventing plastic or overprocessed looks.

faqItems.question: What exactly is being compared in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: You compare the original image against an enhanced/upscaled version produced by Topaz Wonder 3.5, varying only the enhancement strength (Low, Medium, High) across sequential runs to see how detail, noise, and text clarity change.

faqItems.question: How do Low, Medium, and High strengths differ in practice?
faqItems.answer: Low makes subtle, conservative changes that preserve texture and grain while reducing noise. Medium aims for a balanced increase in detail and sharper edges. High applies the strongest denoise/sharpen/detail synthesis, which can boost text and structured graphics but may introduce oversharpening or invented micro-texture on some photos.

faqItems.question: How can I ensure a fair, repeatable comparison?
faqItems.answer: Keep the input image and model constant, change only the strength, and review outputs at the same zoom level. Save each result with a strength label using SaveImageAdvanced so you can compare versions consistently and revisit choices later.

faqItems.question: Can I compare all three strengths side-by-side at once?
faqItems.answer: By default, the workflow compares original vs enhanced for a single strength. To view all three simultaneously, run and save each strength sequentially, then compare the saved files in your viewer. If you want a multi-branch comparison inside ComfyUI, duplicate the TopazImageEnhanceV2 branch and add additional ImageCompare nodes.

bed989744195.title: Video Face Swap
bed989744195.description: The best open source video face swap workflow. Upload a driving video and a picture of your characters face. This LTX 2.3 lora was trained by @Alissonerdx.
bed989744195.metaDescription: ComfyUI video face swap with LTX 2.3 LoRA. Load a video and face image, stabilize with ReservedRegionFrameComposer, and export via VHS_VideoCombine.
bed989744195.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow performs a video face swap by applying a single reference face image to every frame of a driving video, then recombining the frames into a final clip. The pipeline starts with VHS_LoadVideo to decode the source video into frames and LoadImage to bring in your reference face. A custom face-swap node (dc72113f-8276-4a5a-af12-85d6bec89ed5) drives the actual face transfer using the LTX 2.3 LoRA trained by @Alissonerdx. PrimitiveFloat and PrimitiveInt nodes expose key controls (such as effect strength, region size, or frame step), while ImageResizeKJv2 aligns the reference face scale to your target footage.

To stabilize results and keep the background intact, the workflow composites the generated face back onto each original frame with ReservedRegionFrameComposer. This node lets you define a consistent “reserved” region for the face and blend it with feathered edges, reducing temporal jitter and preserving hair, lighting, and scene motion. ComfyMathExpression is used to derive dynamic values (for example, region size from video resolution), keeping settings in sync with whatever you load. For quality checks, ImageConcanate can assemble side-by-side previews of original vs. swapped frames. Finally, the processed frames are encoded to a video using VHS_VideoCombine or CreateVideo, and the result is written out with SaveVideo.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI. Ensure Video Helper Suite nodes are installed (VHS_LoadVideo, VHS_VideoCombine) and place the LTX 2.3 LoRA file in ComfyUI/models/loras. Restart ComfyUI so nodes and models are detected.
Connect your inputs: point VHS_LoadVideo to your driving video and LoadImage to a clear, front-facing reference image. Verify the video resolution/FPS in the VHS_LoadVideo node preview or metadata.

Set alignment and region: use ImageResizeKJv2 to roughly match the reference face size to the target face. In ReservedRegionFrameComposer, adjust the face region position/size and feather so the new face sits naturally and blends smoothly with the original frame.

Tune effect intensity: adjust any PrimitiveFloat/PrimitiveInt controls exposed for LoRA strength, blend/opacity, or frame step. ComfyMathExpression values can help keep region scaling proportional to the video resolution.
Preview a short segment: queue a small frame range to confirm alignment and blending. Use ImageConcanate to compare original vs. swapped frames and refine region size, feather, or strength if needed.

Export the final video: run the full queue to process all frames, then combine them with VHS_VideoCombine or CreateVideo. Save the output with SaveVideo. If you need original audio, configure VHS_VideoCombine to mux audio or add it afterward in a video editor.
suggestedUseCases: Character continuity for talking-head or interview content while preserving the original performance and timing.
Previsualization and animatics where you need to test different actors or characters in existing footage.
Privacy-friendly edits by swapping identifiable faces with a consented or generic face for internal reviews.
Meme and remix videos with side-by-side comparisons using ImageConcanate for quick iterations.
Brand/influencer content where a consistent on-screen identity is needed across varied source clips.

faqItems.question: What models or add-ons do I need to run this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Install Video Helper Suite (for VHS_LoadVideo and VHS_VideoCombine) and place the LTX 2.3 LoRA by @Alissonerdx into ComfyUI/models/loras. The custom face-swap node (dc72113f-8276-4a5a-af12-85d6bec89ed5) applies the LoRA during inference, so you don’t need to manually add samplers in this template.

faqItems.question: How do I reduce flicker or a “swimming” face across frames?
faqItems.answer: Keep the ReservedRegionFrameComposer region stable around the target face and increase feathering for smoother edges. Use a high-quality, front-facing reference image with similar lighting to the driving video. Avoid aggressive frame skipping; process every frame for best temporal consistency.

faqItems.question: Can I keep the original audio from the driving video?
faqItems.answer: Yes, route frames through VHS_VideoCombine and enable or supply the original audio if the node configuration supports it. If your setup doesn’t mux audio in ComfyUI, export the video and add audio back in a video editor.

faqItems.question: What should I do if the face is misaligned or too big/small?
faqItems.answer: Adjust the region size/position in ReservedRegionFrameComposer and rescale the reference face with ImageResizeKJv2. Use PrimitiveFloat/PrimitiveInt controls (and ComfyMathExpression where provided) to keep the region proportional to the video resolution, then preview a short segment before exporting.

bf82f1e42e83.title: HY 3D 2.1
bf82f1e42e83.description: Generate 3D models from single images using Hunyuan3D 2.1.
bf82f1e42e83.metaDescription: Convert 2D images to 3D models with the HY 3D 2.1 workflow using Hunyuan3D 2.1 for detailed and efficient 3D rendering.
bf82f1e42e83.extendedDescription:
The HY 3D 2.1 workflow is designed to transform single 2D images into detailed 3D models using the Hunyuan3D 2.1 model by Tencent. This workflow leverages a series of specialized nodes to process an image and convert it into a 3D mesh. The process begins with the 'ImageOnlyCheckpointLoader' and 'LoadImage' nodes, which prepare the image for 3D transformation. The 'ModelSamplingAuraFlow' node then applies the Hunyuan3D model to generate a latent representation of the image in 3D space. This latent data is further processed by the 'EmptyLatentHunyuan3Dv2' and 'Hunyuan3Dv2Conditioning' nodes to refine the 3D structure.

The workflow continues with the 'KSampler' node, which samples the latent data to ensure the 3D model is as detailed and accurate as possible. The 'VAEDecodeHunyuan3D' node decodes this sampled data into a voxel representation, which is then converted into a mesh using the 'VoxelToMesh' node. Finally, the 'SaveGLB' node exports the 3D model in GLB format, ready for use in various applications. This workflow is particularly useful for artists and developers looking to create 3D content from existing 2D assets, offering a streamlined process that minimizes manual modeling efforts.
howToUse: Load the HY 3D 2.1 workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the 'ImageOnlyCheckpointLoader' node to load the Hunyuan3D 2.1 model.
Upload your 2D image using the 'LoadImage' node.
Initiate the model processing with the 'ModelSamplingAuraFlow' node.
Refine and sample the 3D model using 'KSampler' and 'VAEDecodeHunyuan3D' nodes.
Export the final 3D model using the 'SaveGLB' node.
suggestedUseCases: Creating 3D assets for video games from concept art.
Generating 3D models for virtual reality environments.
Developing 3D printable objects from 2D designs.
Producing 3D visualizations for architectural projects.
Enhancing digital marketing materials with 3D imagery.

faqItems.question: What type of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: High-resolution images with clear details and defined edges are ideal for generating accurate 3D models.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for commercial projects?
faqItems.answer: Yes, as long as you comply with the licensing terms of the Hunyuan3D model and any other resources used.

faqItems.question: What file format is the final 3D model saved in?
faqItems.answer: The final 3D model is saved in the GLB format, which is widely supported for 3D applications.

faqItems.question: Do I need any prior 3D modeling experience to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No prior 3D modeling experience is required. The workflow is designed to be user-friendly and intuitive.

bfba92751be8.title: 2.2 Creator - Diffusion Guidance
bfba92751be8.description: Learn how to guide diffusion for precise image editing with inpainting and controlnet using Z Image Turbo.
bfba92751be8.metaDescription: Guide diffusion for precise image editing using inpainting and ControlNet with Z Image Turbo in ComfyUI.
bfba92751be8.extendedDescription:
The '2.2 Creator - Diffusion Guidance' workflow in ComfyUI is designed to enhance image editing precision by integrating inpainting and ControlNet techniques. At the core of this workflow is the Z Image Turbo model, which facilitates efficient and accurate diffusion processes. The workflow employs a variety of nodes, such as CLIPLoader and VAELoader, to load and process images, while nodes like DifferentialDiffusion and InpaintModelConditioning are used to guide the diffusion process with spatially varying changes. This makes it particularly useful for tasks that require detailed image editing without the need for model retraining.

The workflow leverages ControlNet to provide structural guidance, such as canny edges or depth maps, to ensure that the diffusion process adheres to desired structural elements. This is achieved through nodes like ZImageFunControlnet and Controlnet Preprocessor. By using per-pixel 'strength' maps, the workflow allows for smooth and gradual changes, making it ideal for applications that demand high precision and control, such as inpainting specific image areas while maintaining the integrity of the surrounding context.
howToUse: Load the '2.2 Creator - Diffusion Guidance' workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadImage node to import the image you wish to edit.
Right-click on the Load Image node and select 'Open in Mask Editor' to create a mask over the area you want to inpaint.
Configure the ControlNet Preprocessor to extract necessary features like edges or depth for guidance.
Adjust the KSampler and ModelSamplingAuraFlow settings to fine-tune the inpainting strength and diffusion process.
Run the workflow to apply the guided diffusion and save the edited image using the SaveImage node.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing portraits by editing specific facial features while preserving the overall look.
Restoring old photographs by inpainting damaged areas with high precision.
Creating artistic effects by selectively altering parts of an image.
Generating variations of an image with controlled structural changes.
Improving image compositions by seamlessly integrating new elements.

faqItems.question: What is the role of the ControlNet in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: ControlNet provides structural guidance to the diffusion process by using features like edges or depth maps to guide the image editing, ensuring that the changes adhere to desired structural elements.

faqItems.question: How does Differential Diffusion enhance inpainting?
faqItems.answer: Differential Diffusion uses per-pixel 'strength' maps to apply smooth, gradual, and spatially varying changes, allowing for precise inpainting without retraining the model.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for batch processing?
faqItems.answer: While this workflow is primarily designed for single-image editing, you can adapt it for batch processing by automating the image loading and mask creation steps.

faqItems.question: What are the recommended settings for KSampler during inpainting?
faqItems.answer: For inpainting, it is recommended to set the KSampler denoise parameter between 0.5 and 1.0, and the ModelSampling shift between 3.0 and 10.0, depending on the desired level of detail and smoothness.

c01a333cfbd3.title: Ovis-Image Text to Image
c01a333cfbd3.description: Ovis-Image is a 7B text-to-image model specifically optimized for high-quality text rendering in generated images. Designed to operate efficiently under computational constraints, it excels at accurately generating images containing text content.
c01a333cfbd3.metaDescription: Generate images with accurate, readable text using the Ovis-Image 7B model in ComfyUI. Subgraph-powered workflow with simple controls and one-click saving.
c01a333cfbd3.extendedDescription:
This workflow is a focused text-to-image generator built around the Ovis-Image 7B model, which is optimized to render readable, well-placed text directly inside generated images. The core generation logic is encapsulated in a Subgraph node (5a9f8bf0-ed77-40e3-aca8-c7c1a0bf54e1), keeping the graph clean while exposing the controls you need for prompting and iteration. A MarkdownNote node provides in-graph guidance, and a SaveImage node writes results to your ComfyUI output folder.

Technically, the Subgraph packages the Ovis-Image model loading and inference steps so you can supply a prompt with your desired text and styling descriptors, choose a canvas size, and control reproducibility with a seed. Depending on how the template exposes parameters, you can adjust common settings such as steps or guidance strength inside the Subgraph. Ovis-Image is tuned for high-quality text rendering, so short phrases, clear punctuation, and style hints (e.g., "bold serif title on a chalkboard", "neon script sign") translate well into legible, photorealistic, or stylized results. The SaveImage node captures each run so you can compare variants and iterate quickly.
howToUse: Load the "Ovis-Image Text to Image" workflow in ComfyUI.
Ensure the Ovis-Image model is available on your system (see the Comfy-Org/Ovis-Image model page on Hugging Face). If the model path is missing, open the Subgraph to set or confirm it.

Select the Subgraph node (ID: 5a9f8bf0-ed77-40e3-aca8-c7c1a0bf54e1) and enter your prompt. For best legibility, include the exact text you want rendered and simple style cues (e.g., "Minimal poster with the words 'OPEN HOUSE' in bold sans-serif").

Adjust exposed settings in the Subgraph, such as image size and seed. If available, fine-tune steps or guidance strength to balance fidelity and style. Keep text short and avoid excessive special characters for sharper results.
Queue the prompt. Inspect the image output saved by the SaveImage node in your ComfyUI output directory.
Iterate: tweak the wording, try uppercase, adjust canvas size, or change the seed to explore alternatives. Open the Subgraph internals (see ComfyUI Subgraph guide) if you want to customize defaults.
suggestedUseCases: Social graphics or banners that require crisp, readable headlines directly in the image.
Poster, flyer, or signage mockups where the main design element is stylized text.
UI/UX hero images or feature tiles with embedded titles or callouts.
Branded visuals like badges, stickers, or product labels featuring short phrases.
Concept exploration for typography-driven artwork and logotypes (non-exact font matching).

faqItems.question: How do I get cleaner, more readable text in the image?
faqItems.answer: Keep phrases short (1–5 words), use uppercase for critical words, and include clear style/context cues (e.g., "on a plain white background", "centered title"). Increasing image size can help, and if the Subgraph exposes steps or guidance, modestly raise them to improve fidelity.

faqItems.question: Can I choose an exact font?
faqItems.answer: No. Text-to-image models can follow style hints (e.g., "bold serif", "handwritten script") but do not guarantee a specific font. For closer results, describe font characteristics and context (e.g., "retro neon sign in cursive script").

faqItems.question: Where are images saved?
faqItems.answer: The SaveImage node writes outputs to your ComfyUI output directory. Look for the most recent image after each run. You can change naming or folder behavior by editing the SaveImage node settings.

faqItems.question: Do I need a GPU to run this?
faqItems.answer: A GPU is recommended for practical speed. CPU inference may work but can be significantly slower, especially at larger resolutions. If you encounter memory issues, try smaller canvas sizes or lower batch counts.

Finally, the 'Z-Image-Turbo' model is employed to upscale the image variations by 2x, adding finer details and improving overall resolution. The workflow concludes with the 'SaveImage' node, allowing users to easily store the enhanced images.

Technically, this workflow leverages the Grok model's ability to generate descriptive captions that inform the variation process, ensuring that the new images are both creative and contextually relevant. The integration of the 'Z-Image-Turbo' model for upscaling is particularly useful for applications requiring high-resolution outputs, such as print media or detailed digital presentations. By combining these advanced nodes and models, the workflow provides a powerful tool for artists, designers, and content creators who need to generate multiple high-quality image variations quickly.
howToUse: Start by loading your reference image into the workflow using the 'LoadImage' node.
The GrokImageNode will automatically generate a caption to guide the variation process.
Use the 'ImageCompare' node to ensure the variations maintain similarity to the original image.
Apply the 'Z-Image-Turbo' model to upscale the variations by 2x for added detail.
Preview the results with the 'PreviewAny' node to ensure quality and make adjustments if necessary.
Save the final images using the 'SaveImage' node for easy access and use.
suggestedUseCases: Creating multiple design concepts from a single reference image for client presentations.
Generating high-resolution images for print advertising campaigns.

Enhancing personal photo collections with artistic variations.

faqItems.question: What types of images work best with this workflow?

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the level of variation in the generated images?

faqItems.question: How long does the upscaling process take?
faqItems.answer: The upscaling process using the 'Z-Image-Turbo' model is relatively fast, but the exact time depends on the image size and system performance.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to use this workflow for video content?
faqItems.answer: This workflow is specifically designed for static images. For video content, a different set of nodes and models would be required.

c0a2671af7c4.title: Ideogram v4: Text to Image
c0a2671af7c4.description: Input a text prompt or structured JSON description. Generate an image with precise layout, color, and style control using Ideogram 4.0.
c0a2671af7c4.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Use Ideogram 4.0 for text-to-image with structured JSON prompts for precise layout, color, and style. Includes preview, save, and resolution control.
c0a2671af7c4.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow demonstrates how to generate images with Ideogram 4.0 using either a simple text prompt or a structured JSON caption for precise visual control. The Ideogram4 Caption Prompt Template subgraph guides you to describe a scene summary, style block, background, and optional per-object elements with bounding boxes and hex color palettes. A ResolutionSelector node standardizes width and height, while a MarkdownNote explains the JSON schema so you can author layout-aware prompts without guessing. PreviewAny provides live feedback, and SaveImage writes the final output to disk.

Under the hood, the workflow routes your prompt into a custom Ideogram v4 inference node backed by the ideogram4_fp8_scaled diffusion model and a compatible VAE (flux2-vae). If you provide plain text, the template wraps it for sensible defaults; if you provide structured JSON, it passes through so the model can honor layout, color, and style constraints. This setup mirrors the official caption schema Ideogram 4.0 was trained on, giving you reproducible composition and color control locally. For users who prefer a visual editor, you can optionally add KJNodes and the Ideogram 4 Prompt Builder KJ node to create bounding boxes and palettes interactively.
howToUse: Load the workflow (Ideogram v4: Text to Image) in ComfyUI. Ensure the models are installed: place ideogram4_fp8_scaled.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models and flux2-vae.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/vae.
In the ResolutionSelector node, choose your target aspect ratio and size. Start with common sizes (e.g., 1024×1024 or 1024×1536) for stable results.

Decide your prompt mode: enter a simple text prompt for quick results, or use the provided JSON template (see the MarkdownNote) to specify scene summary, style, background, and per-object entries with bounding boxes and hex colors (e.g., #FF7F50).

If using structured JSON, define each object’s bbox as normalized coordinates (x, y, width, height between 0 and 1), add optional palette hex colors, and keep styles concise and consistent. Paste the JSON into the template input.
Queue the workflow. Watch the output in the PreviewAny node. If composition or colors need adjustment, tweak the JSON (bbox sizes/positions, palettes, style tags) or refine your text and re-run.
When satisfied, use the SaveImage node to export the final image. Optionally iterate over multiple resolutions or prompt variants to compare outputs.
suggestedUseCases: Product shots and packaging mockups with brand-aligned hex colors and controlled object placement.
Poster and cover concepts where title, subtitle, and elements must sit in reserved regions.
UI or app splash illustrations with consistent background styling and anchored icons.
Educational graphics where diagrams or callouts need fixed positions and distinct palettes.
Social media templates that maintain composition across multiple aspect ratios.

faqItems.question: Do I need to write structured JSON, or can I just use plain text?
faqItems.answer: Both work. Plain text prompts are accepted for quick generations. For precise composition and color control, use the JSON template (scene summary, style, background, and optional per-object entries with bbox and hex palettes).

faqItems.question: How should I format bounding boxes and colors in the JSON?
faqItems.answer: Use normalized bbox values in the form {"x": 0–1, "y": 0–1, "w": 0–1, "h": 0–1} relative to the full image. Specify colors as hex strings (e.g., "#1E90FF"). Keep style and background fields short and descriptive.

faqItems.question: Which models does this workflow use and where do I put them?
faqItems.answer: Place ideogram4_fp8_scaled.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models and flux2-vae.safetensors in ComfyUI/models/vae. The custom Ideogram v4 inference node will load them automatically when you run the graph.

faqItems.question: How can I make layout authoring easier?
faqItems.answer: Install KJNodes and use the Ideogram 4 Prompt Builder KJ node to draw regions and build the JSON visually. You can paste its output into this template’s JSON input for consistent results.

c0d1253e51dd.title: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash: Image to Video
c0d1253e51dd.description: Generate videos from text prompts or reference images using Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, a multimodal model that handles text-to-video, image-to-video, keyframe interpolation, and iterative video editing with natural language. Outputs a single MP4 video with optional audio, supporting aspect ratios, resolutions up to 4K, and scene extension. Ideal for cinematic storytelling, product visualization, and rapid video prototyping.
c0d1253e51dd.metaDescription: Create MP4 videos from prompts or a reference image in ComfyUI with Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash. Supports text/image-to-video, up to 4K, optional audio, and scene extension.
c0d1253e51dd.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI tutorial workflow shows how to turn a text prompt or a single still image into a finished MP4 clip using Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash. The core of the pipeline is the GeminiVideoOmniV2 node, which accepts a prompt and (optionally) a reference image to drive image-to-video generation. You can target common aspect ratios and resolutions up to 4K, set clip duration and frame rate, and enable optional audio. The included MarkdownNote provides inline tips, while SaveVideo writes the final video to disk.

Technically, the flow is simple and robust: LoadImage brings in the provided blue_studio_car.png (or your own asset) and feeds it to GeminiVideoOmniV2 when you want image conditioning. The model handles text-to-video and image-to-video, along with internal keyframe interpolation and scene extension, controlled through your prompt and node parameters. GeminiVideoOmniV2 returns the generated clip, and SaveVideo outputs a single MP4 with your chosen fps and path. Leave the image input disconnected for pure text-to-video; connect it to anchor motion, style, and composition to your reference.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure you’re on a recent version. If required by your setup, confirm GeminiVideoOmniV2 has valid API credentials configured.

Add a reference image: place input/blue_studio_car.png (provided) or your own image in the input folder, then set that path in the LoadImage node. Leave LoadImage disconnected if you want text-to-video only.

Open GeminiVideoOmniV2 and enter a clear prompt describing subject, motion, camera moves, and style (e.g., “studio-lit product shot, slow dolly, subtle reflections”). Configure resolution/aspect, duration, fps, and audio if those options are exposed.
Check SaveVideo for output path and fps. Match fps to what you request in GeminiVideoOmniV2 so timing is consistent.
Run the workflow. GeminiVideoOmniV2 will generate the clip, and SaveVideo will write a single MP4 to the specified location. Preview the result.

Iterate: refine the prompt, swap or remove the reference image to switch between image-to-video and text-to-video, adjust duration/fps for pacing, and re-run. Use shorter, lower-res drafts for quick previews, then render at higher resolution.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic product shots from a single packshot or studio still
Rapid storyboard-to-animatic previews for previsualization
Logo or key art motion treatments for social teasers
Extending a still photo into a short establishing shot with gentle camera motion
Quick turntable-style showcases of designs or prototypes

faqItems.question: Do I need to use a reference image?
faqItems.answer: No. Connect LoadImage to GeminiVideoOmniV2 for image-to-video, or leave it disconnected for text-to-video. Using a reference image helps lock style, layout, and subject appearance.

faqItems.question: What resolutions and durations work best?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports up to 4K, but start with lower resolutions and shorter durations for fast iteration. Higher resolution, longer clips, or higher fps will take longer to generate.

faqItems.question: Can it generate audio?
faqItems.answer: Yes, optional audio can be enabled if exposed by the GeminiVideoOmniV2 node. If audio is returned, SaveVideo will include it in the MP4; otherwise, the clip will be silent.

faqItems.question: I get errors or slow responses—how do I troubleshoot?
faqItems.answer: Update ComfyUI, verify your internet connection, and ensure the GeminiVideoOmniV2 node has valid API credentials if required. Reduce resolution/duration for tests, then scale up.

c1959fdc5642.title: Image Upscale
c1959fdc5642.description: This app upscales your image using the best open source upscaling model, SeedVR2.
c1959fdc5642.metaDescription: Simple ComfyUI workflow to upscale images with the SeedVR2 model. Load an image, upscale, and save sharp, high-resolution results.
c1959fdc5642.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow performs high-quality single-image super-resolution using the open-source SeedVR2 upscaling model. It’s a minimal, production-friendly pipeline: LoadImage ingests your source image, the SeedVR2 Upscale node (c35dd4ba-0fe3-47d6-afce-1c56d9fe5beb) increases resolution while reconstructing fine detail, and SaveImage writes the result to disk. Because the graph focuses solely on upscaling, there are no prompts, samplers, or diffusion steps involved—making it fast, repeatable, and easy to tune.

Under the hood, SeedVR2 applies a learned mapping that predicts high-frequency detail at a higher resolution, preserving the original composition and color while improving sharpness and texture. In practice, you load your image, choose the scale factor exposed by the SeedVR2 node (commonly 2x or 4x, depending on how the node is configured), queue the job, and collect the output. This makes the workflow ideal for preparing assets for print, upscaling renders, or polishing AI-generated images without altering their content.
howToUse: Open ComfyUI and load the Image Upscale workflow JSON. You should see three nodes: LoadImage → SeedVR2 Upscale (c35dd4ba-0fe3-47d6-afce-1c56d9fe5beb) → SaveImage.
In LoadImage, select your source image. Use the highest-quality original available for best results.
Open the SeedVR2 Upscale node and set the available scale factor (e.g., 2x or 4x, depending on the node’s options). If you encounter memory limits, try a lower scale or do two passes at 2x.
In SaveImage, set a clear filename prefix to keep outputs organized.
Click Queue Prompt to run the graph. Watch the preview/output to verify sharpness and artifact levels.
Find the upscaled image in your ComfyUI/output folder under the filename prefix you chose.
suggestedUseCases: Upscaling product photos or UI assets for print and high-DPI displays
Enhancing scanned photos or artwork while preserving composition
Polishing and enlarging AI-generated images without changing their look
Preparing 2D game textures or sprites at higher resolution
Improving clarity for architectural renders or technical diagrams

faqItems.question: Does this workflow change the content of my image?
faqItems.answer: No. It uses a learned upscaler (SeedVR2) to reconstruct detail at a higher resolution without prompts or diffusion steps. Composition and colors are preserved, though mild sharpening and texture recovery can occur.

faqItems.question: What scale factors are supported?
faqItems.answer: The available scale factors depend on how the SeedVR2 Upscale node is configured in this workflow (commonly 2x or 4x). Open the node to see the options. If you need very large outputs, consider running 2x twice.

faqItems.question: Where are my results saved?
faqItems.answer: SaveImage writes files to your ComfyUI/output directory using the filename prefix you set in the node. Check that folder after you click Queue Prompt.

faqItems.question: What if I get out-of-memory (VRAM) errors?
faqItems.answer: Try a lower scale factor, close other GPU-intensive apps, or upscale in two passes (e.g., 2x then 2x). A GPU is recommended; CPU execution can work but is significantly slower.

c2586087f709.title: Apply Color Grade from Reference Image
c2586087f709.description: The easiest way to match color grades between your images. Upload a target image and a reference image that has the desired colors and use Nano Banana 2 to extract and apply it onto the target image.
c2586087f709.metaDescription: Match a photo’s color grade to a reference in ComfyUI using GeminiNanoBanana2. Load, batch apply, compare, and save consistent looks in seconds.
c2586087f709.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow applies the color grade from a reference image to one or more target images, giving you a fast, consistent way to match looks across shots. It starts with LoadImage nodes for both the target and the reference. The core of the pipeline is the GeminiNanoBanana2 node (Nano Banana 2), which analyzes the reference image’s color distribution and computes a global color transform. That transform is then applied to the target image to reproduce the reference’s overall palette, contrast feel, and mood without altering composition or sharpness.

For efficiency, BatchImagesNode lets you run multiple target images through the same grade in a single pass, making it ideal for sets, product lines, or sequential frames. ImageCompare gives you a side-by-side view of the original and graded images so you can quickly judge the match before saving. Finally, SaveImage writes the graded outputs to disk using your chosen naming and location. The result is a streamlined, reproducible color-matching workflow suitable for both one-off shots and larger batches.
howToUse: Open the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then locate the two LoadImage nodes: one for your target image(s) and one for the reference image with the desired grade.
Load your target image into the target LoadImage node. Load your chosen reference image into the reference LoadImage node.
If you have multiple targets, feed them through BatchImagesNode so each image in the batch receives the same grade from the single reference.
Confirm the connections into GeminiNanoBanana2: the target stream to its target input and the reference stream to its reference input.
Run the queue. Use ImageCompare to review the original vs. graded result side-by-side and confirm the grade match looks natural.
Set your output folder and filename/prefix in SaveImage, then run to export the graded image(s).
suggestedUseCases: Unifying color across a photo set shot under slightly different lighting conditions.
Matching product photos to a brand-approved color mood or campaign look.
Applying a consistent grade across sequential frames or key stills extracted from a video.
Quickly prototyping mood board looks on new shots for client approvals.

faqItems.question: What does GeminiNanoBanana2 do in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: GeminiNanoBanana2 analyzes the reference image’s color characteristics and computes a global color mapping that is applied to the target image. It transfers the look (palette and overall grade) without changing composition, detail, or geometry.

faqItems.question: Do my target and reference images need to be the same size or aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: No. The grade transfer is based on color distribution, not spatial layout. However, for best results, choose a reference with similar lighting and exposure to your target to avoid extreme corrections.

faqItems.question: Can I process many images at once with the same grade?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Use BatchImagesNode to pass multiple target images through the pipeline. Each will receive the same reference-based grade, and SaveImage will write out each processed result.

faqItems.question: Will this transfer texture or film grain from the reference?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow transfers color characteristics only. Texture, grain, or local detail from the reference isn’t copied. If you need grain or film emulation, apply it as a separate step outside this workflow.

c27ee1ed3d54.title: Motion Collages
c27ee1ed3d54.description: Take a video and transform it into a stop motion sequence with a style reference
c27ee1ed3d54.metaDescription: Turn any video into a stylized stop-motion collage using a reference image or VLM-described style, with controllable frame sampling and holds.
c27ee1ed3d54.extendedDescription:
Motion Collages turns any source video into a stylized stop‑motion sequence guided by a single reference image. The workflow samples frames with VHS_SelectEveryNthImage, holds each selected frame using ImageBatchRepeatInterleaving, and then reassembles the sequence with CreateVideo and SaveVideo. Two alternative style-transfer paths are provided as grouped node blocks you can toggle: an Image‑based path that feeds your style image directly into OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2, and a VLM‑based path that first has AILab_QwenVL_Advanced describe your style image and then uses that text to prompt OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2.

Under the hood, LoadVideo and GetVideoComponents extract frames, resolution, and FPS, with Video Slice available for trimming. ImageListToImageBatch and RebatchImages handle batching so frames flow efficiently through the style stage. ResizeImageMaskNode and GetImageSize keep your style and video dimensions in sync, while ImageRemoveAlpha+ cleans transparency if your style reference has an alpha channel. StringConcatenate assembles clean prompts or filenames, and PreviewImage/PreviewAny help you inspect intermediate outputs. The result is a controllable stop‑motion look: select every Nth frame for the cadence you want, repeat frames to accentuate the hold, and choose either faithful image‑guided transfer (Image‑based) or flexible, text‑described transfer (VLM‑based).
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and decide your method: select the Image based group OR the VLM based group and press Ctrl+B to enable it (bypass the other group).
In the Input section, use LoadVideo to choose your source clip. Optionally, trim it with Video Slice. GetVideoComponents will expose FPS and resolution for reference.

Provide your style: load a reference image with LoadImage. For METHOD 1, the style image is fed directly to OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2. For METHOD 2, send the style image to AILab_QwenVL_Advanced to generate a style description; StringConcatenate can merge that description with any extra guidance you add before it goes to OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2.

Tune the stop‑motion feel: set the selection interval in VHS_SelectEveryNthImage (e.g., 2–6) and choose how long to hold each selected frame with ImageBatchRepeatInterleaving (via its repeat PrimitiveInt). Use ResizeImageMaskNode/GetImageSize to ensure the processed frames match your target resolution.
Preview intermediate outputs with PreviewImage/PreviewAny. If your style image has transparency, enable ImageRemoveAlpha+ to avoid artifacts.
Assemble and export: set target FPS in CreateVideo, review the output in PreviewAny, then write the final file using SaveVideo. If needed, adjust N‑frame selection, repeats, or prompts and rerun.
suggestedUseCases: Stylized social clips and reels that mimic hand-cut, stop‑motion collages
Fashion or product lookbooks with a cohesive reference art style
Music video loops with rhythmic, held‑frame motion
Moodboards and motion treatments for client pitches
Title sequences or interstitials with a graphic, posterized look

faqItems.question: What’s the difference between the Image-based and VLM-based methods?
faqItems.answer: Image-based feeds the style image directly into OpenAIGPTImageNodeV2, typically giving more faithful style transfer. VLM-based uses AILab_QwenVL_Advanced to describe the style first and then prompts the image node, which is more flexible for variations but can be less strictly faithful to the reference.

faqItems.question: How is the stop-motion effect created?
faqItems.answer: VHS_SelectEveryNthImage samples only every Nth frame from the video, and ImageBatchRepeatInterleaving holds each selected frame for multiple steps. Together, these nodes reduce motion fluidity and create the characteristic choppy cadence of stop motion.

faqItems.question: Why do my outputs have mismatched sizing or artifacts?
faqItems.answer: Ensure the style/image processing path matches the video resolution using GetImageSize and ResizeImageMaskNode. If your style image has transparency, enable ImageRemoveAlpha+ to prevent edge artifacts. Preview intermediate frames to catch issues before rendering.

faqItems.question: Does the final video include audio?
faqItems.answer: No. CreateVideo/SaveVideo in this workflow output a silent video. If you need audio, add it later in a video editor or with a separate audio muxing step.

faqItems.question: How can I speed up or reduce costs when using remote model nodes?
faqItems.answer: Increase the N in VHS_SelectEveryNthImage to process fewer frames, and raise the repeat count to maintain duration. Trim with Video Slice and lower the output resolution with ResizeImageMaskNode.

c2aae816fe63.title: Face Swap
c2aae816fe63.description: The best instant AI face swap technology for photos.
c2aae816fe63.metaDescription: ComfyUI face swap workflow: load source and target photos, preview with ImageCompare, and export with SaveImageAdvanced for fast, clean results.
c2aae816fe63.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow performs fast, high-quality face swaps on photos using a minimal, easy-to-tune graph. Two LoadImage nodes bring in your source face (the identity you want to transfer) and the target photo. A custom face-swap processor (node ID: 217f3726-59bc-4170-9ab1-c622bb578338) detects and aligns faces in the target, transfers the source identity onto the target while preserving expression, pose, and lighting, and outputs a composited image. An ImageCompare node lets you visually verify results against the original for quick A/B checks, and SaveImageAdvanced handles clean, repeatable exports.

Technically, the face-swap node encapsulates the core pipeline—face detection, alignment/warping, identity transfer, and blending—so you don’t need to manage separate detection or masking nodes. This makes the workflow compact and robust: you load images, optionally tweak the swap node’s settings (such as which detected face to replace or blend strength, depending on the implementation), preview with ImageCompare, and then save your output with consistent naming and format via SaveImageAdvanced. It’s particularly useful when you need reliable swaps from solid input photos without building a large, complex graph.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and locate the two LoadImage nodes: one for the source face image and one for the target photo.
Click each LoadImage node to browse and select your images. Aim for well-lit, front- or three-quarter-facing photos for the best results.

Open the face-swap node (ID: 217f3726-59bc-4170-9ab1-c622bb578338). If options are available (e.g., which face to replace in multi-person shots or blend/strength controls), set them to match your target photo and desired realism.
Run the workflow. Use the ImageCompare node’s output to A/B the target photo against the swapped result and quickly spot alignment or blending issues.
If needed, adjust your inputs (choose a clearer source face, crop tighter on the face, or tweak the face-swap node’s settings) and rerun until you’re satisfied.
Configure SaveImageAdvanced (format, quality, filename pattern/folder), then execute to export the final swapped image with consistent naming and metadata.
suggestedUseCases: Casting and concept previews: audition different identities in moodboards or comps before a photoshoot.
Continuity and retouching for stills: fix a blink or mismatch in a group photo by swapping in a better take of the same person.
Cosplay and character tests: visualize how a face would look with a specific costume or scene setup.
Product and lifestyle mockups: quickly prototype campaign variants with different talent (with proper rights and consent).
Education and research demos: illustrate face alignment and identity transfer concepts using controlled, consented images.

faqItems.question: What image quality or angles work best?
faqItems.answer: Use sharp, well-lit images with a clear, unobstructed face. Front-facing or slight three-quarter angles work best. Heavy occlusions (hands, hair, masks), extreme profiles, or motion blur can degrade results.

faqItems.question: How do I handle photos with multiple faces?
faqItems.answer: Open the face-swap node (217f3726-59bc-4170-9ab1-c622bb578338). If it provides a face selection control, choose the index/face you want to replace. If not, crop the target image around the intended face and rerun.

faqItems.question: Why does the skin tone or lighting look off?
faqItems.answer: Large lighting or color differences between source and target can show in the blend. Try a source photo matched in lighting and tone, or preprocess with basic color/contrast adjustments. Subtle tweaks to the swap node’s blend/feather (if available) can also help.

faqItems.question: Is the original image modified?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow generates a new, swapped image. SaveImageAdvanced lets you export non-destructively with your chosen format, quality, and filename pattern.

c2c4b45b7df5.title: Wan2.2 Animate, Character Animation and Replacement
c2c4b45b7df5.description: Unified character animation and replacement framework with precise motion and expression replication.
c2c4b45b7df5.metaDescription: Animate or replace characters in video with Wan 2.2 Animate. SAM2 masking + DW pose keep motion while you restyle or swap identities. ComfyUI tutorial.
c2c4b45b7df5.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates a unified approach to character animation and replacement using the Wan 2.2 Animate video diffusion model. It extracts motion from an input video, segments the target subject, and synthesizes a new character (or restyles the original) that follows the same motion. Core components include UNETLoader loading the Wan2_2-Animate-14B_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled_KJ.safetensors checkpoint, VAELoader for decoding frames, CLIPLoader and CLIPTextEncode for positive/negative prompts, and SaveVideo for final output. Motion cues are produced with comfyui_controlnet_aux’s DWPreprocessor (human pose/whole-body keypoints), while subject isolation comes from ComfyUI-segment-anything-2 via DownloadAndLoadSAM2Model and Sam2Segmentation. If you want to lock identity or style from an image, CLIPVisionLoader + CLIPVisionEncode provide additional reference conditioning, and LoraLoaderModelOnly lets you inject a character LoRA.

Technically, the workflow wires LoadVideo through GetVideoComponents, then preprocesses the background and subject: Sam2Segmentation builds a character mask (guided by user “green points”), and DWPreprocessor extracts pose from each frame. PixelPerfectResolution ensures the working size fits your GPU and stays compliant with the WanAnimateToVideo constraint (width and height must be multiples of 16). ModelSamplingSD3 controls your sampler and schedule for the Wan UNet, and comfyui-kjnodes utilities help with the optimized FP8-scaled model. The result is a flexible pipeline for motion-consistent swaps or restyling—use a single reference image, a LoRA, and prompts to steer identity and appearance while preserving the original motion.
howToUse: Install required custom nodes: ComfyUI-segment-anything-2, comfyui-kjnodes, and comfyui_controlnet_aux (see the ComfyUI docs for installing custom nodes). Then load the provided workflow JSON in ComfyUI.

Load models in Step 1: point UNETLoader to Wan2_2-Animate-14B_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled_KJ.safetensors, load VAELoader, CLIPLoader, and CLIPVisionLoader if you’ll use a reference image. Optionally load a character LoRA with LoraLoaderModelOnly.

Import your source video in Step 4 via LoadVideo. GetVideoComponents will expose frames/FPS (and audio if you wire it). In Video size, use PixelPerfectResolution (or the Image Scale control, if present) to set dimensions; ensure width and height are multiples of 16 to satisfy WanAnimateToVideo and avoid OOM.

Provide identity/style guidance in Step 3: either right‑click the canvas and Load Image for a reference, or run once to auto-capture the first frame. If using SAM2, add green points (hold Shift and click) to mark the character; use MaskPreview/PreviewImage to refine the segmentation.

Author your prompts in Step 2 with CLIPTextEncode. Enter a clear positive prompt (e.g., “The character is dancing in the room”) and a strong negative prompt (the provided example removes blur, artifacts, and low quality). Adjust ModelSamplingSD3 settings (steps/scheduler/CFG) for your quality–speed balance.

Run the Sampling + video output group. Inspect intermediate previews, then SaveVideo will render the final video (optionally reattaching audio if routed from GetVideoComponents). If results flicker or identity drifts, try more steps, a fixed seed, tighter masking, or a smaller resolution.
suggestedUseCases: Character replacement: swap an actor with a stylized avatar or branded mascot while keeping the original performance.
Dance/motion reenactment: drive a new character with the body motion captured from trending clips.
Continuity fixes: keep motion and staging, but update wardrobe, color, or art style across shots.
Previsualization: quickly try different character looks over the same blocking before full production.
Social content: rapid identity or style swaps for short-form videos without manual rotoscoping.

faqItems.question: Which models and nodes do I need to run this?
faqItems.answer: Required: Wan2_2-Animate-14B_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled_KJ.safetensors (UNETLoader), VAELoader, CLIPLoader, CLIPTextEncode, SaveVideo. For guidance and masking: comfyui_controlnet_aux (DWPreprocessor), ComfyUI-segment-anything-2 (DownloadAndLoadSAM2Model, Sam2Segmentation). Optional: CLIPVisionLoader/CLIPVisionEncode for reference image conditioning, LoraLoaderModelOnly for character LoRA, and comfyui-kjnodes utilities.

faqItems.question: How do I keep dimensions valid and avoid out-of-memory errors?
faqItems.answer: Use PixelPerfectResolution (or Image Scale, if present) to set a manageable size and ensure width/height are multiples of 16 (WanAnimateToVideo requirement). Start smaller if VRAM is limited, then scale up. Longer videos and higher resolutions increase preprocessing and sampling time.

faqItems.question: How do I get an accurate character mask with SAM2?
faqItems.answer: Load the SAM2 model via DownloadAndLoadSAM2Model, then in Sam2Segmentation add green points (hold Shift and click) on the subject you want. Add a few background (red) points if your node exposes them, and preview with MaskPreview. Iterate: more targeted points near boundaries improve hair and limb separation.

faqItems.question: Can I preserve identity from a single image, and what if faces flicker?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Feed a reference image through CLIPVisionEncode (with CLIPVisionLoader) and/or load a matching LoRA via LoraLoaderModelOnly. If identity flickers, reduce resolution slightly, increase steps, fix the seed, strengthen the mask around the face, and use a concise, consistent prompt with a strong negative prompt.

c365c23d9a69.title: Kling O1: Video to Video
c365c23d9a69.description: Transform videos with Kling O1. Edit video content, change styles, or replace characters using text prompts and reference images.
c365c23d9a69.metaDescription: Transform videos with Kling O1: Edit, style, or replace characters using text prompts and reference images. Ideal for creative video projects.
c365c23d9a69.extendedDescription:
The Kling O1: Video to Video workflow is a powerful tool for transforming video content using the capabilities of the Kling O1 model. This workflow allows users to edit video content, change styles, or replace characters seamlessly by leveraging text prompts and reference images. At its core, the workflow utilizes nodes such as LoadVideo to import video files, and KlingOmniProVideoToVideoNode to apply the desired transformations. This node is particularly adept at interpreting text prompts and reference images to make precise alterations to video frames.

The workflow also incorporates nodes like BatchImagesNode, which facilitates batch processing of images extracted from video frames, allowing for efficient handling of multiple frames at once. The SaveVideo node is used to compile the transformed frames back into a video format, ensuring that the final output is cohesive and ready for use. This workflow is particularly useful for content creators looking to enhance their video projects with creative edits, style changes, or character replacements, making it an invaluable tool in the fields of video production and digital storytelling.
howToUse: Load the Kling O1: Video to Video workflow in ComfyUI.
Use the LoadVideo node to import your video file into the workflow.
Configure the KlingOmniProVideoToVideoNode with your desired text prompts and reference images to specify the transformations.
Enable batch processing by selecting Batch Images and pressing Ctrl-B.
Run the workflow to process the video frames and apply the transformations.
Use the SaveVideo node to compile the transformed frames into a final video output.
suggestedUseCases: Enhancing video content with creative style changes for social media.
Replacing characters in video footage for film and animation projects.
Creating unique video advertisements with customized visual elements.
Developing educational videos with dynamic visual transformations.
Producing music videos with artistic and stylistic edits.

faqItems.question: What types of video formats are supported by this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports common video formats such as MP4 and AVI. Ensure your video is in a compatible format before loading it.

faqItems.question: Can I use multiple reference images for character replacement?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can use multiple reference images to provide a comprehensive guide for character replacement, enhancing the accuracy of the transformation.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure the best quality output from this workflow?
faqItems.answer: For optimal results, use high-resolution reference images and clear, concise text prompts. Additionally, ensure that your video input is of high quality.

faqItems.question: Is it possible to preview changes before finalizing the video?
faqItems.answer: Currently, the workflow does not support real-time previews, but you can process a small batch of frames to review the changes before applying them to the entire video.

c384585f8b2c.title: Kling2.6: Animate Images with Audio
c384585f8b2c.description: Transform static images into dynamic videos with synchronized dialogue, singing, sound effects, and ambient audio.
c384585f8b2c.metaDescription: Transform static images into dynamic videos with synchronized audio using the Kling2.6 workflow in ComfyUI. Perfect for engaging multimedia projects.
c384585f8b2c.extendedDescription:
The Kling2.6: Animate Images with Audio workflow in ComfyUI is designed to transform static images into dynamic, engaging videos that are synchronized with audio elements such as dialogue, singing, sound effects, and ambient audio. This workflow leverages the Kling 2.6 model, known for its robust capabilities in image-to-video conversion, ensuring that visual and audio components are seamlessly integrated. The core of the workflow involves several key nodes, including the KlingImageToVideoWithAudio node, which handles the conversion process by taking a static image and applying specified movements and audio elements to create a cohesive video output. The SaveVideo node then allows users to easily export their animated creations for use in various applications.

Technically, this workflow operates by first loading a static image using the LoadImage node. Users can then define a scene using a structured prompt format that includes scene description, subject description, movement, and audio elements. The KlingImageToVideoWithAudio node processes these inputs to animate the image, synchronizing it with the audio to create a lifelike video. This workflow is particularly useful for creators looking to add dynamic elements to their projects without extensive video editing knowledge, making it accessible for both beginners and experienced users alike.
howToUse: Load your static image into ComfyUI using the LoadImage node.
Define your scene using the prompt format: Scene, Element, Movement, Audio, and Other.
Use the KlingImageToVideoWithAudio node to process the image and apply the defined animations and audio.
Preview the animated video to ensure synchronization and desired effects.
Save the final video using the SaveVideo node for easy export and sharing.
suggestedUseCases: Creating animated storyboards for film or animation projects.
Enhancing social media content with dynamic visuals and audio.
Developing educational videos that require synchronized visuals and narration.
Producing music videos where static album art is brought to life with audio tracks.
Generating promotional content that combines brand imagery with sound effects and voiceovers.

faqItems.question: What types of audio can be synchronized with the video?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports dialogue, singing, sound effects, and pure music, allowing for a wide range of audio-visual combinations.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow for commercial projects?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the Kling2.6 workflow can be used for both personal and commercial projects, provided you comply with any licensing requirements of the models used.

faqItems.question: Do I need prior video editing experience to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No, this workflow is designed to be user-friendly and does not require extensive video editing knowledge. The structured prompt format guides you through the process.

faqItems.question: How can I ensure the audio is perfectly synchronized with the visuals?
faqItems.answer: Carefully define the audio elements in the prompt, including emotion, speech speed, and tone, to match the intended visual movements for optimal synchronization.

c3e308dab99b.title: Product Placement (Flux.2 Klein)
c3e308dab99b.description: Drop in up to 3 product shots and a reference composition, and this workflow places your products into the scene with accurate label text, packaging detail, and lighting that matches the reference. Fully open source stack: Qwen3-VL reads your inputs and writes the edit prompt, Flux.2 Klein 9B handles the multi-image composite, and LTX-2.3 animates the final placement into a product spot. Batch concatenation and auto-scaling keep inputs sharp at any resolution. Runs on Comfy Cloud out of the box, or locally on your own hardware. No closed APIs.
c3e308dab99b.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow for product placement using Qwen3-VL, Flux.2 Klein, and LTX-2.3. Drop in products + reference, get a realistic composite and short video.
c3e308dab99b.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow automates realistic product placement using an open-source stack. You provide up to three product shots plus a reference composition, and the graph places the products into the scene with text-aware detail and lighting that follows the reference. A Qwen3-VL stage inspects your inputs and writes a context-rich edit prompt, Flux.2 Klein 9B performs the multi-image composite, and LTX-2.3 turns the final still into a short, polished product spot. Core utility nodes like LoadImage, PreviewImage, PreviewAny, BatchImagesNode, StringConcatenate, and SaveVideo make it easy to iterate and export.

Technically, the product and reference images are loaded, batched, and auto-scaled so Flux.2 Klein receives sharp, consistent inputs regardless of your source resolution. The prompt is assembled by Qwen3-VL (guided via StringConcatenate) and passed into the Flux.2 sampler to condition placement, label fidelity, and scene lighting. After the composite is approved in PreviewImage/PreviewAny, LTX-2.3 generates a short motion segment from the final placement and SaveVideo writes the result to disk. The custom inference nodes (461b058e-342d-497e-aac1-a5fb6551e33a, fdd45ff8-8dff-43e8-b2c0-2d26053388b8, 6dbca6ef-ca4b-4af8-a99b-b834745f3a9b, 5c2c98c8-2e8f-47ca-9403-686e35a5ef94, 04e3b3b1-a711-485c-be05-f59f9507bd4e, ffacbfba-7659-45df-a3b8-7560f4800088) encapsulate the model runners and scaling/conditioning logic so you can run fully locally or on Comfy Cloud—no closed APIs.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the models are available: Qwen3-VL for prompt generation, Flux.2 Klein 9B for image compositing, and LTX-2.3 for image-to-video. If missing, download and point the custom inference nodes to their weights.

Import your assets: up to three product shots and one reference composition using the LoadImage nodes. Prefer high-resolution PNGs (alpha backgrounds if available) for products, and a well-lit, on-brand reference image.

Generate and review the edit prompt: run the Qwen3-VL stage to analyze the inputs. Inspect the generated instructions in PreviewAny/PreviewImage. If needed, refine the wording or add constraints (e.g., placement, scale, orientation, lighting) in the StringConcatenate node.

Place the products: execute the Flux.2 Klein composite stage. The BatchImagesNode and the auto-scaling node (04e3b3b1-a711-485c-be05-f59f9507bd4e) handle batching and resolution. Review outputs in PreviewImage; iterate on the prompt or input order until labels, edges, and shadows look right.

Animate the result: send the approved still into the LTX-2.3 stage to create a short motion segment (e.g., subtle camera move or lighting emphasis). Adjust duration and fps as exposed by the node, then render.
Export: verify the result in PreviewAny and save using SaveVideo. If you hit memory limits, reduce resolution or animation length, or disable unused product slots before re-running.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid mockups for social ads and marketplace listings using real packaging and on-brand scenes.
A/B testing hero images by swapping different SKUs into the same reference composition.
Pitch decks and client reviews where you need fast, realistic product-in-context visuals.
E-commerce refreshes: update packaging or flavor variants while keeping consistent lighting and framing.
Previsualization for product videos before committing to a full shoot.

faqItems.question: Do I have to use all three product slots?
faqItems.answer: No. The workflow supports 1–3 products. Leave unused LoadImage nodes empty; the BatchImagesNode will process only the images you provide.

faqItems.question: How do I get sharp labels and accurate packaging detail?
faqItems.answer: Use high-resolution product shots (ideally with clean, front-facing labels) and transparent PNGs if possible. Keep the reference image close to your target output resolution. If text or edges look soft, increase input resolution, refine the Qwen3-VL prompt via StringConcatenate, or reduce the final output size.

faqItems.question: Can I run this fully offline?
faqItems.answer: Yes. All stages run locally with open models (Qwen3-VL, Flux.2 Klein 9B, LTX-2.3) through the custom inference nodes (e.g., 461b058e…, fdd45ff8…, 6dbca6ef…, 5c2c98c8…, 04e3b3b1…, ffacbfba…). Ensure you have the model weights installed and paths set in the node settings.

faqItems.question: What if I run out of VRAM or the video render is slow?
faqItems.answer: Lower the working resolution, shorten the LTX-2.3 duration, or disable any unused image slots. You can also run the composite first at a smaller size, lock a good seed, then upscale for a final pass if your hardware allows.

c51538d3e644.title: Prompt Multi Batch Generation
c51538d3e644.description: Send multiple prompts simultaneously to generate independent outputs in a single queue. Connect to Blueprint or Partner Nodes for batch processing of any modality. Use for prompt variation comparisons and batch generation.
c51538d3e644.metaDescription: Compare multiple prompts simultaneously with ComfyUI's batch generation workflow, optimizing time and resources for prompt variation analysis.
c51538d3e644.extendedDescription: The 'Prompt Multi Batch Generation' workflow in ComfyUI offers a powerful approach to comparing multiple prompts simultaneously. howToUse: Open ComfyUI and load the 'Prompt Multi Batch Generation' workflow.
Configure the FL_PromptMulti node with your desired prompts, filling each slot with a different variation.
Connect the workflow to Blueprint or Partner Nodes if batch processing across modalities is needed.
Run the workflow to generate outputs for each prompt simultaneously.

Conducting A/B testing for visual elements in user interface design.
Exploring different artistic styles or themes in digital art projects.
Batch processing of prompts for rapid prototyping in game development.
Evaluating prompt effectiveness in generating specific image attributes for research purposes.

faqItems.question: How does the FL_PromptMulti node improve efficiency?
faqItems.answer: The FL_PromptMulti node allows multiple prompts to be processed simultaneously, reducing the time needed for sequential runs and enabling quicker comparisons.

faqItems.question: What should I consider when using Partner Nodes?

faqItems.question: Can this workflow handle different modalities?
faqItems.answer: Yes, when connected to Blueprint or Partner Nodes, the workflow can process different modalities in a batch, making it versatile for various applications.

faqItems.question: What are the benefits of using this workflow for prompt variation comparisons?

c5cbee07611f.title: Comfy for Advertising - OOH Visualization
c5cbee07611f.metaDescription: Reformat a poster and place it into realistic OOH scenes. Batch aspect ratios, optional prompt-guided scene notes, and perspective placement for fast ad mockups.
c5cbee07611f.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow helps brand and creative teams quickly place an existing poster into realistic Out-of-Home (OOH) scenarios. It’s organized in two clear stages. STEP 1 – POSTER REFORMAT takes your source poster and non-destructively reformats it to multiple aspect ratios (vertical, horizontal, square, or custom) while preserving the original design. This stage is driven by LoadImage, PrimitiveNode (for width/height values), PrimitiveBoolean (to enable/disable formats), ComfySwitchNode (to route only the formats you want), and BatchImagesNode (to package multiple outputs). SaveImage captures clean, reformatted versions ready for placement.

STEP 2 – OOH VISUALIZATION composites a chosen reformatted poster into a real or described environment. You can supply a location photo with LoadImage via the IMAGE ENVIRONMENT group or describe a scene in plain language (for example, "OOH billboard in downtown San Francisco, on top of a two-story building, pedestrian eye level") in the PROMPT ENVIRONMENT group. GeminiImage2Node is used as a prompt helper to convert your plain-language description into structured scene notes and file-name context. Two custom processing nodes (ae42e662-5e2b-4f52-b31d-267bd68f1c6f and 88b611c3-ce43-4e7a-a59f-dd16f57a8853) handle the perspective mapping and blending of the poster onto the target surface, so you can fine-tune scale, skew, and overlay strength for believable placement. howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the STEP 1 – POSTER REFORMAT group. Use LoadImage to import your source poster.

Set your desired aspect ratios and sizes with PrimitiveNode values (e.g., vertical, horizontal, square). Toggle which formats to generate with the PrimitiveBoolean switches; ComfySwitchNode will route only the ones you enable.

c7c1eb5d5df4.title: Cinematic Product Advertisement — Seedance 2.0
c7c1eb5d5df4.description: A one click workflow to create luxurious cinematic ad videos. Upload images of your product, length of the video, number of unique cuts/shots, and add custom instructions (optional). c7c1eb5d5df4.metaDescription: One-click multishot product ads in ComfyUI using Seedance 2.0 with hero/detail image references and LLM-made time-coded prompts for consistent, cinematic results.
c7c1eb5d5df4.extendedDescription:
This workflow, Cinematic Product Advertisement — Seedance 2.0, builds multi-shot, cinematic product ads from a single, time-coded prompt. You provide a hero/environment image and product detail references via LoadImage nodes, set the total length and number of cuts using PrimitiveInt nodes, and optionally add a creative brief. GeminiNodeV2 then synthesizes a structured, time-cued shot plan that Seedance 2.0 consumes as one prompt. The ByteDance2ReferenceNode conditions the generator with your hero and detail images, helping maintain brand consistency and product fidelity across every shot.

Technically, the pipeline is organized into four groups: Inputs; LLM Prompt Generation; Edit Prompt?; and Generate and Save Video. After GeminiNodeV2 outputs the time-coded script, you can lock it into a PrimitiveStringMultiline node and bypass the LLM for reproducibility. The custom utility node (id: 0e2c3eaa-706c-41fd-b300-b6bd9e84a0a4) handles prompt routing/formatting, while the Seedance 2.0 generator node (id: 2b10af74-c412-4c88-b235-6b170aed965c) renders the full sequence in one pass. PreviewAny lets you quickly inspect intermediate outputs, and SaveVideo exports the final clip. This single-prompt, time-cued design makes it easy to iterate on pacing, camera direction, and product emphasis without juggling multiple, per-shot prompts.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open the Inputs group. Use LoadImage nodes to add references: Image 1 is the hero/environment image (used for all shots), and Images 2–3 are product detail references. Add more images by wiring additional LoadImage nodes.

Set the total video length (seconds) and the number of unique cuts/shots using the PrimitiveInt nodes. If the workflow includes a text field wired to GeminiNodeV2 (PrimitiveStringMultiline), add optional brand/style instructions for the LLM.

Run the LLM Prompt Generation group. GeminiNodeV2 will create a single, time-coded prompt (e.g., 00:00–00:03, 00:03–00:06 ...) describing each shot. Use PreviewAny to inspect the generated prompt and ensure it matches your creative intent.

Lock the prompt: copy the LLM’s structured prompt into the Edit Prompt? group’s PrimitiveStringMultiline field. Then bypass/disable the LLM Prompt Generation group so subsequent runs always use your locked prompt for consistent results.

Generate the video in the Generate and Save Video group. The ByteDance2ReferenceNode feeds your hero/detail images into the Seedance 2.0 node (id: 2b10af74-c412-4c88-b235-6b170aed965c), which renders the full sequence. Use PreviewAny to monitor progress and framing.

Save the result with the SaveVideo node. If timing or emphasis needs refinement, edit the time codes or shot descriptions in the locked prompt, adjust the number of cuts or overall duration, and re-render.
suggestedUseCases: DTC product launch teasers highlighting materials, finishes, and brand mood across multiple shots.
E-commerce hero videos for PDPs, combining a stable environment with consistent product angles.
Social ad variations (A/B tests) by iterating shot pacing and copy within a locked environment.
Brand styleboards and pitch comps that keep a unified look while testing different shot plans.
Packaging or hardware close-ups where detail reference images must remain consistent across cuts.

faqItems.question: What is the role of the hero image versus the detail images?
faqItems.answer: The hero image defines the persistent environment/look for every shot. Detail images focus the generator on specific product features (logos, textures, materials). The ByteDance2ReferenceNode conditions Seedance 2.0 with both so the video stays on-brand and product-accurate throughout.

faqItems.question: How do I control what happens in each shot?
faqItems.answer: Edit the time-coded segments in the Edit Prompt? group’s PrimitiveStringMultiline field. For each time range, describe the camera move, product position, lighting, and any transitions. Ensure your segments cover the total duration and reflect the number of cuts you set.

faqItems.question: Can I reuse a great prompt without re-running the LLM?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Paste the prompt into the Edit Prompt? PrimitiveStringMultiline, then bypass the LLM Prompt Generation group. This locks the plan for reproducible renders and faster iteration.

faqItems.question: Any tips for getting the most consistent results?
faqItems.answer: Use a clear, wide hero/environment photo, high-quality product detail images, and concise time-coded directives. Keep the first draft short (fewer cuts, shorter duration), then lengthen or add shots as needed. If you see drift, tighten language in each time segment and avoid conflicting descriptors.

c98e5c457e1e.metaDescription: Create cinematic multi-shot product ads from images in ComfyUI. Gemini scripts MiniMax H3 with time-coded shots; SaveVideo exports the final video.
c98e5c457e1e.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds a cinematic, multi-shot product advertisement video from up to three reference images. In the Inputs group, you supply Image 1 as the hero/environment reference (the scene this image defines is maintained across all shots) and use Images 2–3 for product detail references. Duration and number of unique shots are controlled with PrimitiveInt nodes, while optional brand/style guidance goes into a PrimitiveStringMultiline input. The LLM Prompt Generation group uses GeminiNodeV2 to transform your inputs into a single, time-cued prompt that MiniMax H3 understands (for example: 0–3s Shot 1, 3–6s Shot 2, etc.). The structured prompt, plus your references, then drives the MiniMax H3 node to render a consistent, on-brand video.

What makes this workflow especially efficient is its one-prompt multishot design. MiniMax H3 expects a single prompt containing all shots and their time windows, so the GeminiNodeV2 node formats a clean shot list with camera moves, transitions, and product highlights. You can preview and verify the shot script using PreviewAny and MarkdownNote. Once satisfied, paste the final script into the Edit Prompt? group to "lock" it and bypass the LLM step for fast, repeatable iterations. The Generate and Save Video group then renders the ad and writes it to disk via SaveVideo, giving you a repeatable pipeline for quickly producing consistent product spots.
howToUse: Load the workflow and open the Inputs group. Add up to 3 images using LoadImage: Image 1 = hero/environment (persists across all shots); Images 2–3 = product detail references. You can wire more LoadImage nodes if needed.

Set the PrimitiveInt nodes for total duration and number of unique shots/cuts. Optionally, add brand tone, specific angles, transitions, or must-show features in the PrimitiveStringMultiline instructions.

Run the LLM Prompt Generation group. GeminiNodeV2 will create a single, time-cued multishot script for MiniMax H3. Use PreviewAny/MarkdownNote to inspect the structured prompt and confirm timing and content.

If you want deterministic, repeatable results: copy the generated prompt into the Edit Prompt? text input, then bypass the LLM Prompt Generation group so the MiniMax H3 node uses your locked script directly.

Go to Generate and Save Video and execute the graph. The MiniMax H3 node renders the video from your references and shot list. Use PreviewAny to spot-check output; SaveVideo writes the final clip to your output directory.
Iterate: adjust duration, number of shots, or the prompt (either via GeminiNodeV2 or the Edit Prompt? input) to refine pacing, angles, and product emphasis, then re-run the final group.

Social media ad variations (A/B tests) with consistent branding and different shot orders
