cd0c4f9f61a4.extendedDescription: Seedance 2.5: Reference to Video is a multimodal ComfyUI workflow that turns your curated references into a single, coherent video clip with synchronized sound. You can feed up to 20 still images for character identity and visual style, plus up to 6 video clips to guide motion, and up to 6 audio clips to drive rhythm and lip-sync. The core of the pipeline is the ByteDance2ReferenceNode, which fuses these inputs to generate a 4–30 second sequence of frames and an aligned audio track. LoadImage nodes bring your still references into the graph, and SaveVideo encodes the generated frames (and accompanying audio from the generator) into a final video file.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the ByteDance2ReferenceNode is available. Open the graph and locate the LoadImage nodes, the central ByteDance2ReferenceNode, and the SaveVideo node.

Add up to 20 image references using the LoadImage nodes (e.g., character faces, product shots, brand elements). Connect these to the image inputs on ByteDance2ReferenceNode and arrange/label them so key references appear first.

Inside ByteDance2ReferenceNode, add up to 6 motion reference videos and up to 6 audio clips using the node’s media inputs (file pickers or list inputs). Order them to match your intended narrative flow and set per-modality weights to balance identity/style (images), motion (videos), and rhythm/lip-sync (audio).

Set core generation settings in ByteDance2ReferenceNode: target duration between 4–30 seconds, frame rate, resolution, and a fixed seed for repeatability. Start with a moderate resolution and frame rate to preview quickly, then raise them for final output.

Click Queue/Execute to generate a preview. Review character consistency, motion pacing, and audio sync; adjust reference ordering and weights if needed. Reduce conflicts by lowering the influence of competing references or removing outliers.

When satisfied, increase quality (resolution/bitrate/FPS if supported), then use the SaveVideo node to encode the final clip. Choose an output path and ensure SaveVideo receives the generated frames (and the audio stream from ByteDance2ReferenceNode) before rendering.

Character-driven short episodes where a hero’s face and outfit remain stable across shots, with lip-synced dialogue pulled from voice tracks.

faqItems.question: How many references should I start with?

faqItems.question: How do I keep the character consistent throughout the clip?
faqItems.answer: Use clear, front-facing images with consistent lighting and aspect ratio, place your best identity shots early in the list, and increase the image-reference influence in ByteDance2ReferenceNode. Avoid mixing drastically different hairstyles, angles, or outfits unless you intend to change appearance.

faqItems.question: My audio drifts or lip-sync looks off. What can I do?
faqItems.answer: Use a single, clean vocal track without heavy reverb or background music for best lip-sync. Ensure your target duration and FPS match your audio plan; if the audio is longer than the selected duration, trim it to fit. Re-queue with a fixed seed after adjustments for consistent comparisons.

faqItems.question: What affects performance and render time?
faqItems.answer: Resolution, frame rate, duration, and the number of references all increase compute and memory use. For faster previews, lower resolution and FPS, shorten duration, and limit references. When satisfied with motion and sync, scale up quality for the final render.

cff9f70a9137.title: Wan2.1 ATI
cff9f70a9137.metaDescription: Trajectory-controlled image-to-video with Wan 2.1 ATI in ComfyUI. Paste a path JSON, set prompts, and generate smooth, directed camera or subject motion.
cff9f70a9137.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow generates short, prompt-driven videos from a single image while precisely following a user-defined camera or subject path. It uses the Wan 2.1 I2V ATI model to blend text guidance, a reference image, and a trajectory JSON so the camera move or object motion is not left to chance. Core nodes include UNETLoader (Wan2_1-I2V-ATI-14B_fp8_e4m3fn.safetensors) and VAELoader (wan_2.1_vae.safetensors) for the diffusion backbone, CLIPLoader and CLIPTextEncode for prompt conditioning, CLIPVisionLoader and CLIPVisionEncode for image conditioning, and WanTrackToVideo to apply trajectory control. KSampler (driven by ModelSamplingSD3) performs the denoising, VAEDecode turns latents into frames, and CreateVideo + SaveVideo packages the result.

Technically, the workflow encodes your positive/negative prompts via CLIPTextEncode and extracts vision features from the input image with CLIPVisionEncode. The PrimitiveStringMultiline node holds the trajectory JSON exported from the Trajectory-Annotation-Tool; WanTrackToVideo consumes that JSON and injects per-frame motion control into the sampling process. ModelSamplingSD3 configures the scheduler so KSampler denoises in a way compatible with Wan 2.1’s training setup. After sampling, VAEDecode reconstructs frames, and CreateVideo assembles them at your chosen resolution and FPS. On a 4090D 24GB at 720x480, expect roughly 500 seconds on a cold first run and around 463 seconds on subsequent runs once weights are cached (actual times vary with settings).
howToUse: Step 1: Load models (Step1 - Load models here). In UNETLoader, select Wan2_1-I2V-ATI-14B_fp8_e4m3fn.safetensors. In VAELoader, select wan_2.1_vae.safetensors. Ensure CLIPLoader and CLIPVisionLoader are connected to their respective text and vision encoders.
Step 2: Upload the reference image (Step2 - Upload image). Use LoadImage, then feed it into CLIPVisionEncode so the model anchors appearance and layout to your image.

Step 3: Create and paste a trajectory (Step 3-Plaste Trajectory JSON). Visit the Trajectory-Annotation-Tool, upload the same-aspect image, draw the camera/subject path, then copy the exported JSON into the PrimitiveStringMultiline node. Keep the aspect ratio and planned frame count consistent with your workflow settings to avoid drift or stretching.

Step 4: Write prompts and set sampling (Step4 - Prompt, Sampling & Decoding). Enter your positive prompt in CLIPTextEncode (e.g., the white dragon warrior...), and your negative prompt (e.g., artifacts or styles to avoid, including the provided Chinese list). In KSampler, set steps, guidance scale (CFG), and seed. Ensure ModelSamplingSD3 is connected to KSampler’s sampling settings.

Step 5: Configure video output. In CreateVideo, set the target size (e.g., 720x480) and FPS (e.g., 24–30). Confirm the number of frames/duration matches your trajectory JSON. Higher resolution or more frames require more VRAM.

Step 6: Generate and save. Execute the graph. Preview frames after VAEDecode if needed, then CreateVideo and SaveVideo will write the final file. If results wobble or overshoot the path, refine the trajectory in the tool, adjust CFG or steps, and re-run. Subsequent runs are typically faster due to cached weights.
suggestedUseCases: Hero shots with controlled camera moves around a character or prop (orbit, push-in, arc).
Product spins and showcases where the camera path must match a storyboard.
Stylized B-roll transitions for edits, matching exact motion curves between scenes.
Previsualization of camera motion for animation or VFX using a single concept image.
Logo and title bumpers with smooth, repeatable motion paths.

faqItems.question: What does the ATI version of Wan 2.1 do in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The ATI variant accepts trajectory conditioning so the model follows a user-defined motion path. In this workflow, WanTrackToVideo reads the trajectory JSON and injects that control into sampling, giving you reproducible, path-driven camera or subject movement.

faqItems.question: How do I get stable, non-jittery motion?
faqItems.answer: Keep the trajectory smooth in the annotation tool, match aspect ratio and frame count between the tool and the workflow, fix the seed for repeatability, and start with moderate CFG (e.g., 4–7) and sufficient steps. If motion still wobbles, simplify or smooth the path and reduce conflicting style prompts.

faqItems.question: What hardware and settings are recommended?
faqItems.answer: A 24 GB VRAM GPU (e.g., 4090-class) comfortably handles 720x480 with typical frame counts; first runs often take around 500 seconds, with later runs faster as weights are cached. With less VRAM, lower resolution or reduce frames. Watch usage in ComfyUI and adjust size/FPS accordingly.

faqItems.question: Can I reuse the same trajectory with different looks?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Keep the same trajectory JSON and reference image if you want consistent motion and composition, then vary the text prompt, CFG, or steps to change style. For major layout or scale changes, update the trajectory to match the new intent.

d124e24eca67.title: Quick Ideate to Storyboard to Animated Video (GPT Image 2 + Seedance 2.0)

d124e24eca67.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Turn a character reference and scene prompt into storyboards and an animated clip using OpenAIGPTImage1 and ByteDance2ReferenceNode (Seedance 2.0).
d124e24eca67.extendedDescription:
This workflow turns a single character reference plus a short scene description into a quick storyboard and an animated clip. It chains OpenAIGPTImage1 to generate storyboard stills from your prompt, then feeds your chosen keyframe and reference art into ByteDance2ReferenceNode (Seedance 2.0) to produce motion, finishing with SaveVideo to render a playable file. LoadImage brings your character reference into the graph, while SaveImage lets you export and review the storyboard frames before you animate.

Technically, the pipeline separates ideation from animation so you can iterate fast. OpenAIGPTImage1 handles image generation for visual beats (thumbnails or keyframes) based on your scene prompt. You then select a preferred frame and pair it with your uploaded character reference for consistent identity and styling inside ByteDance2ReferenceNode, which synthesizes a short image-to-video sequence. The final frames are assembled by SaveVideo. This modular approach makes it easy to refine prompts, swap keyframes, or adjust motion strength and duration without redoing earlier steps.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and verify all nodes are present: LoadImage, OpenAIGPTImage1, ByteDance2ReferenceNode, SaveImage, and SaveVideo. If any nodes require credentials (e.g., OpenAI), add them in the node settings.
Use the LoadImage node to import your character reference art. Choose a clean, front-facing image with a consistent pose and aspect ratio similar to your target video for best identity retention.

Open the OpenAIGPTImage1 node and write a concise scene prompt (subject, action, setting, camera angle, mood). Run the node to generate 2–6 storyboard frames, then use SaveImage to export and review them. Pick the keyframe that best matches your scene.

Connect or assign the selected storyboard frame as the starting image (or conditioning frame) for ByteDance2ReferenceNode, and feed in your original character reference image. Set the motion length/duration, reference strength/weight, and seed if exposed for reproducibility.
Execute the animation stage. Preview intermediate frames if available, then feed the output sequence to the SaveVideo node. Set filename and fps (if exposed) and run SaveVideo to render your clip.
Iterate: refine the scene prompt in OpenAIGPTImage1, try alternate keyframes, and tune ByteDance2ReferenceNode’s motion and reference strength to balance character fidelity with expressive movement.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid previsualization for animated shorts or social media clips using a single character reference.
Pitch boards and animatics: generate quick keyframes, then animate a short beat to communicate timing and tone.

d16e25ecd710.title: Ohneis - Product Workflow
d16e25ecd710.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow for batch product image processing and first/last-frame interpolation to create clean stills and short product videos.
d16e25ecd710.extendedDescription:
Ohneis - Product Workflow is a streamlined ComfyUI pipeline for batch-processing product photos and turning them into clean, consistent assets with optional motion clips. It starts with LoadImage and BatchImagesNode to pull in one or more source photos and apply identical processing across the set. The images are passed through GeminiImage2Node, which performs the core image-to-image transformation configured in your workflow (for example, enhancement, style harmonization, or light retouching). A custom utility node (ID: f4fca0c6-bff8-4410-84df-a9d8961ce181) is included for pre/post-processing—such as resizing, padding, or color/format normalization—before final outputs are written by SaveImage.

For motion, ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode generates a short product video by interpolating between two processed stills (typically the first and last in the batch), producing smooth in-between frames for a subtle pan, spin, or reveal effect. SaveVideo then writes the final clip. The combination of batch consistency (BatchImagesNode), controlled image-to-image processing (GeminiImage2Node), and first/last-frame interpolation (ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode) makes this workflow well-suited to e-commerce catalogs and quick social-ready product reels with minimal setup.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and verify required custom nodes are present: GeminiImage2Node and ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode. If any node shows as missing, install the corresponding custom-node package and restart ComfyUI.
Connect your input images to LoadImage (single image) or point BatchImagesNode to a folder of product photos. Confirm the images load at the expected resolution.

Open GeminiImage2Node and the custom node f4fca0c6-bff8-4410-84df-a9d8961ce181. Adjust their parameters for your goal (e.g., strength/style in GeminiImage2Node; resizing or padding in the custom node) so all items in the batch will be processed consistently.

If you want a video, set up ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode by specifying which two processed frames to interpolate between (commonly the first and last outputs from the batch). Review and tweak any frame-count/duration settings inside the node to control motion length and smoothness.
Set output paths in SaveImage and SaveVideo. Run the workflow. Inspect the processed stills for consistency; if needed, iterate on GeminiImage2Node or the custom node settings and re-run.
Once satisfied, export the final images from SaveImage and the motion clip from SaveVideo for use on product pages, ads, or social posts.
suggestedUseCases: Standardizing a set of product photos (size, framing, and style) for e-commerce catalogs.
Generating quick product teaser clips by interpolating between two hero angles.
Batch-enhancing archival product images to meet current brand guidelines.
Creating social-ready product reels from a pair of stills without a full video shoot.
Producing consistent A/B visual variants by applying the same image-to-image transform across a batch.

Its exact effect depends on how you configure its parameters in the workflow. Open the node to adjust strength, style, or other controls to fit your product look.

faqItems.question: How does the ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode create the video?
faqItems.answer: It takes two processed stills (usually the first and last frames from your batch) and interpolates new frames between them, producing a short, smooth transition. Adjust the node’s frame-count or duration settings to control motion length and smoothness, then SaveVideo writes the final clip.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of the custom node f4fca0c6-bff8-4410-84df-a9d8961ce181?
faqItems.answer: It’s a utility step used for pre/post-processing, such as resizing, padding to a target aspect ratio, or other formatting tasks. Open the node to review its parameters and ensure they match your target output (e.g., square thumbnails or specific resolutions).

Technically, the GrokImageNode packages your prompt and generation settings—such as quality (low or medium to control cost), target resolution (1K or 2K), and aspect ratio—then submits them to the Grok service and returns the generated image to the ComfyUI graph. SaveImageAdvanced then saves that image to your output folder with predictable naming, making it easy to iterate. The workflow is ideal for poster and cover design, product and brand visuals, and character‑driven scenes where consistent looks matter, especially when you need sharp, readable short text in the composition.
howToUse: Load the workflow into ComfyUI and open it in the graph view.
Open the GrokImageNode and configure access (e.g., add your API key or credentials if required by your setup).
Enter your prompt. For text-in-image tasks, include the exact phrase you want rendered (you can use quotes) and add brief style or subject cues.
Choose generation settings in GrokImageNode: select quality (low for quick drafts, medium for better fidelity), pick a target resolution (1K or 2K), and select one of the supported aspect ratios.
Configure SaveImageAdvanced to set the output folder and a filename pattern so each run is saved consistently.
Queue the workflow. Review the result, then refine your prompt or settings (quality, aspect ratio, resolution) and run again until you achieve the desired look.
suggestedUseCases: Poster, flyer, and cover mockups where titles and short taglines must remain sharp and legible.
Product and brand visuals featuring brief slogans, model numbers, or logotype-like text elements.
Social banners and ad creative generated across multiple aspect ratios for different placements.
Character-driven scenes or story beats where you want a consistent look across iterations.
Editorial or blog illustrations that call for bold typography and clean compositions.

faqItems.question: When should I use low vs. medium quality?
faqItems.answer: Use low for quick, low-cost drafts and concept exploration. Switch to medium for improved detail and more reliable text legibility. Medium may take longer and cost more, but it’s a better choice for final outputs.

faqItems.question: How do I get crisp, readable text in the image?
faqItems.answer: Keep prompts concise and include the exact text you want (use quotes if helpful). Specify typography cues like 'clean, bold type' and ensure a simple, high-contrast background. Avoid very long strings; short phrases render more cleanly.

faqItems.question: What aspect ratios and sizes can I generate?
faqItems.answer: The GrokImageNode exposes 14 preset aspect ratios and supports 1K or 2K outputs. Pick an aspect ratio that matches the destination (e.g., square for profiles, wide for banners). Choose 2K for higher detail or print-ready work, and 1K for web or fast iteration.

faqItems.question: How can I keep characters or styles consistent across runs?
faqItems.answer: Reuse the same core prompt and descriptors. Keep character attributes stable (e.g., clothing, colors, scene). If your GrokImageNode build exposes a seed field, set and reuse the same seed between runs to reduce variation.

d25788ed5d19.title: Kling O3: Image Genertaion
d25788ed5d19.description: Upload up to 10 reference images to guide the synthesis. Generate a new image using the Kling O3 model based on your provided visual inputs.
d25788ed5d19.metaDescription: Create unique images with Kling O3 by blending up to 10 reference images. Perfect for artists seeking to synthesize multiple visual styles.
d25788ed5d19.extendedDescription:
The Kling O3: Image Generation workflow is designed to create new images by leveraging a set of up to 10 reference images. At its core, this workflow uses the Kling O3 model, a sophisticated image synthesis model known for its ability to blend multiple visual inputs into a cohesive new image. The process begins by loading your reference images using the LoadImage node, which allows the workflow to access and process up to 10 images simultaneously. These images are then handled by the BatchImagesNode, which organizes them for efficient processing and synthesis. The KlingOmniProImageNode is where the magic happens; it takes the batched images and synthesizes a new image that encapsulates the essence of the input images. Finally, the SaveImage node ensures that the generated image is saved to your desired location, making it easy to access and use in your projects.

This workflow is particularly useful for artists and designers who want to create unique images that draw inspiration from multiple sources. By using the Kling O3 model, users can achieve high-quality results that reflect the nuances of the input images. The workflow's ability to handle multiple inputs and produce a single, unified output makes it a powerful tool for creative projects that require a blend of different visual styles or themes.
howToUse: Load the workflow and prepare your reference images.
Use the LoadImage node to upload up to 10 images that will guide the synthesis.
The BatchImagesNode will organize these images for processing.
The KlingOmniProImageNode will synthesize a new image based on your inputs.
Use the SaveImage node to save the generated image to your desired location.
Review and use the generated image in your projects.
suggestedUseCases: Creating a new art piece by blending multiple styles.
Designing a unique logo or brand image using various inspirations.
Generating concept art for video games or films.
Producing composite images for advertising campaigns.
Developing personalized wallpapers or digital backgrounds.

faqItems.question: Can I use more than 10 reference images?
faqItems.answer: No, the workflow is designed to handle up to 10 images. Using more than this may require modifying the workflow.

faqItems.question: What image formats are supported for input?
faqItems.answer: The LoadImage node supports common formats such as JPEG, PNG, and BMP.

faqItems.question: How does the Kling O3 model handle different image styles?
faqItems.answer: The Kling O3 model is adept at synthesizing images by analyzing and blending the styles and elements from the input images.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the influence of each reference image?
faqItems.answer: Currently, the workflow does not support adjusting the influence of individual images, but this can be explored by modifying the workflow settings.

d2cee11e428d.title: Realistic Poster Redesign With Character Transformation
d2cee11e428d.description: Transform uploaded images into realistic poster designs. Change character poses, faces, and clothing while maintaining artistic style and color schemes. Outputs a visually impactful poster with artistic typography.
d2cee11e428d.metaDescription: Transform images into realistic posters with character changes using ComfyUI. Includes pose, face, and clothing edits with artistic style retention.
d2cee11e428d.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow, titled 'Realistic Poster Redesign With Character Transformation,' is designed to transform your uploaded images into stunning, realistic poster designs. Utilizing the Nano Banana Pro model, this workflow allows for intricate changes to character poses, faces, and clothing while preserving the artistic style and color scheme of the original image. The workflow is structured around a series of nodes, including LoadImage, SaveImage, and GeminiImage2Node, which collectively facilitate the transformation process. Additionally, the ComfySwitchNode and StringConcatenate nodes allow users to toggle between poster remake mode and regular image edit mode, offering flexibility in the type of transformation applied.

The workflow is particularly useful for artists and designers looking to create visually impactful posters with artistic typography. By leveraging the capabilities of the Nano Banana Pro model, users can achieve high-quality results that are both aesthetically pleasing and technically impressive. The integration of MarkdownNote and PrimitiveStringMultiline nodes further enhances the workflow by allowing users to add custom text and notes, making it a versatile tool for creative projects.
howToUse: Load your image into the workflow using the LoadImage node.
Select the desired mode using the ComfySwitchNode: 'Poster remake mode' for new designs or 'Image edit mode' for regular edits.
Input any additional text or notes using the MarkdownNote and PrimitiveStringMultiline nodes.
Run the transformation process with the GeminiImage2Node to adjust character poses, faces, and clothing.
Save the transformed image using the SaveImage node to finalize your poster design.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional posters for events with custom character designs.
Redesigning movie posters with updated character appearances.
Developing unique art prints for sale or personal use.
Enhancing personal photography with artistic typography and design elements.

faqItems.question: Can I use this workflow to edit multiple images at once?
faqItems.answer: Currently, the workflow is designed for single-image transformations. You would need to load and process each image individually.

faqItems.question: What types of images work best with this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Images with clear character features and distinct color schemes tend to yield the best results, as the model can effectively apply changes while maintaining artistic integrity.

faqItems.question: How do I switch between poster remake and image edit modes?
faqItems.answer: Use the ComfySwitchNode to toggle between modes. Enter your desired content for the poster in 'Poster remake mode' or proceed with regular edits in 'Image edit mode.'

faqItems.question: Is it possible to customize the typography on the poster?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can customize typography by using the MarkdownNote and PrimitiveStringMultiline nodes to add and adjust text elements.

d32f7ff48696.title: SDPose: Video Multi-Person Detection
d32f7ff48696.description: Upload a video to detect human poses. Supports detection for both single individuals and multiple people within the same scene
d32f7ff48696.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial: Detect and overlay multi-person whole-body poses on video with SDPose-OOD. Customize max detections, preview, and export annotated results.
d32f7ff48696.extendedDescription:
This workflow performs multi-person human pose detection on video using the SDPose-OOD whole-body model. It ingests a video with LoadVideo, extracts frame size and FPS via GetVideoComponents, and feeds each frame into an SDPose subgraph (node ID 01b6a731-fb78-4070-9a38-c87146da9604). Inside the subgraph, an object detector proposes person bounding boxes per frame and the SDPose whole-body checkpoint (sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors) estimates keypoints for body, hands, and face. The PrimitiveInt node controls max_detections, letting you cap how many people are processed per frame in crowded scenes.

The workflow outputs two visualizations: bounding boxes via DrawBBoxes and a pose map overlay blended onto the original frames with ImageBlend. ResizeImageMaskNode ensures the pose map matches the source frame dimensions, and PreviewImage offers a quick sanity check before exporting. Finally, CreateVideo reassembles the annotated frames at the original FPS, and SaveVideo writes the result. The SDPose logic is packaged as a subgraph, so you can right-click to Unpack Subgraph and tweak internal thresholds or routing if you want finer control.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and download the models: place sdpose_wholebody_fp16.safetensors into your checkpoints folder. If provided, place the RT-DETR detector file into diffusion_models as indicated.
Load your video in the LoadVideo node. GetVideoComponents will pass width/height and FPS forward so the pipeline preserves the original timing and aspect.
Set PrimitiveInt:max_detections to the maximum number of people you expect per frame (e.g., 1–6). For crowded scenes, increase this value; for speed, lower it.
Run once and inspect PreviewImage to confirm poses and boxes align correctly. Use ImageBlend’s opacity to control how strongly the pose map overlays the original video.
Optionally, right-click the SDPose subgraph node (01b6a731-...) and choose Unpack Subgraph to adjust internal detection/pose settings or to change how boxes and pose maps are routed.
When satisfied, queue the workflow. CreateVideo will assemble frames and SaveVideo will write the annotated output to your chosen location.
suggestedUseCases: Sports and fitness form review: visualize joint positions and limb angles across reps or drills.
Dance and choreography capture: extract multi-person pose overlays for timing and alignment checks.
Crowd studies and HCI research: quickly assess body dynamics in multi-user interaction footage.
Preprocessing for pose-conditioned generation: export pose maps to drive downstream image/video synthesis.
Content moderation or editorial markup: highlight who is on-screen and how they move without revealing identities.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow track person identities across frames?
faqItems.answer: No. It performs per-frame multi-person detection and pose estimation. IDs are not persisted between frames. For tracking, you would add a tracker outside this subgraph.

faqItems.question: How can I improve detection in crowded or wide shots?
faqItems.answer: Increase PrimitiveInt:max_detections, ensure the input resolution is sufficient, and consider unpacking the subgraph to raise detection confidence or adjust NMS. Note that higher resolution and more detections increase compute time.

faqItems.question: Can I export only the pose maps (without the original video)?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Unpack the subgraph or tap the pose map output before ImageBlend and route it to CreateVideo/SaveVideo. You can also save per-frame images by adding a SaveImage node instead of video assembly.

faqItems.question: What video formats are supported?
faqItems.answer: LoadVideo and SaveVideo rely on your ComfyUI/FFmpeg setup. MP4/H.264 is commonly supported. If you encounter format issues, transcode the input to a standard MP4 and keep the default SaveVideo settings.

d3b539e33bf2.title: ACE-Step 1.5 AI Lyric Song Generation
d3b539e33bf2.description: Input a music style and optional lyrics. Generate a full song with AI-created lyrics and audio.
d3b539e33bf2.metaDescription: Generate full songs with AI-created lyrics and audio using the ACE-Step 1.5 workflow. Perfect for musicians and creators.
d3b539e33bf2.extendedDescription: The ACE-Step 1.5 AI Lyric Song Generation workflow is a sophisticated tool designed to transform a simple music style input and optional lyrics into a complete song with AI-generated lyrics and audio. This workflow leverages the ACE-Step and Google Gemini models to synthesize both text and audio, providing a seamless experience from concept to creation. At its core, the workflow uses nodes like SaveAudioMP3 for outputting the final audio file, and GeminiNode for processing the AI-generated content. The RegexExtract node is instrumental in parsing and refining input data, ensuring that the AI's output is coherent and aligned with the user's intent. This workflow is particularly useful for musicians, content creators, and anyone interested in exploring AI's potential in music production.
howToUse: Load the ACE-Step 1.5 AI Lyric Song Generation workflow in ComfyUI.
Input your desired music style and any optional lyrics into the designated fields.
Ensure the correct models, ACE-Step and Google Gemini, are loaded for optimal performance.
Run the workflow to generate AI-created lyrics and audio.
Use the SaveAudioMP3 node to export your final song as an MP3 file.
Preview your song using the PreviewAny node to ensure it meets your expectations.
suggestedUseCases: Creating unique songs for personal or commercial projects.
Experimenting with AI-generated music for creative inspiration.
Developing soundtracks for videos and multimedia presentations.
Enhancing songwriting processes with AI-assisted lyric generation.
Generating background music for podcasts or live streams.

faqItems.question: What music styles can I input into the workflow?
faqItems.answer: You can input any music style you prefer. The AI is designed to adapt and generate lyrics and audio that align with your specified style.

faqItems.question: Can I use my own lyrics in the song generation process?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can input your own lyrics, and the AI will incorporate them into the song while generating the rest of the content.

faqItems.question: What file format is the final song saved as?
faqItems.answer: The final song is saved as an MP3 file using the SaveAudioMP3 node, which is widely compatible with most audio players.

faqItems.question: Do I need to have any prior experience with AI to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No prior AI experience is necessary. The workflow is designed to be user-friendly, with clear instructions and intuitive nodes to guide you through the process.

d4b951896b54.title: Seedance2.0 Real Human: Image to Video
d4b951896b54.description: Upload a reference video of a real person for identity verification. Use your own photo to validate and generate a personalized video output.
d4b951896b54.metaDescription: ComfyUI Seedance2.0 tutorial: verify real-human photo/video as assets, link with Group ID, then generate a personalized image-to-video result.
d4b951896b54.extendedDescription:
Seedance2.0 Real Human: Image to Video is a compliant, identity-verified image-to-video workflow built with ByteDance partner nodes in ComfyUI. It guides you through creating verified real-human assets first, then generating a personalized video that transfers motion from a reference video to your identity photo. The verification step is handled by ByteDanceCreateImageAsset and ByteDanceCreateVideoAsset, which turn your uploaded portrait and reference video into reusable asset IDs and a shared Group ID that ties same-person assets together for backend recognition.

Once assets are approved and IDs are available, ByteDance2ReferenceNode performs the image-to-video generation using those IDs (instead of raw media) to meet the provider’s legal requirements. PreviewAny lets you quickly check intermediate info or the final clip, and SaveVideo writes the result to disk. LoadImage and LoadVideo handle local file inputs, while the MarkdownNote provides in-graph guidance. The workflow also includes a Save IDs for future reuse section so you can store and reuse your Group ID and asset IDs, avoiding repeat uploads for the same person. Asset limits apply (images up to 9, videos up to 3, audio up to 3).
howToUse: Open the workflow and read the MarkdownNote. If you already have verified assets, keep only the core nodes enabled; otherwise enable the Video Asset Creation Example group (Select and Ctrl-B) to walk through first-time verification.

Create an Image Asset: connect LoadImage to ByteDanceCreateImageAsset and run it to upload and verify your portrait. When the node returns, copy the Image Asset ID and the new Group ID into the Save IDs for future reuse section.

Create a Video Asset: connect LoadVideo (your reference motion clip of the same person) to ByteDanceCreateVideoAsset. Paste the saved Group ID into the node (to link assets to the same identity) and run it. Save the returned Video Asset ID.

Configure generation: in ByteDance2ReferenceNode, use the verified IDs (Image Asset ID for identity and Video Asset ID for motion). For real-human content, do not connect raw image/video inputs—use the asset IDs produced by the Create Image/Video Asset nodes.
Run the graph to generate the personalized video. Use PreviewAny to inspect the output and then connect SaveVideo to export the final clip to disk.

For future runs with the same person, skip the upload/verification steps: re-enter the saved Group ID and asset IDs in the appropriate fields, and re-run only the ByteDance2ReferenceNode to produce new results within asset limits.
suggestedUseCases: Generate compliant, personalized explainer clips by matching your portrait to motion from a verified reference video.
Maintain consistent on-camera identity across projects by reusing the same Group ID and asset IDs after initial verification.
Create internal comms or training videos for staff who have consented, leveraging one-time verification to streamline repeated outputs.
Produce short social updates or announcements with a verified identity and a new motion reference while staying within platform policies.

faqItems.question: Why can’t I connect real-human images or videos directly to ByteDance2ReferenceNode?
faqItems.answer: For real-human content, the provider requires verified assets. Use ByteDanceCreateImageAsset and ByteDanceCreateVideoAsset to upload and verify media first. Then, supply the resulting asset IDs (and Group ID) to ByteDance2ReferenceNode for generation.

faqItems.question: What is the Group ID and how should I use it?
faqItems.answer: The Group ID groups assets that belong to the same person. It’s auto-generated when you first verify an image or video via the Create Image/Video Asset nodes. Save it and reuse it when uploading additional assets of the same person to help backend recognition and keep your library organized.

faqItems.question: What are the asset limits for this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Per the provider limits: up to 9 image assets, 3 video assets, and 3 audio assets per identity group. Stay within these limits when preparing your verified media.

faqItems.question: Do I need to verify again for future projects?
faqItems.answer: No, not for the same assets. Save your Group ID and asset IDs in the Save IDs for future reuse section. You can reference them directly in ByteDance2ReferenceNode for subsequent generations without re-uploading.

d54ddc21563b.title: Seed Audio 1.0: Text + Audio to Audio
d54ddc21563b.description: Upload a reference audio clip and write a text prompt to clone the voice into a new scene. Generate dialogue, background music, and sound effects with up to 3 reference voices.

d5ce59e59ff3.title: Photo to Cartoon Style Caricature
d5ce59e59ff3.description: This workflow is as simple as uploading your picture and selecting one of 15 preset cartoon styles to transform it into.
d5ce59e59ff3.metaDescription: Turn photos into cartoon-style caricatures in ComfyUI. Choose from 15 presets, preview instantly, and save results with a simple, fast workflow.
d5ce59e59ff3.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow turns a regular photo into a cartoon-style caricature using one of 15 preset looks. It starts with LoadImage for your source photo, passes your style choice from a CustomCombo dropdown, extracts the matching preset parameters via JsonExtractString, and assembles any required identifiers with StringConcatenate. The core stylization happens in a custom processing node (UUID d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e), which takes the source image plus the selected style key and outputs a single stylized frame. You can inspect results live with PreviewAny and save the final image via SaveImage.

Under the hood, the preset system keeps results consistent and repeatable across images. The JSON-driven mapping decouples the user-friendly style names from the actual configuration values the processing node expects, making it easy to swap styles without touching low-level settings. Because the heavy lifting is encapsulated inside the d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e node, the graph stays simple and fast to use—no additional model loading or sampler tuning required.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and open it in the graph view.
In the LoadImage node, upload your source photo (frontal, well-lit portraits work best).
Use the CustomCombo dropdown to select one of the 15 cartoon styles. The selection is mapped by JsonExtractString to the exact style key the processor expects.
Run/Queue the workflow. Watch PreviewAny to confirm the look and check for facial detail and edges.
If needed, try another style from the dropdown or adjust any exposed strength/intensity parameters on the d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e node (if available in your version).
Set your desired filename/prefix in SaveImage and run again to export the final caricature to the ComfyUI output folder.
suggestedUseCases: Create consistent, on-brand profile avatars for teams or communities.
Generate fun social media portraits or stickers from selfies.
Quick mockups of character portraits for pitch decks or presentation slides.
Event badges and name tags with a playful, unified cartoon look.
Personalized gifts like printed postcards or merch with caricatured photos.

faqItems.question: Can I add my own custom style to the dropdown?
faqItems.answer: You can extend the presets only if the processing node (d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e) recognizes additional style keys. Update the JSON presets feeding JsonExtractString and add the new option to CustomCombo. If the node doesn’t support the new key, it will fall back or fail.

faqItems.question: Does this require a GPU?
faqItems.answer: It depends on how the custom processing node is implemented on your system. Many stylization nodes prefer a GPU and will run much faster with one, but some builds can run on CPU at reduced speed.

faqItems.question: What image size works best?
faqItems.answer: Portraits at 512–1024 px on the shortest side typically produce clean lines and colors. Crop to the head and shoulders when possible, use even lighting, and avoid heavy motion blur.

faqItems.question: Can I batch-process multiple photos?
faqItems.answer: This graph focuses on single-image input via LoadImage. For batches, duplicate the branch or swap in a batch-capable loader node and feed the same CustomCombo/JSON preset mapping into the processor.

d6109704c9d6.title: Nano Banana 2 Lite: Text to Image
d6109704c9d6.description: Generate images from text descriptions using the ultra-fast Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image model, designed for rapid creation and iteration with no file inputs required. This workflow produces one or more generated images based on your text prompt, with support for interleaved text and image inputs. Ideal for quick concept visualization, rapid prototyping, and iterative design exploration.
d6109704c9d6.metaDescription: Ultra-fast ComfyUI text-to-image with Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image. Type a prompt, generate one or more images, and auto-save results for rapid iteration.
d6109704c9d6.extendedDescription:
Nano Banana 2 Lite: Text to Image is a minimal, speed-focused ComfyUI workflow that turns short text prompts into images using Google’s Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image model. It’s built for rapid concepting and quick iterations—no file inputs required—so you can move from idea to visual in seconds. The workflow produces one or more images per prompt, making side-by-side exploration straightforward.

Under the hood, the GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node handles the API call to Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image, taking your text prompt (and optionally interleaved text+image content when supported) and returning generated images to the graph. Outputs are sent directly to SaveImageAdvanced, which writes the results to disk with your chosen folder and filename settings. Because Flash-Lite Image is optimized for low latency, this setup excels at fast iteration loops—adjust the prompt, re-queue, compare, and refine—with minimal overhead.

While it’s streamlined, the node still exposes practical generation controls (such as output count and size, as provided by the node), letting you balance speed and visual detail for early-stage exploration. If you need reference guidance, the workflow supports interleaved content when the node’s interface enables it, but it’s not required for basic text-to-image generation.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON into ComfyUI (Drag-and-drop the file into the canvas or use ComfyUI’s workflow import).
Open the GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node: enter your text prompt. If required by your setup, add your Gemini API key in the node or in the node’s documented settings.
Adjust generation options exposed by the node (e.g., number of images and image size, if available). Keep prompts concise and specific for the fastest, clearest results.
Configure SaveImageAdvanced: choose an output folder, set a filename prefix/pattern, and confirm image format settings.

Queue the workflow. Review the generated images in the UI and in your save folder. Iterate quickly by refining the prompt or settings, then re-queue. If the node supports interleaved content, add optional image references per the node’s interface for guided generations.
suggestedUseCases: Rapid concept thumbnails for products, environments, or characters
Moodboards and visual direction drafts for creative briefs
Early UI/UX ideation and layout sketches from short prompts
Storyboarding rough frames for videos or presentations
Quick visual variations to compare style, composition, or color themes

faqItems.question: Do I need a local GPU to use this workflow?
faqItems.answer: No. GeminiNanoBanana2V2 calls the Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image API, so generation runs in the cloud. Your machine handles ComfyUI and saving files only.

faqItems.question: How do I provide a Gemini API key?
faqItems.answer: Follow the GeminiNanoBanana2V2 node’s documentation. Typically, you either paste the key in the node’s settings or set it as an environment/config variable recognized by the node.

faqItems.question: Can I use reference images with the prompt?
faqItems.answer: Yes, when the node’s interface supports interleaved text+image inputs. You can mix descriptive text with image parts to guide composition or style. If not needed, simple text-only prompts work out of the box.

faqItems.question: Where are outputs saved and how do I control filenames?
faqItems.answer: SaveImageAdvanced handles saving. Set the output directory and filename prefix/pattern there. The node writes each generated image to disk after inference completes.

d636956bdddc.title: Restore Archival Footage - LTX 2.3 Dearchive LoRA
d636956bdddc.description: Upload an input video or archival footage and restore it with 1 click.
d636956bdddc.metaDescription: One-click ComfyUI workflow to restore archival video using LTX 2.3 with a Dearchive LoRA. Load footage, auto-clean frames, and export at original FPS.
d636956bdddc.extendedDescription:
This workflow restores archival or degraded footage in one pass using an LTX 2.3 backbone guided by a Dearchive LoRA. It starts by decoding your clip with LoadVideo and reading timing/size data via GetVideoComponents, then routes frames through the restoration core before re-encoding to a clean MP4 with SaveVideo. The defaults are tuned to reduce common archive artifacts such as heavy grain, flicker, scratches, and compression noise, while keeping the original framing and timing intact.

Under the hood, two custom nodes (IDs: 14beb77c-6207-496b-9559-1eeb98b2ee76 and 5784f1cc-cf8c-4289-9c5b-2e837048198f) implement the LTX 2.3 model pass and apply the Dearchive LoRA. GetVideoComponents feeds FPS and resolution forward so the SaveVideo node can encode at the correct timing, helping maintain temporal consistency. If the custom nodes expose a LoRA weight/strength parameter, you can fine-tune the level of restoration: higher values push stronger cleaning, lower values retain more original texture.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then open the LoadVideo node and set the path to your source clip (common formats like MP4 or MOV work best).
Inspect the GetVideoComponents node to confirm it reads the correct FPS and resolution; these values should already be wired forward to the rest of the graph.

Locate the restoration core nodes (IDs: 14beb77c-6207-496b-9559-1eeb98b2ee76 and 5784f1cc-cf8c-4289-9c5b-2e837048198f). Leave defaults for a first run. If a LoRA strength or weight setting is available, start around 0.7–0.85 for balanced cleaning.
Open the SaveVideo node and choose an output directory/filename. Ensure its FPS input is connected from GetVideoComponents so the export timing matches the source.
Click Queue/Execute to run. Monitor VRAM usage in your system monitor; longer or higher-resolution clips take more time.

Review the saved result from SaveVideo. If the output looks over-smoothed, lower the LoRA strength (if exposed). If artifacts remain, try a slightly higher strength or process at a lower resolution, then upscale afterward.
suggestedUseCases: Cleaning digitized VHS/camcorder recordings to reduce grain, flicker, and tape noise before re-archiving.
Restoring historical newsreels or silent-era scans while preserving original timing and framing.
Preparing archival B‑roll for documentaries by removing compression artifacts and stabilizing flicker.
Improving low‑bitrate web archives prior to re-encoding for modern delivery platforms.
Refining family archives and home movies for sharing without heavy manual editing.

faqItems.question: Which nodes do the actual restoration?
faqItems.answer: The restoration is performed by two custom nodes in this graph (IDs: 14beb77c-6207-496b-9559-1eeb98b2ee76 and 5784f1cc-cf8c-4289-9c5b-2e837048198f). They run the LTX 2.3 model with a Dearchive LoRA to clean frames. LoadVideo/GetVideoComponents handle decoding and timing; SaveVideo encodes the result.

faqItems.question: Does this workflow preserve audio?
faqItems.answer: ComfyUI’s SaveVideo typically exports without audio unless the graph explicitly routes audio to it. This template uses GetVideoComponents for FPS/size; if audio is not wired to SaveVideo, export will be silent. If you need audio, remux the original track with the cleaned video using a tool like ffmpeg, or add audio passthrough in the graph.

faqItems.question: How can I control how strong the restoration is?
faqItems.answer: If the custom restoration node exposes a LoRA weight/strength parameter, lower values preserve more original grain/texture (e.g., 0.5–0.7), while higher values apply stronger cleanup (e.g., 0.8–1.0). If no strength control is visible, use the defaults and adjust resolution or encode settings to balance sharpness and cleanliness.

faqItems.question: What resolutions and clip lengths are practical?
faqItems.answer: Performance depends on your GPU. 720p–1080p clips of a few minutes are a good starting point. For longer or 4K material, process in segments or downscale first, then upscale after restoration. Reducing resolution or clip length helps avoid VRAM limits and speeds up processing.

d6bda294b8ec.title: Qwen-Image: Text to Image
d6bda294b8ec.description: Generate images with exceptional multilingual text rendering and editing capabilities using Qwen-Image's 20B MMDiT model.
d6bda294b8ec.metaDescription: ComfyUI tutorial for Qwen-Image 20B MMDiT text-to-image with strong multilingual text rendering. Learn setup, prompts, aspect ratios, FP8 tips, and saving results.
d6bda294b8ec.extendedDescription:
This workflow demonstrates text-to-image generation with Qwen-Image’s 20B MMDiT diffusion transformer inside ComfyUI. It centers on a dedicated Qwen-Image generation node (UUID: e5cfe5ba-2ae0-4bc4-869f-ab2228cb44d3), which loads the Qwen-Image model weights and produces an image directly from your prompt. A MarkdownNote node provides inline guidance within the graph, and a SaveImage node writes the final output to your ComfyUI output directory.

Technically, the Qwen-Image node runs the 20B MMDiT model end-to-end, handling prompt conditioning and diffusion steps internally. The official model files are available from the Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI repositories (Hugging Face or Modelscope). The workflow supports practical presets for aspect ratios and resolutions (e.g., 1328×1328 for 1:1, 1664×928 for 16:9, 928×1664 for 9:16, 1472×1140 for 4:3). On an RTX 4090D 24GB, the FP8 e4m3fn configuration has been observed to complete a first image in roughly 90 seconds and subsequent images faster, depending on settings. Qwen-Image is designed to render multilingual text inside images, making it well-suited for posters, signage, UI mocks, and other graphics where readable text is important.
howToUse: Load the provided workflow JSON in ComfyUI and review the MarkdownNote for any embedded setup tips.
Download the Qwen-Image model files from the Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI repository on Hugging Face or Modelscope, then place them in your ComfyUI models directory as instructed by the repo.
Open the Qwen-Image generation node (UUID: e5cfe5ba-2ae0-4bc4-869f-ab2228cb44d3) and select the desired checkpoint/precision variant (e.g., FP8 e4m3fn if available) that fits your GPU VRAM.
Set your image size using one of the tested presets (e.g., 1328×1328 for square, 1664×928 for 16:9, 928×1664 for 9:16, or 1472×1140 for 4:3) to balance quality and speed.
Enter a clear prompt that includes the exact text you want rendered and the target language (e.g., English, Chinese, Arabic). Keep wording concise when you need crisp, readable text.
Run the workflow. Inspect the output saved by the SaveImage node in your ComfyUI output directory, then iterate on prompt, resolution, and model precision as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Poster, flyer, and banner concepts that require readable multilingual titles and captions.
Product packaging mockups with on-box text, labels, or compliance markings.
Signage, storefront, and wayfinding visuals in various scripts and languages.
UI/UX concept art with embedded interface copy, buttons, and dialog text.
Social media graphics and thumbnails that mix imagery with short, sharp text.

faqItems.question: Where do I get the Qwen-Image model files, and how do I install them?
faqItems.answer: Download from the Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image_ComfyUI repositories on Hugging Face or Modelscope. Follow the repo’s placement instructions (typically within your ComfyUI models directory). Then select the checkpoint in the Qwen-Image node.

faqItems.question: What resolutions work best for clean text rendering?
faqItems.answer: Use the provided presets tested with this workflow: 1328×1328 (1:1), 1664×928 (16:9), 928×1664 (9:16), and 1472×1140 (4:3). Larger sizes can improve readability but increase VRAM and render time.

faqItems.question: How much VRAM do I need, and what is FP8 e4m3fn?
faqItems.answer: On an RTX 4090D 24GB, FP8 e4m3fn runs efficiently and can render a first image in roughly 90 seconds, with later runs faster depending on settings. FP8 e4m3fn is a low-precision configuration that reduces memory use. If you have less VRAM, lower the resolution or use a lighter precision/checkpoint if available.

faqItems.question: How can I improve the clarity of multilingual text in the image?
faqItems.answer: Be explicit and concise about the text and language in your prompt; avoid overly long, complex instructions when you need sharp typography. Choose a suitable resolution preset, prefer high-contrast backgrounds, and iterate on wording if characters look ambiguous.

d70243b6fc64.title: Headshot Generator
d70243b6fc64.description: Upload a selfie, pick an outfit with a backdrop and generate a professional quality headshot portrait of yourself.
d70243b6fc64.metaDescription: Create professional headshots from a selfie. Pick outfit and backdrop via presets or custom text. Preview and save results with a clean ComfyUI workflow.
d70243b6fc64.extendedDescription:
This Headshot Generator workflow lets you upload a selfie, choose an outfit and backdrop, and produce a polished, professional portrait. It wires together text controls and image conditioning so your face is preserved while the clothing and background are restyled. Your selfie is brought in with LoadImage and routed into a core generation node (ID: d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e) that handles the actual synthesis. PreviewAny gives you quick visual checks, and SaveImage writes final results to disk.

Outfit and backdrop are managed with text nodes so you can work from presets or free‑type instructions. PrimitiveStringMultiline holds a small JSON block of presets; JsonExtractString pulls fields like outfit and backdrop from that JSON. ComfySwitchNode lets you toggle between preset-driven text and a custom prompt path. StringConcatenate assembles the final instruction text the generator sees (for example, a base headshot prompt plus your selected outfit and backdrop). A CustomCombo node encapsulates supporting pieces of the pipeline, so model loading and sampler details stay tidy while still exposing the key inputs you need for fast iteration.
howToUse: Load the workflow JSON in ComfyUI, then locate the key nodes: LoadImage (selfie), PrimitiveStringMultiline (presets), ComfySwitchNode (prompt source), the core generator (d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e or its CustomCombo wrapper), PreviewAny, and SaveImage.
Click LoadImage and select a clear, front-facing selfie (good lighting, neutral expression, minimal occlusion). Ensure the face is centered and upright.

Choose how to describe clothing and background: either edit the JSON in PrimitiveStringMultiline (include keys like "outfit" and "backdrop") or switch ComfySwitchNode to the custom prompt input and type a free-form description.

Run the graph. The text inputs are combined by StringConcatenate, preset fields are parsed by JsonExtractString, and the selfie plus instructions flow into the generator node. Use PreviewAny to quickly inspect outputs and make adjustments to text or switch settings.

When satisfied, trigger SaveImage to export the final headshot. If your version of the CustomCombo or core generator exposes parameters (e.g., guidance/steps/strength), fine-tune them between runs for sharpness or stronger adherence to your selfie.
suggestedUseCases: Professional LinkedIn or resume headshots that match specific dress codes and neutral studio backdrops.
Consistent team portraits for company websites by standardizing outfit/backdrop presets across multiple runs.
Themed profile photos (e.g., conference lanyard, holiday backdrop) while maintaining accurate facial identity.
Creator or seller profile images for marketplaces and social platforms with brand-aligned colors and backgrounds.
Rapid A/B testing of outfits and backgrounds to decide on a final look before scheduling a studio session.

faqItems.question: How do I add or edit outfit/backdrop presets?
faqItems.answer: Open PrimitiveStringMultiline and edit the JSON. Include keys your JsonExtractString nodes expect (commonly "outfit" and "backdrop"). Example: {"outfit": "navy blazer, white shirt", "backdrop": "soft gray studio backdrop"}. Run the graph to apply.

faqItems.question: My face doesn’t look like me. How can I improve likeness?
faqItems.answer: Use a sharp, well-lit, front-facing selfie with your full face visible and minimal clutter. Crop so your head and shoulders dominate the frame. If your CustomCombo/core node exposes an image influence/strength control, increase it slightly to prioritize the selfie over stylization.

faqItems.question: Can I type plain text instead of using JSON presets?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Toggle ComfySwitchNode to the custom prompt path and enter a clear, single-line or multiline description (e.g., “professional headshot, charcoal suit, light gray seamless backdrop”). The graph will route that text directly to the generator.

faqItems.question: Where do I control quality or resolution?
faqItems.answer: PreviewAny shows quick checks, while SaveImage writes the final render. If your CustomCombo or the core generator node exposes parameters (e.g., resolution, steps, guidance), adjust them there. If not exposed, open the CustomCombo to reveal internal settings.

d78377cf53f4.title: LTX-2.5: FLF2V
d78377cf53f4.description: Generate a video from first and last frame reference images using LTX-2.5, blending both frames into a single animated sequence. Ideal for creating transition shots, morphing between two subjects or scenes, and building multi-shot narratives from still references.
d78377cf53f4.metaDescription: Generate smooth transitions from first and last images using LTX-2.5 in ComfyUI. Load two frames, synthesize in-betweens, and export to MP4/WebM.
d78377cf53f4.extendedDescription:
LTX-2.5: FLF2V is a focused ComfyUI workflow for turning two still images—your intended first and last frames—into a single, coherent video. It’s ideal for creating smooth transitions, morphs between subjects, or bridging shots in a sequence when you only have still references. Two LoadImage nodes supply the start and end visuals, which feed into a single LTX-2.5 FLF2V generator node (cf70afc4-5a03-47ce-8210-734b1de6c6bc). The resulting frames are handed to SaveVideo for encoding to a playable clip. A MarkdownNote is included with inline tips.

Under the hood, the LTX-2.5 node leverages Lightricks’ open video generation model and its keyframes-first “Pixel Diffusion” approach to synthesize in-between frames from your bookend images. Typical controls you’ll use are target resolution, number of frames (or duration), frames-per-second, and a random seed for reproducibility. Many builds also expose blending/easing options to bias the motion toward the first or last frame. SaveVideo then encodes the output at your chosen fps (MP4/WebM, depending on your ffmpeg setup).

For best results, match the aspect ratio and general lighting/composition of your two reference images. Larger frame counts and consistent content between the first and last frames usually produce smoother motion. If you see stretching or cropping, pre-crop your inputs to the same size before loading them into the workflow.
howToUse: Load the LTX-2.5: FLF2V workflow JSON in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote for any inline tips or defaults.
Open the two LoadImage nodes and select your starting image (first frame) and ending image (last frame). Ensure they share the same aspect ratio for clean interpolation.

In the LTX-2.5 FLF2V node (cf70afc4-5a03-47ce-8210-734b1de6c6bc), set your target resolution, number of frames (or duration), frames-per-second, and a seed if you want repeatable results. If the node exposes a blend/easing control, adjust it to favor a linear transition or an ease-in/ease-out feel.
Configure the SaveVideo node: confirm the fps matches your generator settings, choose a filename/output path, and select the desired container (MP4/WebM, depending on your ffmpeg setup).
Click Queue Prompt to generate. Inspect the output; if the motion is too fast or abrupt, increase the frame count or tweak the blend/easing, then re-run.
When satisfied, let SaveVideo write the final clip to disk. Review it in your media player and iterate on parameters as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic transitions between two storyboard frames or scene stills.
Portrait or character morphs for social content and concept visualization.
Before/after product reveals that smoothly interpolate between two shots.
Bridging two environment stills to create a connective sequence in an edit.
Logo-to-scene or icon-to-product transitions for titles and openers.

faqItems.question: Do my two images need to be the same size or aspect ratio?
faqItems.answer: Matching aspect ratios is strongly recommended. The generator will resize inputs to its working resolution, but mismatched aspects can introduce stretching or unwanted cropping. Pre-crop or pad both images to the same dimensions before loading for the cleanest results.

faqItems.question: How do I control the pace and smoothness of the transition?
faqItems.answer: The perceived duration is frames ÷ fps. To slow the transition and make it smoother, increase the number of frames while keeping fps the same. Some builds also include a blend/easing control—use it to ease-in or ease-out of the start/end frame for a more natural feel.

faqItems.question: Can I get repeatable results?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Set a fixed seed in the LTX-2.5 FLF2V node (if exposed). Using the same inputs and parameters with the same seed will reproduce the same video frames, which is useful for iterative tweaks.

faqItems.question: What if I run into performance or memory issues?
faqItems.answer: Reduce the target resolution and/or the number of frames, and ensure both images are pre-sized to the model’s working aspect to avoid extra scaling. A modern GPU is recommended for smooth local generation; if you still see out-of-memory errors, lower the resolution further and iterate.

Next, load your style reference image using another LoadImage node.
Connect both images to the MagnificImageStyleTransferNode.
Configure the MagnificImageStyleTransferNode with desired parameters for style intensity and blending.
Run the workflow to process the images and generate a new styled image.

Educators demonstrating the principles of style transfer in digital media courses.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the intensity of the style transfer?

faqItems.question: Is it possible to use this workflow for batch processing?

d833dc5abe59.title: Seedance 2.0 Multiframe Stitch
d833dc5abe59.description:
This workflow uses a lot of credits!

This workflow allows you to create a stitched multiframe video using seedance 2.0. Great of iterating and inbetweening quickly.
d833dc5abe59.metaDescription: Create smooth in-between frames from two images with Seedance 2.0 in ComfyUI, then stitch them into a video. Fast iteration for motion tests and transitions.
d833dc5abe59.extendedDescription:
Seedance 2.0 Multiframe Stitch is a ComfyUI workflow for generating smooth in-between frames between two key images, then assembling them into a video. At its core is the ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode, which uses the Seedance 2.0 model to synthesize a sequence that transitions from your first frame to your last. This makes it ideal for rapid iteration, motion studies, and quick inbetweening without writing code or handling external tools. Note: running Seedance 2.0 can be credit-intensive, so plan your frame count and resolution accordingly.

Technically, the workflow starts by loading your start and end images with LoadImage. Those images are passed into ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode to generate a multiframe batch of interpolations. ImageBatch ensures the frames are properly grouped for video creation. GetVideoComponents can be used to set or match video properties (such as frame rate) if you are aligning to a reference. Finally, CreateVideo assembles the frame batch into a video stream, and SaveVideo writes the result to disk. The result is a stitched, coherent transition clip built entirely from two stills.

What makes this useful is the combination of controllability and speed: you pick the anchor frames, the node interpolates the motion, and the rest of the graph reliably compiles and saves the output. Keep both input images the same resolution and aspect ratio for best results, and manage cost by reducing frame count, resolution, or iterations if exposed in your node configuration.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm all nodes are available: LoadImage, ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode, ImageBatch, GetVideoComponents, CreateVideo, and SaveVideo.
Use the two LoadImage nodes to select your first (start) and last (end) keyframes. Ensure both images share the same resolution and aspect ratio.

Open ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode and set the key parameters for interpolation (e.g., number of in-between frames and any quality/strength controls the node exposes). Lower values reduce cost; higher values increase smoothness.
If you want a specific playback speed, either connect GetVideoComponents to a reference clip to pull its FPS or manually set the FPS on CreateVideo.
Run the graph to generate the interpolated frame batch and compile it into a video with CreateVideo.
Preview the result in ComfyUI, then use SaveVideo to write the final stitched video to disk. Adjust frame count, FPS, or node settings and re-run as needed.
suggestedUseCases: Product or logo transitions between two designed states for motion tests and quick previews.
Storyboard inbetweens to visualize timing between key panels without full animation production.
Portrait or character pose morphs to explore motion direction and pacing between two poses.
Before/after scene transitions for motion design pitches and concept explorations.
Time-lapse smoothing by interpolating between two representative frames of a longer sequence.

faqItems.question: What does ByteDance2FirstLastFrameNode do in this workflow?

faqItems.question: Why does this workflow use a lot of credits?

d99717df8788.title: Create seamless transitions with LTX 2.3
d99717df8788.description: Create seamless transitions between shots with this LTX 2.3 workflow, featuring the FLW LoRA from Systsms
d99717df8788.metaDescription: ComfyUI LTX 2.3 + SYSTMS FLW LoRA workflow for seamless video-to-video transitions between two clips with prompt-guided control.
d99717df8788.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds seamless, text-guided transitions between two source clips using the LTX 2.3 video diffusion model and the SYSTMS FLW transition LoRA. The MODELS group loads the transformer-only LTX 2.3 backbone via DiffusionModelLoaderKJ, the matching VAE with VAELoaderKJ, and applies the FLW LoRA using LoraLoaderModelOnly to bias the model toward natural, flow-like shot changes. Prompts are encoded with CLIPTextEncode (optionally auto-generated by a Gemini node), then routed through LTXVConditioning and LTXVAddGuide to steer the transition content and style.

Under the hood, the workflow allocates a timeline in EmptyLTXVLatentVideo, manages A/V latent streams with LTXVSeparateAVLatent and LTXVConcatAVLatent, and localizes denoising to the handoff region using SolidMask and SetLatentNoiseMask. Sampling is handled by SamplerCustomAdvanced with CFGGuider, KSamplerSelect, BasicScheduler, and RandomNoise for reproducibility. After inference, VAEDecode reconstructs frames and VHS_VideoCombine assembles them into a final video. LTXVCropGuides provides compositional guides to keep subjects aligned between shots, helping the model generate cleaner, more believable morphs.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and install the required models: LTX 2.3 (22B, transformer only) from https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/tree/main/diffusion_models into models/diffusion_models, the SYSTMS FLW transition LoRA from https://huggingface.co/systms/SYSTMS-FLW-IC-LORA-LTX-2.3 into models/loras, and a compatible VAE into models/vae. (An optional distilled LoRA is available here: https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/blob/main/loras/ltx-2.3-22b-di...).
In the MODELS group, point DiffusionModelLoaderKJ to the LTX 2.3 transformer file, VAELoaderKJ to the VAE, and LoraLoaderModelOnly to the FLW LoRA. Leave LoRA strength at its default to start.

Add your two source clips in the INPUT VIDEOS group and set a frame load cap for each. The frame cap determines how many frames from each clip are used before and after the transition. If provided, use LTXVCropGuides to keep subjects framed similarly across both clips.

Set your prompt in the PROMPT group. You can keep the Google Gemini node to auto-generate a description from the inputs, or disconnect it and type directly into CLIPTextEncode. Recommended formula: "FLW, [Action A] seamlessly transforms into [Action B], [environment/style specifics]".

Open LTX SETTINGS and define resolution and total length on EmptyLTXVLatentVideo (width, height, and total frames). Transition length is computed as: total frames − frames from Clip A − frames from Clip B. Optionally refine where denoising happens by adjusting SolidMask and SetLatentNoiseMask to focus more noise in the transition region and less on the stable parts of each clip.

In SAMPLING, pick your KSampler in KSamplerSelect, set steps and scheduler in BasicScheduler, choose a CFG scale in CFGGuider (3–5 is a good start), and set a seed in RandomNoise for repeatability. Press Queue. The pipeline will sample with SamplerCustomAdvanced, decode with VAEDecode, and export the video with VHS_VideoCombine.
suggestedUseCases: Cinematic shot bridges: morphing an establishing shot into a character close-up without a hard cut.
Stylized scene transitions: transforming one environment into another (e.g., desert to cyberpunk city) while maintaining motion continuity.
Product reveal edits: transitioning from a moving prototype shot to the final product aesthetic mid-motion.
Music video edits: fluid transformations between performance and narrative shots guided by lyrical or thematic prompts.
Trailer teasers: rapid, coherent morphs between key scenes to imply a narrative arc.

faqItems.question: Do I have to use the Google Gemini node for prompts?
faqItems.answer: No. It is optional. Disconnect its string output from CLIPTextEncode and enter your own prompt. Use the template: "FLW, [Action A] seamlessly transforms into [Action B], [details]".

faqItems.question: How do I set the transition duration?
faqItems.answer: Set the frame load caps on Clip A and Clip B, then set the total frame count on EmptyLTXVLatentVideo. Transition length = total frames − Clip A frames − Clip B frames.

faqItems.question: Which files go where in ComfyUI?
faqItems.answer: Place the LTX 2.3 transformer model in models/diffusion_models, the SYSTMS FLW LoRA in models/loras, and the VAE in models/vae. Load them via DiffusionModelLoaderKJ, LoraLoaderModelOnly, and VAELoaderKJ respectively.

faqItems.question: How can I improve stability and reduce drift or flicker?
faqItems.answer: Keep CFG scale moderate (around 3–5), ensure subjects are similarly framed using LTXVCropGuides, and restrict heavy denoising to the handoff region with SolidMask + SetLatentNoiseMask. You can also lower resolution or steps slightly to avoid over-cooking details outside the transition.

db4717458b6a.title: LTX-2.3: ID LoRA
db4717458b6a.description: Generate personalized videos with synchronized audio from a text prompt, reference image, and short audio clip. Use ID-LoRA to adapt a person's appearance and voice in a single generative model.
db4717458b6a.metaDescription: Create personalized, lip-synced videos in ComfyUI using LTX-2.3 with ID-LoRA from a prompt, a face image, and a short audio clip.
db4717458b6a.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow builds personalized, lip-synced video clips by conditioning LTX-2.3 on three inputs: a reference image (appearance), a short audio clip (timing and vocal style), and a structured prompt (scene, transcript, and sound context). The core logic is encapsulated in a subgraph (the custom node with ID 98ee9e5b-467b-40aa-a534-36033f27d0b4), which orchestrates LTX-2.3 generation with ID-LoRA identity conditioning. LoadImage provides the face/pose reference, LoadAudio or RecordAudio supplies your speech, and SaveVideo writes the final video. A MarkdownNote in the canvas summarizes the structured prompt format and links to the LTX-2.3 and ID-LoRA resources.

Technically, ID-LoRA injects a lightweight identity adapter into the LTX-2.3 video diffusion process so the generated person matches the reference image without a full fine-tune. The prompt is split into three tags the subgraph expects: [VISUAL] (scene and appearance), [SPEECH] (the exact words to say), and [SOUNDS] (speaker style and ambient cues). The audio drives mouth shapes and timing, while [SPEECH] helps the model resolve phoneme-level detail for clearer lip articulation. The result is a short video of your subject speaking the provided line, visually aligned to the reference image and temporally synced to the audio.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure the LTX-2.3 model files are available locally (see the Lightricks/LTX-2.3 repository if you need to download weights).
Add a clear, front-facing reference image via the LoadImage node (good lighting, minimal occlusion).
Provide the voice clip: either record a short, clean sample with RecordAudio or import one with LoadAudio (avoid music/noise; keep the speech steady).

Compose the structured prompt in the text field used by the generation subgraph, using three sections: [VISUAL]: describe scene and appearance; [SPEECH]: write the exact transcript; [SOUNDS]: describe vocal style and ambient sounds. Example: [VISUAL]: close-up interview lighting, neutral background. [SPEECH]: "Welcome to our channel; new videos drop every Friday." [SOUNDS]: warm, calm voice; quiet studio room tone.

Run the workflow. The subgraph (98ee9e5b-467b-40aa-a534-36033f27d0b4) will condition LTX-2.3 with ID-LoRA, align mouth movements to your audio and transcript, and produce frames. SaveVideo assembles the output as a video file.

Review the result. If needed, refine by: using a sharper reference image, cleaning the audio, tightening the [SPEECH] transcript to match the clip exactly, or unpacking the subgraph to adjust generation and save settings (e.g., resolution, fps).
suggestedUseCases: Personalized greetings or announcement videos using your own face and voice.
Creator intros/outros where a consistent on-screen identity delivers scripted lines.
Training or onboarding clips featuring a company spokesperson for multiple variations of the same script.
Localized or alternate-language lines: supply the new audio and transcript to keep identity consistent.
Quick previz for dialogue sequences where timing must match a reference read.

faqItems.question: Do I need to train anything to match the person’s identity?
faqItems.answer: No full training is required. The workflow uses ID-LoRA as a lightweight identity adapter applied at generation time. Provide a high-quality reference image to improve likeness.

faqItems.question: What should I put in the structured prompt?
faqItems.answer: Use three tags: [VISUAL] for scene and appearance details, [SPEECH] for the exact words to say (match your audio), and [SOUNDS] for the speaker’s vocal style and any ambient room tone. A precise [SPEECH] section helps produce clearer lip shapes.

faqItems.question: How do I get the best lip sync?
faqItems.answer: Use a clean, dry voice recording (no background music), speak at a steady pace, and ensure the [SPEECH] transcript matches the audio exactly. Choose a front-facing, well-lit reference image so the mouth region is clear.

faqItems.question: Does the output include audio?
faqItems.answer: The workflow drives visual sync from your audio. Whether the final video file contains an embedded audio track depends on the SaveVideo configuration in your setup. If you get a silent video, you can mux the original audio in a video editor or unpack the subgraph to integrate audio muxing.
