fd3af468b1e2.extendedDescription:
Seedance 2.0 Mini: Reference to Video turns two still images into a single, cinematic video with AI-driven camera motion and strong character consistency. In ComfyUI, the workflow is compact and focused: two LoadImage nodes feed the ByteDance2ReferenceNode (the generator that runs the Seedance 2.0 Mini model), and the frames are encoded to a final clip with SaveVideo. By supplying a pair of complementary references—commonly one close-up for identity and one wider image for pose, outfit, or scene—the model blends cues to maintain the same subject across time while moving the virtual camera for a polished, shot-like result.

Technically, ByteDance2ReferenceNode ingests both reference images and synthesizes a sequence of frames conditioned on those visuals. It handles motion, composition, and temporal coherence internally, so you don’t need a separate sampler or flow node. SaveVideo then assembles the generated frames to your chosen resolution and FPS. The minimal node set makes this ideal for rapid iteration: swap references, adjust motion/length settings in the generator, and quickly export clips for storytelling, branded content, or short-film beats where continuity and shot language matter.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the three core nodes are present: two LoadImage nodes, one ByteDance2ReferenceNode, and one SaveVideo.
In each LoadImage node, choose your two reference images. Use one image for identity (clear face/subject) and the other for pose, wardrobe, or scene style. Keep similar aspect ratios when possible.

Open ByteDance2ReferenceNode. Verify the model is set to Seedance 2.0 Mini and, if required, add your API credentials or endpoint. Set generation basics such as duration, resolution, and FPS. Adjust motion strength/trajectory and character-consistency weighting if those controls are available.

Connect the two LoadImage outputs to the ByteDance2ReferenceNode inputs in the intended order (primary identity first, style/pose second). Run a short, lower-resolution test render to validate motion and identity before committing to a full pass.
Configure SaveVideo with your target FPS, format, and output path. Ensure it receives the generated frames from ByteDance2ReferenceNode, then execute the workflow to render the final clip.

Iterate: refine your references (crop for clearer faces, match lighting), tweak motion or duration in ByteDance2ReferenceNode, and re-render. For audio, add it afterward in a video editor since SaveVideo outputs silent video.
suggestedUseCases: Character-driven shorts and vignettes where the same subject must remain consistent across a moving shot.
Branded content or product hero shots using one image for the product identity and another for on-brand scene or pose.
Storyboard beat creation: quickly turn key frames into motion previews with cinematic camera moves.
Mood reels and look-dev: explore lighting, wardrobe, and framing continuity from two guiding stills.
Social trailers and teasers that require fast iteration with consistent subjects and smooth camera motion.

faqItems.question: Do I need two different images, or can I use the same one twice?
faqItems.answer: The workflow is designed for two references: one for identity and another for pose or style. If you only have one, you can feed it to both inputs, but you’ll likely get less dynamic motion or variety compared to using a complementary second image.

faqItems.question: What image preparation yields the best consistency?
faqItems.answer: Use sharp, well-lit images with similar aspect ratios and framing. For identity, ensure the subject’s face and key features are large and unobstructed. Keep backgrounds simple on the identity image and let the second image carry pose, outfit, or scene cues.

faqItems.question: How do I control duration, FPS, and resolution?
faqItems.answer: Set them in the ByteDance2ReferenceNode (for how many frames to generate and at what size) and finalize FPS/encoding in SaveVideo. For faster iteration, start with shorter durations and lower resolutions, then upscale or extend once you’re happy with motion and identity.

faqItems.question: Is the output deterministic? Can I lock a seed?
faqItems.answer: If ByteDance2ReferenceNode exposes a seed parameter, setting it will help reproduce results. Otherwise, expect small variations between runs due to stochastic generation. Keep references and settings consistent to minimize drift.

fd76422c14ea.title: Krea 2: Style Reference
fd76422c14ea.description: Upload a style reference image and input a text prompt. Generate an image matching the prompt while applying the aesthetic style from your reference.
fd76422c14ea.metaDescription: ComfyUI workflow: generate images from a prompt while applying the aesthetic of your style reference images using Krea v2 style conditioning.
fd76422c14ea.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow demonstrates style-conditioned text-to-image generation using the Krea v2 API. You provide one or more style reference images and a text prompt; the graph extracts a style representation from your references with Krea2StyleReferenceNode and uses it to guide image synthesis in Krea2ImageNode. The output is a new image that fulfills your prompt while inheriting the aesthetic from your reference images. LoadImage supplies the style inputs, Krea2StyleReferenceNode encodes them into a style signal, Krea2ImageNode performs the generation request to Krea’s API, and SaveImage writes the result to disk. A MarkdownNote is included to annotate the graph with usage tips.

Technically, the data flows as follows: one or more images from LoadImage feed into Krea2StyleReferenceNode, which produces a style reference output (an embedding/handle) that conditions the generator. Krea2ImageNode combines this style reference with your text prompt and generation settings (e.g., size and other parameters exposed in the node) to create the final image on the Krea backend. You can chain multiple input images through the style node(s) to blend influences from different sources, enabling nuanced control over palette, texture, and overall look while keeping the content determined by your prompt.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and verify the graph shows LoadImage → Krea2StyleReferenceNode → Krea2ImageNode → SaveImage (with a MarkdownNote for guidance).
Configure Krea API access in the Krea2 nodes (enter your API key or follow the node’s credential instructions in ComfyUI).

Add your style reference: use one or more LoadImage nodes and connect their outputs to Krea2StyleReferenceNode. To blend multiple styles, chain additional reference images through the style node(s) as noted in the author tip.
Open Krea2ImageNode and enter a clear text prompt describing the subject and scene you want. Connect the style reference output from Krea2StyleReferenceNode to the style input on Krea2ImageNode.
Adjust generation settings exposed by Krea2ImageNode (e.g., resolution/aspect and any style influence controls if provided). Click Queue/Execute to run the graph.

Review the saved outputs from SaveImage. Iterate by refining your prompt, swapping or reordering style references, or adjusting style strength (if available) to increase or decrease the influence of the reference.
suggestedUseCases: Create brand-consistent social images by applying a brand’s reference look to new campaign prompts.
Generate concept art that blends a specific painterly style with new subject matter.
Produce product hero shots with a unified art direction across multiple SKUs.
Match the mood and grade of film stills or photography references while varying the scene content.
Design UI or illustration mockups that inherit a house style for rapid visual iteration.

faqItems.question: How do multiple style images affect the result?
faqItems.answer: Chaining multiple inputs lets the workflow blend influences from each reference. Earlier references often set broad tone and palette, while later ones can nudge details. If styles conflict, reduce the number of references or adjust their order to prioritize the look you want.

faqItems.question: Where do I set my Krea API key?
faqItems.answer: Krea2 nodes call the Krea API. Enter your API key where the node UI requests credentials or follow your ComfyUI/Krea integration’s setup instructions. Without valid credentials, Krea2ImageNode will not generate results.

faqItems.question: How can I control how strongly the style influences the image?
faqItems.answer: If the nodes expose a style strength or weighting parameter, lower it for a looser influence and raise it for a closer match to the reference. You can also use fewer or more focused references (e.g., a cropped texture or palette) to fine-tune the effect.

faqItems.question: Why does my output not match the content of the style image?
faqItems.answer: This workflow transfers style, not content. Ensure your text prompt clearly describes the subject and composition you want. Use style references that emphasize look (palette, brushwork, lighting) rather than content elements you expect to be copied.

fdab9848b160.title: MiniMax: Video
fdab9848b160.description: Generate high-quality videos from text prompts with optional first-frame control using MiniMax Hailuo-02 model. Supports multiple resolutions (768P/1080P) and durations (6/10s) with intelligent prompt optimization.
fdab9848b160.metaDescription: Generate high-quality videos from text prompts with MiniMax: Video workflow. Supports 768P/1080P resolutions and 6/10s durations with prompt optimization.
fdab9848b160.extendedDescription: The MiniMax: Video workflow enables users to generate high-quality videos from text prompts, leveraging the powerful MiniMax Hailuo-02 model. This workflow is designed to be versatile, supporting multiple resolutions such as 768P and 1080P, and offering video durations of 6 or 10 seconds. A key feature is the optional first-frame control, which allows users to set a specific starting image for the video, providing greater creative control over the output. Technically, this is achieved through the MinimaxHailuoVideoNode, which processes the text input and any initial image to create a coherent video sequence. The workflow also includes nodes like LoadImage for input management and SaveVideo for exporting the final video. MarkdownNote and Note nodes are used to provide guidance and documentation within the workflow.
howToUse: Load the MiniMax: Video workflow in ComfyUI.
Enter your text prompt in the designated field within the MinimaxHailuoVideoNode.
Optionally, load a first-frame image using the LoadImage node or disable it using Ctrl + B if not needed.
Select your desired video resolution (768P or 1080P) and duration (6 or 10 seconds) in the workflow settings.
Run the workflow to generate the video, using the SaveVideo node to export the final output.
Review the video and adjust the text prompt or settings as necessary for different results.
suggestedUseCases: Creating promotional video content for social media platforms.
Generating educational videos from text-based lesson plans.
Producing artistic video sequences for digital art projects.
Developing prototype videos for marketing campaigns.
Enhancing storytelling by visualizing narratives through video.

faqItems.question: Do I need to provide a first-frame image?
faqItems.answer: No, providing a first-frame image is optional. You can disable this feature using Ctrl + B if you prefer the model to generate the entire video from the text prompt.

faqItems.question: What are the supported video resolutions and durations?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports video resolutions of 768P and 1080P, with durations of either 6 or 10 seconds.

faqItems.question: How do I ensure a secure network environment for using this workflow?
faqItems.answer: Ensure your network allows access from '127.0.0.1' or 'localhost' and that you are using our API Node on a website service starting with 'https'.

faqItems.question: Can I adjust the video after generation?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can review the output and modify the text prompt or other settings to refine the video as needed.

fe5600667e2c.title: Sprite Sheet Generator
fe5600667e2c.description: Upload an image of your sprite and receive individual frames of idle, attack, walk and jump animations.
fe5600667e2c.metaDescription: Generate sprite sheet animations from a single image using ComfyUI's Sprite Sheet Generator workflow.
fe5600667e2c.extendedDescription:
The Sprite Sheet Generator workflow in ComfyUI is designed to transform a single sprite image into a comprehensive set of animation frames, including idle, attack, walk, and jump sequences. This workflow leverages advanced nodes such as LoadImage, GeminiImage2Node, and BatchImagesNode to efficiently process and segment the sprite into individual frames. By utilizing models like Google and Nano Banana Pro, the workflow ensures high-quality output that is suitable for various animation needs. Custom nodes like comfyui-kjnodes and comfyui_layerstyle further enhance the workflow by providing specialized processing capabilities.

Technically, the workflow begins by loading the sprite image using the LoadImage node. It then processes the image through a series of nodes that include PrimitiveInt and PrimitiveNode for parameter adjustments, ensuring the sprite is correctly segmented into frames. Nodes such as e6bcb358-3fee-47eb-8c25-30eeee20d90e and 79dc3651-3ca7-4d1d-9246-9a951b834ab9 play critical roles in defining the animation sequences, while SaveImage and SaveVideo nodes handle the output of individual frames and compiled animations. This workflow is particularly useful for game developers and animators who need to quickly generate sprite animations without manually editing each frame.
howToUse: Load the Sprite Sheet Generator workflow in ComfyUI.
Upload your sprite image using the LoadImage node.
Adjust parameters using PrimitiveInt and PrimitiveNode for desired frame segmentation.
Process the image through GeminiImage2Node and BatchImagesNode for animation frame extraction.
Use SaveImage and SaveVideo nodes to export the individual frames and compiled animations.
suggestedUseCases: Creating character animations for video games.
Developing animated sequences for mobile apps.
Producing educational animations for digital learning tools.
Designing interactive media content with animated sprites.
Generating prototype animations for creative projects.

faqItems.question: What image formats are supported for uploading?
faqItems.answer: The workflow supports common image formats such as PNG, JPEG, and BMP for sprite uploads.

faqItems.question: Can I customize the animation sequences?
faqItems.answer: Yes, you can adjust parameters using PrimitiveInt and PrimitiveNode to customize frame segmentation and animation sequences.

faqItems.question: How do I export the animations?
faqItems.answer: Use the SaveImage node to export individual frames and the SaveVideo node to compile and export the entire animation.

faqItems.question: Is this workflow suitable for high-resolution sprites?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the workflow is capable of handling high-resolution sprites, ensuring detailed and quality animations.

fe773d7d7377.title: Seedance 2.0 - Extend Video
fe773d7d7377.description: Uses Seedance 2.0 to seamlessly extend an input video. Enter your prompt for the video that occurs immediately following the driving input video. This workflow detects which frame is the most seamless and allows you to select to trim from that frame.
fe773d7d7377.metaDescription: Extend a video seamlessly with Seedance 2.0 in ComfyUI. Generate follow-on frames, auto-find the best cut point, and export a smooth extended clip.
fe773d7d7377.extendedDescription:
Seedance 2.0 - Extend Video is a ComfyUI workflow that continues an input clip by generating follow-on frames and trimming to the most seamless handoff point. It uses LoadVideo and GetVideoComponents to ingest your source, extract frames, FPS, and audio, and then feeds a follow-up text prompt into the Seedance 2.0 generator (ByteDance2ReferenceNode). The prompt describes what happens immediately after the last frame of your input, and the model predicts a continuation as a batch of new frames. PrimitiveStringMultiline and StringConcatenate are used to assemble the final conditioning text you send into the generator.

Because model-generated continuations won’t perfectly match your last real frame, the workflow includes an automatic cut-point aid. The Preview Images Difference node (f1f7c973-e50b-4ec7-84c5-0ef2eef1fc84) compares each generated frame to the last input frame and visualizes color difference; the darkest preview indicates the closest visual match. You select that index and trim the generated batch starting from that frame with ImageFromBatch+, then concatenate original frames with the trimmed continuation via BatchImagesNode. CreateVideo rebuilds a new clip at the source FPS, AudioConcat preserves or stitches audio as needed, and SaveVideo writes the final extended video. PreviewImage nodes are included to quickly inspect the last source frame and candidate match frames before committing to render.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and ensure required custom nodes are installed: ByteDance2ReferenceNode (Seedance 2.0) and the Preview Images Difference node (ID: f1f7c973-e50b-4ec7-84c5-0ef2eef1fc84).
Connect your input clip to LoadVideo. GetVideoComponents will extract frames, FPS, and audio. Verify the FPS and resolution are correct for your project.

Enter a follow-on description in PrimitiveStringMultiline (what happens right after your input ends). The workflow concatenates this with any preset text via StringConcatenate and feeds it to ByteDance2ReferenceNode to generate a continuation batch.

Queue the graph to produce a first pass. Use the Preview Images Difference output to identify the darkest frame (least color difference to the last input frame). Note its index and preview it alongside the last source frame via the PreviewImage nodes.
Set the chosen start index in ImageFromBatch+ to trim the continuation so it starts at the most seamless frame. BatchImagesNode then concatenates original frames with the trimmed continuation.
CreateVideo assembles frames at the original FPS; AudioConcat preserves or appends audio as configured. Use SaveVideo to export the final extended clip to disk.
suggestedUseCases: Pacing adjustments: extend a shot to hold on a subject longer without a visible jump cut.
Social deliverables: meet minimum duration requirements by adding a seamless tail to short clips.
Transition design: generate extra frames to create smoother match-cuts or dissolve-friendly handoffs.
Loop crafting: find a near-perfect match frame to create cleaner loop points for background videos.
VFX temping: extend establishing shots in pre-vis before committing to reshoots.

faqItems.question: How do I know which generated frame will cut most seamlessly?
faqItems.answer: Use the Preview Images Difference node. It compares each generated frame to the last input frame; the darkest preview indicates the smallest color difference. Set that index in ImageFromBatch+ so the continuation begins at that frame.

faqItems.question: How can I make the continuation feel more consistent with my source footage?
faqItems.answer: Write your prompt to closely describe the immediate next moment (lighting, motion direction, subject pose, background). Keep style cues consistent with the source. Generate more frames than you need, then trim at the best-matching index using the difference preview.

faqItems.question: What about audio—will it continue automatically?
faqItems.answer: GetVideoComponents extracts the original audio, and AudioConcat can stitch it with the extended segment. Since generated frames don’t include new audio, you’ll typically preserve the original track up to the cut or add new audio in post.

faqItems.question: How long can I extend the video?
faqItems.answer: It depends on your hardware and the settings in ByteDance2ReferenceNode (e.g., number of frames to generate). Quality and scene coherence generally decrease the farther you extend, so it’s best to generate a modest overrun and pick the optimal trim point.

fedbcfb05b08.title: Remove Watermark from Video - LTX 2.3 LoRA
fedbcfb05b08.description: Upload an input video with watermarks and remove them with one click.
fedbcfb05b08.metaDescription: One-click video watermark removal in ComfyUI using LTX 2.3 LoRA-guided inpainting. Load, process, and save clean footage with frame-wise consistency.
fedbcfb05b08.extendedDescription:
This ComfyUI workflow removes persistent watermarks from a video by inpainting over them frame by frame with a LoRA-enhanced diffusion pass. It starts with LoadVideo to ingest your clip and GetVideoComponents to extract frames, dimensions, and timing info. The core processing is handled by two custom nodes (UUIDs 3b019976-c705-40af-8f45-081975d72105 and 83cfc570-fff1-4869-8c43-d39ef189634b), which apply an LTX 2.3 LoRA-guided inpainting step across the sequence to reconstruct clean background detail where the watermark sits. Finally, SaveVideo reassembles the processed frames into a new video file.

Technically, the pipeline performs video-to-video inpainting using a Stable Diffusion-style model augmented by the LTX 2.3 LoRA adapter to bias reconstruction toward plausible content while suppressing the watermark. The custom processing stage maintains per-frame consistency and uses mask-driven edits so only the marked area is regenerated, preserving the rest of the frame. Because the work happens at the frame level and is driven by inpainting, the result avoids typical blur or smudge artifacts of traditional filters and holds up better on semi-transparent, corner logos. It’s a practical, one-click solution for cleaning owned or licensed footage without manual rotoscoping.
howToUse: Open the workflow in ComfyUI and confirm the required nodes are present: LoadVideo, GetVideoComponents, the two custom processing nodes (UUIDs 3b019976-c705-40af-8f45-081975d72105 and 83cfc570-fff1-4869-8c43-d39ef189634b), and SaveVideo.
Place the LTX 2.3 LoRA file in your ComfyUI models/loras directory and ensure the compatible base checkpoint is available in models/checkpoints (the custom processing node will reference both).
In the LoadVideo node, select your input video. GetVideoComponents will pull frame size and FPS automatically; keep these defaults unless you need to downscale for speed.

Open the custom processing node that applies the LTX 2.3 LoRA inpainting and review its settings. If exposed, adjust LoRA weight (e.g., 0.6–0.9) and denoise strength (e.g., 0.35–0.6) to balance watermark removal against fine texture retention. Leave other defaults for a first pass.
Queue and run the workflow. Inspect the output frames or the saved clip. If faint ghosting remains, slightly increase LoRA weight or denoise; if background detail softens, reduce them a bit.
When satisfied, let the full video process and collect the final file from the SaveVideo node’s output folder. If you need original audio, remux it from the source using your video editor or ffmpeg.
suggestedUseCases: Removing a channel bug or timecode burn-in from your own production dailies or screeners before client sharing.
Cleaning licensed stock footage after purchase to replace the preview watermark with a clean master.
Restoring archival or home videos by removing date stamps or overlay text you control the rights to.
Preparing social clips from branded masters by removing your own persistent logo for neutral versions.

faqItems.question: What model does this workflow use to remove watermarks?
faqItems.answer: It uses an inpainting pipeline guided by the LTX 2.3 LoRA. Place the LTX 2.3 LoRA in models/loras and ensure a compatible base checkpoint is available in models/checkpoints. The custom processing node (UUIDs 3b019976-c705-40af-8f45-081975d72105 and 83cfc570-fff1-4869-8c43-d39ef189634b) handles applying the LoRA across video frames.

faqItems.question: Will it work on moving or animated watermarks?
faqItems.answer: It’s optimized for persistent, static watermarks (e.g., corner logos or date stamps). Moving, animated, or large-area overlays are harder to inpaint consistently and may require parameter tuning, pre-masking, or manual cleanup.

faqItems.question: Does the output keep the original audio?
faqItems.answer: SaveVideo typically writes the processed video stream only. If you need the original audio, remux it afterward using a video editor or a command like: ffmpeg -i clean.mp4 -i source.mp4 -map 0:v -map 1:a -c copy final.mp4.

faqItems.question: How can I improve results on tough watermarks?
faqItems.answer: Try moderately increasing the LoRA weight and denoise strength, downscaling slightly to reduce processing noise, and ensuring the watermark region is fully covered by the inpainting mask settings in the custom node. For very stubborn cases, process in segments around scene cuts.

ff88e6723334.title: Comfy for Advertising - Talent Casting
ff88e6723334.metaDescription: ComfyUI casting previs: turn a headshot into a branded still and quick motion test using Gemini image-to-image and Kling image-to-video.
ff88e6723334.extendedDescription:
This workflow builds fast, client-ready casting previs for advertising in two passes: a photo-real still and a short motion test. In STEP 1 – PREVIS STILL FRAME, your talent headshot (LoadImage) is combined with a scene description to synthesize a single frame of the talent in context (e.g., tennis court, soda product). Prompt text from MarkdownNote and PrimitiveNode is merged with shot directions using StringConcatenate, and GeminiImage2Node performs image-to-image guided synthesis using the headshot and any optional product/environment references. The resulting frame is saved with SaveImage for quick side-by-side casting reviews.

STEP 2 – PREVIS VIDEO upgrades that still into a short motion clip. ImageBatchMulti assembles one or more selected stills into a batch, and KlingOmniProImageToVideoNode generates a quick image-to-video preview—ideal for validating basic motion like a gentle dolly-in, a sip, and a look-to-can. SaveVideo writes the final clip to disk. Because the video is derived from your approved still, character identity and wardrobe cues tend to remain consistent across frames, making it well-suited for talent casting, pitch decks, and early client sign-off.
howToUse: Load the workflow in ComfyUI and read the MarkdownNote for shot guidance. The author notes describe a medium-wide tennis court setup and a slow dolly-in.
Provide inputs via LoadImage: add the talent headshot first (required). Optionally load a product packshot (soda can) and an environment plate (tennis court) to guide context.

Refine the shot text. Use the INPUT SCENE DESCRIPTION groups to edit scene/brand details. PrimitiveNode fields and MarkdownNote hold descriptors (e.g., wardrobe: tennis attire; action: sip, joyful expression). StringConcatenate assembles these into the final prompt.
Run STEP 1 – PREVIS STILL FRAME. GeminiImage2Node uses the prompt plus your references to generate the casting still. Review the output from SaveImage in your ComfyUI/output directory.

If the still looks right, select it in ImageBatchMulti (you can queue multiple variations). Edit motion notes (e.g., 'camera slowly dollies in; looks at can') in the second INPUT SCENE DESCRIPTION if present.
Run STEP 2 – PREVIS VIDEO. KlingOmniProImageToVideoNode converts the selected still(s) into short clips. Retrieve the file(s) from SaveVideo and review identity/motion before sharing.
suggestedUseCases: Agency casting: preview multiple talents in the same branded setup to compare look, vibe, and on-camera presence.
Pitch/storyboards: generate fast hero frames and motion beats to communicate direction before production.
Client A/B testing: swap product artwork or environments to test brand alignment with the same talent.
Social mockups: produce quick in-situation visuals for campaign planning and placement reviews.
Look continuity checks: validate wardrobe, props, and background consistency before a shoot.

faqItems.question: How do I get the best identity match from the headshot?
faqItems.answer: Use a high-resolution, front-facing headshot with neutral lighting. Load the headshot first as the primary reference. Keep prompts consistent between the still and video steps, and avoid conflicting descriptors (e.g., changing hair color) unless intentional.

faqItems.question: Can I change the wardrobe, product, or environment?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Update the INPUT SCENE DESCRIPTION text and, if available, provide product/environment images via LoadImage. The StringConcatenate node merges these details into the final prompt used by GeminiImage2Node, which will guide the look in the still and carry through to the video.

faqItems.question: What controls the camera movement and action in the video?
faqItems.answer: Your motion cues in the INPUT SCENE DESCRIPTION for STEP 2. Describe actions concisely (e.g., 'talent takes a sip, smiles, then glances at the can; slow 2–3s dolly-in'). KlingOmniProImageToVideoNode uses the approved still plus these cues to generate a short motion pass.

faqItems.question: Where do I find the outputs, and what formats are saved?
faqItems.answer: SaveImage writes the stills to the ComfyUI/output images folder, and SaveVideo writes the motion previews to the ComfyUI/output videos folder. Filenames and formats follow your node settings; check the SaveImage/SaveVideo nodes to adjust naming and codec.

ffbc62a77b85.title: Flux.1 Dev OneReward

ffbc62a77b85.metaDescription: Learn inpainting and outpainting with the Flux.1 Dev OneReward workflow. Perfect for seamless image editing and object removal.

faqItems.question: What is the primary function of the Flux.1 model in this workflow?
faqItems.answer: The Flux.1 model is used for inpainting and outpainting tasks, allowing for seamless filling or extension of image areas.

faqItems.question: Can this workflow be used for video editing?

faqItems.question: How do I edit the mask for inpainting?

faqItems.question: Is it necessary to update ComfyUI before using this workflow?

fffa07892f17.title: Hairstyle Changer
fffa07892f17.description: Try any haircut or hair color before you commit. Upload a selfie and use the hairstyle changer workflow to a variety of hair options.
fffa07892f17.metaDescription: Try haircuts and colors on your selfie in ComfyUI. Switch presets, preview instantly, and save results with a custom hairstyle processor.
fffa07892f17.extendedDescription:
Hairstyle Changer is a ComfyUI workflow that lets you preview different haircuts and hair colors on a selfie before you commit. It starts with LoadImage to bring in your photo, then routes your style choices through ComfySwitchNode and preset strings defined in PrimitiveStringMultiline. Those choices are combined with StringConcatenate and, when needed, pulled from a structured presets block via JsonExtractString. The edited result is displayed in PreviewAny and saved through SaveImage.

At the core is a custom processing node (id: d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e) that applies the hairstyle/color change using the inputs prepared upstream. CustomCombo is used to package the image and text parameters into a clean input for that node. This parameterized design makes it easy to A/B test looks simply by flipping the ComfySwitchNode or tweaking the preset strings—keeping your original photo intact while focusing changes on hair appearance.
howToUse: Load the Hairstyle Changer workflow in ComfyUI. If ComfyUI reports a missing node with id d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e, install the extension that provides it, then reload.
Open the LoadImage node and select a clear selfie (frontal face, good lighting, hair visible). This becomes the base image for all variations.

Choose a hairstyle and color: use the ComfySwitchNode to toggle between preset options. Presets are defined in PrimitiveStringMultiline; the workflow uses JsonExtractString and StringConcatenate to assemble the parameters sent to the processor.
Optionally customize: edit the text in PrimitiveStringMultiline to add or modify presets (e.g., new color names or style descriptions). Ensure keys match what the ComfySwitchNode selects.
Queue/Run the workflow. Inspect the output in PreviewAny. If needed, adjust the selected preset or text parameters and run again until you’re happy with the look.
Save your result with the SaveImage node. For multiple looks, queue several runs with different ComfySwitchNode selections and save each output.
suggestedUseCases: Personal style planning: quickly try bobs, bangs, layers, and color variations before a salon visit.
Salon/client consultations: generate fast visual references for suggested cuts and colorways during appointments.
Wig and color try-ons for e-commerce: preview product styles and shades on a customer’s uploaded photo.
Cosplay and character design: test stylized colors and shapes to match a character without permanent changes.
Social content A/B testing: create multiple hair looks to see which thumbnail or profile picture performs best.

faqItems.question: What kind of selfie works best?
faqItems.answer: A front-facing photo with even lighting, minimal shadows, and hair clearly visible. Avoid hats, heavy hair accessories, or obstructions. A neutral background helps the processor focus on hair.

faqItems.question: Does the workflow change only the hair?
faqItems.answer: It is configured to target hair appearance via the custom processor (node id d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e) and its text parameters. Minor spill to nearby regions can occur; if you see drift, try a tighter crop around the head, reduce extreme style changes in the preset text, and rerun.

faqItems.question: How do I add my own hairstyles or colors?
faqItems.answer: Edit PrimitiveStringMultiline to include new preset entries (e.g., keys like "copper_lob" or "icy_blonde"). Use JsonExtractString to pull those entries, and ensure your ComfySwitchNode points to the correct keys. StringConcatenate will assemble the final parameter string for the processor.

faqItems.question: I get an error about a missing node. What should I do?
faqItems.answer: Install the extension that provides the custom node with id d4c06663-cb1a-4a41-a36b-f09c93e55e7e and restart ComfyUI. Check the ComfyUI console/log for the exact repository or package name if it’s indicated by your setup.
